Summary

This PR adds an option to automatically remove a link when the file it points to can no longer be found. Previously broken links were left in place; with this change users/administrators can choose to have such links removed to keep link lists clean.

What this does

- Introduces a configurable option (UI toggle and config flag) to remove links when the target file is missing.
- Adds detection of missing target files on access and via a background sweep job; when enabled the link is removed rather than left broken.
- Adds a confirmation flow for UI-driven removals and an audit/log entry for automated removals so actions are traceable.
- Adds tests covering detection, removal behavior, and the config toggle.

Behavior details

- Default: option is off to preserve existing behavior and avoid unexpected deletions.
- When enabled:
  - On read/access: if the linked file does not exist, the link is removed and an audit log entry is created.
  - Background sweep: periodic job scans links and removes those whose targets are missing.
  - UI: users can enable/disable the behavior in settings; manual removal still prompts for confirmation.

Migration/compatibility

- No destructive changes to the DB schema are required. The option is opt-in by default.
- Existing links remain untouched unless the feature is enabled and a missing file is detected.

Testing and verification

Manual steps to verify:
1. Create a link to a file.
2. Delete or move the target file so it is no longer found.
3. With the option disabled: confirm the link remains and is marked broken.
4. Enable the option and either access the link or run the background sweep job: confirm the link is removed and an audit entry appears.

Notes for reviewers

- Review the sweep job interval and performance implications for large datasets.
- Confirm logging/audit format meets traceability requirements.
- Ensure the UI toggle placement and wording is clear to avoid accidental enabling.

Summary

Refactor and fix the Groups dialog UI and update the changelog.

What I changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/groups/GroupDialogView.java
  - Cleaned up and refactored the Groups dialog view code to improve readability and maintainability.
  - Fixed several UI issues (layout and alignment problems, dialog sizing/resizing behavior, and focus handling) so the dialog behaves correctly across different window sizes and platforms.
  - Improved accessibility/usability by ensuring controls receive focus predictably and by clarifying control labels/tooltips where appropriate.
  - Strengthened null-safety and reduced potential for runtime exceptions when opening the dialog without an active selection.

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added an entry describing the changes and fixes to the Groups dialog so users are aware of the UI improvements and bug fixes.

Why this change

The Groups dialog previously exhibited layout and focus issues that made it unreliable in certain window configurations and when invoked without a selection. The refactor reduces complexity in the view code, prevents known runtime errors, and results in a more consistent user experience.

Testing

- Manually verified the dialog opens and closes correctly, that controls receive focus, and that resizing behaves as expected.
- Verified that no NPEs occur when opening the dialog without a selected group.

Notes

No external API changes. This is an internal UI improvement and bugfix; users will notice a smoother, more reliable Groups dialog. CHANGELOG updated to reflect the improvement.

Make table column sort order persistent

This PR persists the column sort order so that table column ordering and sort state survive between application runs. The implementation follows the JavaFX column sort-order model and stays close to the MVVM pattern used elsewhere in the codebase.

Key points:
- Persist column sort order across sessions
- Implementation modeled after JavaFX and MVVM patterns
- Unit tests added for the changes
- Manual testing performed in a running JabRef instance
- Changelog updated

Related issues:
- fixes #4800
- fixes #4224
- refs #5713, #5368
- follow-up to #4327 and #5544

Notes and next steps:
- I don’t expect noticeable performance impact compared to master, though no profiler was used to verify this — feedback and benchmarking welcome
- A follow-up enhancement would be to implement sort order per library, which would enable additional use cases (e.g., embedding JabRef as a library)

Fixes #8108 — show preview for available citation styles and add searchable filter

Summary
- Allow previewing citation styles from the "Available" list in the Preview preferences, not only styles in the "Chosen" list.
- Add a search box to filter available styles by name (case-insensitive).
- Ensure the preview viewer and source editor become visible whenever a style is selected in either the chosen or available lists.
- Small robustness fixes in PreviewPreferences for empty preview cycles.

What I changed
- CHANGELOG.md: Added entries describing the feature and search option.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/preview/PreviewTab.fxml: Added a search CustomTextField to the preview preferences UI.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/preview/PreviewTab.java:
  - Wired the search box (prompt icon + text listener) and hooked it to the ViewModel.
  - Use the ViewModel's filtered list for the available list view.
  - Show preview and edit area when either an available or chosen style is selected.
  - Ensure selecting an available item sets the layout in the ViewModel.
  - Minor cleanup around keypress timing logic.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/preview/PreviewTabViewModel.java:
  - Added a FilteredList<PreviewLayout> backed by the available list and exposed it via getFilteredPreviews().
  - Implemented setFilterPredicate(String) to filter available styles (case-independent).
  - Small rework and finalization of a few members; removed an unused listener and some duplicated logic.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/preview/PreviewLayout.java: Added default containsCaseIndependent(String) helper for case-insensitive matching.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/preferences/PreviewPreferences.java:
  - getCurrentPreviewStyle() now handles empty preview cycles safely.
  - getTextBasedPreviewLayout() uses the stored previewStyle field when constructing TextBasedPreviewLayout.

Notes and testing
- Manually tested UI interactions. The new search box filters available styles in real time and selecting an available style displays the preview source and rendered preview.
- The change should address the issue when the preview on the right side was previously only shown for chosen styles.

Checklist
- Fixes #8108
- CHANGELOG updated
- Manually tested UI

If you want I can add unit tests for the filter behavior and a small integration test ensuring preview visibility when selecting items from the available list.

Summary

This PR contains a collection of improvements, bug fixes and tests across importers, preference handling, field definitions and integrity checking.

Key changes

- Importers
  - RisImporter and MedlinePlainImporter: improved format recognition and parsing using stream-based reading and regex checks; normalize various dash characters; better handling of folded/continued lines and entry delimiters.
  - BiblioscapeImporter: parsing/continuation logic preserved; skips empty lines and correctly assembles entries and comments into BibEntry fields.

- OAI2Handler
  - SAX handler: added utility to normalize/correct line breaks (correctLineBreaks) and ensure character buffering is initialized before use.

- Field and entry type model
  - FieldName: added/standardized many field name constants; updated getDisplayName to handle case-insensitive lookups and return sensible display names for common identifier fields (DOI, ISBN, ISSN, PMID, PDF, URL, URI).
  - Added getNotTextFieldNames helper to expose non-text fields.
  - BibtexEntryTypes and InternalBibtexFields: keep comprehensive lists of standard BibTeX entry types and field properties (pagination, dates, person name fields, verbatim fields, etc.) used across validation and UI.

- Integrity checks
  - NoBibtexFieldChecker: implemented runtime determination of BibLaTeX-only fields by comparing BibLaTeX entry types to BibTeX entry types and excluding internal default general fields; checker now reports BibLaTeX-only fields appropriately.
  - Added/updated integrity-related behavior to rely on InternalBibtexFields.DEFAULT_GENERAL_FIELDS so common fields (e.g., comment, DOI, URL) are not flagged.

- Preferences
  - JabRefPreferences: improvements around storing/loading custom entry types per BibDatabaseMode (BibTeX vs BibLaTeX), utility methods for list serialization (quoting/escaping), and several default preference initializations.
  - Exposed methods to manage custom entry types and preview/cleanup defaults.

- Tests
  - Added/updated tests for integrity checks (IntegrityCheckTest) and NoBibtexFieldChecker (NoBibTexFieldCheckerTest) covering a wide range of validation rules (URLs, years, editions, months, journaltitle vs journal, bibtex key generation, page formats, ISSN/ISBN/DOI validation, ASCII checks, file linking relative to .bib location, and BibLaTeX-only field detection).

Why this change

These changes make importers more robust and resilient to real-world input, improve field/name handling and display, and harden the integrity checks so that BibLaTeX-specific fields are reported correctly while avoiding false positives for common/general fields. The added tests lock in expected behavior and prevent regressions.

Notes for reviewers

- Focus review on parsing logic in the importers (folding/continuation handling and entry splitting) and on the NoBibtexFieldChecker logic that computes BibLaTeX-only fields at runtime.
- Some utility methods in JabRefPreferences and FieldName were extended to support the new checks and tests; ensure there are no regressions in preference serialization or display name lookups.

Fix citation key generation for bracketed patterns

What changed
- Implement proper handling of bracketed subpatterns in citation key patterns.
  - Bracketed parts are now included only when they produce non-empty content, avoiding gratuitous separators or empty segments.

- Update CitationKeyGenerator to respect the semantics of BracketedPattern and to avoid producing trailing or duplicate separators when optional parts are omitted.

Why this was necessary
- Previously, patterns that used bracketed (optional) sections could yield keys with extra separators or unexpected empty parts. This produced incorrect or ugly citation keys and caused test failures.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/citationkeypattern/BracketedPattern.java — core logic for parsing/handling bracketed patterns improved.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/citationkeypattern/CitationKeyGenerator.java — generator updated to integrate bracketed-pattern behavior and avoid empty segments.
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/citationkeypattern/BracketedPatternTest.java — tests added/updated to cover optional, empty, and nested bracket scenarios.
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/citationkeypattern/CitationKeyGeneratorTest.java — tests adjusted to assert no extra separators and correct inclusion/exclusion of optional parts.
- CHANGELOG.md — added entry describing the fix.

Tests
- New and updated unit tests cover typical and edge cases for bracketed patterns to ensure stable behavior going forward.

Notes
- This is a bugfix; no user-facing configuration changes are required. The changelog includes a short note describing the fix.

Summary

Fix various copy-to-clipboard issues across the app to make copy actions reliable and consistent on desktop and mobile.

What I changed

- Implemented a robust copyToClipboard utility that:
  - Uses navigator.clipboard.writeText when available and in secure contexts
  - Falls back to a temporary textarea + document.execCommand('copy') for older browsers
  - Ensures the clipboard write completes before removing the temporary element (fixes race conditions)
  - Validates and trims input before copying to avoid copying empty strings
  - Restores focus and previous selection after copy
  - Handles and surfaces permission or write errors gracefully
- Improved UI behavior after copy:
  - Tooltip/button shows a consistent success or failure state
  - Keyboard shortcuts and long-press handlers were fixed to not interfere with native selection on mobile
- Added retry logic for transient failures (small backoff, configurable)
- Added unit tests and integration tests around the copy utility and the main copy button components
- Updated documentation/comments for the utility and exported types

Why this is needed

Users experienced intermittent failures when copying content, lost focus or selection after copying, and inconsistent UI feedback. These fixes make copy features reliable across modern and older browsers and improve error handling and UX.

Testing / QA steps

1. Desktop (modern): click copy buttons and confirm clipboard contains expected text; verify tooltip shows success.
2. Desktop (older browsers): verify fallback mechanism copies text.
3. Mobile: long-press and keyboard shortcut behaviors should not break native selection; confirm copy action works where supported.
4. Simulate permission/clipboard errors to confirm error UI and retry logic.
5. Run unit and integration tests: npm test (or yarn test) and ensure all new tests pass.

Notes

- This is a backwards-compatible patch; no public API changes.
- Marked as a patch release in CHANGELOG.

Summary

This refactors and relocates parsing and string-serialization logic to follow the project convention: types that can be read from a string expose a public static parse(...) factory, and types that can be written to a string expose a public getAsString()/getAsStringList()/getAsStringMap() method. This consolidates parsing/writing behavior with the types they belong to and removes duplicated parsing code.

What I changed

- Introduced parse/getAsString API on domain classes
  - MetaData: added static parse(Map<String,String>) and renamed serialize() to getAsStringMap(); constructor made private to force use of parse
  - FieldFormatterCleanups: convertToString -> getAsStringList; parseFromString -> parse
  - SaveOrderConfig: constructor made private, added static parse(List<String>) and renamed getConfigurationList -> getAsStringList
  - GroupTreeNode: added static parse(List<String>) delegating to GroupsParser
  - GroupsParser: class visibility reduced to package-private; importGroups kept but called via GroupTreeNode.parse
  - CustomEntryType: added static parse(String) and getAsString()
  - BibDatabaseMode: added static parse(String) and getAsString()

- Updated callers to use the new methods
  - BibtexParser: uses MetaData.parse and CustomEntryType.parse
  - BibDatabaseWriter: uses MetaData.getAsStringMap and CustomEntryType.getAsString
  - CleanupPreset and JabRefPreferences: use FieldFormatterCleanups.getAsStringList
  - MetaData: uses SaveOrderConfig.parse and SaveOrderConfig.getAsStringList, and BibDatabaseMode.parse

- Removed duplicated parsing helper
  - CustomEntryTypesManager.parseEntryType removed; parsing logic moved into CustomEntryType.parse

- Tests updated
  - MetaDataTest adjusted to assert against getAsStringMap()

Reasons and benefits

- Keeps parsing/serialization logic next to the relevant type, improving cohesion and discoverability
- Standardizes APIs across types for parsing and string output, matching the conventions described in the issue
- Removes duplicated parsing code
- No intended behavior changes; mostly API/organizational refactor to fix issue #888

Notes for reviewers

- Verify there are no remaining external usages of the removed parseEntryType helper
- Most changes are mechanical renames and small delegations; focus review on CustomEntryType and MetaData parsing to ensure no subtle behavior changes
- The GroupsParser class is now package-private and accessed via GroupTreeNode.parse

References

- Fixes #888 (follow-up: update CHANGELOG and add tests where necessary)

- The existence check is not case-sensitive to handle platforms/files that may differ only by case.
- On overwrite, FileUtil.renameFile is used to replace the existing file before running the cleanup logic.

text:
Add PDF fulltext indexing and background indexing task manager

This PR implements a Lucene-based fulltext indexing subsystem for PDF files and wires it into the GUI:

- Add PdfIndexer: a Lucene-backed indexer that can create a new index, add PDF files (per-entry or per-database), remove entries, and flush the index. It skips online links and non-PDF file types, resolves file paths via the BibDatabaseContext and FilePreferences, and checks file modification timestamps to avoid unnecessary re-indexing. Uses EnglishStemAnalyzer and logs IO errors.

- Add IndexingTaskManager: a background task wrapper and queue for indexing operations. Tasks are enqueued and executed with a TaskExecutor; it updates progress/messages for the UI, supports creating the index, adding/removing files (for database, entries or lists of linked files), and updating the displayed database name.

- Add RebuildFulltextSearchIndexAction: GUI action that prompts the user to confirm rebuilding the fulltext index for the current library, shows notifications, and triggers the rebuild via IndexingTaskManager on a background executor.

- Localization: add/extend UI strings for indexing actions and messages.

- Tests: add/extend unit tests to verify indexing/search behavior
  - PdfIndexerTest: verifies indexing of sample PDFs, ensures non-PDFs and online links are not indexed, tests flushIndex and appending additional metadata documents.
  - PdfSearcherTest: verifies search results for various queries, stop words, empty/null queries and invalid limits.

Notes:
- Proper error handling/logging and user notifications are included for IO failures when accessing the index.
- Uses Apache Lucene (DirectoryReader/IndexWriter/TermQuery) and integrates with existing FilePreferences and BibDatabaseContext APIs.

- "Reader–Writer/Lock" -> "Reader–Writer/Lock" (capitalization after en-dash applied as expected)

- No API changes; this is a bugfix and fully backward compatible.

Fix handling of abstract/review fields in LatexFieldFormatter and add tests.

- Bug: LatexFieldFormatter incorrectly computed the doWrap flag using "!isAbstract || !isReview", which evaluates to true for both "abstract" and "review" fields (since a field cannot be both at the same time). As a result, newlines and original formatting in abstract and review fields could be wrapped/altered unexpectedly.

- Fix: Change the logic so wrapping is disabled for either abstract or review fields (doWrap = !(isAbstract || isReview) / !isAbstract && !isReview), preserving their formatting and newlines.

- Tests: Add two unit tests (preserveNewlineInAbstractField and preserveNewlineInReviewField) to assert that newline characters are preserved and the entire field is returned wrapped in the configured value delimiters (i.e. "{...}") for both "abstract" and "review".

Files changed:
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/exporter/LatexFieldFormatter.java — fix boolean logic for doWrap
- src/test/java/net/sf/jabref/exporter/layout/LatexFieldFormatterTests.java — add tests for abstract and review fields

This ensures abstract and review fields are treated as non-wrappable as intended, preventing accidental line-wrapping and preserving multi-line content.

- Implement BibEntryWriter behavior that: writes required fields first, optional fields next and remaining fields in alphabetical order; respects InternalBibtexFields display/writeable flags (when writer is created with write=true, writable-but-non-displayable fields such as __markedentry are included); preserves original parsed serialization for unchanged entries; supports writing without prepended newlines.

- This change is limited to GUI behavior/code clarity; no major feature additions were made.
- If further issues are noticed around accessibility or internationalization, follow-up PRs will address them.

- Validates constructor input (throws IllegalArgumentException if the fetcher set is null).

text:
Fix invisible notification message

Summary:
The notification message text was sometimes rendering invisible (especially in certain themes or when overlays were present). This PR fixes styling and accessibility so notifications are visible and announced reliably.

Root cause:
- Notification CSS contained an incorrect color/opacity rule that made text blend with the background or become transparent.
- z-index/layout rules could place the message behind other UI elements.
- The container lacked an appropriate ARIA role/aria-live attribute for screen readers.

What changed:
- Updated notification CSS to use a dedicated theme variable for foreground (ensuring sufficient contrast in light/dark themes) and removed unintended opacity/visibility overrides.
- Adjusted stacking (z-index) and layout so notification messages render above overlays and are not clipped.
- Added role="status" and aria-live="polite" to the notification container so assistive tech announces messages.
- Added unit and visual tests (Storybook snapshot) to prevent regressions.

Impact:
- No public API changes.
- Fixes invisible notifications across themes and improves accessibility and test coverage.

  - BackupManager: start the background backup task when a database file exists, and trigger backups on BibDatabaseContextChangedEvent. The shutdown routine now checks for file existence and type before deleting the backup file to avoid exceptions. Also improved task submission handling.
  - Adjusted UI usages to the new autosaveandbackup package.

- Parser improvements
  - BibtexParser: improved handling to purge the DBID and encoding comment lines consistently via a shared purge method.

- Minor API and implementation cleanups
  - Removed some unused imports and null-check helpers in favor of direct checks and Optional.

  - Updated unit tests to reflect the sharedDatabaseID rename and added a test ensuring DBID lines are not treated as user comments.

Summary

This PR adds a Referer header to outbound API calls to address authentication/validation requirements reported in issue #2789.

Why

Some API endpoints require a Referer header for request validation and logging. Without it, requests can be rejected or lack important context for debugging. Adding the Referer fixes the behavior described in #2789.

What changed

- Added logic to include a Referer header on API requests issued by the app's network client.
- Ensured the header value is derived from the app configuration / current origin in a secure way (no user-sensitive data is included).
- Updated unit tests to verify the Referer header is present and correctly formatted.
- Minor updates to docs/comments describing the rationale and test coverage.

Compatibility

- Backwards compatible: default behavior is the same for environments that do not set an explicit referer value; the header will be omitted or set only when a valid origin is available.
- No changes to public APIs or database schema.

Testing / How to verify

1. Run unit tests: confirm new tests pass.
2. Start the app and perform an API call that previously failed. Inspect the outgoing request (browser devtools or proxy) and confirm a Referer header is included with the expected origin.
3. Verify target API accepts the request and behavior from issue #2789 is resolved.

Fixes

text:
Introduce a robust DOI utility and integrate DOI-aware behavior across importers and UI components.

Summary of changes:
- Add DOI utility (net.sf.jabref.logic.util.DOI)
  - Parses DOIs from many formats: plain DOIs, urn:doi:, doi:, and HTTP(S) DOI URLs.
  - Safely handles HTTP DOI decoding/encoding and constructs resolver URIs (RESOLVER constant).
  - Provides helper methods build(String) (returns Optional<DOI>), findInText(String) and getters for plain DOI and encoded URI.
  - Properly validates input and avoids throwing on invalid inputs via Optional-based API.

- Integrate DOI API in multiple components:
  - ClipBoardManager: detect DOI strings on the clipboard and fetch BibTeX entries via DOItoBibTeXFetcher.
  - DOItoBibTeXFetcher: fetch BibTeX via DOI URL, cleanup encoding for page ranges, and optional title formatting.
  - MergeEntryDOIDialog: use DOItoBibTeXFetcher to fetch and merge DOI-based data into entries.
  - JabRefDesktop: open doi fields by resolving DOI to a browser URL.
  - PdfContentImporter: scan first page of PDFs for embedded DOIs (using DOI.findInText) and fetch BibTeX entry if found; share a static DOItoBibTeXFetcher instance.
  - DoiResolution: follow DOI redirects and search for PDF links, using DOI.getURIAsASCIIString() when available.
  - DOICheck formatter: use DOI.build to normalize DOI fields to resolver URLs.

- Tests:
  - Add comprehensive DOITest unit tests covering acceptance/rejection of many DOI forms, proper decoding/encoding of percent-encoded characters, URI construction, and finding DOIs inside text.

Why:
- Make DOI handling consistent and reliable across the application.
- Support many DOI input formats and edge cases (URLs, percent-encoded characters, URNs).
- Improve user experience: clipboard DOI recognition, PDF DOI detection, DOI-based fetch/merge, and safe opening of DOI links.

Notable implementation details:
- DOI.build returns Optional to avoid exceptions when checking strings.
- getURI/getURIAsASCIIString return encoded resolver URIs, ensuring safe use in browser/openers.
- PdfContentImporter now looks for DOI on the first page and delegates fetching to DOItoBibTeXFetcher.
- DOItoBibTeXFetcher uses Accept: application/x-bibtex and applies optional title formatting based on preferences.

This PR centralizes DOI logic and updates callers to rely on the new DOI API for parsing, validation and URI handling.

Fix group search performance (#2852)

Summary
- Add a debounce to the group search input to avoid triggering expensive searches on every keystroke.
- Rework RecursiveTreeItem child/list handling and filtering so branches are not re-tested repeatedly. This reduces CPU usage and UI lag when typing a search.
- Treat “All entries” as the default when no group is selected (show all entries) and exclude it from selected-groups state.

What changed
- Group search debounce
  - GroupTreeController: the search field now uses a FxTimer (400 ms) to delay updating the ViewModel filterTextProperty until the user pauses typing. This prevents frequent, costly search runs while typing.

- Selection / AllEntries handling
  - GroupSidePane: when no groups are selected we now show all entries by using the AllEntriesGroup as the selected group.
  - GroupTreeController: do not add the AllEntriesGroup to selectedGroups reported to the ViewModel. Also handle empty selection correctly.
  - GroupTreeViewModel: persist empty selection (clear selected groups) when the selection becomes empty.

- Recursive tree & filtering improvements
  - RecursiveTreeItem: refactored to store child tree items (FilteredList<RecursiveTreeItem<T>>) instead of raw child values and to use BindingsHelper.mapBacked to create tree items up-front for faster access.
  - Filter predicate is bound and cached per RecursiveTreeItem; showNode now checks the node value and recursively inspects child tree items efficiently (avoids repeatedly calling childrenFactory to re-create children and re-test them).
  - This change reduces repeated predicate evaluations on deep group trees and greatly improves responsiveness of group filtering.

- Utility change
  - BindingsHelper.mapBacked signature updated to return MappedList<B, A> to match usage in RecursiveTreeItem.

Files touched
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/groups/GroupSidePane.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/groups/GroupTreeController.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/groups/GroupTreeViewModel.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/util/BindingsHelper.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/util/RecursiveTreeItem.java

Notes
- This is intended as a pragmatic performance improvement. The RecursiveTreeItem changes are somewhat invasive and described by the author as an "ugly" but effective optimization; further cleanup or a cleaner design may follow.
- Fixes: #2852

Checklist (manual)
- Manual testing recommended (typing into group search, selecting/clearing groups, large group hierarchies)
- No new unit tests were added in this change

Summary

Fixes incorrect handling of module "use"/format conversion for import statements. Previously some imports bypassed the format conversion step and could result in incorrect module resolution or runtime errors when mixing formats (CommonJS/ESM). This change ensures format conversion is applied consistently to all imports.

What I changed

- Apply the use/format conversion stage to all import kinds (named, default, namespace, and side-effect imports).
- Centralized conversion logic so imports go through the same transformation path to avoid duplicated or skipped code paths.
- Added unit/integration tests covering mixed-format import scenarios and updated snapshots where necessary.

Why this matters

- Prevents subtle runtime errors that occurred when certain imports were not normalized to the project/module format.
- Improves consistency of import resolution and makes behavior predictable when working with both CJS and ESM modules.

Compatibility and notes

- This is intended to be a bugfix with no breaking API changes. Existing imports should continue to work but will now be normalized more consistently.
- Slight overhead from the unified conversion path is expected to be negligible; performance-sensitive areas were reviewed.
- If you see any import-related regressions, please include an example import statement and the module format involved so it can be reproduced.

Testing

- Added tests for all import types with mixed source formats.
- Ran the full test suite and updated snapshots where conversion changes were expected.

Summary

This PR removes an obsolete user preference setting that controlled the legacy behavior. The preference, its UI toggle, storage key, and related backend handling have been deleted. The application now uses the new default behavior unconditionally.

Why

The preference is no longer necessary following the full rollout of the new behavior. Keeping it around added code complexity, required extra branches in logic, and caused maintenance burden. Removing it simplifies the codebase and reduces potential for bugs.

What changed

- Deleted the preference setting and its key from the settings schema.
- Removed the corresponding UI control from the preferences/settings page.
- Removed backend code that read and honored the preference, including API surface and feature gates.
- Added a migration to drop the preference column/storage key where applicable (or removed stale defaults from persisted settings files).
- Updated unit/integration tests and feature tests to reflect the single default behavior.
- Updated documentation and changelog references to remove mention of the removed preference.

Migration/Upgrade notes

- For most deployments there is no user-facing migration required: users will automatically experience the new default behavior.
- A database migration is included to remove the now-unused preference column from the user settings table. Please run database migrations as part of the deployment.
- If any external automation relied on toggling this preference via API, update them to reflect the new behavior (no toggle endpoint/field available).

Testing & QA

- Existing tests that referenced the preference have been updated or removed.
- Verified behavior in staging that users receive the new default behavior by default.
- Manual QA: checked settings page to ensure toggle is absent and no residual UI artifacts remain; confirmed API responses no longer include the preference field.

Impact

- This is a backwards-incompatible removal of the preference flag; consumers of the API or automation that referenced the setting must be updated.
- End users will see the new behavior always enabled (as intended after the full rollout).

Notes / Follow-ups

- If needed, reintroduce a feature-flag based rollout in a separate PR rather than a user preference.
- Monitor error logs and user feedback after deployment for any regressions related to this change.

Related issues

- Resolves: removes legacy preference setting introduced in earlier releases (see related issue/PRs if applicable).

Summary:
- Fix issues in DefaultFileUpdateMonitor that could cause the file watcher thread to continue running after the monitor is disposed and/or throw exceptions when watched files are deleted or renamed.

- Update CHANGELOG.md to document the bug fix and note the improved stability of file monitoring.

Details:
- Ensure the WatchService is closed when the monitor is stopped to prevent leaking threads.
- Add guards to prevent null pointer-like conditions and ignore events for already-removed watchers.
- Simplify shutdown logic to avoid race conditions between event processing and stopping the monitor.

Testing:
- Manually verified that watchers stop on project/entry close and that deleting/renaming watched files no longer causes exceptions.

Notes:
- No public API changes. This is an internal bugfix and cleanup.

text:
Refactor PDF fulltext indexing task manager and PdfIndexer API

Summary
- Reworked IndexingTaskManager to use a thread-safe ConcurrentLinkedQueue of Runnable tasks instead of queuing BackgroundTask instances. The manager now maintains an explicit running flag and a per-run counter for number of indexed files, and it updates progress/messages on the JavaFX thread via DefaultTaskExecutor.
- Simplified task enqueueing: individual indexing operations (create index, add single file, remove single file) are enqueued as Runnables. Higher-level helpers iterate entries/linked files and enqueue per-file tasks.
- Changed PdfIndexer.createIndex signature and behavior: createIndex() no longer takes a BibDatabase and no longer iterates entries itself — it only (re)creates the index. Adding files to the index is done by calling addToIndex(...) separately.
- Updated RebuildFulltextSearchIndexAction and tests to match the new PdfIndexer and IndexingTaskManager API.
- Added new localization strings for progress and indexing title.

Details / notable changes
- IndexingTaskManager
  - Replaced Queue<BackgroundTask<Void>> with ConcurrentLinkedQueue<Runnable> and added a lock + isRunning flag to manage execution state.
  - Enqueueing now uses enqueueTask(Runnable) which starts execution if the manager is not already running.
  - The manager counts indexed files (numOfIndexedFiles) and updates a localized progress message and progress property on the JavaFX thread.
  - Removed wrapping each operation in BackgroundTask subclasses; instead, per-file actions are enqueued as lambdas that call PdfIndexer methods.
  - updateDatabaseName now updates the title property with a localized string on the JavaFX thread.

- PdfIndexer
  - createIndex signature changed to createIndex() and now only recreates the Lucene index (no longer accepts BibDatabase nor iterates entries).
  - addToIndex(BibDatabaseContext) iterates entries and files and delegates per-file addition to the task manager.
  - Tests and callers updated to call createIndex(); then addToIndex(context).

- RebuildFulltextSearchIndexAction
  - Adjusted calls to IndexingTaskManager.createIndex(PdfIndexer) and to addToIndex(PdfIndexer, BibDatabaseContext) per the new API.

- Tests
  - PdfIndexerTest and PdfSearcherTest updated: mock context.getEntries() to return database.getEntries(), call indexer.createIndex(); indexer.addToIndex(context) instead of the old combined createIndex(database, context).

- Localization
  - Added "Indexing for %0" and "%0 of %1 linked files added to the index" to JabRef_en.properties for displaying title and progress.

Migration notes
- Callers must now call PdfIndexer.createIndex() to create/reset the index, and then call addToIndex(...) to enqueue files for indexing. The IndexingTaskManager API changed accordingly.

This refactor improves concurrency correctness, simplifies task management, and provides clearer per-file progress reporting.

text:
Fix repeated escaping of % sign in LaTeX cleanup (fixes #2451).

What I changed
- Prevent re-escaping of already-escaped percent signs: percent signs are now only escaped once (already-escaped sequences like "\\%" are preserved, and unescaped percent signs become "\\%").
- Extracted and reused several regexes as compiled Pattern constants to make the logic clearer and avoid repeated replaceAll side effects (REMOVE_REDUNDANT, REPLACE_WITH_AT, REPLACE_EVERY_OTHER_AT, MOVE_NUMBERS_WITH_OPERATORS, MOVE_NUMBERS_RIGHT_INTO_EQUATION, ESCAPE_PERCENT_SIGN_ONCE).
- Reworked parts of LatexCleanupFormatter to use these Patterns instead of chained replace/replaceAll calls.
- Added tests: escapePercentSignOnlyOnce and escapePercentSignOnlnyOnceWithNumber, and kept the existing preservePercentSign test.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to mention the fix.

Why
Running the LaTeX cleanup multiple times could double-escape percent signs. This change ensures percent escaping is idempotent and improves the robustness/readability of the formatter by using compiled regex patterns.

Other
- Tests added and manual testing performed.
- See issue #2451 for context.

This pull request addresses the issue of storing absolute paths to auxiliary (aux) files in JabRef, which can cause problems when sharing libraries across different machines. The changes introduced in this PR ensure that the paths to aux files are stored as relative paths with respect to a new `LaTexFileDirectory` in the metadata.

3. **Relative Path Retrieval**: The `getFilePath()` method in `TexGroup` now returns the relative path of the aux file.
4. **User-Specific Directories**: Users can define their own `LaTexFileDirectory` similar to the existing `userFileDirectory`.

- Manually tested the change in a running JabRef.
- No automated tests were added.

Introduce a JavaFX-based DialogService and wire it into the UI so dialogs and file choosers are handled consistently from JavaFX code and Swing-hosted dialogs.

Key changes
- Add FXDialogService: a full DialogService implementation using JavaFX dialogs (information, warning, error, confirmation, custom dialogs, file/directory choosers, progress dialog, print dialog, archive file chooser and snackbar notifications).
- JabRefFrame now owns a DialogService instance (initialized in the constructor as an FXDialogService) and exposes getDialogService(). Many parts of the UI now use this service instead of directly creating dialogs.
- JabRefGUI exposes a static getMainFrame() so non-UI classes can obtain the frame and its DialogService when needed.
- DefaultInjector now provides DialogService dependencies by returning JabRefGUI.getMainFrame().getDialogService() for injection, integrating the new dialog service into the dependency injection flow.
- Updated callers to use JabRefGUI.getMainFrame().getDialogService(): external file type editor (ExternalFileTypeEntryEditor) uses it to show JavaFX file chooser from a Swing dialog, collab change view models (EntryAddChangeViewModel, EntryDeleteChangeViewModel) use it when creating preview panels, and JabRefFrame uses it for confirmation/notification dialogs.

Why
- Centralize and modernize dialog handling using JavaFX while keeping compatibility with existing Swing dialogs.
- Allow components to receive a DialogService from the frame (and through dependency injection) instead of relying on global state.

Notes
- No behavioral changes to dialog semantics are intended; this refactor prepares for further dialog unification and easier testing/mocking of dialog interactions.

This PR fixes an issue where entries imported by identifier (or pasted as DOI/entry) did not get a citation key generated and were not handled consistently w.r.t. duplicate detection and post-import cleanup. - Fixed import-by-ID and paste flows to use ImportHandler.importEntryWithDuplicateCheck so citation keys are generated and duplicates are handled.
  - GenerateEntryFromIdAction: use ImportHandler and simplify background result handling.
  - EntryTypeViewModel: use ImportHandler instead of ad-hoc duplicate/key logic after fetch.
  - MainTable.paste: call importEntryWithDuplicateCheck for each pasted entry (removed BibDatabaseMode argument).
- Extended ImportHandler:
  - Added importEntryWithDuplicateCheck(BibDatabaseContext, BibEntry) that does cleanup, duplicate resolution dialog (KEEP_LEFT/BOTH/MERGE), generates citation keys when importer preferences require it, sets automatic fields, inserts the entry and adds it to groups.
  - Refactored existing importEntries/importEntries flow to use bibDatabaseContext consistently and reuse helper methods.
  - Added DialogService injection and small fixes to UndoableInsertEntries usage.
- Wiring changes: several view-models/constructors updated to pass DialogService where required (BibtexExtractorViewModel, ImportEntriesViewModel, UnlinkedFilesDialogViewModel, MainTable, etc.).
- Removed now-unused resource strings and updated CHANGELOG.md.

- Core logic: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/externalfiles/ImportHandler.java (new method + refactor)

Summary

- Added two new search pseudo-fields: `anykeyword` and `anyfield`.
  - `anykeyword` lets you search for a whole keyword in the `keywords` field (matches full tokens, not substrings).
  - `anyfield` searches across all fields of an entry and can be combined with specific-field constraints (e.g., `anyfield=fruit and keywords!=banana`).

What I changed

- Implemented search support:
  - Updated GrammarBasedSearchRule to treat:
    - `entrytype` checks via BibEntry.TYPE_HEADER (no magic string).
    - `anykeyword` as a special-case that checks entry.getKeywords() for a token match.
    - `anyfield` as a special-case that searches across all fields (and still allows combining with specific-field filters).
  - Adjusted the logic so the set of fields searched is filtered correctly and returned correctly for does-not-contain semantics.

- Replaced literal "entrytype" usages with BibEntry.TYPE_HEADER in several places to centralize the header name:
  - OvidImporter: use BibEntry.TYPE_HEADER when parsing and when setting the entry type.
  - XMPSchemaBibtex & XMPUtil: read/write the entry type using BibEntry.TYPE_HEADER and remove it from text properties after creating the entry.

- Tests:
  - Added unit tests in SearchQueryTest to cover:
    - `anykeyword` matching and non-matching cases
    - `anyfield` usage, including combinations with specific field constraints and negation

- Documentation:
  - Updated CHANGELOG.md to mention the two new pseudo-fields (`anykeyword` and `anyfield`) and how they can be used.

Why

- The new pseudo-fields improve search expressiveness and make it easier to search by individual keywords or across all fields without enumerating them.
- Replacing the magic "entrytype" string with BibEntry.TYPE_HEADER reduces risk of typos and centralizes the header name for consistency across import/export/XMP code paths.

Notes

- Behavior: `anykeyword==pineapple` matches when one of the comma-separated keywords equals `pineapple` (not substring). `anyfield` performs the same matching semantics but across all fields of the entry.
- All changes are covered by unit tests added to SearchQueryTest.

- Update Capitalize implementation to treat hyphenated words as a single token when capitalizing the first character, i.e., only the first character of the entire string (or first character after whitespace when applicable) is capitalized, but characters immediately after hyphens are left unchanged.
- Add unit tests covering hyphenated inputs and existing cases to prevent regressions.

- "co-op" -> "Co-Op"
- "email-address" -> "Email-Address"

Behavior after:
- "co-op" -> "Co-op"
- "email-address" -> "Email-address"

Why: This aligns Capitalize with expected title-casing for hyphenated words in our codebase and avoids unintended capitalization that can affect display strings and identifiers.

Notes:
- Change is backward-compatible for most usage; only hyphen-following capitalization behavior is adjusted.
- Tests added to cover hyphen, space, and leading/trailing characters.

Summary

This PR contains a set of bug fixes and small improvements around file handling, LaTeX parsing, group parsing and related dialogs. Changes are backwards compatible and focus on better preference usage, more robust parsing and safer file interactions.

Key changes

- Preferences
  - PreferencesService: added/updated support for remembering last-used directories so file choosers can reopen in the previous location.

- File utilities
  - FileUtil: centralized and hardened file/path handling (normalization and safe checks) so callers don’t have to repeat boilerplate and to reduce crashes when dealing with files.

- LaTeX parsing and citation UI
  - ParseLatexDialogViewModel & LatexCitationsTabViewModel: improved integration with preferences and FileUtil, added more robust validation and error handling for user input and imported LaTeX files, and fixed cases where invalid selections could cause exceptions.

- Groups parsing and UI
  - GroupsParser: fixed parsing edge-cases (trimming, handling empty fields/escaped characters) to avoid NullPointerExceptions and to correctly import/export group data.
  - GroupDialogViewModel: improved validation and defaulting when creating or editing groups to avoid crashes on invalid input.

- Existing study search
  - ExistingStudySearchAction: now uses the preference-managed last directory and FileUtil for safer file opening, and improved error handling/reporting when the selected file cannot be processed.

- Changelog
  - CHANGELOG.md: updated with notes summarizing the fixes and improvements introduced in this PR.

Why this change

These improvements reduce crashes caused by invalid input or missing/incorrect file paths, make the dialogs behave more consistently (remembering the last folder), and make group and LaTeX parsing more robust when importing data created by other tools or by hand.

Notes

No public API breaking changes. The changes are internal, aim to improve UX and reliability, and should make importing files and working with groups/LaTeX citations less error-prone.

text:
Fix exception in preview when using regex search and support regex searches without a specified field

What this PR fixes
- Fixes exceptions in the HTML preview when using regular-expression based search patterns (Fixes #6777).
  - The JavaScript regexp literal used by the preview was incorrectly constructed and failed when the pattern contained unescaped forward slashes or when a single-term regex was used.
- Ensure field-less comparisons respect regex mode when parsing grammar-based queries.

Summary of changes
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preview/PreviewViewer.java
  - Create JS regex literals more robustly with a new helper createJavaScriptRegex(Pattern) that escapes unescaped forward slashes and returns a JS regexp literal with flags.
  - Use a consistent unmark/mark callback flow to avoid executing invalid JS when no pattern is present.
  - Add constants for the JS callback/unmark snippets and a Pattern to detect unescaped slashes.
  - Note: the helper documents that JS vs Java regex engines differ; the method only handles escaping necessary for JS literal construction (not full semantic parity).

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/search/SearchQuery.java
  - Refactored escaping logic into an EscapeMode enum (JAVA, JAVASCRIPT). Each mode implements how to escape a literal token.
  - Improved joining of search words into a single regex using streams and proper escaping only when regex mode is disabled.
  - Cleaned imports and small formatting updates.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/search/rules/GrammarBasedSearchRule.java
  - When no explicit field is present, choose the appropriate search rule (regex vs contains) via SearchRules.getSearchRule so regex mode is respected for field-less comparisons.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/search/rules/SearchRules.java
  - Broadened visibility of getSearchRule to package-private static so it can be reused by GrammarBasedSearchRule.

Tests
- Updated ContainBasedSearchRuleTest to use assertTrue/assertFalse and refactored makeBibtexEntry to fluent builder style.
- Added GrammarBasedSearchRuleTest to verify regex matching and non-matching behavior for grammar based rules when regex mode is enabled.

Notes and limitations
- The JS regex creation method escapes forward slashes and other characters as needed to safely embed the Java pattern as a JavaScript literal. It does not attempt to reconcile differences in full regex feature support/semantics between Java and JavaScript engines.

Validation
- Added and updated unit tests covering the changed behavior.
- Manually tested the preview and search features in running JabRef to verify regression is fixed.

This PR fixes #6777 by ensuring the preview's JS regexp is built safely and by making field-less grammar searches honor regex mode.

Summary

This PR implements an alternative branch for merging duplicate entries by combining information from both records. It introduces a new "Keep merged entry only" action in the duplicate-resolution UI, shows a preview tab for the merged result, and wires the merged-entry flow into duplicate-search, import inspection and import handling logic so that merged entries can be created, inserted and properly handled (including undo edits and removal of originals).

User-visible changes

- New button in duplicate resolver dialog: "Keep merged entry only". Selecting it will create a merged entry and remove the old entries.
- New tab in the duplicate dialog to preview the merged entry (both short/preview and full BibTeX record). The merged entry is also shown in a dedicated merge panel.
- Duplicate resolution during import, import inspection and duplicate search now support merging: merged entries can be added to the database while originals are removed.
- Preview dialog width increased to better show merged content.
- Changelog entry added: Feature: Merge information from both entries on duplication detection.

Technical highlights

- DuplicateResolverDialog
  - Added KEEP_MERGE constant and a MergeEntries instance to build and preview merged entries.
  - Added a "merged entry" preview tab and a new button for keeping the merged entry only.
  - Added getMergedEntry() accessor and changed setEntries/getSelected to support three-way preview (upper, lower, merged).
  - Added a ChangeListener to populate the full-BibTeX view when switching tabs.

- DuplicateSearch
  - Collects merged entries returned by the duplicate dialog and inserts them into the database (with undo support) while removing originals.
  - Introduced UndoableInsertEntry usage for merged insertions.

- ImportInspectionDialog / ImportMenuItem / JabRefFrame.addBibEntries
  - Import flow updated to support the KEEP_MERGE resolution: removed originals are replaced by merged entries, generate keys if requested, and correct undo edits are recorded.
  - Import reporting now includes counts for added, replaced and "added information to" (merged) entries.
  - Minor refactors and addition of serialVersionUIDs for anonymous/inner classes and table components.

- MergeEntriesDialog
  - Fixed the order of undo edits so insert of the merged entry is registered when replacing originals.

Other changes

- Minor formatting and refactors (braces, parenthesis, enhanced readability).
- Updated copyright year headers in a couple of files (2003-2015).
- Slight preview layout/size adjustments.

Files changed (high level)

- CHANGELOG (feature note)
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/DuplicateResolverDialog.java (major UI + logic changes)
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/DuplicateSearch.java (accept merged entries and add them)
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/ImportInspectionDialog.java (support merge option during import inspection)
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/JabRefFrame.java (handle merged entries when importing)
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/mergeentries/MergeEntriesDialog.java (undo/insertion fix)
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/importer/ImportMenuItem.java (import flow adjustments and counters)

Notes & follow-ups

- Naming and some minor structural choices were flagged as TODOs by the author; these can be revisited in follow-up PRs.
- This branch is intended to match PR #227 but condensed into two commits; expect follow-ups for polishing and renaming.
- Please review changes to import/duplicate flows carefully to ensure behavior matches expected user workflows and that undo semantics are correct.

text:
Introduce BibEntry core model implementation with comprehensive field management and utilities.

Key highlights:
- Stores entry id and type with safe setters and event notifications. Setting type posts FieldChangedEvent and maintains changed flag.
- Uses an observable concurrent map for fields so entries can be bound in the UI. Provides field binding helpers including getFieldBinding and getCiteKeyBinding.
- Implements robust get/set/clear field APIs that post FieldChangedEvent or FieldAddedOrRemovedEvent via an EventBus and maintain old/new values through FieldChange objects.
- Resolves field aliases and crossreferences: getResolvedFieldOrAlias tries local value, aliases, and looks up fields in a referenced entry from the BibDatabase. Special handling for InProceedings mapping booktitle/booksubtitle/bookauthor from referred entry.
- Date handling: generic logic to synthesize date/year/month/day from date field and vice versa in genericGetFieldOrAlias.
- Caching and latex stripping: caches latex-free field values using LatexToUnicodeAdapter; invalidates caches on updates. Also caches words of fields for fast lookup via getFieldAsWords.
- Keyword management: helpers to get, add, remove, replace, and serialize keywords using KeywordList, respecting a configurable delimiter.
- Linked file support: parse, serialize and manage linked files through getFiles, setFiles and addFile.
- Clone produces a shallow copy with a new id and copied fields map.
- Serialization support: toString delegates to CanonicalBibtexEntry, stores parsed serialization and commentsBeforeEntry, and tracks whether entry has changed.
- Listener management: registerListener and unregisterListener for events, plus getObservables for UI bindings.
- Utility methods: getTitle, getPublicationDate, getDOI, getAuthorTitleYear, equals and hashCode implementations based on type, fields and comments.

This class centralizes entry-level logic and eventing, enabling consistent field resolution, caching, UI bindings and change notification for the rest of the application.

What this change does
- When opening the library, check whether the "Keep search string" option is enabled. If it is, automatically apply the stored search string so the library content is filtered on open.

- Maintain existing debounce/focus behavior where appropriate to avoid unnecessary duplicate searches.

1. Enable the "Keep search string" option (if it's a user setting).
2. Open the library, enter a search string (e.g. "foo"), and confirm results are filtered.
3. Close the library and reopen it. The search input should still show "foo" and results should already be filtered by "foo" without further input.
4. Disable "Keep search string", perform a search, close and reopen the library — the search input should be cleared and unfiltered results should be shown.
5. Verify keyboard/focus behavior is unchanged (typing still works, no extra unexpected focus jumps).

Notes
- No public API changes. This is purely a UI/UX behavior fix.
- The change avoids extra or duplicate search calls by respecting existing debounce logic.

Summary

This PR improves PDF annotation importing to correctly handle annotations created by Foxit Reader and other annotations that use integer quad-point coordinates. It adds targeted tests and fixes a few related issues.

Key changes

- Add support for Foxit-style annotations that store quad points as integers by extracting marked text with a new TextExtractor class (handles both COSFloat and COSInteger).
- Refactor marked-annotation handling in PdfAnnotationImporter: use FileAnnotationType.isMarkedFileAnnotationType(...) to detect marked annotations and use TextExtractor to extract text from QuadPoints.
- Ignore annotations without a subtype and explicitly exclude Link and Widget annotation subtypes from being treated as supported file annotations to avoid false positives and errors.
- Improve validation/log messages and add early-return behavior for invalid paths (tests expect empty list when path is invalid or unreadable).
- Extend FileAnnotationType enum: add SQUIGGLY and a boolean flag to indicate linked/marked annotation types; add helper methods isMarkedFileAnnotationType(...) and isLinkedFileAnnotationType().
- Add unit tests (PdfAnnotationImporterTest) and sample PDF fixtures for Foxit highlights, squiggly and strikeout annotations.
- Update CHANGELOG.md to document the Foxit-related fixes and correct an issue-number link.

Why

Foxit stores quad point coordinates sometimes as integers and creates annotation types (e.g. Squiggly, StrikeOut) that were not fully handled before. The previous implementation assumed COSFloat and used PDFTextStripperByArea extraction inline, which failed for these files. This PR makes extraction robust to integer coordinates and better detects/filters supported annotation subtypes, enabling correct display/import of Foxit-created annotations.

Testing

- New tests cover: invalid paths, directory/document-type handling, Foxit highlight, squiggly, and strikeout examples (using fixtures under src/test/resources/pdfs).
- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance as noted in the related issue.

Fixes/addresses: https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/2839 (support annotations created by Foxit; see linked comment).

- Fixes incorrect behavior when resolving cross-references between BibEntry instances. The resolution now correctly treats the 'crossref' field as a reference to another entry's key and merges fields from the referenced entry only when appropriate.

Why this matters
- Previously, crossref resolution could produce incorrect or unexpected field values on entries that used cross-references. This fix ensures BibEntry instances correctly inherit missing fields from their cross-referenced entries, matching user expectations and BibTeX semantics.

Notes for reviewers
- Unit tests included demonstrate the corrected behavior and should pass on all supported platforms.
- No user-facing API changes; behavior is a bugfix and should be backward compatible.

text:
Fix default directory of the "LaTeX Citations" tab

What I changed
- The LaTeX Citations tab now uses the directory of the currently opened database as its default directory instead of the last used file dialog or last database save. This fixes koppor#538.
- Introduced FileUtil.getInitialDirectory(BibDatabaseContext, PreferencesService) to centralize logic for choosing the initial directory (database folder when available, otherwise the global working dir).
- Updated usages to use the new helper:
  - LatexCitationsTabViewModel: use FileUtil.getInitialDirectory for initial value and when checking for directory changes.
  - ParseLatexDialogViewModel: use FileUtil.getInitialDirectory for the initial latexFileDirectory.
  - GroupDialogViewModel: open file dialog with the database latex directory (or fallback to getInitialDirectory).
  - ExistingStudySearchAction: compute workingDirectory from active database via FileUtil.getInitialDirectory (and removed local helper).
- Minor improvements and fixes:
  - GroupsParser: improved logger message formatting.
  - PreferencesService: clarified getWorkingDir/setWorkingDirectory methods in the interface javadoc.
  - CHANGELOG: small typo fixes and added a note about this change.

Why
- Previously, many UI dialogs used the last used working directory, which led the LaTeX Citations tab to start in a directory unrelated to the opened database. Users expect LaTeX-related dialogs to default to the current database directory.

Notes
- I intentionally did not change how LatexFileDirectory metadata is stored (e.g. whether it is relative to the .bib file). That would be a separate discussion / follow-up PR.
- Manually tested in a running JabRef; screenshots included in original issue/PR description.

Issue
- Fixes: https://github.com/koppor/jabref/issues/538

What this PR does

Adds user notifications when writing metadata to PDF files so users receive immediate feedback on progress, success, and errors.

Summary of changes

- Show an informational notification when metadata writing starts (per-file or batch).
- Show a success notification when metadata is successfully written, including the file name and a short summary of updated fields.
- Show an error notification when writing fails, including the error message and a suggestion to retry.
- Integrates NotificationService with the PdfMetadataWriter logic, emitting events for start/success/error.
- Adds unit tests and updates localization strings for the new messages.

Implementation notes

- Notifications are non-blocking to avoid interrupting the user workflow and aggregate per-batch results when multiple files are processed.
- Existing APIs are preserved; this is backward compatible.

Testing

- Added automated tests for success and failure notification flows.
- Manually tested with single and multi-file metadata writes.

Future work

- Add optional notification settings (verbosity, disable/enable) and richer undo/rollback UI in a follow-up PR.

Summary

- Added a new CLI utility GenerateCharacterTable that emits a LaTeX document listing all characters from HTMLUnicodeConversionMaps. The generated table contains the Unicode code point number, the symbol (when printable), the LaTeX \symbol{nnn} form, the LaTeX representation chosen for the character and the literal LaTeX code. This helps visually verify and audit the HTML-to-LaTeX conversion table.

What I changed

- Added: src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/cli/GenerateCharacterTable.java — a small program that prints a LaTeX file (to stdout) showing each mapped character for manual inspection.
- Modified: src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/logic/util/strings/HTMLUnicodeConversionMaps.java — many fixes and additions to the numeric→LaTeX conversion map:
  - Corrected or improved LaTeX representations for multiple code points (examples: degree sign, double-prime, therefore, not-subset, hair space, various punctuation and diacritic entries).
  - Fixed escaping issues and inconsistent uses of math/text mode so outputs are more reliable in LaTeX (e.g. Celsius, ell, primes, subscripts, ligatures, etc.).
  - Added or filled many missing entries (diacritics, spacing, subscripts, ligatures, parallel symbol, and more).
  - Commented-out or adjusted questionable entries (a few Cyrillic examples and a few entries previously producing wrong LaTeX sequences).
  - Replaced some LaTeX sequences that required unusual packages with more common commands where appropriate (and noted package requirements where needed).

- Updated: src/test/java/net/sf/jabref/logic/layout/format/HTMLCharsTest.java — expectation adjusted for an entry that was corrected in the map (test changed to expect the corrected mapping).

Rationale

- The generated LaTeX table makes it much easier to inspect and validate that the HTML→LaTeX mappings produce the intended results across fonts and packages.
- The changes fix broken or awkward LaTeX code in the conversion map and add many missing/incorrect entries encountered during manual inspection.

Notes

- This change is primarily preparatory/maintenance: it does not change runtime behavior of the conversion API beyond correcting/filling the mapping data.
- The new CLI prints a raw LaTeX document; rendering depends on the TeX environment and available fonts/packages. The tool is intended for offline/manual verification.
- Related to issue #1761 but that issue’s requested changes are not fully included here.

Testing

- Existing tests updated where needed; manual inspection / generation of the LaTeX table was used to find and correct problematic entries.

text:
This PR changes the shared database structure and adds support for automatic migration between old and new table layouts (see #9312).

Summary of changes
- PostgreSQL: a new schema jabref is created and all JabRef shared tables are placed in that schema (table names otherwise unchanged).
- MySQL / MariaDB: all shared tables are renamed by adding a JABREF_ prefix (e.g. ENTRY -> JABREF_ENTRY).
- Oracle: existing behavior/identifiers kept as-is where possible.
- A new metadata key VersionDBStructure is added to the shared METADATA table to track the database-structure version. This is used to detect whether migration is needed.
- Automatic migration: when the stored VersionDBStructure is older than the processors CURRENT_VERSION_DB_STRUCT, data from the old tables are copied into the new names/locations. Old tables are not dropped automatically to avoid data loss — they must be removed manually.

Implementation details
- MetaData: added VersionDBStructure field, getters/setters, equals/hashCode/toString changes; serialization and parsing updated to store/restore the variable.
- DBMSProcessor: checkBaseIntegrity now considers VersionDBStructure for PostgreSQL/MySQL to validate structure version. Added abstract methods escape_Table(String) and getCURRENT_VERSION_DB_STRUCT(). The codebase was updated to use escape_Table(...) for table identifiers where appropriate.
- PostgreSQLProcessor: creates jabref schema and uses qualified table names (jabref."ENTRY" etc.). Implements escape_Table returning jabref."<name>" and CURRENT_VERSION_DB_STRUCT = 1. Includes migration step from un-scoped tables to jabref schema when needed.
- MySQLProcessor: creates JABREF_* tables, implements escape_Table to prefix table names with JABREF_. Implements CURRENT_VERSION_DB_STRUCT = 1 and migration from old unprefixed tables when detected.

- The accelerator assigned to context menu items could overlap with the same accelerator on the main menu, causing unexpected behavior when a global shortcut was pressed. - Context menu MenuItems no longer have an Accelerator set. They remain accessible via mouse (right-click) and by selecting them with the keyboard when the context menu is open, but they will not respond to global shortcut keys.

1. Open the application and focus on a component that shows a context menu (e.g. entry list or entry editor).

4. Open the context menu and try navigating with arrow keys and Enter — the items should still be selectable from the open context menu.

- This change avoids fragile event filtering and keeps global accelerators unambiguous.

- Renaming and moving of linked files now correctly creates needed folders and proceeds without erroneously trying to create a directory with the file name.

No public API changes.

text:
Closes #4817

Problem
- Renaming file entries during the cleanup operation was performed off the JavaFX application thread. Field changes must be executed on the JavaFX thread which can lead to threading issues if performed from a background thread.

What I changed
- Moved the call that sets the updated files (entry.setFiles(files)) into the JavaFX thread using DefaultTaskExecutor.runInJavaFXThread(...).
- Added the necessary import for DefaultTaskExecutor.
- The cleanup method now returns the FieldChange Optional produced by the Callable executed on the JavaFX thread.

Files changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/cleanup/RenamePdfCleanup.java
  - Wraps entry.setFiles(files) in DefaultTaskExecutor.runInJavaFXThread and returns the resulting Optional<FieldChange>.

Why
- Ensures field changes are performed on the JavaFX thread to avoid concurrency/threading issues and follow JavaFX rules for modifying UI-related/model state.

Testing
- Manually tested the renamed-file cleanup in a running JabRef instance.

Notes / follow-ups
- This problem might affect other cleanup tasks that modify fields — consider auditing other cleanup implementations and performing similar changes where necessary.
- Checklist from issue: CHANGELOG and tests are not yet updated/added.

Risk
- Low: change confines execution of an existing call to the JavaFX thread and does not alter logic beyond ensuring thread-safety.

text:
Fix and harden file saving and locking behavior

What this PR does
- Refactors FileSaveSession and FileBasedLock to improve resource management and error handling during file save operations.
- Ensures file locks are always released (including on exceptions) and that streams/temp files are cleaned up correctly.
- Improves concurrency safety when acquiring and releasing locks to avoid leaving files locked after failed saves.
- Adds clearer logging/error messages to aid debugging when save or lock operations fail.

Why this change
- Previously, certain failure paths could leave a file lock engaged or leave temporary save artifacts behind, causing subsequent save attempts to fail or applications to appear to hang. This change makes save operations more robust and predictable.

Notes
- Behavior is backward compatible for callers: public APIs are preserved but some internals were reorganized for safer try-with-resources style usage and deterministic cleanup.
- Unit tests were added/updated to cover the failure and cleanup scenarios (where applicable).

Files changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/exporter/FileSaveSession.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/util/io/FileBasedLock.java

Reviewers: please focus on the lock acquisition/release logic and the exception paths in FileSaveSession to ensure no remaining edge cases leave locks or temp files behind.

Summary

Add two new key modifiers: `title` and `camel`.

What this does

- `title` modifier: converts strings into Title Case (capitalizes the first letter of each word and normalizes separators).
- `camel` modifier: converts strings/keys into lower camelCase (removes separators and capitalizes subsequent words, e.g. "some_key-name" -> "someKeyName").

Motivation

These modifiers make it easy to transform keys/labels consistently in templates and data processing without needing custom utility code in every consumer.

Implementation details

- Implemented transformation helpers for title-casing and camel-casing.
- Registered both modifiers with the modifier/transform registry so they can be used in templates or mapping pipelines.
- Updated parser/compiler integration so modifiers are applied at the correct step.
- Added unit tests covering edge cases (multiple separators, leading/trailing separators, already-cased input, empty strings).

Backward compatibility

Non-breaking: existing behavior is unchanged unless templates or code opt into the new `title` or `camel` modifiers.

Files to review

- Modifier implementations (helper/transform files)
- Modifier registry/registration
- Parser/compiler changes applying modifiers
- Unit tests for `title` and `camel`

Notes

- The `camel` modifier produces lower camelCase. If an upper CamelCase variant is needed, we can add an `upperCamel` (PascalCase) modifier later.
- Examples:
  - `"hello_world" | camel` -> `"helloWorld"`
  - `"hello-world" | title` -> `"Hello World"`

Fix capitalization for hyphenated words and zero-width spaces (fixes #9068).

- TitleParser: strip zero-width Unicode characters (U+200B, U+200C, U+200D, U+FEFF) before parsing so they no longer interfere with capitalization.

- CHANGELOG: documented the fix.

Why
- Capitalization previously failed for words containing dashes (many different Unicode dash characters) and for text containing zero-width spaces. These changes ensure hyphenated words are capitalized correctly and that stray zero-width characters are removed before processing. The public wrapper and added tests make the numeric comparator behavior testable and prevent regressions.

Summary: Interrupt any currently running tasks when the system begins shutdown. This change ensures tasks receive an interrupt/cancel signal as part of the shutdown sequence so they can stop promptly and release resources.

What changed:
- During shutdown we now iterate through active tasks and issue an interrupt/cancel notification instead of waiting for them to finish silently.
- Shutdown waits for tasks to acknowledge interruption up to a configurable timeout, then proceeds to force cleanup to avoid hanging indefinitely.
- Improved logging to record which tasks were interrupted and whether they completed within the timeout.

Why: Previously long-running or blocked tasks could keep shutdown from completing or cause resource leaks. Explicitly interrupting tasks makes shutdown faster, more deterministic, and safer under failure conditions.

Compatibility: Default behavior preserves previous shutdown semantics except for the interruption step; a configurable timeout allows tuning to match existing deployments. No breaking API changes.

Tests: Added unit/integration tests to verify tasks receive interrupts, obey the timeout, and that shutdown completes even if some tasks fail to stop.

Notes: If callers rely on tasks finishing normally during shutdown, consider handling the interrupt in task code to perform any necessary finalization.

Add GlobalSearchBar Swing component integrating a JavaFX TextField to provide local and global search functionality for the main UI. Key features:

- UI elements: embedded JavaFX search TextField, toolbar buttons for global search toggle, regular expression, case sensitivity, search display mode (cycle), open results in dialog, help and a results JLabel.
- Integration with preferences: respects and persists SearchPreferences (global search, regex, case sensitivity, search mode).
- Live search: subscribes to the search field textProperty and triggers searches via SearchWorker for the current library; supports clearing the search when the field is empty.
- Global search support: performs searches across all open libraries via GlobalSearchWorker and allows opening results in a dedicated SearchResultFrame.
- Result feedback: updates result count, sets JavaFX Tooltip with a TextFlow description, applies pseudo-class states for no-results / results-found, and enables/disables the "open results" button.
- Search query handling: builds SearchQuery objects, validates queries, informs the user on illegal expressions, and updates the BasePanel current search state.
- Auto-completion: exposes setAutoCompleter to attach an AutoCompleteSuggestionProvider using person-name converters and append strategy.
- Focus and selection helpers: focus(), endSearch(), setSearchTerm(), setDontSelectSearchBar() helpers to manage focus behavior.
- Keyboard handling: custom KeyAdapter consumes arrow keys to keep focus inside the field and prevents propagation of common keybindings (CUT, COPY, PASTE, DELETE_ENTRY, SELECT_ALL) back to the main frame.
- Platform specifics: uses CustomJFXPanel on Linux to avoid platform issues, otherwise JFXPanel; initializes JavaFX scene on the FX thread.

Summary

This PR improves the Linked Files preferences UI and behavior by adding live validation and preview for file name patterns, wiring the UI to preferences, and providing localized messages. The changes make it easier for users to construct and validate filename patterns for linked files and ensure the pattern is persisted in JabRef preferences.

What I changed

- Updated LinkedFilesTab.fxml to add UI elements for pattern entry, a live preview/sample, validation feedback, and associated tooltips/help text.
- Implemented logic in LinkedFilesTab.java to bind UI controls to the view model, show validation state, and handle saving/cancelling of the preferences dialog.
- Enhanced LinkedFilesTabViewModel.java with validation for filename patterns, generation of a sample/preview filename, and properties for binding to the view.
- Added or updated preferences key(s) in JabRefPreferences.java so the filename pattern setting is persisted via JabRef preferences.
- Updated l10n/JabRef_en.properties with new/updated localized strings used by the Linked Files preferences UI.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to reflect the new feature/changes.

Why

- Previously users had no immediate feedback when editing filename patterns, which made it hard to detect mistakes. Live validation and a preview help prevent invalid patterns and improve UX.
- Persisting the setting ensures user changes remain across restarts.

Notes for reviewers / testing

1. Open Preferences -> Linked Files.
2. Edit the filename pattern field. Verify that:
   - The preview/sample updates live to show what an example filename would look like.
   - Invalid patterns trigger visible validation feedback (error message/highlight).
3. Save the preferences and confirm the pattern is persisted (restart JabRef or re-open the dialog).
4. Check the localized strings in English for clarity and correctness.

If any behavior should differ (validation rules, sample values, or persistence keys), please point them out so I can adjust accordingly.
