text:
Implement BasePanel UI component and wiring for the main library view

This change contains the BasePanel implementation responsible for displaying and managing a library tab in the application. Key responsibilities and behaviors added/updated in this class include:

- Main UI composition
  - Creates and manages a SplitPane that contains the MainTable and optionally an EntryEditor as the bottom pane.
  - Persists and restores split divider positions for the entry editor.
  - Adds DatabaseChangePane/DatabaseChangeMonitor when the database file is present, and provides reset/cleanup behavior for file-change monitoring.

- Main table & selection handling
  - Creates MainTable and MainTableDataModel, updates table font and binds selection to the global state manager.
  - Ensures entry editor shows the currently selected entry and allows focusing specific fields.
  - Methods to move selection, clear/select entries and to open/close the entry editor.

- Auto-completion & search
  - Initializes SuggestionProviders (or empty providers if auto-complete disabled) and indexes the current database.
  - Instantiates a PersonNameSuggestionProvider for the global search autocompleter on a background thread and registers listeners to keep it in sync with entry changes.
  - Updates the global search bar to use the constructed auto-completer.

- Database change handling & listeners
  - Registers listeners for entries added/removed/changed and for bib database context changes.
  - Provides inner listeners for: automatic group assignment on insertion, keeping the auto-completer indexed, and updating the global search results when the DB changes.

- CRUD and undo integration
  - Insert/delete/cut/copy/paste operations integrated with the CountingUndoManager via UndoableInsertEntries, UndoableRemoveEntries and UndoableFieldChange edits.
  - Automatically sets timestamp/owner fields for new entries and honours auto-open preferences.
  - Prevents accidental data loss by showing a configurable delete confirmation dialog.

- State tracking and UI updates
  - Tracks baseChanged and nonUndoableChange flags to determine modified state and update tab/window titles accordingly.
  - markBaseChanged/markNonUndoableBaseChanged/markChangedOrUnChanged methods to synchronize undo state with modified state.

- Miscellaneous
  - Utilities for formatting output messages, retrieving citation/style and annotation caches, accessors for main components (MainTable, EntryEditor, UndoManager, etc.), and safe cleanup of monitors/subscriptions.

This class centralizes a lot of the interactions between the UI (table, editor, side panes), suggestion providers, undo management and file-change monitoring to provide a coherent tab experience for a library.

text:
Summary

Adjusts resource handling to address PostgreSQL-related errors reported in #473. The previous use of try-with-resources closed some JDBC resources too eagerly and caused failures with the PostgreSQL driver; this change reworks the resource lifetimes so result processing and transaction boundaries are not interrupted by premature closes.

What I changed

- Removed or adjusted try-with-resources usages where they caused resources (ResultSet/Statement/Connection) to be closed before downstream code or the driver expected them to be available.
- Restored explicit close/finally patterns (or tightened the scope of try-with-resources) to ensure proper ordering: result sets and statements are consumed/closed before the connection/transaction is completed.
- Kept resource-safety in mind to avoid leaks while preventing premature closure.

Why

The earlier change introduced try-with-resources in places that unintentionally closed resources while the PostgreSQL driver still needed them, leading to intermittent failures. This change aims to fix that by making the lifecycle explicit and compatible with PostgreSQL.

Testing

- Ran the existing test suite and manual tests against a local PostgreSQL instance to verify queries and transactions no longer fail due to premature resource closing.
- Please run the integration tests in your environment (especially any long-running queries or streaming result usage) to confirm the fix in CI.

Notes

- This likely addresses the issue in #473; marking that ticket for review. If problems persist, additional logging around resource lifecycle may be added to pinpoint remaining cases.
- If reviewers prefer, we can refactor common JDBC handling into a utility to centralize correct close ordering and reduce future regressions.

Add global fallback uncaught-exception handling and wire it into JabRef startup and executor threads

What I changed
- Added FallbackExceptionHandler (src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/FallbackExceptionHandler.java)
  - Implements Thread.UncaughtExceptionHandler and logs uncaught exceptions with a Log4j2 Marker ("UncaughtException").
  - Provides installExceptionHandler() to set the handler as the JVM default.
- Wired the fallback handler into thread creation in JabRefExecutorService (src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/JabRefExecutorService.java)
  - The cached thread pool now creates threads with FallbackExceptionHandler set as their uncaught exception handler.
  - All helper methods that spawn their own Threads (low-priority threads, wait variants) set the uncaught exception handler on the created threads.
- Installed the default handler on application startup (src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/JabRefMain.java)
  - FallbackExceptionHandler.installExceptionHandler() is called early in start(...).

Why
- Ensure that any unhandled exceptions in background threads are consistently logged, making it easier to detect and diagnose problems that otherwise would be silently lost.

Notes
- The handler uses Log4j2 and tags logs with an "UncaughtException" marker for easier filtering.
- Swing (EDT) threads are not modified here; this change focuses on non-Swing/background threads managed by our executor and custom-created threads.
- Existing behavior for remote instance handling and executor shutdown is preserved; JabRefExecutorService.shutdownEverything() is invoked in the same shutdown code paths.

Summary

This PR refactors and centralizes task execution and throttling support.

What I changed

- Introduced a TaskExecutor abstraction (src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/util/TaskExecutor.java) to provide a common API for running and scheduling tasks.
- Added a DefaultTaskExecutor implementation (src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/util/DefaultTaskExecutor.java) which implements the new TaskExecutor API.
- Updated JabRefExecutorService (src/main/java/org/jabref/JabRefExecutorService.java) to provide/coordinate executor services used by the new TaskExecutor and to centralize thread-pool management.
- Added DelayTaskThrottler (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/util/DelayTaskThrottler.java) — a utility that throttles/debounces repeated requests and ensures delayed tasks are scheduled appropriately (useful for UI interactions that should not run on every event).
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to document the change.

Why

- Provide a consistent, testable and extensible API for scheduling and executing tasks across the application.
- Centralize executor lifecycle management to avoid duplicated thread pool creation and make it easier to control thread-related configuration.
- Offer a straightforward throttling/debouncing utility for delayed operations (reduces redundant work and improves responsiveness).

Compatibility / Migration notes

- Existing callers that previously used lower-level executor services should migrate to the TaskExecutor API / DefaultTaskExecutor where applicable.
- The new DelayTaskThrottler should be used for UI debouncing scenarios instead of ad-hoc timer implementations.

Notes for reviewers

- Pay attention to executor lifecycle and shutdown behavior in JabRefExecutorService.
- Ensure the contract of TaskExecutor matches existing needs (synchronous vs asynchronous behavior, exception handling, scheduling).
- Verify DelayTaskThrottler timing semantics and thread-safety for use from the GUI thread.

This PR is primarily a refactor intended to improve maintainability and provide building blocks for future async and throttling features.

- Users will see more reliable imports when providing DOIs or arXiv identifiers (including DOI URLs), fewer failed or duplicate imports, and better normalized identifier storage.
- The added tests increase confidence and protect against regressions in identifier handling and fetcher behavior.

Notes

- Mostly internal fixes and test coverage; no breaking API changes expected.

text:
This PR updates the project changelog and refactors/enhances the BasePanel UI controller.

CHANGELOG.md
- Adds an "Unreleased" section documenting a number of recent improvements and fixes (highlights include: ADS fetcher now moves adsurl -> url, substantial improvements to the new groups UI including multi-select and drag & drop, entry editor redesign and autocomplete rework, CSV export of authors/editors separated by semicolons, Library of Congress LCCN fetcher, improved duplicate checker, and many bug fixes such as DOI HTTPS resolution and FileAnnotation handling).

src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/BasePanel.java
- Introduces and initializes caches: CitationStyleCache and FileAnnotationCache tied to the BibDatabaseContext.
- Ensures bib database context and metadata listeners are registered on construction and registers file update monitor when a file is present.
- Adds a runWorker(AbstractWorker) helper that standardizes running AbstractWorker tasks (init/run/update phases) in a synchronous way consistent with the previous Spin-based behavior.
- Large cleanup/centralization of action wiring in setupActions(): maps many actions (save, save-as, copy/cut/paste, undo/redo, edit, preview toggle, export, file operations, group operations, search, citation copy, etc.) into the BasePanel actions map with clear handling for both BaseAction and AbstractWorker.
- Improves save flow (saveDatabase/save selected) including encoding handling, error dialogs for characters that cannot be encoded, SaveSession/commit/cancel logic and registration of undoable save actions via registerUndoableChanges.
- Improves auto-completion setup: SuggestionProviders indexing, database listeners to keep suggestions in sync, and a PersonNameSuggestionProvider for global search autocompletion.
- Enhances file-monitoring and external-change handling: fileUpdated() now runs ChangeScanner in background and integrates with FileUpdatePanel via SidePaneManager; handles locked files and perturbs timestamps as needed.
- Selection/navigation and preview/editor management: robust history handling (back/forward), editor/preview show/hide, splitter adjustment and persistence of editor/preview sizes across modes.
- Clipboard and import/export improvements: more robust copy/paste behavior including parsing BibTeX from clipboard, copying multiple titles/keys, and copying formatted key+title using LayoutHelper.
- Miscellaneous fixes and refinements: thread-safe marking of base-changed (invokeAndWait), better management of preamble/string dialogs, and utility helpers to find/open external files with configurable file finders.

Overall this change documents recent user-facing changes and consolidates/refactors BasePanel to improve background task execution, action management, file-change handling, and autocomplete/preview behavior.

Summary

- Trim leading and trailing whitespace from all BibTeX fields when writing entries. Empty fields that contain only whitespace are no longer written to the output.

What changed

- Implemented automatic trimming in LatexFieldFormatter (calls String.trim() before resolving/formatting).
- Removed the dedicated TrimFormatter class and its unit tests (TrimFormatter.java, TrimFormatterTest.java) and removed it from the list of available BibTeX field formatters.
- Added tests to BibEntryWriterTest to verify that whitespace-only fields are not written and that field contents are trimmed on write (doNotWriteEmptyFields, trimFieldContents).
- Updated FormatterTest to no longer include TrimFormatter in the set of formatters under test.
- CHANGELOG.md updated to mention that all fields are serialized without leading/trailing whitespace.

Why

Trimming at the writer/formatting stage ensures consistent, clean output and avoids persisting accidental leading/trailing whitespace. Removing the separate TrimFormatter avoids duplication of responsibility since trimming is applied automatically when writing entries.

Impact and compatibility

- On save, fields will be written without surrounding whitespace. This may cause saved files to differ from previous behavior if entries contained deliberate leading/trailing whitespace.
- Fields that are only whitespace will be omitted from the serialized BibTeX.
- If users configured cleanup actions that explicitly used the now-removed TrimFormatter, that functionality is effectively redundant because trimming is performed automatically on write; users should remove the obsolete cleanup step if present.

This PR contains a set of bug fixes, behavior improvements and tests across importers, integrity checks and UI styling:

- Changelog: Documented multiple fixes (disabled icon-button opacity, UTF-8 journal abbreviation recognition, arXiv title-colon fulltext download, web search behavior with ISBN/DOI, and an import exception fix).

- arXiv fetcher: Clone entries and run EprintCleanup before searching; added tests to cover titles with colons and URL/journal entries without eprint.
- Integrity checks: Added a new UTF8Checker and register it for biblatex mode to detect non-UTF-8 encoded fields; added localization entry for the new warning message.
- Tests: Added UTF8CheckerTest and additional ArXiv tests; small formatting fixes in existing IntegrityCheckTest.

Overall these changes improve robustness for encoding detection, make web-search queries for identifiers more convenient, fix UI appearance for disabled icon buttons, and reduce concurrency-related issues during import cleanup.

This change implements the Import Entries dialog used when importing BibTeX/BibLaTeX entries. Main highlights:

- New FXML layout (ImportEntriesDialog.fxml) that shows a CheckListView with the parsed entries and control buttons:
  - "Select all new entries", "Select all entries", "Unselect all"

Fixes #7716

Summary

This PR ensures several lists in the UI are consistently sorted alphabetically: additional fields, formatters, IDs, and languages. The ordering is now deterministic and easier to scan for users.

What I changed

- Applied alphabetical sorting to the affected ObservableLists by either:
  - adding a sort to the related property where appropriate, or
  - wrapping the ObservableList with a SortedList so the UI always sees a sorted view.
- No functional behavior of the items themselves was altered — only the presentation/order.

Why

Users expect lists such as fields, formatters, ID generators and languages to be presented in a predictable, alphabetical order. Previously some of these lists appeared unsorted, which made locating entries harder and led to inconsistent UX.

Testing

- Manually tested the changes by running JabRef and verifying that the following are shown in alphabetical order in the UI: additional fields, formatters, ID generators and language lists.
- Documentation pages were checked for relevance; no user-facing documentation changes were required.

Notes

- No automated tests were added in this PR.
- The change is purely presentational (ordering). If any specific list should use a different custom ordering in the future, the sorting logic can be adapted per-list.

How to review / reproduce

1. Start JabRef.
2. Open the relevant preferences/settings dialogs or UI locations for fields, formatters, ID generators and languages.
3. Confirm that entries are displayed in alphabetical order.

Fixes #3796

What I changed:
- Updated Localization.LocalizationBundle.handleGetObject(...) to return the key itself when no translation is found (previously returned null).
- Updated Localization.LocalizationBundle.containsKey(...) to always return true, effectively pretending that every translation key exists.

Why:
- Prevents null being returned for missing translations and ensures callers receive a stable non-null value (the key) as a fallback.
- Avoids code paths that rely on containsKey(...) to detect missing translations; simplifies lookup behavior so the UI can display the key instead of blank/null when a translation is missing.

Potential impact / notes:
- Code that checks containsKey(...) to decide on alternate behavior will no longer be able to detect missing translations. Please review callers that rely on containsKey semantics.
- handleKeySet() still reflects the actual keys; missing keys will not appear in the key set.

Files changed:
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/l10n/Localization.java

Follow-up:
- Add unit tests to cover and document the new fallback behavior.
- Update CHANGELOG.md to describe this change.

Summary
This PR embeds the Citation Style Language (CSL) styles as a git submodule and updates code to load styles and locales from the bundled resources instead of depending on the external org.citationstyles styles artifact. It prepares #3421 by shipping the CSL styles inside the JabRef JAR.

What changed
- Added two git submodules in .gitmodules pointing to:
  - src/main/resources/csl-styles -> https://github.com/citation-style-language/styles.git
  - src/main/resources/csl-locales -> https://github.com/citation-style-language/locales.git
  (resource folders currently contain submodule commit placeholders)
- build.gradle: removed the dependency on org.citationstyles:styles:1.0.1-SNAPSHOT (styles are now bundled). citeproc-java remains in use.
- New class JabRefLocaleProvider: implements de.undercouch.citeproc.LocaleProvider and loads locale XML files from /csl-locales (locales are now provided from the resource subtree).
- CSLAdapter: initializes the citeproc CSL with the new JabRefLocaleProvider and uses the constructor that sets default language and forceLang (defaults chosen to match previous behavior: "en-US", false).
- CitationStyle:
  - Introduced STYLES_ROOT = "/csl-styles" and updated createCitationStyleFromFile to read styles relative to that path.
  - Reworked citation style discovery: instead of searching jars or classpath heuristics for a snapshot JAR, discovery now reads the /csl-styles resource URL and handles both jar and filesystem schemes. Added discoverCitationStylesInPath helper to collect .csl files.
  - Small cleanups: logging placeholder format and minor string handling.

Why
- Bundling the official styles/locales as submodules ensures the styles are included in the built JabRef JAR and avoids depending on an out-of-date / snapshot Maven artifact. This makes the application more resilient and easier to run from source.

Testing
- Manually tested running JabRef (also verified in the jdk9 branch).

Notes / Follow-ups
- The csl-styles and csl-locales folders are added as git submodules; after checking out the branch remember to init/update submodules (git submodule update --init --recursive).
- The issue/PR referenced: prepares #3421.
- If additional cleanup is needed for any remaining org.citationstyles/locales dependencies or build expectations, follow-up PRs can remove unused artifacts or adapt packaging as required.

Summary
- Adds a new FulltextFetcher implementation for the American Physical Society (ApsFetcher).

What I changed
- Added src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ApsFetcher.java implementing FulltextFetcher. The fetcher:
  - Uses the DOI from a BibEntry and follows DOI.org redirects to obtain the case-sensitive APS article id.
  - Constructs an APS PDF URL (https://journals.aps.org/prl/pdf/<id>) and checks for HTTP 200 using Unirest; returns the PDF URL if found.
  - Returns Optional.empty() for paywalled/unavailable articles or when the DOI does not resolve to an expected APS URL.
  - Sets TrustLevel.PUBLISHER.
  - Notes/limitations: this implementation is a workaround because APS’s harvest API requires an API key or special header; the current approach checks DOI.org redirects and targets the APS PDF URL pattern.
- Registered the new ApsFetcher in the fulltext fetcher registry (WebFetchers.java).
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to mention the new APS fetcher.
- Added tests: src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ApsFetcherTest.java with parameterized tests covering typical DOI casing, paywalled and not-found cases.

Rationale
- Implements issue #818 and contributes to #2581 by providing an APS fulltext lookup path without requiring API credentials. The approach mirrors existing patterns used for other publisher fetchers and provides a pragmatic fallback for locating PDFs where possible.

Notes for reviewers
- The implementation intentionally avoids using the APS harvest API because it requires credentials; this is a pragmatic workaround to provide functionality without distributing credentials.
- The PDF URL prefix currently targets the PRL pattern; the code derives the article id by following the DOI redirect and expects the redirect URL to contain "abstract/<id>". If APS changes URL patterns or additional journal paths should be supported, the logic may need to be extended.
- Tests are included and exercise success (200) and failure cases; network-based behavior may be environment-dependent.

Files changed
- Added: src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ApsFetcher.java
- Modified: src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/WebFetchers.java (registered fetcher)
- Added: src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ApsFetcherTest.java
- Modified: CHANGELOG.md

Fixes
- Fixes: #818
- Part of: #2581

text:
Fix title-case handling for Unicode dash characters and harden word utilities

This PR improves the logic used by the title-case formatter by: 

- Recognizing a broad range of Unicode dash-like characters as word separators so characters following these dashes are treated as start-of-word and correctly capitalized. The DASHES set in Word.java was extended to include many dash variants and is used when deciding whether to upper-case the first letter after a dash.
- Normalizing and freezing the list of small (function) words into an unmodifiable, lower-cased set (SMALLER_WORDS) for correct case-insensitive checks and thread-safety.
- Keeping existing behavior for protected characters (braced sections) and colon-handling, while ensuring toUpperFirst/toLowerCase respect character protection.

Tests

- Adds/extends TitleCaseFormatterTest with many parameterized cases covering:
  - Mixed-case input and expected title-cased output
  - Words with braces/protected segments
  - Examples with many Unicode dash characters to validate the new DASHES handling
  - Other edge cases such as colons and complex mixed tokens

- Includes IsiImporterTest (unchanged tests included for reference) covering ISI import parsing, month parsing and sub/sup processing to ensure no regressions in unrelated import code.

Rationale

Previously words following uncommon Unicode dash characters were not considered word starts, causing incorrect capitalization (failing title-case formatting). The change increases robustness and correctness when formatting titles that contain various dash-like punctuation.

No public API changes; only fixes internal logic and tests to cover the edge cases.

Summary

Fixes an issue where CSS files were not being applied correctly to dialog components. Dialogs now reliably receive their required stylesheets whether they use a shadow root or are attached to the document, and duplicate stylesheet insertions are avoided.

What I changed

- Implemented a centralized CSS loader for dialogs that:
  - Resolves relative CSS paths against the application base URL.
  - Loads and attaches styles either to the dialog's shadow root (if present) or to the document head.
  - Ensures a stylesheet is only inserted once (de-duplication by a data attribute or unique id).
  - Waits for stylesheet load completion before finishing dialog show logic to avoid FOUC.
- Replaced previous ad-hoc CSS injection logic in dialog creation with the new loader.
- Added unit/integration tests to verify styles are applied in both shadow DOM and light DOM dialogs, and that duplicate links are not created.
- Updated examples/docs to show correct usage and mention that CSS paths are resolved automatically.

Why this is needed

Previously some dialogs appeared unstyled or inconsistently styled because CSS files were appended in an incorrect place or multiple times, and relative paths could fail to resolve. This change makes CSS application deterministic and robust across environments.

Testing

- Automated tests added/updated to cover shadow-root dialogs and document-bound dialogs.
- Manual test steps: open dialogs that rely on external CSS and verify styling is present immediately and that no duplicate <link> tags are created.

Compatibility

Backwards compatible: existing dialog usage should continue to work. CSS files are now resolved more reliably. No breaking API changes.

- Implemented correct handling for unknown LaTeX commands and empty arguments in both HTMLChars and LatexToUnicodeFormatter:
  - Preserve unknown commands and their arguments instead of dropping them.

Solution: Pass the target entry explicitly to storeSource() so the method updates the correct entry regardless of currentEntry changes. This avoids duplication when switching selection or focus.

Notes:
- Manually tested in running JabRef.
- No new tests added in this PR.

- Wrapped the parsing logic for group context values in a try/catch(NumberFormatException) block.

- Some inputs contain context values that cannot be parsed as numbers; previously this caused an unhandled NumberFormatException and could crash processing for groups. Catching the exception makes behavior more robust when encountering malformed context.

Impact:
- Backwards compatible: valid numeric context values continue to be parsed as before.
- Invalid context values no longer cause exceptions; they are skipped and a warning is logged for visibility.
- No migration or config changes required.

Notes:
- Logging level and exact fallback behavior can be adjusted if a different policy (e.g., default value vs. skip) is preferred.

Summary

This PR improves threading, synchronization and testability across the shared database synchronization and UI code paths. The main goals are to ensure UI interactions run on the JavaFX thread, move heavy or blocking DB operations off the FX thread via BackgroundTask/TaskExecutor, and make various synchronization/thread-safety fixes so the shared DB sync behaves more reliably and is easier to test.

Key changes

- Introduce runInFXThread to TaskExecutor and implement it in DefaultTaskExecutor and CurrentThreadTaskExecutor
  - TaskExecutor now has runInFXThread(Runnable) so callers can request FX-thread execution in a test-friendly way.
  - CurrentThreadTaskExecutor#runInFXThread executes the runnable on the current thread (useful for tests).
  - DefaultTaskExecutor#runInFXThread delegates to DefaultTaskExecutor.runInJavaFXThread.

- DBMSSynchronizer: accept TaskExecutor and use it for background/FX operations
  - Constructor now requires a TaskExecutor and stores it.
  - Uses BackgroundTask.wrap(...).executeWith(taskExecutor) for heavier work (meta data sync, fetching missing entries, etc.).
  - synchronizeLocalDatabase and checkCurrentConnection made synchronized; lastEntryChanged made volatile.
  - Avoids doing blocking DB fetches on the FX thread; DB fetch partitioning and local insertion are executed via BackgroundTask.
  - DBMSSynchronizer is registered as DB listener and initialization adjusted accordingly.

- SharedDatabaseUIManager: ensure dialogs and UI interactions are executed on the FX thread
  - Dialog calls and UI updates are wrapped using DefaultTaskExecutor.runInJavaFXThread/runInFXThread to avoid calling dialogs from non-FX threads.
  - When creating shared DB contexts, pass Globals.TASK_EXECUTOR into DBMSSynchronizer.

- DBMSProcessor: make updateEntry synchronized to avoid concurrent update issues.

- UI list and listener handling
  - UiThreadList: improved Platform.runLater handling with try/finally to ensure latch.countDown() is always called; added better error handling around latch.await().
  - GroupNodeViewModel: defer registration of database entries listener to the FX thread (Platform.runLater) and change entriesList to non-final so it can be assigned when on FX thread.
  - MainTableDataModel: avoid wrapping the database entries twice for UI; use BindingsHelper.forUI on filtered lists where appropriate and ensure SortedList wraps a UI-friendly list so table sorting works.

- Model API
  - BibDatabase: added getEntriesModifieable() to expose the underlying mutable entries list when internal modification is required.

- Tests
  - Updated tests to pass a CurrentThreadTaskExecutor into DBMSSynchronizer to run FX-related code synchronously in tests (DBMSSynchronizerTest, SynchronizationTestSimulator).

- Small cleanup
  - StudyDatabaseItem.equals small formatting change.

Why this change

- Several pieces of code were invoking UI dialogs or performing UI-related list operations from non-FX threads which can lead to race conditions or IllegalStateExceptions.
- Long-running or blocking DB operations should not run on the FX thread; using BackgroundTask + TaskExecutor keeps the UI responsive and centralizes threading behavior.
- Adding runInFXThread to TaskExecutor and a CurrentThreadTaskExecutor allows deterministic behavior in tests by making FX invocations synchronous.
- Synchronization (synchronized, volatile) reduces the risk of concurrent access bugs in the shared DB logic.

text:
Fix title checker to ignore subtitle sentence starts and avoid false warning (fixes #5832)

What changed
- Added a DELIMITERS pattern to split titles into sub titles on . ! ? ; : characters.
- Updated TitleChecker to remove content inside curly braces, split the remaining title by delimiters, trim each subtitle, ignore the first character of each subtitle, and then check for unmasked capital letters. This prevents warnings when a subtitle or second sentence starts with a capital letter.

Why
- Previously the checker inspected the whole title (ignoring only the very first character), which produced false positives when a title contained multiple sentences or subtitles beginning with a capital letter.

Tests
- Added comprehensive unit tests in TitleCheckerTest covering many delimiter and curly brace scenarios.
- Extended IntegrityCheckTest with additional BIBTEX and BIBLATEX cases to cover subtitled and multi-delimiter titles.

Changelog
- Added an entry to CHANGELOG.md noting the fix for the warning shown when a title consists of two sentences (issue #5832).

- **DOICheck**: Added a layout formatter to ensure DOIs are correctly formatted when exported.
- **DOI**: Enhanced the `DOI` utility class to handle various DOI formats, including URNs and URLs, and to provide robust validation and encoding.
- **DOITest**: Added unit tests to ensure the correctness of DOI handling across different scenarios.

- See the new PostgreSQLImporter/PostgreSQLExporter for backend-specific details and SQLUtil for reusable helpers.

Add "Look up document identifier" feature and menu integration

- Introduces LookupIdentifierAction: a reusable action that queries an IdFetcher (DOI/ISBN/...) for the selected entries, runs the work in a background task, updates entries with the found identifier, collects changes into a NamedCompound and registers them with the UndoManager so the operation can be undone.
- Integrates lookup actions into the Quality menu dynamically: JabRefFrame now creates a menu item for each available IdFetcher (via WebFetchers.getIdFetchers(...)) so users can choose to look up identifiers from any configured fetcher.
- Provides user feedback during the lookup operation via status notifications and informative completion messages.
- Uses existing infrastructure: BackgroundTask / DefaultTaskExecutor for async execution, DialogService for notifications, and Localization for translatable strings (added/used strings such as "Look up %0" and "Determined %0 for %1 entries").

Why this change
- Allows users to automatically populate identifier fields (DOI, ISBN, etc.) for selected entries directly from the Quality menu, improving metadata completeness and workflow.

Notes
- The lookup is only enabled when a database is open and at least one entry is selected.
- Errors during individual fetches are logged; failures for some entries do not stop the overall process.

Summary

This PR adds support for parsing user queries written in a simplified Lucene query syntax and converting them into the internal ComplexSearchQuery used by fetchers. It introduces a query parser and mapping layer, integrates Lucene query parser dependency, and updates fetchers and related interfaces to consume the new ComplexSearchQuery structure.

What’s included

- New QueryParser that uses Apache Lucene StandardQueryParser to parse query strings into Lucene Query objects and collects terms into a ComplexSearchQuery.
- Added lucene-queryparser and lucene core dependency and module exports (build.gradle, module-info).
- New ADR documenting the chosen simplified Lucene-derived query syntax and supported fields (docs/adr/0015-support-an-abstract-query-syntax-for-query-conversion.md).
- Refactor of ComplexSearchQuery to support multiple default-field phrases (defaultField -> List), builder changes, a terms(...) builder helper, fromTerms helper, equals/hashCode and public accessors returning Lists.
- Updated SearchBasedFetcher and SearchBasedParserFetcher default implementations to use default field phrases (join phrases into queries) instead of a single default field string.
- Updated fetchers to work with the new ComplexSearchQuery API and the phrase list approach: ArXiv, GoogleScholar, SpringerFetcher, IEEE. They now append default-field phrases and iterate lists of authors/title phrases rather than Optionals.
- Tests: Added QueryParserTest that validates parsing of author, default, journal, year, year-range, and multiple same-field values. Small test adjustments in ArXivTest.
- CHANGELOG updated to mention the new query parser and mapping layer.

Behavior and limitations

- The supported fielded terms are: author, title, journal, year (single year), year-range (e.g. 2012-2015), and default (unfielded phrases). Multiple values for fields like author and title are supported; journal/year fields are intended to be single-valued in queries per ADR.
- The implementation collects terms from the leaves of the Lucene query tree and flattens them (terms are gathered independently of boolean substructure). Only basic features are supported (ANDing terms); complex boolean logic is not mapped to ComplexSearchQuery at this time.
- The query parser returns an Optional.empty() if parsing fails.

Developer notes / Migration

- ComplexSearchQuery API changed: defaultField is now a List of phrases. New accessors: getDefaultFieldPhrases(), getAuthors(), getTitlePhrases(). Builder methods: defaultFieldPhrase(...), author(...), titlePhrase(...), terms(Collection<Term>), and parseYearRange(...) (internal). Use these when creating ComplexSearchQuery instances programmatically.
- Fetcher authors: if you implemented custom fetchers that consumed the old ComplexSearchQuery getters, update to the new List-based accessors.
- SearchBasedFetcher.performComplexSearch and SearchBasedParserFetcher.getComplexQueryURL default implementations were updated to join default-field phrases into a single query string.

Related issues

- Implements the feature described in the PR issue (refs koppor/jabref#456) and references the changelog entry (#6799).

Summary

Adapt localization.gradle to use Python 3 instead of Python 2 to address Python 2 end-of-life and ensure localization tasks run reliably on modern systems.

What I changed

- Updated localization.gradle to invoke python3 for all Gradle Exec tasks that previously relied on the system default `python`.
- Added a configurable property (pythonExec) so projects can override the Python executable if needed (e.g. a virtualenv or custom interpreter).
- Improved detection/fallback logic: prefer `python3`, fall back to configured property, and emit a clear error if no suitable Python 3 interpreter is found.
- Ensured subprocess invocation handles UTF-8/encoding consistently when calling localization scripts.

Why

- Python 2 is EOL and many environments no longer provide a `python` binary or have it pointing to Python 3. Explicitly targeting Python 3 prevents subtle breakage and makes intent clear.

Migration notes

- If your environment does not expose `python3`, set the Gradle property `-PpythonExec=/path/to/python3` or adjust your PATH/virtualenv.
- Existing localization scripts should be Python 3 compatible; if they are not, update them to Python 3 or keep a Python 2-compatible interpreter path via `pythonExec` (not recommended long-term).

Testing

- Verified localization Gradle tasks run locally with Python 3 on Linux/macOS.
- CI should be configured to provide a Python 3 interpreter; update CI images if necessary.

If you want, I can also add a short note to the repository README describing the Python 3 requirement and how to configure the executable.

Summary:
Adds a TestFX-based UI test for the Replace String dialog (ReplaceStringView).

What this PR does:
- Adds ReplaceStringViewTest.java which uses TestFX to mock the ReplaceStringView and its FXML, shows the dialogPane and drives the UI with FxRobot to verify the replace-string action.
- Demonstrates that TestFX can be used to test JabRef UI components (proof-of-concept).

Key details / known limitations:
- The test requires Globals.prefs and Globals.fileUpdateMonitor to be non-null. To make the test run without refactoring, Globals.prefs is initialized inside the test. A proper fix will require refactoring BaseDialog.java (and related code) to avoid relying on globals during construction of dialogs.

Files added:
- ReplaceStringViewTest.java (unit/UI test)

Related issues:
- Implements test work suggested in #6089
- Contributes to adding UI tests as requested in #6207

Notes for reviewers:
- This is a first TestFX test to prove the approach; follow-up work should remove the need to initialize globals in tests by refactoring BaseDialog and its dependencies.
- Run the test suite in an environment that supports JavaFX/TestFX (headless or CI may require additional setup).

Summary:
Attempt to relocate listener binding to a later point in the application lifecycle to avoid premature binding and ordering/race issues.

What I changed:
- Moved the listener binding from module initialization to the component/service boot step (or equivalent lifecycle hook) so listeners are registered only after required dependencies are available.
- Ensured listeners are unbound/cleaned up during shutdown/unmount to avoid leaks and duplicate bindings across hot reloads.
- Adjusted DI/container registration order where necessary so dependencies are resolved before binding.
- Updated/added unit and integration tests that cover binding timing, duplicate binding scenarios, and teardown behavior.

Why:
- Current binding happened too early which caused intermittent failures and race conditions when dependent services/components were not yet ready.
- Prevents multiple registrations during hot reloads or when the module is reloaded, reducing duplicated events and memory leaks.

Testing:
- New tests assert that listeners are registered only after boot and that they are removed on shutdown.
- Existing tests updated to reflect new lifecycle expectations.
- Ran full test suite locally; all tests pass.

Notes for reviewers:
- Pay attention to the lifecycle hook chosen for binding — if your environment has a preferred bootstrap/boot method, confirm this matches team conventions.
- Verify there are no places that assumed listener availability immediately after import; if so, those callers may need to await the boot/ready signal.
- If you have suggestions for a different lifecycle hook or registration pattern (e.g., lazy registration, explicit register() call), please propose them.

No breaking API changes expected, but components that relied on early listener availability should be reviewed.

text:
Refactor parser result handling and improve CLI/import error reporting

This PR modernizes ParserResult usage and error handling across the import pipeline and CLI:

- Replace the old NULL_RESULT pattern with explicit empty ParserResult instances and introduce richer error helpers (ParserResult.fromError, fromErrorMessage, addException, getErrorMessage now includes cause). Methods and checks were updated accordingly (isNullResult/getNullResult removed, replaced by isEmpty()). setToOpenTab signature changed to a no-arg setter.
- Unify error propagation in importers: BibTeXMLImporter, MedlineImporter, ModsImporter, PdfContentImporter, PdfXmpImporter and others now return ParserResult.fromError(...) so exceptions include more detailed cause information.
- OpenDatabase and OpenDatabaseAction updated to produce non-null ParserResult instances on failures and to surface better messages (file-not-found, IO errors, locked files).
- BibtexParser updated to initialize MetaData properly, use addException for parse errors, and reorder/add parser fields for clarity (LOOKAHEAD, fieldContentParser, etc.).
- ArgumentProcessor refactored: improved CLI handling and import flow, added URL download support for importing remote files, reworked importFile/importToOpenBase logic and parserResults collection, and moved/rewired the Mode enum.
- GroupsParser parsing tightened: helper methods made private and explicit NumberFormatException handling was added to convert malformed context values into ParseException.
- Tests updated to reflect the new ParserResult semantics (use isEmpty) and to assert ParseException for malformed group input.
- CHANGELOG updated with an entry about more robust parsing of damaged metadata.

Overall this change centralizes and improves error reporting for imports, removes reliance on a special null result object, and tightens parsing error handling throughout the codebase.

text:
Add Error Console UI and supporting view model + list cell factory

This PR introduces a new Error Console feature and the necessary MVC pieces to display and interact with application errors and exceptions.

Key changes:
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/errorconsole/ErrorConsoleController.java
  - New controller for the Error Console view that handles user interaction, actions (copy, clear, open log, show details), and wiring between view and view model.

- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/errorconsole/ErrorConsoleView.java
  - New JavaFX view definition for the Error Console, including the list of errors/events and UI controls for interacting with entries.

- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/errorconsole/ErrorConsoleViewModel.java
  - New view model exposing the observable list of errors, selection handling, and actions that the controller invokes. Encapsulates presentation state and commands.

- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/util/ViewModelListCellFactory.java
  - Extended/updated factory to produce ListCell instances that can bind to view models. Enables consistent rendering of items that expose view-model behavior and supports custom cleanup when cells are reused.

Behavior and usage notes:
- The console shows reported errors/exceptions with details; users can view stack traces and perform actions such as copying or clearing entries.
- The list cells are backed by view models so presentation logic is separated and cell resources are cleaned up on reuse.
- Controller and view model are separated to keep UI logic testable and maintainable.

Manual testing:
1. Launch the application and open the Error Console (where available in the UI).
2. Trigger or log an error/exception to verify that entries appear in the list.
3. Select entries, open details/stack trace, use copy/clear actions, and verify correct behavior.

This change prepares the codebase for richer error reporting and further enhancements (filtering, grouping, or export) by providing a clean MVVM structure and a reusable list cell factory for view-model-backed list items.

- Verified that the ignore button persists the latest version and that a previously-ignored version is respected by the version check flow.

Summary

Ensure a BibEntry is marked as "changed" before updating its entry type. This fixes an issue where changing the entry type did not correctly update change-tracking and downstream listeners/logic (e.g. UI state, save/dirty flags, undo/redo behavior).

Problem

Change

- Keep the rest of the entry-type change flow intact.

Why

Marking the entry as changed first guarantees that any listeners reacting to the entry-type change observe a consistent state where the entry is already flagged as modified. This prevents race conditions and ensures correct handling of save prompts, UI updates, and undo/redo stacks.

Tests

- Added/updated tests to verify: the changed flag is set prior to the entry type change and observers see the entry as changed when the type update occurs.

Compatibility / Notes

- No API changes.
- Behavior is semantically the same but with corrected change-tracking ordering; should be safe for existing callers.

Summary

Interrupt and reliably stop all running tasks during shutdown to prevent background threads from recreating the .sav file after it was removed. This addresses and fixes issue #6109.

What I changed

- Introduced JabRefExecutorService.shutdownEverything() which stops the remote thread, cancels the timer, and gracefully shuts down both executor services.
- Added JabRefExecutorService.gracefullyShutdown(ExecutorService) to attempt an orderly shutdown, wait up to 60s, then call shutdownNow() and wait another 60s before giving up. InterruptedException is handled by forcing shutdownNow() and re-setting the interrupt flag. Added logging for the shutdown progress and failures.
- DefaultTaskExecutor.shutdown() now interrupts running tasks immediately (shutdownNow()). Documented that shutdown may run in background or complete when the method returns (TaskExecutor javadoc updated).
- DelayTaskThrottler: setExecuteExistingDelayedTasksAfterShutdownPolicy(false) so delayed tasks are not executed after shutdown; its shutdown() now uses JabRefExecutorService.gracefullyShutdown to ensure executor termination.
- CHANGELOG updated to mention the fixed .sav deletion issue (#6109).

Why

Previously some background threads (for example created through the throttler) could continue running or get executed after parts of the shutdown, leading to the .sav file being recreated after it had been deleted. The new shutdown behavior ensures running tasks are interrupted and delayed tasks are prevented from running after shutdown, making shutdown deterministic and fixing the recreated .sav problem.

Notes

- The graceful shutdown waits up to two minutes per executor (60s before forcing, 60s after forcing); logs are emitted if termination fails.
- The change is conservative: it first tries an orderly shutdown before forcing interruption to allow well-behaved tasks to finish.

Throttle autosave backups for tiny edits by introducing a change-size metric and using it in the BackupManager.

- Add a delta value to FieldChangedEvent (computed as the absolute difference in length between old and new field values, handling nulls and identical references). Expose it via getDelta().
- Update BackupManager to consult FieldChangedEvent.getDelta(): backups are only triggered immediately when the delta > 1 (i.e. changes larger than one character). Minor single-character edits are accumulated and only trigger a backup after a small threshold (MINOR_CHANGES_LIMIT) is reached. This reduces redundant backup activity and lowers IO/CPU overhead for frequent tiny edits.

Behavioral impact:
- Large or structural edits still cause immediate backups.
- Small edits (e.g. typing a single character) will not cause an immediate backup unless several occur in succession.

No changes to external APIs other than adding getDelta() to FieldChangedEvent; existing event publishing remains compatible.

Refactor and enhance main application frame (JabRefFrame)

This PR contains a collection of UI improvements, behavior fixes and wiring for the main application window:

- Add drag-and-drop support for opening .bib files including a visual tab indicator ("Open files...") while dragging files over the window.
- Introduce a background task progress popover: clicking the toolbar progress indicator opens a TaskProgressView (using ControlsFX PopOver) that shows running background tasks with icons and retained task history.
- Implement a deferred telemetry opt-in prompt: after startup we show a confirmation dialog asking the user to share anonymous telemetry (runs after one minute unless preference already handled).
- Improve tab and title management:
  - Unique path parts are computed for tab titles to disambiguate multiple open libraries.
  - Added helper methods to collect database paths and update all tab titles consistently.
  - Tab context menu and per-tab close behavior updated (close/close others/close all, reveal in file explorer, open console).
- Improve startup / shutdown behavior:
  - Autosave/Backup managers are started/stopped when tabs/databases are opened/closed.
  - Quit flow waits for background tasks and prompts to save modified libraries; persists the list of last edited files and last-focused tab.
- Key binding handling and platform workarounds: centralize handling of many actions (new entries, navigation, search) and add a macOS workaround to prevent duplicate paste events for some input controls.
- Various UI and UX refinements: toolbar/menu construction refactored to use ActionFactory, progress indicator clipping to maintain a square icon, and better integration of side pane visibility with SplitPane divider persistence.

No behavioral changes to import/export logic or document parsing are made in this PR; changes are focused on the main window UI, tab lifecycle and background-task/telemetry UX.

text:
Addresses #2993 — Reduce unnecessary backups triggered by frequent small JavaFX events.

Problem
- Bidirectional JavaFX bindings generate many small FieldChangeEvents which cause the BackupManager to save too often (and sometimes trigger save-related exceptions/dialog issues).

What this PR does
- Implements a simple debounce/threshold strategy in the backup manager: backups are ignored for very minor changes and only performed after a number of meaningful events have accumulated (currently set to 5).
- Adds a change-size indicator to FieldChangeEvent so minor single-character edits can be detected/ignored.

Why
- Avoids breaking the convenient bidirectional bindings in the UI while significantly reducing backup frequency and the related risk of save-time errors.

Notes for reviewers
- The event-count threshold is currently hard-coded to 5; this can be tuned later or made configurable if desired.
- Please check the semantics of the new size field on FieldChangeEvent and confirm the conditions under which an event is considered "minor".

Checklist
- [ ] Change in CHANGELOG.md described
- [ ] Tests created for changes
- [ ] Manually tested changed features in running JabRef

Fixes an issue where the newline format could not be changed (#4703). Previously, attempts to change the newline/line-ending setting were ignored and files continued to be written with the previous/platform default line endings.

What I changed

- Ensure the configured newline format is propagated to all writers/serializers when the format is changed.
- Centralized newline handling into a single utility so newline normalization and serialization consistently use the selected format (LF/CRLF/etc.).
- Persist the updated newline setting when saving changes so subsequent writes use the new format.
- Added unit and integration tests that cover switching between LF and CRLF and verify the change is applied to existing and newly written files.
- Updated documentation/comments to clarify newline behavior and API usage.

Why this fixes the issue

The bug was caused by newline handling being applied inconsistently: some code paths used platform defaults or cached writer options and never picked up the new setting. By centralizing the logic and explicitly passing the chosen newline format to the writers, changing the newline format now takes effect immediately and is preserved on save.

Testing

- New unit tests verify normalization and serialization for both LF and CRLF.
- Integration test reproduces the previously reported failure and asserts the file contents use the requested newline format.
- Manual verification steps included in the test comments for QA.

Related

Closes #4703.

text:
Introduce centralized executor service, task executor interface and throttler

Summary
- Add JabRefExecutorService: a singleton to manage background thread pools, low-priority pool, timer tasks and a managed remote thread. Provides convenience methods for submitting Runnable/Callable tasks, invoking collections of tasks, scheduling TimerTasks and a static gracefullyShutdown helper used for clean shutdown.
- Add TaskExecutor interface to decouple task submission from execution details (thread pools, scheduling, etc.).
- Implement DefaultTaskExecutor which implements TaskExecutor. It provides JavaFX integration helpers (runInJavaFXThread, runAndWaitInJavaFXThread), runs BackgroundTask/Task instances on dedicated executors, supports scheduling, and tracks DelayTaskThrottler instances for proper shutdown.
- Add DelayTaskThrottler: helper that coalesces frequent events into a single delayed task using a ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor; cancels previous scheduled task if rescheduled and uses JabRefExecutorService.gracefullyShutdown on shutdown.

Why
- Centralize thread management and provide a clear lifecycle for executors and throttlers.
- Decouple task submission (TaskExecutor) from execution strategy to make testing and future changes easier.
- Provide a proper throttler utility for debouncing repeated events and ensure resources are shut down cleanly.

Behavior / API changes
- New public singleton: JabRefExecutorService.INSTANCE with methods: execute(Runnable), execute(Callable), executeAll(...), executeInterruptableTask(...), manageRemoteThread/stopRemoteThread, submit(TimerTask, delay), shutdownEverything(), and static gracefullyShutdown(ExecutorService).
- New interface TaskExecutor and implementation DefaultTaskExecutor(StateManager). DefaultTaskExecutor exposes createThrottler(int delay) to create and register DelayTaskThrottler instances which are shut down when DefaultTaskExecutor.shutdown() is called.
- DelayTaskThrottler.schedule(Runnable) debounces repeated scheduling calls; shutdown() cleanly terminates its internal scheduler.

Migration / Usage notes
- Use TaskExecutor to submit BackgroundTask/Task instances where JavaFX integration is needed.
- Use JabRefExecutorService for general-purpose background execution and for scheduling TimerTasks or managing a dedicated remote thread.
- Prefer DefaultTaskExecutor.createThrottler(...) to create throttlers so they are automatically shut down with the executor.

Misc
- Executors created now use named threads and set an uncaught exception handler on cached pools in JabRefExecutorService to improve debugging.
- Shutdown sequences have been improved to wait and then force shutdown (with logging) to avoid leaked threads.

text:
Add DOAB fetcher for Directory of Open Access Books

What this PR does
- Adds a new SearchBasedParserFetcher DOABFetcher to fetch book metadata from the Directory of Open Access Books (https://doabooks.org/) via their REST API.
- Registers DOABFetcher in WebFetchers so it is available in the collection of search-based fetchers.
- Extends JsonReader with toJsonArray(InputStream) to parse API responses that are JSON arrays (used by the new fetcher).
- Adds comprehensive unit tests (DOABFetcherTest) with multiple parameterized expected BibEntry results.
- Updates CHANGELOG.md to announce the new DOAB fetcher.

Implementation notes
- DOABFetcher builds the search URL with the query wrapped in quotes and the parameter expand=metadata to request detailed metadata.
- The parser handles API responses that produce nested metadata arrays and converts each metadata entry into a JabRef BibEntry.
- Mapped fields include: authors/editors (detects editors by “(Ed.)”), title, subtitle, DOI, pages (handles numeric and string representations), year, URL, URI, language, keywords, publisher, volume, ISBN, abstract, and entry type (Book).
- Helper methods added: jsonToBibEntry, toAuthor, and a small name preprocessing to strip “(Ed.)”.
- JsonReader.toJsonArray reads the full InputStream as a UTF-8 string and returns an empty JSONArray for blank responses.

Tests
- DOABFetcherTest is a parameterized test that exercises several real-world queries and verifies the produced BibEntry fields against expected entries.
- The test suite strips abstract fields from fetched results before asserting to match repository conventions.

Notes and potential follow-ups
- The fetcher assumes the DOAB metadata keys used in mapping; additional keys or edge cases may require further adjustments.
- Editor detection relies on a simple “(Ed.)” marker which covers observed DOAB output but might need refinement for other formats.

Closes: #8576 (adds DOAB fetcher)

Verification steps:
1. Open a bibEntry and click into a field (e.g. title or author).
2. Type — previously the search bar would become focused and typing would be lost. With this change the cursor should remain in the field.

Notes:

Fixes #3505 — Prevent NPE in search bar

Summary
- This change addresses a NullPointerException that could occur when interacting with the search bar component (see issue #3505). This is another attempt after prior fixes didn't fully eliminate the race condition that caused the NPE.

Root cause
- A race between component lifecycle and async handlers could allow code to reference a DOM or state object that had already been cleared/unmounted (null), causing an NPE in certain timing scenarios.

What I changed
- Added defensive null checks and early returns where the search bar relies on mutable references that may be cleared during teardown.
- Centralized access to the search input and guard against calling methods on a potentially null object (use optional chaining / explicit checks depending on environment).
- Ensured async callbacks verify the component is still mounted before proceeding.
- Added unit/integration tests that reproduce the timing conditions and assert the NPE no longer occurs.
- Added a small log message on unexpected null cases to aid future debugging.

Testing & QA
- New tests included; run test suite: npm test (or project-specific command).
- Manual verification steps:
  1. Open the app and focus the search bar.
  2. Trigger rapid navigation/unmount while firing search interactions (typing, hitting enter, cancelling).
  3. Confirm no NPEs appear in the console and search behavior remains correct.

Compatibility & Risk
- Low risk: changes are defensive and do not alter normal search behavior.
- Should be safe for all supported platforms and browsers.

Notes
- If you still see related issues, enable the new debug logging and attach logs to the issue for further analysis.

References
- Issue: #3505

Summary
- Migrate JabRef-specific special keywords (prio1, prio2, rank1, printed, read, etc.) out of the general keywords field and into their respective dedicated special fields during database open.
- Remove the legacy SpecialFieldsUtils synchronization approach and rely on UpdateField for field updates and a dedicated PostOpenMigration to convert existing keyword-encoded special values.

What changed
- Added migration: SpecialFieldsToSeparateFields
  - Scans keyword values on database load and moves known special keywords into the corresponding special fields, then removes those keywords from the keywords field.
  - The migration uses a mapping for known values: printed -> PRINTED; prio1/prio2/prio3 -> PRIORITY; qualityAssured -> QUALITY; rank1..rank5 -> RANKING; read/skimmed -> READ_STATUS; relevant -> RELEVANCE.
- Replaced usages of the deprecated SpecialFieldsUtils.updateField/sync methods with org.jabref.logic.util.UpdateField.updateField and Optional-based handling in:
  - SpecialFieldAction
  - SpecialFieldViewModel
  - ManageKeywordsViewModel
- On database open (OpenDatabase), the post-open migrations now include SpecialFieldsToSeparateFields (and the keyword delimiter is passed to the migration constructor).
- Removed the SpecialFieldsUtils class and its unit tests (SpecialFieldsUtilsTest).
- Added unit tests for the new migration: SpecialFieldsToSeparateFieldsTest
- CHANGELOG: added note about the migration of JabRef-specific meta-data from keywords to dedicated fields (issue #6840).

Impact / Migration notes
- Existing projects that encoded special values inside the keywords field will have those values migrated to dedicated special fields the next time the database is opened in this version.
- Keyword synchronization behavior has been removed from the old SpecialFieldsUtils. Field updates now use UpdateField to produce single FieldChange results; special->keyword sync is no longer performed automatically during normal field updates.
- Tests and internal code were updated to reflect the new migration-driven approach.

Related issue
- Closes/addresses #6840 (migration of JabRef-specific metadata from keywords to separate fields).

Add JSTOR fetcher and ID-based lookup support

- Register new JstorFetcher in WebFetchers.getIdBasedFetchers.
- Implement JstorFetcher:
  - New class implements SearchBasedParserFetcher, FulltextFetcher and IdBasedParserFetcher.
  - getUrlForIdentifier(String) builds citation/text URLs for JSTOR identifiers: accepts numeric stable IDs and full JSTOR/stable URLs (strips query strings) and handles DOIs by detecting "/" in the identifier; numeric IDs are prefixed with the 10.2307 namespace.
  - Parser reads input as UTF-8 and detects whether the response is raw BibTeX (starts with "@") or HTML. For HTML responses it extracts "cite-this-item" elements, downloads citation text from JSTOR's citation endpoint, concatenates results and parses them as BibTeX.
  - Updated CITE_HOST constant and added URL_QUERY_REGEX to strip query parts.
  - Added no-op doPostCleanup implementation.
  - findFullText signature simplified (removed FetcherException) and behavior unchanged.
- Tests updated (JstorFetcherTest):
  - Added a DOI-backed expected entry and a new searchById test that verifies lookup by numeric stable ID and full JSTOR URL with query string.

This enables fetching entries from JSTOR by search and by identifier/URL/DOI and improves parsing of JSTOR responses that may return either BibTeX or HTML citation links.

text:
Fix arXiv fetcher failing by removing custom CookieHandler

Background
- The arXiv fetcher could fail to retrieve content in some cases. Investigation suggested our custom CookieHandler implementation interfered with HTTP connections to arXiv (it was registered as the system default and thus invoked for every connection).

What this PR does
- Remove the custom CookieHandler implementation (CookieHandlerImpl.java) entirely.
- Remove the call that tried to set that CookieHandler from URLDownload.
- Minor whitespace/formatting cleanup in ArXiv.java (no behavioural changes there).

Rationale
- URLDownload and the platform's default cookie handling are sufficient; we don’t need our own CookieHandler implementation.
- Removing the custom handler prevents it from being invoked for all HTTP connections, which resolves the arXiv fetcher issue.

Result
- All unit tests and manual checks (including arXiv ID lookups and full-text retrieval) work again.

Notes
- Related issue: #1776
- The exact reason why the custom handler broke arXiv requests is unknown; but removing it fixes the problem and avoids registering a custom global CookieHandler that affects all connections.

text:
Refactor and harden MainTable rendering, selection and sorting behavior

This patch modernizes and cleans up MainTable.java and improves robustness, rendering and sorting behavior:

- Use Optional for safe access to table entries (getBibEntry) and avoid IndexOutOfBounds/NPEs.
- Introduce CellRendererMode enum and centralize cell-status logic (required/optional/resolved/other) in getCellStatus.
- Improve cell rendering logic: clearer handling of grayed-out states, marked entries, completion/incompletion and resolved fields.
- Move renderer initialization into a static updateRenderers() method and add mixColors helper for consistent color blending.
- Make renderers configurable from preferences (colors, marked levels) and update marked/number renderers accordingly.
- Enhance tooltip behavior to show full cell content when it is truncated in the cell.
- Improve selection and keyboard navigation: override column/row selection actions to move between entries (Tab/Shift-Tab, selectNextRow/selectPreviousRow) and add key bindings for selectFirst/selectLast.
- Wire up DnD transfer handlers consistently for both table and scroll pane; add a setUI override to avoid a NPE workaround regression when changing UI.
- Rework comparator/sorting setup: use TableComparatorChooser with SortedList, add comparators for first column, ranking and icon columns, and persist primary/secondary/tertiary sort fields + directions to preferences when the user changes sort order.
- Add helpful utility methods: isFileColumn, getSelectedEntries, getSortingColumn, getMainTableColumn and others to encapsulate common queries.
- Minor scrolling/visibility improvements: scrollTo, scrollToCenter and ensureVisible behave more predictably.

Overall this change reduces NPE risk, centralizes renderer/state logic, improves keyboard and DnD behavior, and ensures sort state and column widths are handled and persisted more robustly.

text:
Add Content Selector management and suggestion support

This PR implements the view-model logic for the Content Selector dialog and adds tests for the content selector suggestion provider and the dialog view model.

Key changes
- Implement ContentSelectorDialogViewModel to manage content-selector fields and their keywords:
  - Load existing content selectors from MetaData and populate the UI lists
  - Provide adding/removing of field names and keywords (with duplicate checks and confirmation dialogs)
  - Keep keyword lists sorted alphabetically
  - Persist changes back to MetaData and update the LibraryTab (setupMainPanel + markNonUndoableBaseChanged)
  - Fall back to a set of default fields when no selectors exist (author, journal, keywords, publisher)
- Implement logic to compare/update keywords correctly (set-based comparison) to avoid unnecessary writes

Tests
- Add ContentSelectorSuggestionProviderTest to validate suggestion merging and ordering (includes database-sourced suggestions and provided lists; case-insensitive start matching; alphabetical ordering of results)
- Add ContentSelectorDialogViewModelTest to validate: default initial fields, adding/removing fields and keywords, uniqueness checks, alphabetical keyword display, and persistence to the BibDatabaseContext MetaData

Behavioral notes
- Duplicate fields/keywords show appropriate error dialogs (via DialogService) and are not added
- Removing fields or keywords prompts for confirmation
- Saving writes only changed/added selectors and clears removed selectors from MetaData

This change enables users to manage content selectors (fields + keyword lists) in the UI and ensures suggestions are merged and ordered consistently. Tests cover the core behaviors and edge cases.

text:
Make main table sorting persistent and persist sort types

- Implement persistent column sort order and sort types in the main table (Fixes #5730).
- User-visible: the order of sorted columns and each column's sort direction are now saved and restored across restarts.

What changed (high level):
- ColumnPreferences now stores an ordered list of MainTableColumnModel representing the column sort order instead of a map of column names -> SortType. DEFAULT_WIDTH was renamed to DEFAULT_COLUMN_WIDTH.
- MainTable now restores the saved sort order on startup by mapping stored column models to the actual TableColumn instances and re-populating getSortOrder(). It also clears existing sort order before applying preferences.
- MainTableColumn and MainTableColumnModel now expose and persist a sortType property (TableColumn.SortType) and bind the column's sortType property bidirectionally to the model so changes are tracked.
- Icon columns get a default ICON_COLUMN_WIDTH; MainTableColumnModel selects default widths accordingly and initializes default sort type to ASCENDING.
- PersistenceVisualStateTable listens to column model width and sortType changes and stores both column widths, sort types and the sort order via JabRefPreferences.
- Preferences API updates in JabRefPreferences:
  - New preference keys: COLUMN_SORT_TYPES and COLUMN_SORT_ORDER (replacing the old column-in-sort-order map approach).
  - createMainTableColumns now reads persisted sort types; getColumnPreferences and storeColumnPreferences handle the new sort type and sort order data.
  - Added MainTablePreferences (stores column preferences, resize mode and extra-file-columns flag) and corresponding storeMainTablePreferences/getMainTablePreferences.
- TableColumnsTabViewModel adapts to use MainTablePreferences and stores the extra-file-columns setting in the new MainTablePreferences object.

Migrations and tests:
- PreferencesMigrations was updated to migrate old preferences and emit default ASCENDING sort types for migrated columns.
- Tests updated to expect COLUMN_SORT_TYPES to be written during migration.

Other notes:
- The extra file columns flag was moved out of ColumnPreferences into MainTablePreferences.
- Various small refactors and renames (e.g., resizeColumnsToFit -> getResizeColumnsToFit) to reflect the new preference shapes.

This change ensures that table sorting configuration is fully persisted (which columns are used for sorting, in which order, and each column's direction) and properly migrated from older preference formats.

- Prevent crashes or unexpected behavior when panels are opened and closed rapidly or when databases are changed externally.
- Improve maintainability of BasePanel by consolidating lifecycle cleanup in one place.

- Manual verification of opening/closing libraries, switching between libraries, selecting entries and deleting entries. No regressions observed in these scenarios.

This change updates build.gradle (run task) to add several --add-opens JVM options so the com.jfoenix dependency can access internal JavaFX packages without causing IllegalAccessExceptions when running JabRef on Java 9+. Fixes #3376 — Treat CrossRef titles as optional

Summary:
- Prevent a NullPointerException / error when fetching entries from CrossRef that do not contain a title array.

What I changed:
- In CrossRef.jsonItemToBibEntry(), the title field is read defensively: if the title JSONArray is missing, the entry title is set to an empty string instead of calling getJSONArray(...) which caused an error. The subtitle handling already used the same safe approach.
- Added a changelog entry noting the fix.

Why:
- Some CrossRef records do not provide a title array. The previous implementation assumed the array existed and threw an error for such records. Making title optional avoids the exception and allows those entries to be imported (with an empty title).

Testing:
- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance.
- No unit tests were added in this change.

Notes:
- This PR updates CHANGELOG.md and the CrossRef fetcher implementation. Tests should be added in a follow-up to cover missing title cases.

Summary
- Add telemetry source tracking for user actions (distinguish whether an action was triggered from a button or a menu).
- Improve action naming used in telemetry for legacy wrapper commands and edit actions by using command.toString() when appropriate.

- Improved action name detection: if the command is an OldDatabaseCommandWrapper, OldCommandWrapper, or contains "EditAction" in its name, JabRefAction now uses command.toString() as the action name.
- Added toString() overrides to OldCommandWrapper, OldDatabaseCommandWrapper and the EditAction inner class in JabRefFrame to ensure meaningful names are available.

Files touched
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/actions/Sources.java (new)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/actions/JabRefAction.java (add source-aware constructor, action naming improvements, telemetry with properties)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/actions/OldCommandWrapper.java (toString override)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/actions/OldDatabaseCommandWrapper.java (toString override)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/actions/ActionFactory.java (pass Sources when creating/configuring actions)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/JabRefFrame.java (EditAction.toString override)

Rationale
- Distinguishing the UI origin (button vs menu) of an action in telemetry enables better usage analytics and helps prioritize UI improvements.
- Using command.toString() for wrapped/legacy commands and edit actions ensures telemetry shows readable, accurate action names instead of anonymous/opaque class names.

- No change to command execution or UI behavior; changes only affect telemetry reporting and action naming for analytics.
- Telemetry is still optional and only recorded when Globals.getTelemetryClient() is present.

Testing notes
- Verify telemetry events include the Source property when triggering actions from buttons and menus.
- Verify existing telemetry (when source not provided) remains unchanged.
- Confirm no regressions in action enabling/disabling or event handling.

text:
Improve DOI parsing, normalization and fetching

This PR makes several fixes and enhancements around DOI handling and DOI-based fetching:

- Robust DOI parsing and normalization (src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/identifier/DOI.java)
  - Accepts many DOI/short-DOI forms including URN, doi: prefix, doi.org URLs and common vendor domains (dx.doi.org, doi.acm.org, etc.).
  - Strips leading/trailing whitespace and removes non-ASCII characters before parsing.
  - Supports short DOIs (doi.org/<short>) and shortcut forms (doi.org/abcd) by normalizing to the internal 10/xxx form.
  - Correctly encodes/decodes problematic characters when constructing resolver URIs (%, \" , #, space, ?, etc.).
  - Provides helpers to get resolver URIs and to respect a custom base URI.

- DOI fetcher improvements (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/DoiFetcher.java)
  - Detects the DOI registration agency via the DOI agency resolver and delegates to the Medra fetcher if the agency is mEDRA (mEDRA returns non-parsable BibTeX).
  - Performs post-processing cleanup of fetched BibTeX entries (normalize pages, clear URL field where appropriate).
  - Adds APS-journal detection and, if appropriate, sets the article id into the pages field when page numbers are missing.
  - Improves error handling around network/parse/JSON errors.

- Localization and preferences (src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties)
  - Added strings for "Copy DOI url" and "Custom DOI URI" / "Use custom DOI base URI for article access" to support UI for copying DOI URLs and custom DOI resolver base.

- Tests (src/test/java/org/jabref/model/entry/identifier/DOITest.java)
  - Adds a large suite of parameterized unit tests covering the many DOI and short-DOI formats, encoding/decoding, whitespace and non-ASCII cleaning, and findInText behavior.

- Changelog (CHANGELOG.md)
  - Adds notes about DOI-related improvements (trimming whitespace and non-ASCII characters, copy DOI option, etc.) under Unreleased.

Why

These changes fix numerous real-world failures when users paste or import DOIs from varied sources (URLs, URNs, messy text, vendor-specific DOI hosts). They also improve reliability when fetching metadata from DOIs (including handling of special mEDRA cases and APS article IDs).

Files changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/identifier/DOI.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/DoiFetcher.java
- src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties
- src/test/java/org/jabref/model/entry/identifier/DOITest.java
- CHANGELOG.md

Notes for reviewers

- Pay attention to the regular expressions and the CHARS_TO_REMOVE cleaning pattern for potential edge cases.
- The new DOI.AGENCY_RESOLVER usage and JSON parsing in DoiFetcher.getAgency() should be reviewed for correctness and robustness against different agency responses.
- The DOITest suite contains comprehensive examples — it is a good reference for expected parsing behavior.

Summary

This PR improves the autosave/backup flow and search-query highlighting by wiring model change notifications into the autosave and UI notification systems, and updates model classes to provide reliable modification tracking. It also updates the changelog.

What I changed

- AutosaveManager.java
  - Refactored autosave logic to react to model change events instead of polling raw state. Autosave now listens for modification notifications and triggers backups/saves more reliably and consistently.
  - Improved lifecycle handling to avoid duplicate tasks and to ensure proper shutdown.

- SearchQueryHighlightObservable.java
  - Added/updated observable implementation for search query highlighting so UI components can subscribe to highlight changes and update in response to model events.
  - Centralized the highlight change publishing to reduce duplicated code and make the behavior predictable.

- BibDatabase.java, BibEntry.java, MetaData.java
  - Exposed or refined change/modified tracking and notification hooks used by the AutosaveManager and the search highlight observable. These changes make modification state propagation more reliable across the model.
  - Small API refinements to make it easier for listeners to subscribe to relevant model changes (entry edits, metadata updates, and database-level modifications).

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Documented the changes and noted improvements to autosave and search highlighting behavior.

Why this is needed

- Autosave previously could miss some modification events or run into duplicated background tasks; by wiring model change notifications directly into the AutosaveManager we get timely and reliable backups with fewer edge cases.
- Search highlighting behavior is now driven by a single observable source, which reduces bugs where UI components got out of sync with the model.
- Making modification tracking explicit in model classes improves overall robustness and makes it easier for future features to react to changes.

Testing

- Manual testing of editing entries and metadata to confirm autosave and backup behavior triggers as expected.
- Verified search result highlighting updates correctly when queries change and when entries are edited.

Compatibility and Migration

- Public APIs were kept stable where possible; changes are mostly additions/refactors to allow observers to subscribe to modification events. No user-facing settings were removed.

Notes

If you maintain any custom code that listened to lower-level database state, prefer subscribing to the new/updated modification events on BibDatabase, BibEntry, or MetaData to receive consistent notifications.
