This PR improves validation and file handling for groups, especially for TeX-based (TexGroup) configurations, and tightens several group-related validators.

Changes:
- Add robust validation for TexGroup file path:
  - Resolves relative paths against the library's LaTeX file directory.
  - Ensures the provided path is absolute, points to an existing regular file and that the extension is .aux.
  - Validation errors are shown via the dialog service and the dialog close event is consumed when validation fails.
- Improve file-browse behavior for TexGroup:
  - The file chooser now relativizes the selected file against known LaTeX file directories (using FileUtil.relativize) so stored paths are relative where possible.
- Add/enable validators for keyword and free-search groups:
  - Validate empty search terms and invalid regular expressions for both keyword and free-search group types.
  - Validators are dynamically added/removed when the corresponding group type is selected.
- Miscellaneous:
  - Expose validation status getters for the various validators so the UI can react to validation state.
  - Catch and report exceptions during group creation (resultConverter) to the user via the dialog service.

Why:
- Prevents invalid TexGroup configurations (missing or wrong file types) and provides clearer feedback to users.
- Ensures file paths are stored in a consistent (relative) way when appropriate.
- Provides stricter input validation for keyword/search groups to avoid runtime errors and improve UX.

Fix online link detection in entry editor

Fixes #8510

What changed
- Reworked LinkedFile.isOnlineLink to use a compiled URL regex (URL_PATTERN) instead of simple startsWith/contains checks. This prevents false positives when strings like "www" appear inside local file paths (e.g. "/home/www.google.de.pdf") and avoids the exception in the entry editor.
- Added unit tests in FileFieldParserTest to cover edge cases: paths containing "www" in filenames, URLs with and without "www", and URL entries with descriptions.
- Small Javadoc cleanup in SearchBasedParserFetcher to fix incorrect {@link ...} formatting.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to document the fix.

Why
- The previous implementation treated any path containing "www." as an online link, which incorrectly flagged local files that included "www" in their names and could lead to exceptions. Using a proper URL pattern provides robust detection of online links (http/https/www at the beginning) while leaving local file paths untouched.

Files changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/LinkedFile.java: introduce URL regex and use it in isOnlineLink
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/util/FileFieldParserTest.java: add test cases for the fixed behavior
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/SearchBasedParserFetcher.java: minor javadoc fix
- CHANGELOG.md: add entry describing the fix

Tests
- New/updated unit tests verify correct detection of online links and that filenames containing "www" are not misdetected as URLs.

Add PdfEmbeddedBibFileImporter and XMP loading helper

- Introduces PdfEmbeddedBibFileImporter: a new Importer that extracts embedded .bib files from PDF documents and parses them into BibEntry objects.
  - Scans both the document-level embedded files name tree and page annotations (file attachments).
  - Filters embedded files by .bib extension and picks the first available platform-specific embedded file variant (Unicode/DOS/Mac/Unix/fallback).
  - Parses embedded BibTeX content using the existing BibtexParser and returns a ParserResult.
  - importDatabase(Path, Charset) is implemented; importDatabase(BufferedReader) and importDatabase(String) explicitly throw UnsupportedOperationException to direct callers to the Path-based API.
  - Handles encrypted PDFs via XmpUtilReader.loadWithAutomaticDecryption and returns a localized error message when decryption is unsupported. IO and parse exceptions are propagated as ParserResult errors.

- XmpUtilReader: expose loadWithAutomaticDecryption(Path)
  - Adds/uses a public static loadWithAutomaticDecryption(Path) helper that opens a PDDocument (using PDFBox) and is reused by the new importer and existing XMP-reading code.
  - Keeps existing XMP parsing utilities (readXmp/readRawXmp/getXmpMetadata) intact.

Notes
- Adds the ability to import embedded .bib files from PDFs (document names and attachment annotations) without changing existing import flows.
- Error handling ensures encrypted PDFs and parsing/IO errors are surfaced as ParserResult errors with proper messages.
- No unit tests included in this change; relies on existing BibtexParser and PDFBox APIs.

Prevent citing entries without BibTeX keys from OpenOffice/LibreOffice

- Problem: Pushing citations from JabRef to OpenOffice/LibreOffice could attempt to cite entries that do not have BibTeX keys.
- Fix: Before pushing entries, JabRef now checks that all selected entries have non-empty cite keys. If any entry lacks a key the user is prompted to generate keys. If the user agrees, keys are generated using the current label pattern and the changes are recorded as a single undoable action.

  - pushEntries(...) now aborts if entries lack keys and the user declines generating them.
- Localization: Added the prompt key Cannot_cite_entries_without_BibTeX_keys._Generate_keys_now? to multiple JabRef_*.properties files (en, de, fr, es, it, ja, ru, sv, tr, zh, etc.).
- CHANGELOG.md: Added entry referencing issue #1682.

Related issue: Fixes #1682. Changes have been manually tested in a running JabRef.

- Bug: both pseudo-class constants (CLASS_NO_RESULTS and CLASS_RESULTS_FOUND) used the same pseudo-class name "emptyResult", so the search field could not be styled differently for the "no results" and "results found" states.

text:
Add APS (American Physical Society) fulltext fetcher

This PR introduces a new FulltextFetcher for APS journals (ApsFetcher) and integrates it into the list of available fulltext fetchers.

What changed
- Added ApsFetcher implementation (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ApsFetcher.java)
  - Uses the entry DOI to resolve the APS article id by following DOI.org redirects (to preserve APS-specific case-sensitivity)
  - Constructs the APS PDF URL (https://journals.aps.org/prl/pdf/{id}) and checks availability with an HTTP HEAD request (Unirest)
  - Returns a URL for the PDF when available; otherwise returns empty
  - Trust level is set to PUBLISHER
- Registered ApsFetcher in WebFetchers so it is used when searching for fulltext (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/WebFetchers.java)
- Added unit tests for the fetcher (src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ApsFetcherTest.java)
  - Tests cover DOI with original case, lowercase DOI (ensures redirect/casing handling), and cases where PDF is not available
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to mention the new APS fetcher

Motivation
- Implements support for retrieving PDFs from the American Physical Society journals using DOIs. This closes gaps reported in #818 and is part of work tracked in #2581. Follow-up from #6026.

Notes
- The implementation uses a DOI.org redirect workaround because the APS Harvest API requires an API key/header; this approach aims to derive the exact APS id and check the journal PDF URL.
- Tests are included to validate the main behaviors; network interactions are exercised as part of the tests.

Checklist
- [x] CHANGELOG updated
- [x] Tests added
- [x] Manually tested in running JabRef

Fixes: #818
Part of: #2581

text:
Summary

This WIP refactors the app's save logic to address the issues raised in #4173: after removing the status bar, save errors are currently swallowed and users don't get clear feedback. The goal of this change is to centralize save/error handling and ensure save failures are reliably surfaced to the user.

What this PR changes

- Introduces a centralized SaveController that owns save flow and error propagation (replaces scattered save handlers).
- Adds user-facing error reporting for save failures (notification/toast-based) so problems are not swallowed.
- Ensures save lifecycle events (start, success, failure) are emitted and can be observed by UI components.
- Improves handling of common failure modes: network errors, conflicts, permission errors.
- Adds unit tests around the new save logic and basic integration tests for error reporting.

Why

With the status bar removed we lost an important visible channel for reporting save problems. This refactor ensures save failures are surfaced consistently via notifications and through a single save controller, so callers can react appropriately and users are informed.

How to test

1. Open the app and edit a document.
2. Trigger a save and verify normal success path still works (no regression).
3. Simulate a network error (offline or mocked) and verify a clear notification is shown describing the failure and offering retry.
4. Simulate a conflict or permission error and verify appropriate error messaging is shown.
5. Confirm that no save errors are silently swallowed (check logs & UI).

Notes / TODO (WIP)

- UI/UX for notifications needs polishing (copy & styling).
- Add end-to-end tests to cover autosave and background save edge cases.
- Review and harden any remaining code paths that directly manipulate persistence without going through the new SaveController.

Related

Fixes/addresses: #4173

Please review the SaveController interface and the new error reporting integrations. Feedback welcome before I finalize the UI polish and add e2e tests.

Summary: Work in progress to switch citeproc’s JavaScript runtime to V8. This PR introduces an embedded V8 integration to execute citeproc-js, replacing the previous JS engine/approach. The goal is more consistent, faster, and better-isolated execution of citeproc templates.

What changed:
- Added V8 integration and minimal runtime wrapper to evaluate citeproc-js code.
- Hooked citeproc invocation points to the new V8 wrapper.
- Adjusted build configuration and dependencies to include the V8 binding crate.
- Basic glue code for data marshalling between Rust and V8 (JSON in/out).

Current status / WIP notes:
- Core integration is present but not fully polished.
- Some tests are failing; further work needed on error handling and memory lifecycle management.
- CI configuration for building the native V8 dependency is not complete.

How to test:
- Run the existing citeproc tests locally (expect some failures at this stage).
- Manual smoke test: run the citeproc command/path that invokes bibliography generation and verify output.

Next steps:
- Fix failing tests and harden error handling around the V8 context lifetime.
- Improve marshalling for complex data types and reduce JSON roundtrips where possible.
- Add CI support for building/running with the V8 native dependency.
- Add benchmarks to compare performance with previous runtime.

Request for reviewers:
- Please review the integration approach and the safety/ownership around the V8 context.
- Feedback on build/CI implications and any platform concerns would be appreciated.

Notes: This is labeled WIP while the integration and tests are completed. No public API changes are intended other than the runtime implementation; keep that in mind when reviewing.

text:
Implemented .jstyle file filter and remember last-opened style directory

Summary of changes:
- Add support for filtering ".jstyle" files in the OpenOffice/LibreOffice style selection dialog (feature request #1294).
- Style selection dialog now opens in the directory of the last selected style and stores that path in preferences when a style is added.
- BrowseAction extended to accept an optional file-extension filter (used to pass ".jstyle" for the Add Style dialog).
- FileDialogs updated to treat an empty extension string as "no filter" (replaces previous use of Globals.NONE). Globals.NONE was removed.
- Fixed a NullPointerException when an invalid jstyle was selected: StyleLoader now validates styles before adding or restoring them from preferences; invalid styles are logged and no longer prevent the dialog from opening.
- Small UI and code cleanups (popup alignment, spacing, and improved error logging).

Notable files changed: CHANGELOG.md, Globals.java, FileDialogs.java, BrowseAction.java, StyleSelectDialog.java, StyleLoader.java, AddFileDialog integration, and a couple of file-list/entry editor callers to use the new behavior.

User-visible behavior:
- When adding/selecting styles, the file chooser starts in the last style folder used and filters for .jstyle files when appropriate.
- Bad/invalid style files no longer cause NPEs; they are rejected and an error is logged.

Changelog updated to reflect the new feature and the bugfix.

Re-add backwards compatibility for legacy LayoutFormatter names (including FormatChars)

Summary
- Restores support for old/renamed layout formatter identifiers (e.g. FormatChars) by mapping legacy names to the current formatter implementations.
- Replaces the previous reflection-based instantiation of LayoutFormatters with an explicit name->formatter switch in LayoutEntry#getLayoutFormatterByName.
- Adjusts getOptionalLayout to be an instance method and updates callers accordingly.
- Minor refactors and cleanup in LayoutEntry (imports, local variable scoping, removed obsolete code comments).
- Removes two unused constants: FILETYPE_PREFS_EXT (Globals) and PE_HEIGHT (GUIGlobals).

Why
- Users and custom exports referencing legacy formatter names (per older docs and exported layouts) broke when classes were renamed/moved. This change restores compatibility by recognizing legacy names and returning the appropriate formatter instances.
- The explicit mapping avoids fragile reflection and gives more control over name aliases and location changes.

Behavioral notes
- The switch maps many legacy names to current implementations, e.g.:
  - "FormatChars", "LatexToUnicode" -> LatexToUnicodeFormatter
  - "HTMLToLatexFormatter", "HtmlToLatex" -> HtmlToLatexFormatter
  - "UnicodeToLatexFormatter", "UnicodeToLatex" -> UnicodeToLatexFormatter
  - "JournalAbbreviator" -> JournalAbbreviator(repository)
  - And many Author* and other legacy formatter names -> corresponding current classes
- Unknown formatter names now return a NotFoundFormatter(name) (preserving existing behavior for missing formatters).

Notes / TODO
- This is an alternative approach to #1114 (uses a big switch instead of reflection).
- Tests were not added in this change. Coverage for legacy name mappings should be added.
- CHANGELOG entry should be added describing the regained backwards compatibility.
- The repository contains deprecated Author* formatters (per docs); consider removing them in a future cleanup once downstream users have migrated.

Files changed (high level)
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/logic/layout/LayoutEntry.java: added mapping logic, refactored getOptionalLayout and formatter instantiation
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/Globals.java: removed unused FILETYPE_PREFS_EXT constant
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/GUIGlobals.java: removed unused PE_HEIGHT constant

Checklist
- [ ] Add CHANGELOG.md entry
- [ ] Add tests for legacy formatter name mappings
- [ ] Decide on removal of deprecated Author* formatters in a follow-up

Remove automatic Unicode conversion for the bibtex key field (both internal storage and display in the main table), as suggested by @koppor in #2671. Keys are now preserved exactly as entered rather than being normalized/converted to ASCII.

What I changed:
- Removed any Unicode-to-ASCII conversion logic that ran when reading/saving the "key" field.
- Removed Unicode conversion in the main table cell renderer so the bibtex key is shown unchanged.

Why:
- Users expect their BibTeX keys to be preserved, including non-ASCII characters. Normalizing or converting keys silently can be surprising and may break reproducibility or user workflows.

Summary: Add support for exporting a single corporate author to MS Office XML. Previously a lone corporate author could be omitted or exported using person-specific fields; this change ensures the corporate name is serialized into the appropriate Office XML author element.

What I changed:
- Detect a single contributor with type corporate and treat it as an organization rather than trying to split into given/family names
- Serialize the corporate name into the MS Office XML author metadata element so Word/Office consumers receive the organization as author
- Preserve existing behavior for person authors and for multiple contributors

Tests: Added unit tests that verify a single corporate author is present in the generated Office XML and that formatting contains no stray commas or empty name parts. Also added an integration test that ensures Office consumers receive the correct author metadata.

Compatibility: Backwards compatible for existing exports of person authors. Empty corporate names are ignored to avoid invalid XML metadata.

Notes: This fixes reported issues where corporate authors were missing or malformed in exported .docx/.xml files.

text:
Introduce TaskExecutor.runInFXThread and synchronous test executor; refactor async execution for testability

This PR makes it easier to write deterministic tests for code that interacts with the JavaFX thread by introducing a small abstraction and a synchronous test implementation, plus some related refactorings and cleanups.

Key changes

- Add runInFXThread to TaskExecutor (interface): documents expected behavior and provides a way to run Runnables on the FX thread or the current thread depending on the executor implementation.

- Add CurrentThreadTaskExecutor: a TaskExecutor implementation that executes tasks synchronously on the current thread (including runInFXThread). This is intended for tests to avoid asynchronous scheduling and make behavior deterministic.
  - execute(BackgroundTask) now runs the task synchronously, calls the onRunning/onSuccess/onException callbacks as appropriate and returns a completed or failed Future.
  - schedule(...) delegates to execute(...) since delay is irrelevant in the synchronous executor.
  - runInFXThread runs the runnable immediately (on the current thread) for tests.

- Update DefaultTaskExecutor: implements the new runInFXThread method by delegating to static helper DefaultTaskExecutor.runInJavaFXThread(Runnable). Also provides runAndWaitInJavaFXThread/ runInJavaFXThread helpers to run code on the JavaFX thread (blocking or non-blocking) and includes proper error logging.
  - DefaultTaskExecutor still executes BackgroundTask and Task instances on real background threads and schedules delayed tasks via ScheduledExecutorService.
  - StateManager is injected into DefaultTaskExecutor (used to manage background tasks shown to the user).

- Use the new synchronous executor in tests: DBMSSynchronizerTest and SynchronizationTestSimulator (and their helper code) instantiate DBMSSynchronizer with CurrentThreadTaskExecutor to make database synchronization tests deterministic.

Other notes and small fixes

- GroupNodeViewModel and other classes work with the TaskExecutor abstraction and use DefaultTaskExecutor.runInJavaFXThread where necessary to ensure UI updates happen on the FX thread.
- UiThreadList ensures list change notifications are fired on the FX thread, waiting when called from a non-FX thread.
- Several DBMS/DBMSSynchronizer changes remain functionally identical but benefit from the improved testability.

Why

Previously many components directly used Platform.runLater or DefaultTaskExecutor static helpers. That made tests depending on FX thread scheduling flaky or required awkward workarounds. By moving the responsibility to TaskExecutor and providing a CurrentThreadTaskExecutor, tests can run synchronously without a JavaFX runtime and produce deterministic results. The DefaultTaskExecutor still provides correct behavior for production.

Impact

- No functional behavior change for production code using DefaultTaskExecutor.
- Tests that use CurrentThreadTaskExecutor become deterministic. The DBMS synchronization tests have been updated accordingly.
- New API method TaskExecutor.runInFXThread allows future code to use the executor for FX-thread execution and remain testable.

Support two-argument biblatex citation macros in AUX parser

Summary
- Update DefaultAuxParser to correctly recognize biblatex citation macros that provide an extra numeric argument (e.g. \abx@aux@cite{0}{KEY}). The regex for citation matching now accepts an optional numeric brace pair before the citation key.

Why
- Some LaTeX/biblatex toolchains write citation macros with two argument forms. Previously these lines were not parsed correctly which could lead to missed citation keys and unresolved entries when generating a minimal BibDatabase from an .aux file.

What changed
- DefaultAuxParser: expanded the CITE_PATTERN to allow an optional numeric argument before the key so both single-argument and two-argument citation macros are supported.
- Tests: added a unit test (testTwoArgMacro) and resource papertwoargmacro.aux to ensure the behavior matches the existing single-argument case (same resolved entries and counts).

Notes
- No change to behavior for standard single-argument citation macros. The new pattern is backwards-compatible and prevents false negatives when parsing .aux files produced by biblatex variants.

Summary

This PR introduces configurable behavior for keyword-based groups, updates the Groups preferences UI, fixes an issue in the IEEE Xplore fetcher, and updates the changelog.

What changed

- Preferences
  - Added new preference keys to JabRefPreferences to control keyword group matching behavior (exposed options include regex matching, case sensitivity, and word-delimiter handling).

- Keyword group behavior
  - KeywordGroup has been updated to honor the new preferences when matching entries. Matching logic is more flexible and respects the configured options for regex vs. literal matching, case sensitivity and delimiter handling.

- Preferences UI
  - GroupsPrefsTab now exposes the new keyword-group settings to the user, with appropriate labels/tooltips so users can configure group-matching behavior from the GUI.

- IEEE Xplore fetcher
  - IEEEXploreFetcher received a reliability fix related to query handling and result parsing (improves encoding/response parsing robustness when fetching records).

- Changelog
  - CHANGELOG.md updated to document these changes.

Why this is useful

These changes let users fine-tune how keyword groups select entries (for example enabling regex or enforcing case sensitivity), making group creation and automatic membership more accurate and predictable. The fix to the IEEE Xplore fetcher improves import reliability from that source.

Notes

- Defaults are preserved for existing users; the preferences UI allows changing behavior going forward.
- No behavioral change to existing groups unless the new preferences are adjusted.

Fixes a bug in the ACM fetcher that caused entries to be imported incorrectly (some records were skipped or fields were missing).

- Corrected the entry extraction and field mapping logic so each ACM record is converted into a full import entry (title, authors, abstract, DOI/URL, publication date, and metadata).

- Improved duplicate detection/fallback behavior (prefer DOI, fall back to URL) so distinct records are not dropped.
- Added error handling and clearer logging around malformed records.
- Added/updated unit tests to cover the previously failing import scenarios.

Testing & Notes:
- Added tests that reproduce the original failure and verify the fix.
- Manually verified imports against a sample ACM query with pagination and missing DOI cases.
- No breaking API changes; behavior is backward-compatible but more robust.

WIP: Fix LaTeX field formatter

Summary
- Fixes several issues in the LaTeX field formatter that prevented correct rendering and produced incorrect output for common LaTeX inputs.

Problems addressed
- Incorrect escaping/handling of backslashes and special characters in field values leading to broken output.
- Formatter dropped or collapsed whitespace in some cases.
- Preview rendering would sometimes fail when value contained inline/display mode delimiters.
- Formatter did not gracefully handle null/empty values.

What this change does
- Properly preserves and escapes LaTeX source so the raw value is unchanged while the rendered output is correct.
- Distinguishes between inline and display modes and ensures delimiters are respected.
- Adds defensive checks for null/empty values to avoid runtime errors.
- Adds unit/integration tests covering typical LaTeX inputs and edge cases.

Testing
- Automated tests added for: simple expressions, backslash-heavy expressions, inline vs display mode, empty/null values.
- Manual test steps: create fields with LaTeX content (e.g. "x = \frac{a}{b}", "\\sum_{n=1}^\infty", inline $...$ and display $$...$$), verify preview and rendered output match expected visuals, and that the stored raw value is unchanged.

Remaining work / TODO
- Further input sanitization and performance tuning for very large LaTeX blobs.
- Finalize snapshot/spec updates and address any CI failures.

Notes for reviewers
- This is still WIP: review the escape/serialization logic and tests, and advise on any integration considerations with the app's math rendering engine.

Add Linux native desktop integration (src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/desktop/os/Linux.java).

This implements NativeDesktop for Linux and provides: openFile, openFileWithApplication, openFolderAndSelectFile, openConsole, detectProgramPath (stub), and getApplicationDirectory.

Key behaviors:
- openFile: tries java.awt.Desktop.open and falls back to xdg-open; if an ExternalFileType specifies an "open with" application, it starts that viewer via ProcessBuilder. Process output and errors are forwarded to the logger using StreamGobbler and executed on JabRefExecutorService.
- openFileWithApplication: uses the supplied application command (split on spaces) to launch the file; falls back to Desktop/xdg-open if no application is specified.
- openFolderAndSelectFile: inspects DESKTOP_SESSION and chooses the appropriate file manager command (nautilus, dolphin, caja, nemo) with --select when possible; defaults to xdg-open on the file's parent. Simple escaping for spaces is applied in selected commands.
- openConsole: resolves /etc/alternatives/x-terminal-emulator to detect the terminal emulator and launches it with the working directory set (supports gnome-terminal, xfce4-terminal, konsole), otherwise executes the resolved emulator in the target directory.
- detectProgramPath: currently a stub that returns the program name.
- getApplicationDirectory: returns /usr/lib/.

Additional notes:
- Uses @AllowedToUseAwt because Desktop integration requires AWT.
- Logging is done via slf4j; process streams are consumed to avoid blocking.
- There are pragmatic fallbacks (xdg-open, executing resolved terminal) and some simple string handling/escaping. Further improvements could refine command escaping and program path detection.

What I changed
- Added an Id-based search implementation for JSTOR by implementing IdBasedParserFetcher in JstorFetcher.
- Registered JstorFetcher as an IdBasedFetcher in WebFetchers so it is available for identifier lookups.
- Implemented getUrlForIdentifier to construct JSTOR citation/text URLs from different identifier forms (stable IDs, DOI-based URLs, and JSTOR links), stripping query parameters.
- Enhanced the parser in JstorFetcher to handle both plain BibTeX input and HTML pages: it now reads the input stream as text, checks whether it starts with '@' (BibTeX) and parses accordingly; otherwise it extracts citation links from the JSTOR HTML and downloads the corresponding BibTeX via the citation/text endpoint.
- Added a no-op doPostCleanup method required by the IdBasedParserFetcher interface.
- Minor method signature and import updates (buffered reader, charset handling, stream collection, URL regex handling).

Why
- This enables lookup-by-identifier for JSTOR resources (both numeric stable IDs and DOI-based entries), improving fulltext/meta retrieval when users provide an identifier or URL.

Tests
- Added tests in JstorFetcherTest to cover id-based search behavior: searching by numeric stable id and by a JSTOR URL containing a DOI and query string. Existing search and fulltext tests remain.

Notes
- This change addresses the feature request in #6627 (Add IdBasedSearchFetcher to jstor).
- No CHANGELOG update was included in this PR.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/JstorFetcher.java: implement IdBasedParserFetcher, add getUrlForIdentifier, improve parsing logic and imports.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/WebFetchers.java: register JstorFetcher in ID-based fetchers set.
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/JstorFetcherTest.java: add tests for identifier-based search (stable id and DOI URL).

Summary: Prevents initiating a file download when the file is already attached to the current record or form. This avoids duplicate attachments and unnecessary network activity.

What I changed:
- Added a check before triggering file download that verifies whether the file is already attached (by comparing file id, checksum, or filename + size depending on available metadata).
- If the file is already attached, the download is skipped and a user-friendly message is shown (or a no-op is performed in non-UI contexts).
- Centralized the duplicate-detection logic into a reusable helper/service to keep callers simple and consistent.

Why:
- Users were able to download/attach the same file multiple times, causing duplicate attachments and potential confusion.
- Preventing redundant downloads reduces wasted bandwidth and backend storage operations.

Behavior changes:
- Attempting to download a file that's already attached now results in no new attachment. In the UI, a toast/notice informs the user that the file is already attached.
- Existing flows that expect re-downloading to replace or update attachments are unaffected only if they explicitly bypass the duplicate check.

Testing:
- Added unit tests covering the duplicate-detection helper.
- Added integration tests that simulate attaching a file and attempting to download it again to confirm no duplicate attachment occurs.
- Manual test steps: attach a file to a record, click download for the same file — verify no duplicate and the user sees the notice.

Notes:
- The duplicate detection is conservative: it first checks unique file id where available, then falls back to checksum or filename+size to handle older uploads.
- If callers need to force a re-download/reattach, they can call the new helper with force=true.

No database migrations required.

Implement LinkedFileViewModel to provide comprehensive UI-backed operations for LinkedFile objects.

This change adds/updates the view-model responsible for managing linked files for an entry and wires it into dialogs, preferences and background tasks. Main capabilities:

- File validation: adds a FunctionBasedValidator to check whether a linked file exists (skips check for online links) and exposes fileExistsValidationStatus().
- Open and reveal: handles opening a linked file in the desktop and opening its containing folder, with appropriate error dialogs.
- Rename and move operations: supports renaming (including user prompt), moving to the default file directory, and combined move+rename. It performs conflict checks and asks the user to overwrite when necessary; errors are reported to the user.
- Delete: asks the user whether to remove the link or delete the file from disk, handles permission errors and logs failures.
- Download support for online links: download() and prepareDownloadTask() infer file type (from MIME type or URL), pick a unique filename, bind download progress to the view, and replace the online link with the downloaded local file on success. Download failures and existing-file conflicts are reported via dialogService.
- XMP metadata writing: writeXMPMetadata() runs XMP writing in a background task.
- UI state properties: download progress and ongoing flags, isAutomaticallyFound, canWriteXMPMetadata, and observable aggregation for view updates.
- Icon resolution: getTypeIcon() resolves an icon via ExternalFileTypes.
- Helper functions: methods for generating/truncating description+link strings, checking if generated file name/path match existing ones, and accepting/marking automatically found files.

Other notes:
- Uses LinkedFileHandler, TaskExecutor and BackgroundTask to avoid blocking the UI.
- Error handling: dialogService is used consistently to show errors; handleDownloadError centralizes download error reporting.

This adds the necessary application logic to manage linked files from the GUI, including online-to-local download flow and metadata writing, improving user feedback and preventing file conflicts.

- Add a generated DEVELOPERS list and plumbing to include it in the application Help/About pages.

  - Fetches members of the GitHub team (ID 727640) via the GitHub API and writes their names into a DEVELOPERS file.

Summary

This PR migrates the localization synchronization tasks from Jython to Python 3 and updates CI configs to ensure Python 3 is available. It also includes a small whitespace cleanup in the French localization file.

What I changed

- .travis.yml: added Python support (python: "3.6") so Travis provides Python 3 during builds.
- circle.yml: request Python 3.6.2 in the Circle CI machine configuration.
- localization.gradle:
  - Removed the Jython configuration/dependency and replaced JavaExec tasks with Exec tasks.
  - Added a new task localizationStatusVersion that verifies python3 is available and at least version 3.6 (throws a helpful error otherwise).
  - Updated localization tasks (localizationStatusWithMarkdown, localizationStatus, localizationStatusExtended, localizationUpdate, localizationUpdateExtended) to call python3 scripts/syncLang.py with appropriate arguments instead of launching Jython.
- src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_fr.properties: removed an extra blank line (minor whitespace cleanup).

Why

The project synchronization scripts are Python 3 compatible and Jython is no longer required. Switching to the system python3 runtime simplifies maintenance and avoids the need to bundle Jython. The version check ensures a minimum Python 3.6 runtime is present because the sync script requires it.

Notes for maintainers / testing

- Ensure python3 (>= 3.6) is installed on CI and developer machines. The new localizationStatusVersion task will fail early if Python 3.6+ is not found.
- Run the localization tasks to verify behavior: ./gradlew localizationStatus, ./gradlew localizationStatusWithMarkdown, ./gradlew localizationUpdate (they will invoke python3 scripts/syncLang.py).

Fixes

- Fixes #3414

Improve Linked Files preferences tab

Summary
- Rework the Linked Files preferences UI and view model: add validation, bindings and better integration with FilePreferences.
- Validate the Main file directory using a FunctionBasedValidator and show validation state with an icon decorator.
- Wire up autolink options (starts-with, exact, regex) and expose a regex help button that opens the help page.
- Ensure Browse opens a directory chooser and updates the preference.
- Use java.nio.Path (Path.of) for directory handling and existence checks.

Files changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/linkedfiles/LinkedFilesTab.fxml
  - Layout for Linked files preferences (file directory, autolink options, filename/directory pattern).
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/linkedfiles/LinkedFilesTab.java
  - New bindings between controls and LinkedFilesTabViewModel.
  - Configure help button, directory browse action and validation visualization (ControlsFxVisualizer + IconValidationDecorator).
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/linkedfiles/LinkedFilesTabViewModel.java
  - Added properties backing the UI, a FunctionBasedValidator for mainFileDirectoryProperty, and mainFileDirBrowse() to show a directory dialog.
  - Properly sets and stores FilePreferences and AutoLinkPreferences values.
  - Uses Path.of and Files.exists/isDirectory for validation.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/preferences/JabRefPreferences.java
  - Added/used MAIN_FILE_DIRECTORY preference constant and adjusted getFileLinkPreferences/getFilePreferences wiring (now persisting main file directory using the preferences key).

Behavior changes
- The Main file directory input is validated; invalid directories prompt an error dialog when saving preferences.
- The autolink regex input is disabled unless the regex option is selected.
- The Browse button opens a directory chooser initialized to the current main file directory.
- File name and directory pattern controls are bound to FilePreferences defaults and persisted on save.

Notes for reviewers
- Validation visualization is initialized via Platform.runLater to ensure controls are ready before visualization is attached.
- The view model still preserves the previous AutoLinkPreferences behavior while providing a clear mapping to the new UI controls.
- Pay attention to preference key MAIN_FILE_DIRECTORY usage (comment left in code: "REALLY HERE?"). This change centralizes the main file directory in the java.util.prefs store and keeps FilePreferences in sync via EasyBind listeners.

- Update Unreleased -> Changed: improved the preferences and descriptions in the "Linked files" preferences tab. [#8148]

Tests & validation
- Added unit tests that cover clearing of special fields when keywords are removed.
- Manually tested the feature in a running JabRef instance.

Other
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to describe the change.

Fixes #3432.

Summary

This WIP PR refactors the file save / lock handling logic to make lock creation and error handling clearer and to surface network-related filesystem errors.

What changed

- FileSaveSession.java
  - Added handling to check for an existing lock file before creating one. If a lock exists, we wait for it via FileBasedLock.waitForFileLock(file) and fail with SaveException.FILE_LOCKED if the wait times out.
  - After waiting (or if no lock existed) we explicitly call FileBasedLock.createLockFile(file) to acquire the lock.
  - Added a catch for FileSystemException to turn network/path resolution errors into a SaveException with message "The network path was not found." so these conditions are not silently swallowed.
  - Other IOExceptions while creating the lock are logged. (There is a TODO noting that proceeding without a valid lock may be unsafe, especially for the main library file.)
  - Added import for java.nio.file.FileSystemException.

- FileBasedLock.java
  - createLockFile(Path) behavior changed: it now returns true when the lock file was created successfully, and false when the lock file already existed. The javadoc was updated to reflect the corrected semantics.
  - The method no longer swallows IOExceptions during file creation; it writes the lock file and propagates IOException to the caller.
  - Keeps deleteOnExit() for the created lock file.

Rationale

- The goal is to make lock acquisition explicit and fail fast for filesystem/network problems that previously could be swallowed. Distinguishing FileSystemException allows a clearer error message for network path issues.
- Returning and throwing meaningful results/exceptions makes the calling code (FileSaveSession) able to react appropriately (wait, fail, or log) rather than silently continuing.

Notes / TODOs

- The code currently logs IOExceptions during lock creation and continues; this is questionable for the main library file. We should decide whether to abort saves if a lock cannot be created.
- This is a WIP; additional cleanup, tests, and integration with user feedback (status bar / dialogs) are still needed so errors are visible to users (see issue #4173).

Files changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/exporter/FileSaveSession.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/util/io/FileBasedLock.java

Related issue: #4173 (Save logic concerns and better error reporting)

Summary

This PR updates the IACR ePrint fetcher implementation, adds corresponding English localization strings, and includes unit tests to validate behavior.

What changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/IacrEprintFetcher.java
  - Improved robustness of the IacrEprintFetcher: fixed request/query handling and response parsing to avoid errors on malformed/empty responses.
  - Improved extraction of bibliographic fields (title, authors, year, eprint id/type, URL, etc.) and handling of missing fields.
  - Added proper handling for HTTP error or empty-result cases so the fetcher returns an empty result list instead of throwing.
  - Cleaned up URL/parameter encoding and defensive checks to prevent NPEs.

- src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties
  - Added/updated English localization keys used by the fetcher for user-facing messages and logging.

- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/IacrEprintFetcherTest.java
  - Added/updated unit tests to cover successful fetch, no-result, and error scenarios.
  - Tests verify correct parsing of returned entries and ensure graceful handling of empty or error responses.

Why

These changes make the IACR ePrint fetcher more reliable in face of API quirks and network issues, ensure correct field extraction for imported entries, and provide tests to prevent regressions.

Notes

- No breaking API changes are intended; behavior changes are limited to improved error handling and parsing.
- Tests provide coverage for typical success and failure modes to guard future changes.

Add HelpAction to open online help pages from the UI

- Introduces net.sf.jabref.gui.help.HelpAction, a MnemonicAwareAction that keeps a reference to a HelpFile and opens the corresponding page on help.jabref.org when activated.
- Builds the help URL from the application's language preference (JabRefPreferences.LANGUAGE) and falls back to English if the chosen language is not in the supported set (en, de, fr, in, ja).
- Provides convenience UI helpers:
  - getHelpButton(): returns a small icon-only JButton wired to the action
  - getHelpLabel(String): returns an underlined, blue, hand-cursor JLabel which opens the help page on click
- Uses JabRefDesktop.openBrowserShowPopup(...) to open the help page in the default browser.

Why
- Centralizes help-opening logic into a reusable action and improves access to documentation from different UI locations (buttons or inline labels).
- Honors user language preference and gracefully falls back to English when a localized help page is not available.

Testing / verification
- Verify that clicking the help button or help label opens the browser and navigates to the correct URL: https://help.jabref.org/{lang}/{page} or https://help.jabref.org/en/{page} if the language is unsupported.
- Test with different LANGUAGE preference values (supported and unsupported) to confirm correct behavior.

Notes

text:
Fix NullPointerException when fetching BibTeX from DOI (fixes #1455)

Summary
- Prevent NPEs and improve robustness when retrieving BibTeX data via DOI by using Optional instead of nullable returns and by validating DOI/URL construction.
- Normalize DOI-to-URI conversion and rename method to getURIAsASCIIString for clarity.
- Clean up fetched BibTeX encoding (replace en-dash in page ranges), and apply optional title formatting (units and case protection) according to preferences.

What I changed
- DOItoBibTeXFetcher
  - getEntryFromDOI now returns Optional<BibEntry> and has overloads to preserve existing ParserResult-based warnings.
  - Validates DOI before constructing a URL; handles MalformedURLException, FileNotFoundException, and IOException by returning Optional.empty() and reporting warnings when a ParserResult is supplied.
  - Downloads BibTeX, fixes encoding issues (en-dash replacement), parses entry, and optionally formats title field.
  - Minor cleanup and clearer logging.
- DOI utility
  - Renamed getURLAsASCIIString to getURIAsASCIIString to better reflect behavior (returns encoded URI string).
- Call sites updated to use Optionals and the new URI method:
  - ClipBoardManager: handle Optional<BibEntry> when fetching DOI from clipboard.
  - MergeEntryDOIDialog: use Optional result and fallback to null when needed.
  - PdfContentImporter: insert entry only when present.
  - JabRefDesktop and DoiResolution: use getURIAsASCIIString when converting DOIs to links.
  - DOICheck: use getURIAsASCIIString when formatting DOIs.
- Tests
  - Updated DOI tests to assert getURIAsASCIIString results.

Why
- Previously getEntryFromDOI could return null and callers sometimes did not check, causing NPEs (see issue #1455). Switching to Optional forces explicit handling of absent results and centralizes error handling in the fetcher. The DOI->URI normalization fixes incorrect link generation in multiple modules.

Compatibility notes
- API change: DOItoBibTeXFetcher#getEntryFromDOI now returns Optional<BibEntry>. Callers must handle Optional (updated throughout repository in this PR).
- DOI#getURLAsASCIIString was renamed to getURIAsASCIIString; tests and usages were updated accordingly.

text:
Add GlobalSearchBar Swing/JavaFX component for application-wide and local searches

Summary
- Introduces GlobalSearchBar (JPanel) which provides a central search UI used in the main frame.
- Uses an embedded JavaFX TextField (JFXPanel / CustomJFXPanel on Linux) so the search input can use JavaFX functionality (tooltip with rich TextFlow, pseudoclasses, etc.).

Key features
- Search input with live updates: EasyBind subscribes to the searchField textProperty to trigger performSearch() on change.
- Search controls: toggles for global search, regular expression, and case sensitivity; button to cycle search display modes.
- Global vs local search: a global search toggle and handling to either perform a GlobalSearchWorker or open local findings in an external SearchResultFrame.
- Search execution: SearchWorker and GlobalSearchWorker are used to perform searches asynchronously; previous workers are cancelled when a new search is started.
- Validation & feedback: invalid search expressions are detected, user is informed with a message and visual pseudoclass changes; successful searches update a results label and show a rich tooltip describing matches.
- Integration with preferences: SearchPreferences persist settings for global search, regular expressions, case sensitivity, and search display mode.
- Autocompletion support: setAutoCompleter hooks in an AutoCompleteSuggestionProvider<Author> and uses AutoCompletionTextInputBinding with person name conversion and append strategy.
- Result management: search queries are stored in the current BasePanel (setCurrentSearchQuery), and SearchResultFrame reuse/validation logic is implemented (validateSearchResultFrame).
- Keyboard handling: a SearchKeyAdapter consumes arrow keys (preventing focus loss) and common keybindings (cut/copy/paste/delete/select-all) so they don't propagate back to the JFrame.
- UI niceties: Open current results in dialog button (with tooltip that changes depending on global/local search), result label formatting, and appropriate focus behavior (focus(), endSearch()).

Implementation details
- The component keeps a SearchQueryHighlightObservable for communication of search highlight state.
- getSearchQuery() synchronizes the current search query with the active BasePanel.
- Empty search clears the search state and updates the main table model to disable search highlighting.
- Several actions and key bindings are prepared (some commented TODOs remain where key mapping conversion is required).

Notes / TODO
- There are TODO comments noting that some keymap conversions still need implementing.
- The JavaFX integration requires that the JavaFX thread be used for UI work via DefaultTaskExecutor.runInJavaFXThread.

This change centralizes and encapsulates search UI behavior and state management, improves user feedback for searches, and provides both local and global search flows with asynchronous execution and autocompletion support.

Summary

This PR adds paging support to the relevant list endpoints and helpers. The change implements basic page-based pagination, exposes paging parameters on API endpoints, and returns pagination metadata in responses. This implements the behavior requested in issue #5518 (contributed by @JoHaHu).

What changed

- Introduced a pagination utility/module to centralize paging logic and defaults (default page size, max page size).
- Updated list endpoints/services to accept page and per_page query parameters (and to fall back to sensible defaults).
- Modified database/query layer to apply limit/offset based on page/per_page parameters to avoid loading all records.
- Responses for paged endpoints now include pagination metadata: total, page, per_page, total_pages, next_page, prev_page (when applicable).
- Added/updated unit and integration tests covering boundary cases (page out of range, per_page limits, default behavior).
- Updated API documentation to show new parameters and example responses.

Behavior and compatibility

- Default behavior: when page/per_page are not provided, endpoints use the previous default behavior but with a default per_page applied (configurable in the pagination utility).
- Backwards compatibility: existing clients will continue to receive data; new paging metadata is additive and should be safe for existing consumers.
- Limits: per_page is capped at a configured maximum to protect against very large requests.

Notes for reviewers

- Please review the pagination utility for naming and default values; these are intentionally centralized to make future changes (e.g., cursor pagination) easier.
- Verify that all list endpoints that should be paginated have been updated. If any endpoint should remain unpaginated, let me know and I will adjust.
- Follow-up work: consider adding cursor-based pagination for very large datasets or streaming endpoints.

References

- Issue: #5518
- Author: @JoHaHu

Summary

This PR refactors journal abbreviation storage and parsing, deduplicates temporary file helper code, and updates affected tests.

Key changes

1) JournalAbbreviationRepository
- Replaced three maps and a SortedSet with a single HashSet for storing Abbreviation instances (initial capacity 16000).
- Introduced helper methods isMatched and isMatchedAbbreviated for case-insensitive matching against name, ISO and Medline abbreviations.
- Lookups (isKnownName, isAbbreviatedName, getAbbreviation) now use stream filtering over the set and return Optional results.
- addEntry now detects duplicates via set containment, logs overwritten entries and stores the new entry.
- addEntries now accepts a Collection<Abbreviation>.
- getAbbreviations now returns an unmodifiable Set instead of a SortedSet (sorting removed).
- getNextAbbreviation, getMedlineAbbreviation and getIsoAbbreviation were simplified to map over the Optional returned by getAbbreviation.

Motivation/Notes: This simplifies storage and reduces memory overhead for the large built-in abbreviation lists (over 15k entries). It also changes ordering semantics (no guaranteed sorting) and lookup characteristics (stream-based matching). Reviewers should note the behavioral change from sorted storage to an unordered set.

2) AbbreviationParser
- Switched from LinkedList to HashSet for abbreviations (initial capacity 5000) to avoid duplicates and improve performance.
- Removed an explicit contains check prior to adding; relying on Set semantics to handle duplicates.

3) FileUpdateMonitor
- Removed duplicated getTempFile implementation and consolidated into a single private static synchronized getTempFile method returning Path. The method creates a temporary file and marks it deleteOnExit, logging on failure.
- Adjusted javadoc to reflect Path return type.

4) Tests
- Updated ManageJournalAbbreviationsViewModelTest expected ordering to reflect changed storage order.
- Removed now-invalid sorting test from JournalAbbreviationRepositoryTest and adjusted other assertions that relied on the old ordering/behavior.

Compatibility and impact

- Public API changes: getAbbreviations now returns Set<Abbreviation> (was SortedSet). addEntries signature changed to accept Collection<Abbreviation> (was List). Callers relying on ordering or SortedSet semantics must be updated.
- Behavior: repository no longer preserves sorted order. Lookup still performs case-insensitive matching across full name, ISO and Medline abbreviations, but uses a stream over the set rather than map lookups.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/journals/AbbreviationParser.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/collab/FileUpdateMonitor.java

text:
Summary

- Fix and clarify file locking behavior when saving files. Ensure proper detection of existing lock files, creation of new lock files, and propagate filesystem errors for network paths.

What changed

1. FileSaveSession
- Added explicit handling for FileSystemException when creating lock file. If caught, a SaveException is thrown with message: The network path was not found.
- Changed lock logic: first check for an existing lock via hasLockFile; if present, wait for it via waitForFileLock and fail if it remains locked. After that, explicitly call createLockFile to obtain the lock.
- IOException during lock creation is now logged, with a TODO noting that proceeding without a valid lock file may be unsafe.

2. FileBasedLock
- createLockFile semantics reversed and errors no longer swallowed:
  - Returns false if the lock file already existed; returns true when it successfully creates the lock file.
  - Now writes the lock file using Files.write and lets IOExceptions bubble up instead of catching and logging internally.
  - The Javadoc return description updated to match the new return behavior.

Fix capitalization behavior around hyphens/en-dashes and conjunctions in title-case formatting

What changed
- Corrected capitalization logic for words following hyphens/en-dashes so they are capitalized as expected.
- Added explicit DASHES and CONJUNCTIONS sets in Word to recognize a wide range of dash characters and to treat conjunctions specially when determining capitalization after dashes.
- Improved Word methods (toUpperFirstIgnoreHyphen, toUpperFirstTitle and supporting isConjunction) to implement the new rules.
- Ensured existing handling of protected characters (braced sections) is preserved.

Why
- Previously words after en-dash characters were not always capitalized correctly and conjunctions after en-dashes could be handled incorrectly. This caused title-case/Capitalize formatting to produce wrong results in several cases.

Tests
- CapitalizeFormatterTest exercises many cases (braced parts, hyphenated words, mixed case, unmatched braces) to verify the Capitalize formatter behavior remains correct and covers the hyphen-related fixes.

References
- Addresses the title-case/en-dash capitalization issues described in the changelog fixes (see entries referencing capitalization after en-dash and conjunction handling).

text:
Add IEEEXplore fetcher to import records from IEEE Xplore

- New class IEEEXploreFetcher implementing EntryFetcher to query the IEEE Xplore REST API and import BibTeX entries.
- Builds a POST search payload and handles IEEE-specific query quirks (uses .QT. for quoted phrases).
- Downloads BibTeX for found records and supports an option to include abstracts (GUI checkbox).
- Preprocesses returned BibTeX to fix malformed HTML escapes (adds missing ampersands), escapes percent signs, and converts HTML entities to LaTeX using HtmlToLatexFormatter.
- Parses BibTeX and applies cleanup/normalization for many fields:
  - Title: image alt replacement, handling of /sub, /sup and /spl constructs, infinity replacement, unit formatting, and case protection.
  - Author: whitespace normalization, ordering of Jr./Sr. parts, and separator normalization.
  - Month: parses a variety of month formats into BibTeX month tokens or ranges.
  - Pages: converts single-page and page ranges to correct BibTeX form.
  - Publication/booktitle: normalizes proceedings naming, applies journal abbreviation preferences (IEEE abbreviations), and handles Early Access/accepted-for-publication cases.
  - Abstract: cleans sub/sup and special sequences similar to title processing.
  - URL: normalizes IEEE Xplore links to full http URL.
  - Keywords: replaces semicolon separators with the configured keyword separator.
- Limits downloads and warns when total hits exceed MAX_FETCH (100) to reduce server load.
- Adds cookie management for requests and proper request headers for JSON and bibtex retrieval.
- Error handling: logs errors and shows messages in the import inspection dialog on failures; supports stopFetching to cancel ongoing import.

This change integrates IEEE Xplore import into the application with robust preprocessing and field cleanup to improve the quality of imported entries.

Summary:
This PR addresses several PostgreSQL-related issues that were causing intermittent failures, slow queries, and schema mismatches. The fixes are intended to stabilize DB connections, correct query and schema problems, and improve overall performance and observability. Because some issues were subtle, the title includes a question mark — please validate behavior in staging before rolling to production.

What changed (high level):
- Adjusted connection handling and pooling parameters to reduce timeouts and max-connection exhaustion.
- Added retry logic for transient connection errors to improve resilience.
- Corrected SQL query issues (ambiguous column references/schema qualification) to prevent runtime errors.
- Added missing/updated migrations to align database schema with application models and added targeted indexes to improve slow queries.
- Improved timezone handling and ensured queries use parameterized/prepared statements to avoid injection risks.
- Added extra logging and metrics around DB errors and slow queries to aid debugging.
- Included unit/integration tests and migration checks where applicable.

Why:
- Reduce production incidents caused by connection/timeouts and schema drift.
- Improve query performance and reliability.
- Make DB error conditions easier to diagnose with better logs/metrics.

Testing & deployment notes:
- Run the test suite (unit + integration) and apply migrations in a staging environment to validate schema changes.
- Monitor connection pool usage, slow queries, and error rates after deploying to staging.
- Verify critical workflows that previously failed (e.g., background jobs, API endpoints that hit DB) under realistic load.

Rollback / Safety:
- Schema changes include migrations; ensure backups and/or the ability to roll back migrations if needed.
- If problems appear after deployment, revert this PR and investigate logs/metrics collected by the added instrumentation.

Follow-ups:
- Confirm pool parameter values with the infra/DBA team and tune for production load.
- Consider running explain/analyze on remaining slow queries to find additional indexing opportunities.

Fix field inheritance (implements biblatex rules) — fixes #5045

What I changed
- Implemented the biblatex crossref field inheritance rules in BibEntry: added a new private helper getSourceField(...) that encapsulates the mapping logic between a child (target) field+type and the parent's (source) type.
- Updated getResolvedFieldOrAlias(...) to consult the mapped source field when a field is missing and the entry has a crossref.
- Added special mappings and restrictions: forbidden fields (IDS, CROSSREF, XREF, ENTRYSET, RELATED, SORTKEY) are not inherited; mapped fields for multi-volume/book/collection/proceedings and IEEEtran Periodical → Article cases (e.g. bookauthor → author, maintitle/mainsubtitle/maintitleaddon → title/subtitle/titleaddon as appropriate), and prevented same-name inheritance for title/subtitle/titleaddon/shorttitle in the specified cases. Falls back to same-name inheritance when allowed.
- Added extensive unit tests (CrossrefTest) covering forbidden fields, author inheritance, main/book/journal title mappings, cases where title inheritance must not occur, and generic same-name inheritance for many fields.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to note the fix.

Why
This implements the complex biblatex inheritance behavior for cross-referenced entries so that child entries resolve missing fields according to biblatex rules rather than always using the same-name inheritance. This resolves crossref inheritance issues reported in #5045.

Files changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/BibEntry.java — new mapping logic and use in resolved field lookup
- src/test/java/org/jabref/model/entry/CrossrefTest.java — new tests for the different inheritance scenarios
- CHANGELOG.md — recorded the fix

Notes
- Tests were added and the behavior was manually verified in a running JabRef instance.
- This change focuses on field-level inheritance rules; no UI changes.

Summary

This PR adds support for nested bracket expressions and customized fallback fields inside bracketed citation key patterns (e.g. patterns like [field:(fallback)] and deeper nesting such as [author:([title:(year:...)])]).

What I changed

- Bracket parsing: contentBetweenBrackets now supports nested brackets by tracking sub-bracket depth and correctly handling '[' and ']' as well as quoted segments. This allows bracket content to contain additional bracketed expressions.
- Modifier application: applyModifiers signature updated to accept a Function<String,String> expandBracketContent, and parentheses-based alternate text modifiers are now expanded via expandBrackets instead of a plain substring. This enables nested expansion and fallbacks inside the alternate-text parentheses.
- Integration: CitationKeyGenerator updated to pass the appropriate expandBracketContent function into applyModifiers.
- Tests: Added parameterized unit tests in BracketedPatternTest covering several fallback/nested cases and a unit test in CitationKeyGeneratorTest to validate fallback field behavior.
- Changelog: Added an entry noting support for customized fallback fields in bracketed patterns.

Notes

- The change preserves previous behavior for simple patterns while enabling nested/fallback patterns to be parsed and expanded recursively.
- Adds test coverage for the new functionality.

Fixes: #7111

text:
Summary

When opening a library, JabRef now creates the tab immediately and shows a loading indicator while the database parser runs. Entries are displayed as soon as parsing completes (or progressively, depending on parser behavior), instead of waiting to create the tab only after parsing finishes.

What this PR does

- Create the library tab up front and show a loading animation / progress indicator while the database is being parsed.
- Populate the UI with entries after parsing completes (and allow progressive display when entries are parsed incrementally).
- Keeps existing startup behavior optional: for startup loading a splash/progress dialog would look better (suggested), but this PR focuses on in-app tab loading UX.

Why

Previously JabRef would only create a tab after the full database parsing finished. This produced a perceived delay and poor feedback to users when opening large libraries. Creating the tab and showing a loading indicator makes the application feel more responsive and informs users that loading is in progress.

Known issues / TODO

- There is a remaining bug: after data is loaded the group pane sometimes still shows 0 entries. Navigating away from the tab and back refreshes the correct entry counts. This needs a follow-up fix.
- Applying a blocking splash screen on startup is suggested but not implemented here; could be added in a follow-up if desired.

Testing

- Manually tested the changed features in a running JabRef instance.
- Screenshots demonstrating the new loading tab / indicator are included below.

Closes #6417

This PR updates and improves the duplicate-detection / import inspection and merge UI and related import flows. Key changes:

- Duplicate resolution
  - Enhanced DuplicateResolverDialog: tabbed view with short preview, complete BibTeX source and merged-entry preview; actions for keeping upper/lower/both, merging, and an option to auto-remove exact duplicates. Displays LaTeX-formatted BibTeX source in the Complete record tab.
  - DuplicateSearch now runs the searcher in a dedicated low-priority thread via JabRefExecutorService, collects duplicate pairs asynchronously and presents them to the user via the improved resolver dialog. Supports remembering an "auto remove exact duplicates" choice.
  - Duplicate handling integrated into import and import-inspection paths (KEEP/REMOVE/MERGE/BREAK handling).

- Import inspection and import flow
  - ImportInspectionDialog improvements: interactive table with preview, selection controls, progress handling, generation of BibTeX keys, group assignment support, context menu actions for linking/downloading/attaching files and URLs, autoset-links integration and per-entry file/menu handling. Duplicates found during inspection can be resolved using the DuplicateResolverDialog; merged results are added to the inspection list for final import.
  - ImportMenuItem: import results are merged and either passed to ImportInspectionDialog (if enabled) or added directly to the current/new database. Handles parser warnings, key generation and duplicate resolution during automated imports.
  - addImportedEntries / addBibEntries (JabRefFrame): import routing now uses the inspection dialog when configured and applies duplicate resolution, merging, replacement and undo grouping consistently.

- Merging entries
  - MergeEntriesDialog: modal UI to merge two selected entries, with options to insert merged entry and keep the old ones or replace the two old entries. Undo edits are recorded.

- Misc.
  - Several UI and threading improvements: use of JabRefExecutorService, better blocking/unblocking of the main frame when performing long operations, and tighter integration with existing undo infrastructure.
  - Many related classes updated to cooperate with the new dialogs and flows: DuplicateResolverDialog, DuplicateSearch, ImportInspectionDialog, JabRefFrame, MergeEntriesDialog, ImportMenuItem.

User-visible effects: more powerful and clearer duplicate resolving and merging workflows (including merged-entry preview and full BibTeX source view), improved import inspection with file attachment/download/context actions, and more robust background duplicate searching.

text:
Keep unknown meta data

This PR changes the handling of unknown meta data items so they are no longer deleted when reading/writing. Instead we preserve unknown meta entries and try to retain their original formatting as much as possible. A few minimal, safe customizations are applied: escaping of `;` and insertion of newlines where appropriate, but the meta-data format is not fully parsed or restructured.

Behavioral notes
- Unknown meta items are preserved on read/write.
- You can rename a 'groupstree' meta data item and it will be kept and formatted in the same way under the new name.
- Full parsing/normalization of meta data formatting is intentionally not implemented here; this PR prefers preservation and will be adapted if concrete use cases require deeper parsing.

Quality and testing
- CHANGELOG.md updated
- Tests added to cover the change
- Manual testing performed with a running JabRef

This aims to avoid data loss for custom/unknown metadata while keeping changes minimal and safe.

text:
Summary

Convert Unicode characters in generated BibTeX keys to ASCII-safe representations to ensure compatibility with BibTeX parsers and citation tools.

What I changed

- Implemented a normalization step that converts common Unicode characters to ASCII equivalents when generating bibtex keys.
- Strip or replace characters that are invalid in BibTeX keys (spaces, punctuation, combining marks) and collapse repeated separators.
- Added fallback behavior to ensure resulting keys are non-empty and unique (append numeric suffix when collisions occur).
- Added unit tests covering various Unicode inputs (accents, ligatures, non-Latin scripts, emojis) and edge cases (empty fields, identical normalized keys).

Why this is needed

Some bibliographic sources contain non-ASCII characters in author names, titles, or other fields used to derive bibtex keys. BibTeX and many tools expect keys to be ASCII-only and to avoid certain punctuation; this change improves interoperability and reduces broken citations.

Examples

- "García" -> "Garcia"
- "Æther" -> "AEther"
- "Smørrebrød" -> "Smorrebrod"
- "作者" (Chinese characters) -> "author" (fallback heuristic) or "uXXXXuYYYY"-style deterministic transliteration depending on configuration
- "title: An emoji 😊" -> "titleAnEmoji"

Backward compatibility

- Existing keys already stored in .bib files are not modified; this affects only newly generated keys.
- The normalization behavior is deterministic; a small risk of key collisions is handled by appending numeric suffixes.

Testing

- Unit tests added for normalization, invalid-character stripping, uniqueness handling, and integration test for full key generation pipeline.

Notes / Future work

- Allow configuration of transliteration strategy (ASCII transliteration vs. Unicode codepoint encoding) and custom replacement maps.
- Consider exposing a hook to preserve or customize diacritics for systems that accept UTF-8 keys.

Files changed

- src/bibtex/key_generator.* (normalization and collision handling)
- tests/test_key_generator.* (unit/integration tests)

Fix threading cleanup in performSearch

This change removes the shared ImportCleanup usage from CompositeSearchBasedFetcher.performSearch. The previous code invoked a single ImportCleanup::doPostCleanup on entries produced by a parallel stream, which was not thread-safe and could lead to exceptions when importing entries from a web search and to incorrect handling of the library mode (BibTeX/biblatex). The cleanup mapping has been removed and related unused imports were cleaned up. The CHANGELOG.md was updated to document the fixes.

Fixes #7606
Fixes #1018

text:
Introduce file-based locking for safe, concurrent-aware file saves and encapsulate lock logic in a new utility class.

Summary of changes:
- Add FileBasedLock utility with APIs to manage simple lock files:
  - hasLockFile(Path) — check whether a .lock file exists for a target file.
  - waitForFileLock(Path) — wait (with retries) until a lock file disappears.
  - getLockFileTimeStamp(Path) — read the lock file last-modified time (Optional<FileTime>).
  - createLockFile(Path) — create a .lock file (writes a small token and marks it deleteOnExit).
  - deleteLockFile(Path) — delete the .lock file if present.
  - Constants: .lock suffix and LOCKFILE_CRITICAL_AGE for future use.
  - Default retry behavior: 10 attempts, sleeping 500ms between checks.

- Integrate FileBasedLock into FileSaveSession.commit(Path):
  - Check for existing lock and wait for it to be released; throw SaveException.FILE_LOCKED when waiting fails.
  - Create a lock file before copying the temporary file to the target and ensure the lock file is removed in a finally block.
  - Handle network path errors (FileSystemException) explicitly, and log other IO errors when creating the lock file.
  - Preserve existing POSIX permissions (when supported) by reading them before overwrite and restoring them after copying.
  - Continue existing behavior: optional backup creation, copy temporary -> target, and deletion of temporary file (or warn if deletion fails).

Other notes:
- The lock file mechanism is conservative: it waits a limited number of times (default ~5 seconds total) before giving up.
- FileBasedLock is intentionally minimal and file-system based; it writes a small marker and uses filename.lock next to the original file.
- Logging and error handling added for visibility when lock creation or permission operations fail.

These changes improve robustness when multiple instances try to save the same file concurrently and make file save operations safer on POSIX systems by preserving permissions.

Fixes incorrect detection of online links in the entry editor so links are recognized reliably while editing text.

What was happening
- The entry editor sometimes failed to recognize URLs (for example links with leading “www.”, or URLs followed by punctuation) and thus the UI didn’t offer link actions or highlight links correctly.
- Edge cases around trailing punctuation, surrounding parentheses, and caret/selection changes caused inconsistent detection.

What I changed
- Improved the link detection logic used by the entry editor to:
  - Recognize URLs with http/https and those starting with www.
  - Trim common trailing punctuation (.,;:!?), and handle surrounding parentheses/brackets so links aren’t accidentally cut off.
  - Update detection to run on selection/caret changes so the editor’s link-related UI stays in sync while typing or navigating.
- Added unit tests covering the main edge cases and a small integration check for the entry editor UI behavior.

How to test
1. Open the entry editor.
2. Paste or type various link forms: http://example.com, https://example.com, www.example.com, example.com (if supported).
3. Include links followed by punctuation or wrapped in parentheses, e.g. (https://example.com), and verify the editor recognizes the link correctly.
4. Move the caret and change selection around links; confirm the link actions/highlighting update appropriately.

Notes
- No breaking API changes. This is an internal fix to the editor’s detection logic.
- If you see any link form that still isn’t recognized, please add an example to the test suite and I’ll extend the detection rules.

text:
Add CSL citation-style support

This change introduces a new citation-style subsystem to JabRef, including:

- New classes under org.jabref.logic.citationstyle:
  - CSLAdapter: Adapter around de.undercouch.citeproc.CSL that creates and reuses a CSL engine for rendering bibliographies. makeBibliography(...) is synchronized because the underlying CSL engine is not thread-safe. The adapter supports switching styles and output formats and registers citation items with the engine.
  - CitationStyle: Represents a citation style (file path, title, source). Provides utilities to load styles from the bundled /csl-styles folder or from the filesystem, parse the CSL XML to read the title (with prolog stripping), discover available styles (works both from classpath and inside JARs), and provide a default style (/ieee.csl).
  - JabRefLocaleProvider: LocaleProvider implementation that loads and caches CSL locale XML files from /csl-locales using CSLUtils.

- Item data conversion and formatting:
  - JabRefItemDataProvider (inner class of CSLAdapter) converts BibEntry -> org.jbibtex/BibTeXEntry -> CSLItemData using BibTeXConverter. It applies RemoveNewlinesFormatter and HTMLChars formatting and handles the Month field (converting #mon# to short name) so CSL receives compatible month values.

- Submodules and build integration:
  - .gitmodules added entries for src/main/resources/csl-styles and src/main/resources/csl-locales so the project can include the official CSL styles and locales repositories as submodules.
  - Code uses de.undercouch.citeproc helper classes (already present as dependency) for reading styles/locales.

- Robustness and logging:
  - CitationStyle handles both classpath and external style files, with logging for IO and parsing errors.
  - Locale loading wraps IOExceptions as UncheckedIOException so callers receive informative failures.

Why:
- This enables rendering formatted bibliographies using CSL styles packaged with the application or loaded from disk, supports locale loading, and avoids repeatedly recreating the expensive CSL engine by reusing instances where possible.

Notes / considerations:
- makeBibliography is synchronized to avoid concurrent use of the non-thread-safe CSL engine; this design favors reusing one engine over creating many.
- CitationStyle discovery works when running from sources and from JARs (uses FileSystem for jar URI scheme).
- Error handling is conservative: failures to parse or load styles/locales are logged and result in absent Optionals or exceptions where appropriate.

text:

Summary:
When closing a library tab by clicking the 'x', the tab closing flow did not call the LibraryTab.closeTab() method. That meant backup and autosave managers were not properly shut down for that tab. - Ensure tab-close action (clicking 'x') routes through the existing closeTab() method instead of directly removing the tab, so shutdown/cleanup is performed.

Why:
- To properly stop the backup and autosave managers when a library tab is closed via the tab header close button, preventing leftover background activity and potential resource leaks.

Testing:
- Manually tested in a running JabRef to verify backup/autosave managers are shut down when closing a tab with the 'x'.

Notes:
- No automated tests or changelog entry were added in this PR.

- Localization and changelog: Added new resource strings and updated CHANGELOG to announce the new Customization tab (issue #7337).
- Tests: Updated IdentifierEditorViewModelTest to supply a mocked PreferencesService.

Summary

- Open ImportInspectionDialog when a fetched article already exists in the database (referenced in CHANGELOG Unreleased).
- Prevent JavaFX embedded text components from unintentionally triggering global Swing keybindings by consuming certain key events in the JFXPanel used by the EntryEditor and GlobalSearchBar.

Details

- Import flow: If a fetch returns an article that is already present in the current library, the ImportInspectionDialog is started so the user can inspect/merge the fetched information instead of silently overwriting or ignoring it.

- Keybinding handling in embedded JavaFX components:
  - Added listeners on the JFXPanel containers (EntryEditor and GlobalSearchBar) to intercept and consume common shortcuts (CUT, COPY, PASTE, SELECT_ALL, DELETE, and other editor navigation/close shortcuts). - Entry editor and search UX improvements:

  - GlobalSearchBar: refined global/local search handling, search mode toggle, autocompletion hookup and search result window validation.

Other

- The fetcher popup and toolbar key mappings are kept and integrated with the updated behavior so users can still update entries from web fetchers, generate keys, auto-link files and use undo/redo from the entry editor toolbar.

This change fixes UX issues where editing/searching in JavaFX controls accidentally triggered global shortcuts and makes fetch handling more explicit and user-friendly when duplicates are encountered.
