- Wires the new migration into OpenDatabase.performLoadDatabaseMigrations so it runs automatically when opening databases.
- Adds SpecialFieldsUtils (marked deprecated) providing helpers to sync special fields and keyword values between BibEntry fields and the keywords field. Includes methods to update fields, export/import keywords and synchronize sets of keywords for special-field detection.
- Adds unit tests: SpecialFieldsToSeparateFieldsTest and SpecialFieldsUtilsTest to validate migration behavior and keyword/special field synchronization.

Notes:
- SpecialFieldsUtils is deprecated and contains a comment suggesting refactoring and integration into BibEntry to provide a cleaner API for setting special fields and optional keyword synchronization.
- No user-visible changes other than migrated entries: special-field keywords are removed from keywords and set as dedicated fields, improving consistency and future handling of special fields.

Users previously could encounter inconsistent behavior when editing/creating custom entry types (for example losing field selections, saving invalid names, or seeing confusing dialog behavior). Testing

- Verified validation messages appear for empty and duplicate names and that valid changes are persisted.

Summary
Fixes an issue where DEL, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V and Ctrl+A typed in the global search field would also trigger the corresponding actions in the main table (e.g. deleting or modifying entries). This PR prevents those key events from being propagated to the JFrame keybindings when the search field is focused.

What I changed
- GlobalSearchBar: add a KeyAdapter on the JFXPanel containing the JavaFX TextField to detect key events and consume ones that map to application key bindings (CUT, COPY, PASTE, DELETE_ENTRY, SELECT_ALL). This prevents propagation of those shortcuts to the main table.
- EntryEditor: replace an anonymous KeyListener implementation with KeyAdapter (same pattern used to avoid empty method stubs).
- Minor cleanups in GlobalSearchBar: small import/formatting tweaks, make a button final, and ensure tooltip is set on the JavaFX thread.
- CHANGELOG.md: add entry describing the fix.

Why
Previously key events from the embedded JavaFX search field would bubble up and be interpreted by the main application keybindings, causing unintended actions on the main table. Consuming the relevant key events at the JFXPanel level prevents that behavior.

Fixes
- Fixes #3067

Testing
- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance. 

Notes
- No unit tests were added in this PR.

text:
Add support for per-user LaTeX file directories and integrate them into TexGroup file resolution and UI

This PR introduces support for storing a LaTeX-specific file directory per user in the library metadata, exposing it in the Library Properties UI, persisting it in exported metadata, parsing it on import, and using it for resolving and relativizing TexGroup paths.

Main changes
- Model / metadata
  - MetaData: add laTexFileDirectory map + getters/setters/clearers and exposure via getLaTexFileDirectories(). Equality now accounts for the new map.
- UI / preferences
  - LibraryPropertiesDialog.fxml: add a new field and browse button for "LaTex file directory" and adjust layout row constraints.
  - LibraryPropertiesDialogView / ViewModel: add property, binding, browsing handler, and store logic to read/write the metadata. Detect changes for marking library dirty.
  - Localization: add "LaTex file directory" label to English resources.
- Groups & TexGroup
  - TexGroup: constructors updated to accept MetaData (and optionally a user identifier). Files are now expanded against configured LaTeX file directories and returned as relative paths when possible. File monitor registration uses the final expanded path. Implemented helpers to relativize/expand using configured directories.
  - GroupDialog: use basePanel's MetaData to create TexGroup instances and relativize chosen aux file paths when browsing.
  - GroupsParser / MetaDataParser: parsing now supplies MetaData when creating TexGroup instances; metadata parser recognizes the new "fileDirectoryLatex-<user>" entries and sets MetaData accordingly. GroupsParser import signatures updated accordingly.
- Persistence / serialization
  - MetaDataSerializer: serialize LaTeX file directories using key fileDirectoryLatex-<user>.
  - FileHelper: add relativize helper for resolving relative paths against a list of file directories.
- Tests
  - Updated and added tests to account for the new MetaData/ TexGroup constructors and LaTeX file directory behavior (GroupsParserTest, TexGroupTest, BibtexDatabaseWriterTest, BibtexParserTest, GroupSerializerTest).
- Misc
  - Small docstring fix in BibDatabaseContext and minor code formatting/consistency fixes.

Behavioral summary
- Users can configure a LaTeX-specific file directory in Library Properties; this is stored per user in metadata.
- When creating a TexGroup or choosing an AUX file, the code will try to make the displayed path relative to configured LaTeX file directories. When loading a TexGroup from metadata, configured directories are used to expand/resolve absolute/relative paths.
- Metadata keys for LaTeX directories are persisted as "fileDirectoryLatex-<user>" for compatibility with saved libraries.

Compatibility
- New metadata keys are additive and backwards-compatible; older libraries without the keys are unaffected. Tests updated accordingly.

Files touched (high level)
- Model: MetaData, TexGroup, FileHelper, BibDatabaseContext
- GUI: LibraryPropertiesDialog.fxml, LibraryPropertiesDialogView(.java), LibraryPropertiesDialogViewModel.java, GroupDialog.java
- Import/Export: MetaDataParser, MetaDataSerializer, GroupsParser
- Tests: multiple updated tests to reflect new constructors and metadata handling

This change centralizes LaTeX directory handling and improves TexGroup path resolution and user experience when browsing/inspecting aux files.

Summary

Introduce an explicit, runtime-computed list of BibLaTeX-only fields and stop relying on FIELD_ALIASES_LTX_TO_TEX. This fixes #2390 by deriving BibLaTeX-only fields from the declared BibTeX and BibLaTeX entry types and excluding fields that JabRef treats as general/internal defaults.

What I changed

- Implement dynamic computation of BibLaTeX-only fields in NoBibtexFieldChecker. The set is now computed from BibtexEntryTypes.ALL and BibLatexEntryTypes.ALL at runtime (method getAllBiblatexOnlyFields) and excludes InternalBibtexFields.DEFAULT_GENERAL_FIELDS. This makes the check responsive to runtime/customized entry types.
- Added InternalBibtexFields.DEFAULT_GENERAL_FIELDS to centralize the default fields shown in the General tab. Preferences now use this list to set language-dependent default values.
- Converted several hard-coded uses of the literal "comment(s)" field name to use FieldName.COMMENT constant and added the constant rename (FieldName.COMMENTS -> FieldName.COMMENT). Updated importers and OAI handler accordingly (BiblioscapeImporter, MedlinePlainImporter, RisImporter, OAI2Handler, InternalBibtexFields).
- Treated ISBN and ISSN as BibTeX fields as well (updates in BibtexEntryTypes where appropriate).
- Tests updated and extended:
  - IntegrityCheckTest: tests for person name fields now run using BibLaTeX mode so they don't trigger NoBibtexFieldChecker when those fields are BibLaTeX-only.
  - NoBibTexFieldCheckerTest: added multiple tests to assert correct detection of BibLaTeX-only fields (e.g. afterword, journaltitle, location) and to assert that fields like comment, institution, keywords are not erroneously flagged.
- Minor cleanups and javadoc/style tweaks in InternalBibtexFields and JabRefPreferences.
- CHANGELOG updated to mention the integrity check change and the comment/ISBN/ISSN adjustments.

Rationale and notes

- Previous implementation relied on EntryConverter.FIELD_ALIASES_LTX_TO_TEX which turned out to be insufficient to determine the full set of BibLaTeX-only fields. Computing the set from entry type definitions is more complete.
- Computation is non-static and done on each check so that if users customize entry types at runtime the checker will reflect those changes. A full solution that incorporates user-configured custom tab fields (JabRefPreferences custom tab content) would require a larger architectural change and was out of scope for this PR.
- ISBN/ISSN were treated as BibTeX fields based on practical usage and existing bibliography styles.

Files changed (high level)

- Logic & importers: NoBibtexFieldChecker, BiblioscapeImporter, MedlinePlainImporter, RisImporter, OAI2Handler
- Model: FieldName, InternalBibtexFields, BibtexEntryTypes
- Preferences: JabRefPreferences (use DEFAULT_GENERAL_FIELDS)
- Tests: IntegrityCheckTest, NoBibTexFieldCheckerTest
- CHANGELOG.md

Tests

- New and updated unit tests included and adjusted to reflect the new behavior. They cover detection of BibLaTeX-only fields and ensure common fields (comment, keywords, institution) are not flagged.

Issue

Fixes #2390 (better detection of BibLaTeX-only fields).

Fix threading issues (fixes #3485 and #3435)

Summary
- Prevents UI freezes and intermittent race conditions by improving how work is scheduled and how shared state is accessed.
- Moves long-running/background work off the JavaFX thread and ensures all UI updates are performed on the JavaFX Application Thread.
- Adds proper synchronization/confinement for shared resources and tightens task lifecycle/error handling to avoid spurious exceptions and races.

Why
- The changes address the root causes reported in the linked issues: conflicting access to shared state and work being executed on the UI thread.

What changed
- Refactored task scheduling so background computations run on background threads and any UI mutations are wrapped with Platform.runLater (or equivalent).
- Introduced synchronization/confinement for previously racy accesses to shared data structures.
- Improved cancelation/error handling for background tasks to reduce leaks and inconsistent states.

Testing
- CHANGELOG.md has been updated.
- Manually tested the affected flows in a running JabRef instance; reproductions from #3485 and #3435 no longer occur.
- Unit/integration tests for these concurrency fixes are not included in this PR (TODO).

Notes / Follow-ups
- Please review the threading and synchronization changes carefully for potential deadlocks or regressions.
- Add automated tests covering the concurrency scenarios and update any documentation if necessary.

Why this change

These fixes make the OpenOffice citation support more robust in the face of missing or malformed styles and prevent application crashes caused by unhandled nulls and resource leaks. They also improve diagnostics so issues can be diagnosed more easily.

Notes

No user-visible behavior changes are intended beyond better stability and clearer logging; if a style is missing or invalid, the code now falls back safely instead of causing a crash.

Summary

This PR fixes several threading-related issues by ensuring that UI and entry-model updates are executed on the JavaFX application thread. It addresses two reported issues: #3485 (exception when double-clicking an entry in the integrity check dialog) and #3435 (entry type could not be changed when the entry editor was open).

What I changed

- BasePanel
  - Ensure entry.setType(...) runs on the JavaFX thread via DefaultTaskExecutor.runInJavaFXThread(...) when changing entry types (fixes #3435).
  - Various small formatting/whitespace cleanups and minor refactorings to improve readability.
  - Added a newline in GroupTreeListener for consistency.

- EntryEditor
  - Made typeLabel final to better reflect usage and avoid potential threading visibility issues.
  - Wrap subscriptions and tab/field focus operations in DefaultTaskExecutor.runInJavaFXThread(...) so tab selection and focus requests run on the JavaFX thread (fixes race conditions that could cause exceptions, related to #3485).
  - Minor formatting fixes.

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Documented the fixes for the two issues (#3485 and #3435).

Rationale

Updates that touch UI components (tab selection, focus requests) or mutate entry state that is observed by UI code must be performed on the JavaFX application thread. Moving these operations to DefaultTaskExecutor.runInJavaFXThread prevents race conditions and exceptions that occurred when background threads triggered UI-affecting actions.

Testing

- Manually tested in a running JabRef build. The reported scenarios (double-clicking entries in the integrity check dialog and changing entry types while the entry editor is open) no longer produce the previously observed exceptions or failures.
- No automated tests were added in this PR.

Related issues

Fixes #3485
Fixes #3435

Summary

Fixes for the BibTeX parser to make it more robust when files are missing newlines and to accept entries that contain only a key. Also fixes a bug in parsing the encoding header when it is immediately followed by other content (e.g. an @-entry) on the same line.

What I changed

- Core fixes
  - Make the BibTeX parser accept entries that only contain a key (e.g. @article{test}). (src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/importer/fileformat/BibtexParser.java)
  - Improve parsing of encoding header lines so the encoding is extracted correctly even if the encoding line is immediately followed by an @ symbol (prevents the @ and trailing content from becoming part of the encoding). (src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/importer/OpenDatabaseAction.java)
  - Improve robustness when there is no newline between header/preamble/entries so preamble and entries are parsed correctly.

- Tests added/updated
  - Added tests covering files without newlines and entries with only a key:
    - OpenDatabaseActionTest.correctlyParseEncodingWithoutNewline
    - BibtexParserTest.parseRecognizesEntryOnlyWithKey
    - BibtexParserTest.parsePreambleAndEntryWithoutNewLine
    - BibtexParserTest.parseFileHeaderAndPreambleWithoutNewLine
  - Adjusted some test string formatting for consistency.
  - Added test resource encodingWithoutNewline.bib (src/test/resources/net/sf/jabref/importer/encodingWithoutNewline.bib)

- Changelog
  - Updated CHANGELOG.md to mention the parser improvements (more robust against missing newlines and import of entries with only a key).

- Minor cleanups
  - Removed several stray blank lines in OpenDatabaseAction for code formatting.

Why

These changes fix parsing issues reported when BibTeX files do not include expected newlines (for example when header, preamble and entries are concatenated on a single line). They also handle entries that only declare a key without fields and avoid mis-parsing the encoding header when it is adjacent to an @-entry token. Several unit tests were added to prevent regressions.

Notes

- Tests reference issue #669 in comments (coverage for cases that previously failed).
- All added tests should exercise the new behavior and ensure correct parsing of encoding, preamble and entries in the no-newline scenarios.

Summary

Do not let exceptions thrown by the XMP parser abort processing. This change adds a defensive workaround for IllegalArgumentException (and other parsing exceptions) thrown while parsing XMP metadata so that a single malformed XMP block no longer breaks the whole import/processing flow.

What I changed

- Wrap XMP parsing in a try/catch and handle IllegalArgumentException (and other unexpected exceptions) by logging a warning and skipping the faulty XMP metadata.
- Ensure the caller continues processing the remaining metadata/entries instead of failing fast.
- Documented the change in CHANGELOG.md.

Why

Some PDF/entry files contain malformed or unexpected XMP data which caused IllegalArgumentException inside the XMP parser and aborted processing. This made imports brittle and resulted in lost/partial work. Catching and handling these exceptions makes imports more robust and avoids crashing due to a single malformed metadata block. This fixes #9383.

Testing

- Manually tested in a running JabRef build to verify that malformed XMP no longer stops processing and that a warning is logged.
- No automated tests added in this PR.

Notes / Follow-ups

- This is a pragmatic workaround. The underlying root cause in the XMP parsing logic should be investigated and, if possible, fixed to allow correct parsing of the data.
- Consider adding unit/regression tests to cover malformed XMP cases in a follow-up PR.

text:
Summary

- Improve PDF annotation import: fix display of annotations created by Foxit Reader, add support for additional marked annotation types, and refactor extraction code for robustness and clarity.

Key changes

- Introduced TextExtractor: new class that extracts text from marked annotations using QuadPoints bounding boxes. It centralizes the previous extraction logic, supports COSFloat and COSInteger values, and throws IOExceptions on invalid coordinates.
- Refactored PdfAnnotationImporter:
  - Replaced inline rectangle/text extraction with TextExtractor.
  - Use FileAnnotationType.isMarkedFileAnnotationType to detect marked annotations (highlight, underline, squiggly, strikeout, etc.).
  - Exclude annotations with null subtype and ignore Link/Widget subtypes explicitly.
  - Improved logging messages in validatePath (file names are now quoted).
  - Simplified creation of linked marked annotations and error handling when extraction fails.
- Enhanced FileAnnotationType enum:
  - Added new types (SQUIGGLY) and a boolean flag linkedFileAnnotationType to mark annotation types that are linked/contain marked text.
  - Added helper methods isMarkedFileAnnotationType(String) and isLinkedFileAnnotationType() for clearer type checks.
- Tests:
  - Added unit tests covering invalid paths, directories, non-PDF document types, and new PDF fixtures (Foxit highlights, squiggly, strikeout) to ensure correct import and linking of note annotations.
- Changelog:
  - Fixed issue number in CHANGELOG and added an entry noting the fix for FileAnnotations created by Foxit Reader.

Why

These changes fix several issues around extracting and displaying marked text from PDFs, in particular annotations created by Foxit Reader and annotations that use integer quadpoint coordinates. The refactor improves maintainability and makes annotation type handling more explicit and robust.

text:
Introduce JabRefFrame — the main application window and central UI controller.

Summary of responsibilities and changes in this class:
- Builds the main application UI: menu bar, toolbar, side pane and tabbed library area, and binds them to preferences and application state.
- Implements drag-and-drop support for opening .bib files with a visual "Open files..." drop indicator tab.
- Registers and handles global key bindings (new entry shortcuts, navigation, search focus, paste workaround on macOS, etc.).
- Adds a telemetry opt-in notification that is shown after startup if needed.
- Implements graceful quit handling:
  - Waits for background tasks and asks the user whether to force quit.
  - Prompts to save modified local libraries before closing.
  - Converts shared databases to local on close and shuts down autosave/backup services.
  - Persists last-opened files and window settings on teardown.
- Integrates autosave and backup management when opening/closing tabs and starts AutosaveManager/BackupManager where appropriate.
- Provides tab management and context menu actions (open folder, open console, close, close others, close all) and supports adding LibraryTab instances and ParserResult imports (including an import inspection dialog).
- Adds a background task indicator in the toolbar with a popover showing running tasks, bound to the StateManager task list and progress.
- Binds application-wide state using EasyBind (open databases list, active database, focus owner, search query propagation, window title updates, selection sync, etc.).
- Integrates Undo/Redo event handling and registers undo listeners per tab.
- Adds support for PushToApplications, FileHistory, special fields menu (conditional), and numerous menu/tool actions for import/export, library operations, lookup and tools.

Notes on implementation details:
- Uses Platform.runLater for UI-thread-only bindings (focus owner) and DefaultTaskExecutor/BackgroundTask for background operations.
- Uses Preferences (JabRefPreferences) to persist UI settings such as side pane width and last opened files.
- Uses DialogService for all user dialogs and confirmations.

This class centralizes many high-level responsibilities for window lifecycle, user interaction, and coordination between UI components and application services.

Add configurable entry preview system with UI, persistence, and multiple layout backends

This PR implements a comprehensive preview subsystem and preferences UI that lets users configure, edit and cycle through different entry preview layouts. Main changes and additions:

- New Preview preferences tab (PreviewTabView + PreviewTabViewModel)
  - Manage "available" and "chosen" preview layouts with drag-and-drop and buttons
  - Edit text-based preview layouts with a rich CodeArea (with XML-like syntax highlighting), cut/copy/paste/select-all context menu, keyboard quick-search in the lists, and validation (chosen list must not be empty)
  - Reset selected layout to default, reorder chosen layouts, and toggle showing preview as a separate tab
  - Asynchronously discover citation styles and add them to the available list
  - Proper handling of newline placeholder (__NEWLINE__) between UI and model

- Preview runtime components
  - PreviewPanel: hosts the preview viewer in the UI, integrates with preferences and file-drag operations to add/copy/move files to the entry
  - PreviewViewer: uses a WebView to render preview HTML, runs preview generation in background tasks, supports copy/print, selection drag (HTML), and highlights search matches using mark.js integration

- New/updated preview layout implementations and interfaces
  - PreviewLayout interface introduced for consistent layout generation
  - TextBasedPreviewLayout: implements the customizable preview style (based on existing custom export filters). Stores/loads text and builds a Layout for rendering
  - CitationStylePreviewLayout: wraps citation-style based layouts (CSL) and exposes source/file path
  - BstPreviewLayout: supports BST-based preview files (parses and runs a VM, post-processes results and cleans LaTeX)

- Preferences persistence and API updates
  - JabRefPreferences: adds preview-related preference keys and load/store logic (cycle of preview layouts, current position, panel height, preview style text, show-as-tab flag)
  - Migration/backwards compatibility: ensures at least default text preview exists in cycle if none stored

- UX and bugfixes/workarounds
  - WebView theme handling: work around JavaFX bug by loading dark theme CSS as data URL when needed
  - PreviewViewer registers for active search query updates and highlights matches inside the rendered preview
  - Improved preview update behavior (background generation with progress messages and error handling)

Notes for reviewers/testing:
- New preferences should be visible in Preferences → Entry preview and persisted across restarts
- Try adding/removing/reordering layouts, editing a Text-based preview, and ensuring preview updates when switching selections/losing focus
- Test drag-and-drop of files onto the preview (copy/move/link depending on modifier keys) and selection drag from preview (HTML)
- Verify citation styles are discovered and added to the available list (discovery runs asynchronously)

This change centralizes and modernizes preview functionality and preferences, and enables flexible preview customization for users (text-based, CSL, BST).

Add right-click context menu for main table header and support utilities

What I changed
- Introduced MainTableHeaderRightClickMenu: a ContextMenu shown on right-clicking the main table header. It lists the current table columns as radio menu items, allows removing a column from the table, and includes a shortcut to open the Preferences dialog on the Table tab.
- Hooked the menu into MainTable constructor so it is registered for the main table.
- Added MainTableColumnFactory.createColumn(MainTableColumnModel): a factory method that creates a specific column instance for a given column model (index, groups, files, identifiers, library name, extra files, special fields, normal fields).
- Exposed PreferencesDialogView.getPreferenceTabList() so callers can programmatically select a preferences tab (used by the new context menu to open the Table preferences).
- Added TableTab.getList() to expose the TableView of MainTableColumnModel for potential external use.
- Minor whitespace/indentation cleanup in MainTable and small formatting adjustments; no behavioral changes intended in those sections.

Why
- The new header context menu provides a quick way to manage table columns (remove a column) and jump directly to the Table preferences.
- The factory method centralizes creating a column from a column model which helps when adding columns dynamically or from UI actions.

Notes and caveats
- The context menu currently removes columns but add-column logic in the menu is only a stub (createColumn is invoked but the created column is not added back to the table). Additional work may be required to support adding columns back via the menu.
- MainTableHeaderRightClickMenu uses the PreferencesDialogView to open the preferences and selects the Table tab index (3). This relies on the exposed getPreferenceTabList method.
- Some debug prints and a static reference to MainTable are present in the new context menu implementation and may need cleanup later.

- Ensures a consistent error response for clients

- Handler logs the full exception (stack trace and context) and returns a generic 500 response
- Configuration flag added to control whether detailed error information is included in responses (defaults to false in production)
- Unit and integration tests added to cover handler behavior

Backward compatibility:
- Default behavior is safe and backward-compatible; existing specific exception handlers still take precedence
- Handler can be disabled or tuned via the provided configuration option

Testing:
- Tests verify that unhandled exceptions are caught, logged, and produce the expected 500 response
- Tests also cover configuration that toggles detailed error output

Notes for reviewers:
- Check logging format and sensitivity of any data included in logs
- Confirm configuration names and default values align with project conventions

Add PersonNamesChecker to validate person/company name fields and corresponding unit tests

Summary:
- Introduces PersonNamesChecker, an integrity checker that validates values intended to contain person (author/editor) names.
- Adds PersonNamesCheckerTest to cover expected valid and invalid inputs.

Behavior:
- Ignores blank values.
- Detects leading/trailing separators (e.g., starting/ending with "and" or commas) and reports localized messages suggesting the field should start/end with a name.
- Strips braces (using RemoveBrackets) so corporate names in braces (e.g., "{JabRef}") are treated correctly.
- Parses the value with AuthorList and ensures the supplied string matches one of the two standard BibTeX name formats: "Last, First and ..." or "First Last and ...". If not, it returns a localized error that includes the database mode name (BibTeX/biblatex).

Tests added:
- Valid single and multi-author forms in both "Last, First" and "First Last" styles.
- Rejects a malformed string with too many commas.
- Accepts initials-only names (e.g., "M. J. Gotay").
- Accepts corporate names in braces and combinations of corporate + person names.

Notes:
- The checker relies on AuthorList parsing logic and RemoveBrackets to handle a range of name edge cases (initials, von/jr parts, hyphens, and braced parts).
- Error messages are localized via Localization.lang(...) and include the formatted database mode name.

text:
Add OpenOffice/LibreOffice bibliography integration: introduce OOBibBase and OOBibStyle classes to manage citations and bibliographies in Writer documents.

Key points:
- OOBibBase
  - Connects to a running OpenOffice/LibreOffice instance and enumerates Writer documents.
  - Selects and binds to a document, accesses its text, bookmarks and reference marks.
  - Insert and refresh citation markers: insertEntry(), refreshCiteMarkers(), insertReferenceMark(), removeReferenceMark().
  - Builds and rebuilds a bibliography text section in the document: createBibTextSection2(), clearBibTextSectionContent2(), populateBibTextSection(), rebuildBibTextSection().
  - Combines adjacent cite markers when appropriate (combineCiteMarkers()).
  - Supports numbered and author-year citation styles, multi-cite sorting, uniquefiers and page info storage as custom document properties.
  - Finds cited keys/entries across provided databases and can generate a standalone BibDatabase containing only cited entries (generateDatabase()).
  - Utilities: parseRefMarkName(), getCitationContext(), getUniqueReferenceMarkName(), getSortedReferenceMarks() and related helpers.
  - Robust handling for UNO exceptions and disposed connections (wraps DisposedException into ConnectionLostException where necessary).

- OOBibStyle
  - Represents a bibliography style for OpenOffice; can be loaded from a file or an internal resource.
  - Parses style files into sections (NAME, LAYOUT, PROPERTIES, CITATION, JOURNALS) and exposes properties for citation formatting.
  - Supports granular citation configuration: brackets, separators, bibtex-key citations, number grouping, italics/bold, character format, et al. handling, Oxford comma, etc.
  - Provides formatting helpers: getCitationMarker(), getNumCitationMarker(), insertPageInfo(), createAuthorList(), getReferenceFormat() and layout mapping per entry type.
  - Automatically maintains a local copy of the loaded style and can reload when the underlying file changes (ensureUpToDate()).
  - Integrates with JabRef layout/formatter infrastructure (Layout, LayoutHelper, LayoutFormatterPreferences, OOPreFormatter).

Other notes:
- Includes extensive parsing and formatting logic for different citation scenarios (bibtex key markers, numbered markers, author-year in-text and parenthetical markers), uniquefier grouping and normalized markers used for uniqueness detection.
- Emphasizes safety when applying character formats to citations by testing formats before removing existing reference marks to avoid document corruption.

This change brings a full-featured OpenOffice bibliography backend to the codebase, enabling insertion, updating and formatting of citations and bibliographies inside Writer documents using JabRef styles and layout formatters.

Add remote client and server lifecycle management for JabRef's remote operation

- RemoteClient
  - Implements ping() and sendCommandLineArguments(String[] args) to communicate with a running JabRef instance via the Protocol abstraction.
  - Uses a socket with a 1000ms timeout (TIMEOUT constant) and connects to the IP configured in RemotePreferences.
  - Properly sends RemoteMessage enums and validates responses (expects PONG with Protocol.IDENTIFIER for ping).
  - Handles IOExceptions gracefully and logs debug messages on failures. On unexpected responses during ping, logs an error with a localized message advising to try another port.
  - Uses try-with-resources to ensure Protocol/socket resources are closed.

- RemoteListenerServerLifecycle
  - New lifecycle manager for RemoteListenerServerThread exposing open, start, stop, openAndStart and close methods.
  - Handles BindException when trying to open the configured port and logs a clear warning to instruct the user that the port might already be in use.
  - Ensures safe thread lifecycle: start only manages the thread via JabRefExecutorService if the thread is open and hasn't been started before (checks Thread.State.NEW).
  - stop() interrupts the server thread, clears the reference and stops the managed remote thread in JabRefExecutorService; close() delegates to stop().
  - Robust handling of IOExceptions during opening of the server thread.

Overall this change centralizes and hardens remote operation support: it adds a small timeout for socket operations, explicit lifecycle control for the server thread, improved logging and localized user-facing error messages for port conflicts and communication failures.

What this PR does
- Disable the entry preview 'fit to width' behavior by default. New installations will have fit-to-width turned off so images and PDFs are shown at their native size unless the user explicitly enables fit-to-width. This avoids unexpected zooming and layout changes that confused many users (refs #8146, #6348).

- Rename linked file settings for clarity. The settings and UI labels related to linked file handling have been renamed to clearer, more consistent wording. Preference keys have been migrated so existing user settings are preserved.

Why
- Many users expect preview content to display at its natural size and were surprised by the automatic scaling when fit-to-width was enabled by default. Turning it off by default reduces confusion while keeping the option easily available.
- The linked file settings terminology was inconsistent and confusing. The renaming improves discoverability and makes the intent of each option clearer.

Compatibility / Migration
- Existing users keep their current fit-to-width preference (no forced change); only new installations get fit-to-width disabled by default.
- Preference keys for the renamed linked-file settings are migrated at startup, so users' current settings continue to work after the update.

Testing / QA notes
- Manual testing performed in running JabRef to verify: default fit-to-width off on fresh profile; toggle still works from the preview toolbar; existing profiles retain their fit-to-width value.
- Verify the renamed settings appear in Preferences and that values from old keys are preserved after migration.

Related
- Fixes #8146
- Fixes #6348

Checklist (left for maintainer review)
- CHANGELOG entry: not included in this PR
- Tests: none added (manual testing performed)
- Documentation: consider updating user docs to reflect the renamed settings and default behavior

text: Add DublinCoreExtractor to map between DublinCore XMP metadata and JabRef BibEntry objects. The extractor reads common DC properties (creator/contributor, title, description, date, identifier, publisher, subjects, type, rights, source) and maps them to the corresponding BibTeX fields (author, editor, title, abstract, year/month, doi, publisher, keywords, entry type, and unknown fields for rights/source). Dates are parsed robustly via DateConverter and the extractor avoids treating a default 1-Jan value as a real month (to prevent spurious month values). Custom BibTeX fields are supported via dc:relation entries prefixed with bibtex/, and month parsing is handled specially to override corrupted XMP month values. Writing back to XMP is supported via fillDublinCoreSchema: field values are collected and written to the DC schema (with lexicographic ordering), privacy-filtered fields are skipped, keywords are split/added, and the PDF format and entry type are recorded. extractBibtexEntry returns Optional.empty when no fields were extracted. Overall this improves XMP import/export fidelity and preserves custom BibTeX fields in PDF metadata.

Summary

Details

- Add defensive null checks and state checks to prevent potential NPEs during shutdown or restart.
- Improve logging of monitor lifecycle events and error conditions to make debugging easier.

Why
- Users reported sporadic issues where the file update monitor did not stop correctly or threw exceptions when the application was closing or when libraries were reloaded. These changes make the monitor more robust and easier to diagnose.

Testing
- Covered basic start/stop scenarios and verified that resources are released on stop. Logging was added to assist future troubleshooting.

Notes
- No public API changes; behavior preserved except for improved stability and cleanup.

Refactor and rename serialization/parse APIs for metadata, entry types, groups and save order

Summary
- Renamed and standardized methods for converting objects to string lists and parsing from string lists: e.g. convertToString() -> getAsStringList(), parseFromString() -> parse(), serialize() -> getAsStringMap().
- Moved parsing responsibilities into model classes and provided factory/parse methods where appropriate (MetaData.parse, GroupTreeNode.parse, CustomEntryType.parse, SaveOrderConfig.parse, BibDatabaseMode.parse).
- Made several constructors private and exposed static parse(...) factory methods to centralize parsing logic and improve encapsulation.
- Removed CustomEntryTypesManager.parseEntryType and moved its logic into CustomEntryType.parse; added CustomEntryType.getAsString() for serialization.
- Reduced visibility of GroupsParser (package-private) and added GroupTreeNode.parse as the public entry point to parse groups.
- Updated all call sites to use the new method names and factories (BibtexParser, JabRefPreferences, CleanupPreset, BibDatabaseWriter, MetaDataTest, etc.).

Files/changes of note
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/MetaData.java: constructor made private; added MetaData.parse(Map) factory; renamed serialize() -> getAsStringMap(); updated usages and parsing to use new parse/getAsStringList helpers; switched to GroupTreeNode.parse and SaveOrderConfig.parse and FieldFormatterCleanups.parse.
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/exporter/BibDatabaseWriter.java: now uses metaData.getAsStringMap(); CustomEntryType serialization uses customType.getAsString().
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/logic/cleanup/CleanupPreset.java and src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/JabRefPreferences.java: updated to use FieldFormatterCleanups.getAsStringList() and FieldFormatterCleanups.parse().
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/exporter/FieldFormatterCleanups.java: renamed convertToString() -> getAsStringList(), parseFromString() -> parse().
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/importer/fileformat/BibtexParser.java: uses MetaData.parse(...) and CustomEntryType.parse(...).
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/logic/groups/GroupTreeNode.java and GroupsParser.java: added GroupTreeNode.parse(...) wrapper; made GroupsParser package-private.
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/model/entry/CustomEntryType.java: added parse(...) and getAsString(); moved entrytype comment parsing here.
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/logic/config/SaveOrderConfig.java and src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/model/database/BibDatabaseMode.java: added parse(...) factory methods, made constructors private, and added getAsString() for BibDatabaseMode.
- Tests updated (MetaDataTest) to use new method names.

Rationale
- Unify method names and responsibilities for serialization and parsing to make the API clearer and more consistent.
- Improve encapsulation by moving parsing logic into the related model classes and exposing controlled factories instead of public constructors or scattered parsers.
- Reduce the public surface area of internal parser helpers (GroupsParser) while preserving compatibility via wrapper methods.

- This is a refactor-only change; functionality is preserved but several public method names and constructors have changed. Tests
- Updated MetaDataTest expectations to reflect the renamed methods.

This WIP pull request introduces a new fetcher for APS. The fetcher is intended to retrieve data from the APS service/endpoint and integrate it with our existing fetcher framework.

What this change adds

- A new fetcher module: src/fetchers/aps_fetcher (implementation and interface glue)
- Config options: configuration keys and environment variables to set APS endpoint, credentials, and fetch parameters
- Basic authentication support and request scaffolding (token-based auth placeholder)
- Pagination handling and retry/backoff skeleton
- Logging and error handling stubs consistent with other fetchers
- Documentation stub explaining configuration and usage
- Unit test placeholders and initial tests for request construction and basic parsing

Why

We need a dedicated component to pull data from APS in a consistent, testable way that aligns with our existing fetcher architecture. This enables downstream processing pipelines to consume APS data without ad-hoc integration code.

How to review / test

- Look at src/fetchers/aps_fetcher for structure and how it implements the fetcher interface
- Configure environment variables or config file to point to an APS test endpoint and set credentials
- Run the unit tests: `yarn test` / `go test` / `pytest` (project-specific command) — note some integration tests are not included yet
- Manually exercise the fetcher via the existing fetcher runner (example):
  - Set APS_ENDPOINT and APS_TOKEN
  - Run the fetcher and verify logs show successful requests and parsed output

- Complete full authentication flow (refresh tokens / OAuth) for APS
- Flesh out robust pagination handling for large datasets
- Add comprehensive integration tests against a real or mocked APS instance
- Implement caching and rate-limit handling if required by APS
- Finalize documentation and examples
- Remove WIP flag and ensure CI passes before merging

Notes

- This is intended to be non-breaking: existing fetchers remain unchanged
- Requesting early feedback on module structure, config approach, and placement within the fetcher registry

text: This pull request replaces the existing citation style processor with the V8 engine, which significantly improves performance when previewing citations. To achieve this, platform-dependent JARs are built using the `javaFlavours` plugin, and the `ShadowJar` task is used to create fat jars for each platform. text:
Summary

This PR refactors and improves how JabRef performs saves, autosaves, and backups. It centralizes save logic, introduces safer atomic file writes, improves autosave scheduling/throttling and UI feedback, and fixes related issues to avoid data loss and redundant disk writes.

Key changes

- Centralized save management: Introduce/extend GlobalSaveManager to become the single place for save operations; SaveAction, SaveAllAction and SaveDatabaseAction now use the centralized API.
- Atomic writes: Add AtomicFileOutputStream and switch file writers (JabRefFileWriter and exporters) to use atomic file output to ensure incomplete writes cannot leave damaged database files.
- Autosave and backup improvements: Refactor AutosaveManager and BackupManager to improve coordination with the centralized save manager and to ensure backups and autosaves are scheduled and executed reliably.
- Autosave throttling: Add DelayTaskThrottler to debounce/throttle frequent save/autosave requests so we avoid excessive disk writes while still persisting data in a timely manner.
- UI integration and events: Add AutosaveEvent and AutosaveUiManager to provide UI feedback about autosave progress and status; JabRefFrame and SharedDatabaseLoginDialogViewModel updated to integrate with autosave/login behaviors.
- Exporter changes: Update TemplateExporter and MSBibExporter to use the new safe file writing approach (through JabRefFileWriter/AtomicFileOutputStream).
- Tests: Update SaveDatabaseActionTest to reflect new save flow and ensure save behavior correctness.
- CLI and startup: Minor adjustments in ArgumentProcessor to align with the new saving/backup/autosave flow.

Motivation

These changes aim to make save operations more robust (preventing partial or corrupted files), reduce unnecessary I/O from frequent saves, and provide better user feedback about autosave/backup operations. Centralizing save logic also reduces duplication and makes future changes easier.

Notes for reviewers

- Focus on the GlobalSaveManager and AtomicFileOutputStream to validate correctness and exception handling for atomic replacements.
- Verify that autosave throttling behavior matches expected timing (DelayTaskThrottler) and that AutosaveEvent notifications are emitted where appropriate.
- Ensure that exporters still produce identical output and that tests cover critical save scenarios.

text:
Fixes #2789 — Add Referer header to IEEEXplore API calls

Summary:
- Add a Referer HTTP header to requests made by the IEEEXplore fetcher to satisfy the API/server requirement that rejects requests without a valid referer.
- This resolves the reported "Invalid search term" error when performing web searches with the IEEEXplore fetcher.

Why:
- IEEEXplore returns an error for requests that lack an expected Referer header. Adding the header makes requests appear to come from a valid source and allows searches to succeed.

Implementation:
- Set the Referer header (for example: https://ieeexplore.ieee.org or the appropriate JabRef search URL) on outgoing HTTP requests from the IEEEXplore fetcher.
- Change is limited to the fetcher/network call; no external API or UI changes.

Testing / QA steps:
1. Start JabRef (version 4.0.0-beta or later with this change).
2. Perform a web search using the IEEEXplore fetcher (use an example search term that previously returned "Invalid search term").
3. Verify that results are now returned instead of the error.

Notes:
- No breaking changes; behavior is backward compatible.
- Fixes the original report in issue #2789.

text:
Add LocalizationConsistencyTest to validate and enforce consistency of localization property files

What this PR does
- Introduces LocalizationConsistencyTest which adds a set of unit tests to verify the correctness of localization files (for both "JabRef" and "Menu" bundles).
- Tests implemented:
  - allFilesMustHaveSameKeys: Ensures all language property files contain the same keys as the English reference.
  - ensureNoDuplicates: Detects duplicate keys in any properties file (uses DuplicationDetectionProperties to capture duplicates while loading).
  - keyValueShouldBeEqualForEnglishPropertiesMenu / keyValueShouldBeEqualForEnglishPropertiesMessages: Ensures English message/menu files have values equal to their keys (menu test strips ampersands used for mnemonics).
  - findMissingLocalizationKeys / findMissingMenuLocalizationKeys: Scans source for localization keys that are missing in the properties files and prints snippets to paste into the English and non-English files.
  - findObsoleteLocalizationKeys / findObsoleteMenuLocalizationKeys: Detects obsolete keys present in English properties that are not referenced in source and fails with instructions to remove them.

Why
- Keep localization files synchronized across languages.
- Prevent duplication and stale entries in .properties files which can cause runtime issues or untranslated UI strings.

Developer notes / How to fix test failures
- If tests report missing keys, the test prints out blocks you can paste into the English properties file and blank entries for non-English files. After adding to English, run:
  gradlew -b localization.gradle generateMissingTranslationKeys
  to propagate keys to other languages.
- If tests report obsolete keys, remove the printed keys from the English properties file and then run the generator to remove them from non-English files.
- Run gradlew check (or your IDE test runner) to run the new tests.

Formatting / contribution reminders
- Follow the project contribution guidelines: run gradlew format when needed and add appropriate CHANGELOG entries if this change is user-visible.

This PR aims to prevent regressions in localization and make it easier for contributors to keep language files consistent.

Disable Google Scholar integration tests on all CI environments to avoid spurious failures caused by Google blocking CI servers.

What I changed:
- Updated GoogleScholarTest.java: replaced per-service CI checks (CircleCI/SnapCI) with a single DevEnvironment.isCIServer() check in all affected tests (linkFound, noLinkFound, findSingleEntry, find20Entries).

Google blocks requests originating from CI infrastructure causing the Google Scholar fetcher tests to fail on CI. The tests already had comments suggesting they should be disabled on CI; this change makes that explicit and applies it to all CI providers by using the generic CI environment variable.

Notes:
- This is a temporary measure to keep CI green. We can revert these changes once the Google Scholar fetcher tests are fixed or an alternative testing strategy is in place.
- Related issue: refs #2173.

Fix NumberFormatException thrown by BracketedPattern parsing.

Summary:
- Prevents Integer.parseInt from being called on empty or non-numeric tokens when parsing bracket expressions, which previously resulted in an uncaught NumberFormatException.

Cause:
- The bracket-range parsing logic attempted to parse numeric endpoints without sufficient validation of the token content. Malformed or empty numeric components triggered NumberFormatException.

What I changed:
- Added validation checks for numeric tokens before attempting to parse them.
- Added defensive parsing (and a controlled catch) to convert parse errors into a clear, descriptive pattern-syntax error instead of an NFE.
- Tightened boundary checks for range endpoints.
- Added unit tests that cover empty, non-numeric and other malformed bracket patterns as well as the previously failing case(s).

Compatibility / behavior changes:

- Enable multi-selection deletion when using Remove groups > Keep… so users can delete more than one group in a single action.
- Update the frontend to allow selecting multiple groups, show a combined confirmation dialog (listing names and count), and prevent accidental deletion of protected/default groups.

- Tests: added unit and integration tests covering multiple-group deletion, permission enforcement, and error cases.

Behavior notes
- Previously only single-group deletion was supported; this PR restores and extends that capability to multiple groups.
- Default/system groups remain protected and cannot be deleted; attempting to include them will show a descriptive error.
- Deletions are transactional: either all selected groups are deleted or none are, with errors reported back to the UI.

Manual QA steps
1. Select multiple non-protected groups in the groups list. 2. Choose Remove groups > Keep… 3. Confirm deletion in the dialog (verify names and count). 4. Verify groups are removed and no partial deletions occurred.

No database migrations are required.

- Problem: When importing annotations, the map key used to store annotations was file.toString() (full path). This produced keys containing the full file path, which can differ across environments and didn’t match other code expecting just the filename.

Summary
Add listening for change events to automatically set the database "dirty" status when data is modified.

Why
Previously the database dirty flag was not consistently updated when records were created, updated, or deleted. This caused the UI and other consumers to miss unsaved changes and to behave incorrectly after in-memory modifications.

What I changed
- Subscribed the Database to relevant change events (add/update/remove/destroy/change) emitted by models/collections so any in-memory modification will set database.isDirty = true.
- Reset the dirty flag when a successful save/commit occurs (save/transaction completion handlers clear the flag).
- Ensure listeners are removed when the database or connections are closed to avoid memory leaks.
- Added unit tests to cover: marking dirty on create/update/delete, clearing after save, and proper cleanup of listeners.

Notes for reviewers
- Main logic lives in the Database event handling layer and the save/commit paths. Please pay attention to the event selection to ensure we don’t mark dirty for ephemeral/read-only events.
- No breaking changes expected; behavior improves correctness for tracking unsaved changes.

text:
Add TitleChecker to integrity checks with unit tests

This PR implements a TitleChecker that verifies title capitalization for BibTeX-mode databases and integrates it into the integrity check suite. Key behavior:
- Skips checks when the database is in biblatex mode.
- Removes any text inside curly braces before performing checks (so intentionally-protected capitals are ignored).
- Splits titles into subtitles on delimiters (., !, ?, ;, :) and ignores the first character of each subtitle (first letter may be capitalized).
- Flags subtitles that contain additional unprotected uppercase/titlecase letters as an integrity warning with the message "capital letters are not masked using curly brackets {}".

Included tests (TitleCheckerTest and updates in IntegrityCheckTest) cover many cases:
- Subtitles separated by different delimiters and by continuous delimiters (e.g. "...", "!!").
- Titles where capitals are correctly masked with curly braces.
- Titles where unmasked internal capitals are detected.
- Ensures behavior differs correctly between BibTeX and BibLaTeX modes.

This change improves automated detection of improperly protected capital letters in titles, helping users keep .bib files BibTeX-compatible.

Fix cookie and redirect handling for remote downloads and the arXiv fetcher.

What I changed

- Implemented/updated CookieHandlerImpl to properly collect Set-Cookie headers and provide Cookie headers for subsequent requests.

Summary

Temporarily remove the custom SSL truststore configuration to help diagnose and isolate the cause of https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/9171. The code that created/forced a custom truststore and set the javax.net.ssl system properties is commented out.

What changed

- File modified: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/JabRefMain.java
- The following lines were commented out in configureSSL(SSLPreferences):
  - TrustStoreManager.createTruststoreFileIfNotExist(Path.of(sslPreferences.getTruststorePath()));
  - System.setProperty("javax.net.ssl.trustStore", sslPreferences.getTruststorePath());
  - System.setProperty("javax.net.ssl.trustStorePassword", "changeit");

Why

- Previously JabRef set a custom truststore and password on startup. That can override the JVM/system defaults and may be the root cause of the HTTPS/connectivity issue tracked in #9171.
- By disabling this custom configuration we can determine whether the problem goes away when the application uses the JVM/system truststore.

Impact

- JabRef will no longer force a custom truststore from user preferences at startup. It will fall back to the JVM/system default truststore behavior.
- This is intended as a temporary change for debugging. If needed, the configuration can be restored or replaced with a different approach after the root cause is identified.

Testing notes / How to validate

- Verify that HTTPS-based features still work (e.g. fetching metadata, remote content download, web-based integrations).
- Check behavior on systems where a custom truststore was previously required to ensure we understand regressions.
- Compare behavior before and after this change to see if it resolves the issue referenced in #9171.

Follow-ups

- If this change fixes #9171, consider a more robust approach: document the reason for custom truststore usage and implement a less intrusive solution (or better error handling and informative messaging for users who need custom certificates).
- Update CHANGELOG.md and user/developer documentation if a permanent change to SSL handling is decided.

Fixes #2762 — CSV export now separates all author and editor names with semicolons instead of the word "and".

What I changed
- Added a new LayoutFormatter (AuthorAndToSemicolonReplacer) that replaces occurrences of " and " with "; ".
- Registered the new formatter in LayoutEntry so it can be used by layouts.
- Updated the OpenOffice CSV layout (openoffice-csv.layout) to use the new formatter for both author and editor fields.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to describe the change.
- Added tests: AuthorAndToSemicolonReplacerTest (parameterized unit tests for the formatter) and CsvExportFormatTest (integration-style tests verifying single and multiple authors/editors are exported with semicolons).

Why
Previously the CSV export left the word "and" between names, which is inconvenient for CSV consumers that expect semicolon-separated name lists. This change produces semicolon-separated names for authors and editors in CSV exports.

Notes
- All changes are covered by tests and were manually tested in a running JabRef instance.
- Documentation/help pages may need updating (issue created on help.jabref.org as noted).

Fixes #7387 — Correct Unicode-to-LaTeX conversion for characters above the 'char' range

What I changed
- Fixed an issue where the Unicode-to-LaTeX formatter processed text as Java char units and therefore split surrogate pairs, producing incorrect conversions for code points greater than the maximum value of the primitive type char (supplementary characters, e.g. U+1XXXX).
- Reworked the formatter to be code point–aware (using code point iteration / proper surrogate pair handling) so supplementary Unicode characters are handled correctly during conversion.

Why this was necessary
- The previous implementation could produce wrong LaTeX escapes or corrupted output for characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane because it treated each UTF-16 code unit independently.

Tests and verification
- Added unit tests that cover conversion of supplementary Unicode characters to ensure correct output.
- Manually tested the changed features in a running JabRef instance.

Other notes
- CHANGELOG.md updated to reflect the fix.
- No UI changes or screenshots.
- Documentation not changed as this is an internal formatter bug fix.

text:
Fixes #9312 — Change database structure to avoid very generic table names and add schema support for PostgreSQL.

What this PR does
- PostgreSQL: adds a new schema named `jabref`. Table names remain unchanged but are now scoped to the `jabref` schema.
- MySQL / MariaDB: prefixes all JabRef tables with `JABREF_` to avoid name clashes with existing databases.
- Oracle: kept code unchanged as much as possible.
- Table fields/schema (columns) are unchanged — only table naming/placement changed.

Versioning & automatic migration
- Introduces a new variable `VersionDBStructure` in the `METADATA` table to record the database-structure version.
- At startup (checkBaseIntegrity / VersionDBStructure) JabRef compares the DB structure version in the database with the expected version and will perform an automatic migration when required.
- IMPORTANT: to prevent data loss, old tables are NOT deleted by the migration. After migration, legacy tables must be removed manually once you have verified that everything works.

Notes for users and DB administrators
- Automatic migration will be applied where needed; verify backups before upgrading.
- After successful migration, you may drop the old/legacy tables manually.

Other changes
- Tests added for the changes where applicable.
- CHANGELOG and developer/user documentation checked/updated as needed.
- Manually tested in a running JabRef build.

Checklist (from PR)
- CHANGELOG: updated
- Tests: created where applicable
- Manual testing: done
- Developer & user docs: checked/updated

- XmpParser.* (parsing + exception handling)

Summary of changes

- Web search UX and fetch flow
  - WebSearchPaneViewModel: detect DOIs and ISBNs in the query and dispatch to the dedicated DoiFetcher/IsbnFetcher before using the selected SearchBasedFetcher. Runs searches in a background task and shows results in ImportEntriesDialog. Improves reliability of direct ID lookups and user feedback.

- Import cleanup utility
  - Added ImportCleanup to perform post-import format conversion of BibEntry objects and collections (ConvertToBibtexCleanup / ConvertToBiblatexCleanup) depending on target BibDatabaseMode.

- arXiv fetcher improvements
  - Major enhancements to ArXiv fetcher: robust API query construction, paging support, id-based lookup, improved parsing of Atom responses, clearer error handling for API error responses, and limits validation (max results).
  - ArXivEntry inner class maps parsed Atom nodes to BibEntry fields (title, authors, abstract, date, eprint, eprintclass, doi, journal reference) and captures PDF links as LinkedFile entries.
  - Added performSearchPaged, performSearchById, findIdentifier and findFullText functionality; properly marks trust level as PREPRINT.

- Integrity checks
  - IntegrityCheck orchestrates field and entry checkers and includes an overall database DOI duplication check. In biblatex mode, UTF8Checker and JournalInAbbreviationListChecker are included; in bibtex mode, ASCIICharacterChecker and other bibtex-specific checks are applied.

- UTF-8 encoding validation
  - New UTF8Checker verifies that entry fields are UTF-8 encoded using the system file.encoding and a CharsetDecoder. Provides UTF8EncodingChecker utility for byte[] checks and returns IntegrityMessage for non-UTF-8 fields.

- UI / theming
  - Base.css: refined theme variables and styling rules (colors, accents, toolbar, controls, selection behaviors, tooltips, etc.) to consolidate application look-and-feel and make derived color usage consistent.

- Localization
  - JabRef_en.properties: updated/added localization strings (including messages relating to web search, DOI handling and customization, and other UI texts).

- Tests
  - Added/updated unit tests for ArXiv (ArXivTest), IntegrityCheck (IntegrityCheckTest) and UTF8Checker (UTF8CheckerTest) to cover search, id lookup, encoding detection and overall integrity behavior.

Notes
- Many changes focus on robustness (better error handling, parsing, background task management) and on providing more accurate/expected behavior when a user enters identifiers (DOI/ISBN/arXiv id) or performs web searches. Import and post-import conversion are centralized via ImportCleanup to ensure consistency between bibtex and biblatex workflows.

Summary
This PR improves the built-in issue reporting by automatically including log/environment details in the generated report text so users do not need to paste them manually.

Background / motivation
See #2573. The previous attempt to include arguments (see PR #1383) relied on an explorer mechanism that truncates long arguments on some platforms, so users still had to paste missing info manually. That is inconvenient; this change provides the most relevant log and environment details directly in the report.

What changed
- Append relevant log and environment details to the generated issue body when opening the "Submit issue" dialog.
- Include JabRef version, Java version, OS, and recent log excerpts so maintainers have more context immediately.

Limitations
- Very long command-line arguments can still be truncated by the OS/explorer; this PR mitigates the manual work but cannot fully bypass OS-level truncation in all cases.

How to test
1. Open Help → Submit issue. 2. Verify that the issue text contains JabRef version, Java version, OS details and a short excerpt from the log. 3. Confirm that you no longer need to paste log details manually.

Related
Closes #2573. References PR #1383 for prior behavior.

This PR fixes and clarifies the command-line help text and option descriptions for JabRef's CLI. It rewrites argument descriptions, improves formatting, and fixes several incorrect or ambiguous messages so the help output is easier to read and understand. This addresses issue #2016.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/cli/JabRefCLI.java
  - Reworked many option descriptions and arg names to be clearer and consistent.

The previous CLI help had several errors, unclear argument formats, and inconsistent descriptions. These changes make the output more accurate and user-friendly and prevent confusion when using command-line options.

- There are no functional changes to option handling beyond argument/description formatting, though argName strings were standardized.

Major refactor: introduce and adopt BibDatabaseContext and strengthen save/open/export/import and backup/autosave flows

Summary
- Introduce BibDatabaseContext to encapsulate a BibDatabase together with its metadata, file path, encoding and preferences. Move codepaths to work with BibDatabaseContext instead of raw BibDatabase where appropriate.
- Update UI and actions (JabRefGUI, JabRefFrame, OpenDatabaseAction, SaveDatabaseAction) to open, save and manage databases through BibDatabaseContext.
- Update exporters/writers (BibDatabaseWriter, BibtexDatabaseWriter) to accept/operate with the new context and to respect encoding/metadata when writing files.
- Update import pipeline: ParserResult and BibtexParser changes to better surface parsing results/warnings and integrate with the context-based flow. Adjusted related tests.
- Backup/autosave improvements: BackupManager logic updated to work with the context and avoid incorrect assumptions; AutosaveUIManager and BackupUIManager updated to reflect changes. SharedDatabaseUIManager updated similarly.
- Shared database support: add NotASharedDatabaseException and SharedDatabasePreferences to model and manage shared-database behavior and preferences. UI now better handles shared DB scenarios and exceptions.

Why
- Centralizing file/encoding/metadata information in BibDatabaseContext simplifies downstream logic and reduces duplication and bugs related to missing context (file path, encoding, metadata).
- This refactor enables more robust autosave/backup behavior and better handling of shared databases, while making export/import flows clearer and less error-prone.

Tests
- Updated BibtexParserTest and BibtexImporterTest to reflect parser changes and to assert ParserResult behavior.

Compatibility / Notes
- Public APIs that previously accepted BibDatabase may now accept BibDatabaseContext; callers in the codebase have been updated accordingly. External extensions/plugins may need to be adjusted if they relied on old method signatures.
- Error handling for shared databases has been made explicit via NotASharedDatabaseException; callers should handle this where relevant.

- Notes: This is a pragmatic workaround that does not use the APS Harvest API (which requires keys/headers). Also updates the changelog to mention the new APS fetcher.

Fixes issue #6197 — prevent downloading a file when the same file is already attached to the entry. Instead of blindly downloading and overwriting or renaming, JabRef now detects the conflict early and shows an error dialog informing the user that the file already exists.

- Modified src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/LinkedFileViewModel.java
- In prepareDownloadTask(), compute the suggested file name and the final non-overwriting name. If the computed final name differs from the suggested name (meaning a file with that name already exists), stop the download and build an error message.
- Centralized error reporting in handleDownloadError(...) to show either the custom "file already exists" message or the original exception message.

Behavioral details:
- When attempting to download a file via Lookup -> Search full text documents online, if the same filename is already attached for the entry, a dialog is shown saying the file already exists and the download is canceled.

Testing:
- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance following the reported reproduction steps.
- Screenshots demonstrating the alert were attached in the original issue/PR description.

Notes:
- No unit tests were added for this change (manual verification performed).

- Proper handling of remote links: rename/move are no-ops for online links.
- Uses DialogService (FXDialogService) for confirmations and error dialogs and logs IO issues via Apache Commons logging.
- Uses databaseContext and user preferences (Globals.prefs) to resolve file directories and filename patterns.
- Basic icon support (returns PDF icon by default) with a TODO to infer correct icon from ExternalFileTypes in a future improvement.

The class centralizes cleanup utilities, user prompts and error handling for linked-file interactions, simplifying the entry editor and making behavior consistent across actions.

text:
Summary

- Introduce a centralized key binding system and wire it into UI components.
- Add telemetry opt-in prompt shown shortly after startup.
- Extend action wrapper to allow tracking the user interaction source when sending telemetry.

Details

- Key bindings
  - Added KeyBinding enum and KeyBindingRepository to manage default and custom key bindings.
  - Components now obtain accelerators and resolve key events via KeyBindingRepository (e.g. PreviewPanel uses it to set menu accelerators and to handle the COPY_PREVIEW shortcut).
  - KeyBindingRepository supports loading custom bindings and mapping KeyEvent -> KeyBinding.

- Actions & telemetry
  - JabRefAction extended with an overload that accepts a Sources value so telemetry events can include the UI source (e.g. button/menu).
  - Telemetry helper methods added to send events and include the source property when available.

- UI/frame
  - JabRefFrame: keyboard handling now consults the global key prefs repository for mapped bindings.
  - A tracking/telemetry opt-in prompt is scheduled to appear after a short delay on startup (asks the user to share anonymous statistics). User choice is recorded in preferences.
  - Drag-and-drop, task indicator and progress pop-over code integrated with tabbed pane (no functional change, but integrated with other updates).

- Localization
  - Added English strings for telemetry prompt and related messages in JabRef_en.properties.

Why

- Centralizing key binding logic makes it easier to manage and customize shortcuts and ensures consistent behavior across components.
- Adding action-source-aware telemetry improves analytics granularity while respecting the new opt-in model.

- Verify keyboard shortcuts (default ones) still work across the app and that the PreviewPanel responds to COPY_PREVIEW and preview-cycle shortcuts.
- Check that preview context menu shows keyboard accelerators.

Add Plain References Parser powered by GROBID

This PR integrates a new feature that extracts BibTeX entries from plain text references using a GROBID backend. Key changes:

- Feature: New "Plain References Parser" dialog (ExtractBibtexDialog.fxml / ExtractBibtexDialog) and view model (BibtexExtractorViewModel) that let users paste plain references (separated by double empty lines) and parse them into BibTeX entries.
- GROBID integration: GrobidService implements the HTTP interaction with a GROBID server. GrobidCitationFetcher wraps GrobidService and converts GROBID responses to BibEntry instances. The fetcher splits input on double blank lines and filters blank parts.
- UI integration: The new action is wired into the UI (toolbar & menus) via the existing ExtractBibtexAction. The parse button is disabled until text is entered; a tooltip and prompt text were added.
- Import handling: Parsed entries are imported into the current database using ImportHandler (background task + notifications). Telemetry tracking is performed for parsed entries.
- Tests: Added unit tests for GrobidCitationFetcher and GrobidService to verify parsing, splitting behavior, and server responses (GrobidServiceTest, GrobidCitationFetcherTest).
- Localization: Added strings for the Plain References Parser UI to JabRef_en.properties.

Notes:
- The default GROBID server URL is currently set to http://grobid.cm.in.tum.de:8070 (GrobidService). Network availability of that server affects the service tests.
- Error handling: GrobidService throws IOException for invalid/empty responses; GrobidCitationFetcher filters failed parses and returns an empty list when appropriate.

This change reintroduces the ability to extract references from plain text using GROBID (see changelog entry).

text:
Fixes #6199 — EndNote XML import: correctly import PDF/URL links when not wrapped in a style tag

Problem
- JabRef's EndNote XML importer assumed URL-like content was always wrapped in a <style> element. When publishers or EndNote exports provide the URL as plain text (no style tag), the importer failed to pick up the link.

Solution
- Allow mixed content in the EndNote XML schema by setting the relevant complexType attribute mix=true so elements may contain both child elements and plain text.
- Update the importer parsing logic to check for a style child element: if present, use the text inside it; otherwise use the element's plain text content. This ensures URLs are imported whether or not they are wrapped in style tags.

What I changed
- Modified EndNote XSD (enable mixed content) so the parser can read both subelements and vanilla text.
- Updated EndNote importer code to prefer style element content when present and fall back to plain text when not.
- Added unit tests covering both cases (URL wrapped in style and URL as plain text).
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to describe the user-visible fix.

Testing
- Unit tests added to verify both wrapped and unwrapped URL extraction.

- See issue #420 for background and rationale.

Summary:
Add paging support across the API and client so large result sets can be requested and returned in pages.

What I changed:
- API: Added pagination parameters (page, per_page) to list endpoints and implemented paged queries in controllers/services.
- Response format: List endpoints now include pagination metadata (page, per_page, total_count, total_pages) and optional next/prev links in the response body/headers.
- Client/UI: Updated list views and client fetch logic to request specific pages and render pagination controls.
- Tests: Added/updated unit and integration tests to cover paged responses and boundary cases (first/last page, empty results, invalid params).
- Docs: Documented new query parameters and response format in the API docs and updated README usage examples.

Behavior and usage:
- Default page = 1, default per_page = 20 (configurable).
- Clients can pass ?page=<n>&per_page=<m> to control paging.
- Metadata returned with each list response allows clients to render pagination controls and follow next/prev links.

Backward compatibility:
- Existing endpoints continue to return the same list content by default (page=1, per_page default), so no breaking changes expected.

Notes:
- Per-page limits are enforced to prevent overly large responses.
- See updated tests and API docs for examples of request/response shapes.

Summary

This draft PR implements an option in Preferences to use a custom base URL when opening DOIs. It adds a new "Customization" preference tab where users can enable a custom DOI base URI and enter the base address to be used when opening the DOI field's external link. The feature addresses request #7337.

What changed

- UI
  - Added a new Customization preferences tab (CustomizationTab.fxml, CustomizationTab.java) with a checkbox and text field to enable/enter a custom DOI base URI.
  - Registered the new tab in PreferencesDialogViewModel.
  - Added localization keys for the new UI text (JabRef_en.properties).

- Preferences
  - Introduced DOIPreferences to hold the two DOI-related settings (useCustom, defaultBaseURI).
  - Added methods to PreferencesService and implemented them in JabRefPreferences to load/store these settings, and added sane defaults (USE_CUSTOM_DOI_URI = false, BASE_DOI_URI = "https://doi.org").

- DOI handling
  - DOI model (DOI.java) now exposes getExternalURIWithCustomBase(String) and uses a helper to build URIs from a provided base, so custom bases are respected.

- Editor behavior
  - IdentifierEditorViewModel now receives PreferencesService and, when opening an external link for the DOI field, uses the custom base URI if enabled; otherwise falls back to the default behavior.
  - IdentifierEditor was updated to pass PreferencesService to the view model.

- Tests
  - Updated IdentifierEditorViewModelTest to inject a mocked PreferencesService.

- Misc
  - CHANGELOG updated to mention the new Customization tab and custom DOI URI option.
  - Minor formatting/refactor in GeneralTab (moved ControlsFxVisualizer field).

Files touched (high level)
- Added: src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/preferences/DOIPreferences.java
- Added: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/customization/CustomizationTab.java
- Added: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/customization/CustomizationTabViewModel.java
- Added: src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties (keys)
- Added: src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/customization/CustomizationTab.fxml
- Modified: IdentifierEditor, IdentifierEditorViewModel, DOI model, PreferencesService, JabRefPreferences, PreferencesDialogViewModel, tests, CHANGELOG.md

Behavioral notes

- If "Use custom DOI base URI for article access" is enabled and a base URI is set, clicking the DOI external link will open the DOI using that base. Otherwise the original resolver (https://doi.org) is used.
- The text field input is stored verbatim as the base and used to construct the URI using Java's URI components (scheme/host/path). There is currently no complex validation or normalization (e.g. adding or removing trailing slashes) beyond what URI.create()/URI constructors accept.

Testing & status

- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance; screenshot included in issue/PR description.
- This is submitted as a draft: placement in the preferences UI, exact wording, and validation/normalization of entered base URI can be discussed and improved.

Follow-ups / TODO

- Add validation for the custom base URI (show error/warning when invalid or incomplete).
- Add unit tests for DOI.getExternalURIWithCustomBase and the viewmodel behavior when custom DOI is enabled.
- Consider adding examples or presets (e.g. https://doi.org, https://dx.doi.org) or help text in the UI.

References
- Fixes/addresses: #7337

If you prefer different placement for the setting or different labeling/validation, I can update the UI and behavior accordingly.

Summary

This PR fixes a bug where secondary sorting did not work for some special fields (e.g. Relevancy, Quality, Print status and other special fields) because no comparator was set for those columns. As a result, secondary sort criteria were ignored for those special-field columns.

What I changed

- Added a generic SpecialFieldComparator and use it as the default comparator for special-field columns. This ensures all special fields have a comparator when sortable.
- Kept the RankingFieldComparator for the RANKING special field (it still uses its specific comparator).
- Removed the now-unnecessary ReadStatusFieldComparator file and the old PriorityFieldComparator reference (the new SpecialFieldComparator covers these cases).
- Updated SpecialFieldColumn to set the new comparator for all non-RANKING special fields and made imports reflect the change.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to mention the fix.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/util/comparator/ReadStatusFieldComparator.java — removed
- CHANGELOG.md — added entry about this fix

Why this fixes the issue

Secondary sorting in the main table requires the column to provide a comparator. Previously some special fields did not have a comparator set, so they could not participate correctly in multi-level sorting. By providing a general SpecialFieldComparator for those fields, secondary sorting now works as expected.

Testing

- Unit tests added/updated where applicable.
- Manually tested in the running application (examples shown in the original issue: Relevancy as first criteria and Year as second, both ascending and descending).

- Ranking still uses RankingFieldComparator as before.
