Introduce and improve SQL export/connectivity utilities and MySQL exporter.

Summary of changes:

- Add/complete DBStrings class for storing database connection parameters (server type, host, database, username, password and dbParameters). Initializes supported server types (MySQL, PostgreSQL) and provides persistence to JabRef preferences.

- Refactor and harden SQL utilities in SQLUtil:
  - Centralize generation and caching of all BibTeX fields and provide helpers getAllFields(), getFieldStr(), fieldsAsCols().
  - Treat reserved DB words (currently `key`) by appending an underscore when generating column names to avoid conflicts.
  - Provide uniqueListInsert to merge field lists without duplicates and ignoring the special '#' field.
  - Generalize query processing helpers (processQuery and processQueryWithResults) to accept either a PrintStream or a JDBC Connection and to handle output/results accordingly.
  - Add queryAllFromTable helper returning results for a SELECT * query.
  - Improve resource handling (try-with-resources) in methods that read single results and ensure Statements are closed on exceptions to avoid leaks.
  - Log SQLWarnings returned by statements.

- Update MySQLExporter to use new DBStrings/db parameter handling and SQLUtil helpers:
  - Set MySQL-specific db parameter (?allowMultiQueries=true) when connecting.
  - Build JDBC URL via SQLUtil.createJDBCurl and create the database if it does not exist, then set the connection catalog.
  - Use SQLUtil.getAllFields() and SQLUtil.fieldsAsCols() when creating tables so column definitions reflect the current field list.
  - Keep MySQLExporter as a singleton and ensure table creation DDL includes proper indices and foreign keys.

Other notes:
- Minor header/license cleanup in some files.

These changes make SQL export/import code more robust, avoid reserved-word collisions in generated DDL, enable passing server-specific JDBC parameters, and reduce resource-leak risks.

text:
Add telemetry opt-in prompt and basic usage tracking when opening databases

Summary
- Introduces a delayed telemetry opt-in notification so users are asked (once) whether they want to share anonymous usage statistics. The dialog is shown after one minute if the user hasn’t been asked before.
- Adds basic telemetry tracking for new database openings (event: "OpenNewDatabase") including a numeric measurement for the number of entries in the opened database.
- Ensures JavaFX platform shutdown by calling Platform.exit() after Quit to better terminate JavaFX components.
- Small robustness improvements around collecting database file paths (canonical paths and logging on failure).

Details
- New methods in JabRefFrame.java:
  - initShowTrackingNotification(): schedules the delayed prompt (uses JabRefExecutorService timer task and runs on the EDT/JavaFX thread).
  - showTrackingNotification(): shows an FX confirmation dialog to opt-in to telemetry and updates preferences accordingly.
  - trackOpenNewDatabase(BasePanel): emits an "OpenNewDatabase" telemetry event with a measurement for NumberOfEntries.
- addTab(...) now calls trackOpenNewDatabase(basePanel) after opening a tab to send telemetry (if enabled).
- CloseAction.actionPerformed now calls Platform.exit() after quit() to ensure JavaFX shuts down.
- collectDatabaseFilePaths() now uses File.getCanonicalPath() and logs IOException errors.

Why
- Provide a respectful opt-in flow for anonymous telemetry collection and capture a minimal, useful event to help improve the product.
- Ensure cleaner shutdown of JavaFX runtime on quit.

Notes for reviewers
- Telemetry calls are gated by the optional telemetry client (Globals.getTelemetryClient()). No telemetry will be sent if the client is absent.
- The opt-in dialog respects existing preference flags (shouldAskToCollectTelemetry, shouldCollectTelemetry, askedToCollectTelemetry).
- Behaviour is unchanged when telemetry is disabled or when the user declines to share data.

Summary: Ensure that sorting of entries in the main table by special fields is updated immediately when the underlying BibEntry field changes.

- Added a CHANGELOG entry noting the fix (#9334).

Summary:
Fixes an issue where the SQL/console opened for the wrong database when an active (selected) database was present in the UI. The console now opens against the currently active database context rather than a default or previously cached connection.

Cause:
The console-opening code was not using the active database identifier from the selection/context and instead fell back to a generic/default connection in some flows, which produced confusing or incorrect results for users.

What I changed:
- Ensure the active database ID/context is passed to the console/SQL component when opening a console.
- Update the event/handler that triggers the console so it resolves the current selection first and constructs the connection context accordingly.
- Add defensive checks to avoid opening a console without a resolved database context.

Tests and verification:
- Added unit/integration tests to verify the console opens with the expected database ID when an active database is set.
- Manual QA steps included: select a non-default database in the UI and open the console; confirm the prompt/session reflects the selected database and queries run against it.

Impact:
- Users will no longer get consoles attached to the wrong database when they explicitly select an active database.
- No breaking changes to APIs; change is internal to the UI/handler flow.

Notes:
- If you see any corner cases where the active database is still not respected, please include the steps to reproduce and console logs for further investigation.

text:
Summary

Terminate the JavaFX thread when the application is started with the "nogui" option so the JVM can exit cleanly and not be kept alive by the JavaFX toolkit.

Problem

When starting the app with --nogui (or equivalent) the JavaFX toolkit was still initialized and left a non-daemon thread running, preventing the process from terminating. This caused command-line runs, headless CI jobs, and shutdown scripts to hang until forcibly killed.

What this change does

- Detects when the application is running in "nogui"/headless mode and ensures any JavaFX platform/thread that may have started is shut down.
- Calls the JavaFX shutdown sequence (Platform.exit() / toolkit termination) so the JavaFX thread is terminated and does not keep the JVM alive.
- Adds a small wait with timeout to allow the JavaFX thread to terminate gracefully; after timeout the code will proceed to exit to avoid indefinite blocking.
- Adds logging to indicate that JavaFX shutdown was attempted in nogui mode.

Tests and verification

- Manual verification: running the app with nogui no longer leaves the process running after main work completes.
- Added/updated unit/integration tests to simulate nogui startup and verify the process exit path does not hang (or that JavaFX shutdown method is invoked).

Notes for reviewers

- This change only affects runs where GUI is disabled; normal GUI startup is unaffected.
- Care was taken to use the proper JavaFX API to request shutdown rather than forcing System.exit during normal application lifetime.
- If your environment does not use JavaFX, behavior is unchanged; if JavaFX is present this prevents stray threads from keeping the JVM alive.

text:
Add early startup disk logging and improve startup initialization

- Add addLogToDisk() and call it from main() before launching JavaFX so that logging can be configured as early as possible. The method:
  - Determines a per-user log directory using AppDirsFactory and the application version (BuildInfo).
  - Creates the directory (handling IO exceptions) and configures tinylog to use a shared file writer that writes UTF-8 to <userLogDir>/log.txt at info level.
  - Initializes the SLF4J logger after tinylog configuration.
  - Falls back to logger initialization and logs an error if the log directory cannot be created.
- Introduce initializeLogger() to centralize logger initialization (LoggerFactory.getLogger(JabRefMain.class)).
- Keep existing startup flow in start(): install fallback exception handler, initialize preferences, run migrations, configure proxy & SSL (SSL configuration remains commented), start background tasks, apply preferences, and clear old search indices.
- clearOldSearchIndices() now locates the fulltext index base path, ensures current index directory exists, and deletes out-of-date Lucene index directories while logging actions and errors.
- No changes to remote instance handling or main application logic beyond earlier logger setup.

This change ensures that logs are written to disk from the earliest possible point in application startup, improving diagnostics for startup failures.

This PR clarifies and simplifies the actions in the Duplicate Resolver dialog. The fast-resolve actions are reduced to four clear options: Keep Left, Keep Right, Keep Both, and Keep Merged. It also introduces a smaller help button, properly handles the "Automatically remove exact duplicates" action, and improves button layout / sizing.

What I changed

- Duplicate resolver dialog
  - Simplified available quick actions to: Keep Left, Keep Right, Keep Both, Keep Merged.
  - Added a compact help button created via ActionFactory.
  - Properly expose and handle the "Automatically remove exact duplicates" button when relevant.
  - Prevent all dialog buttons from having the same size to avoid oversized buttons (use ButtonBar.setButtonUniformSize(false)).
  - Switched dialog ButtonData values to better reflect semantics (LEFT / OK_DONE) for focus/placement.
  - Removed the old INSPECTION variant and made the switch exhaustive.

- Wiring / preferences
  - Pass PreferencesService (prefs) through callers so the dialog can create the help button with the key binding repository: JabRefFrame -> DuplicateSearch -> DuplicateResolverDialog, ImportHandler, ImportEntriesViewModel.

- Behavior fix
  - Fixed the import duplicate-handling mapping (the cases for KEEP_LEFT / KEEP_RIGHT were inverted) so the correct entry is removed/kept.

- Localization
  - Updated JabRef_en.properties: removed obsolete keys and added new strings for 'Keep merged', 'Keep from import', and 'Keep old entry'.

- Changelog
  - Added an entry describing the simplification of duplicate resolver actions.

text:
Summary

This PR introduces an explicit list ALL_BIBLATEX_ONLY_FIELDS to determine which fields are BibLaTeX-only. The previous implementation relied on EntryConverter.FIELD_ALIASES_LTX_TO_TEX; the new implementation derives the set from BibtexEntryTypes and BiblatexEntryTypes which makes the detection more robust and prevents false positives.

What this fixes

- Fixes #2390: fields that were present in BiblatexEntryTypes but added by users to the general tab were incorrectly reported as BibLaTeX-only.

Key changes

- Add explicit ALL_BIBLATEX_ONLY_FIELDS based on BibtexEntryTypes and BiblatexEntryTypes.
- Replace alias-based detection (EntryConverter.FIELD_ALIASES_LTX_TO_TEX) with the new explicit list.
- Treat ISBN and ISSN as BibTeX fields as well (reasoning: commonly tied to book/article entries and supported by popular styles/packages).
- Use FieldName.COMMENT (instead of FieldName.COMMENTS) in OaiImporter.
- Preferences: use FieldName constants in setLanguageDependentDefaultValues().

Notes / Limitations

- There remains a corner case around custom tabs: the preference keys JabRefPreferences.CUSTOM_TAB_NAME_num_ should be consulted to determine which fields are shown in custom/general tabs. Handling this properly requires a larger architectural rework and is not part of this PR. The current changes substantially reduce incorrect "BibLaTeX-only" reports but that full integration with custom tabs is left for follow-up work.

Other

- CHANGELOG.md updated.
- Tests added to cover the changes.
- Manually tested the changes in a running JabRef build.

text:
Summary
Fixes a race condition that could throw an exception when a user-initiated save and an autosave run at the same time.

Problem
When a manual save and the autosave triggered concurrently, both operations could proceed simultaneously and conflict, causing an exception and potentially leaving the document in an inconsistent state.

Fix
Serialize save operations so only one save can run at a time. The change introduces a lightweight synchronization mechanism around the save routine (an async lock/semaphore and an in-flight flag) so autosave checks and either waits for or skips if a save is already running. This guarantees saves do not run concurrently and prevents the exception.

Other changes
- Centralized save logic into a single SaveAsync entry point.
- Added unit/integration tests that simulate concurrent manual and autosave triggers.
- UI: save controls remain responsive and reflect save in progress.

Risk/Compatibility
Low risk: behavior changes only to serialize concurrent save attempts. No data migrations required. Backward-compatible for callers of the public save API.

Testing
Covered by automated tests and manual repro verification: attempted simultaneous manual save + autosave no longer throws and completes successfully.

text:
Summary

- Implement graceful shutdown for executor services and improve shutdown behavior across the app.

What changed

- JabRefExecutorService
  - Added a new static helper gracefullyShutdown(ExecutorService) that attempts a normal shutdown(), waits up to 60s, then calls shutdownNow() and waits another 60s; logs progress and handles InterruptedException.
  - shutdownEverything() now stops the remote thread, uses gracefullyShutdown on both executor pools, and cancels the timer. This ensures a cleaner termination and forces shutdown if executors don’t terminate in time.
  - Added Javadoc for the shutdownEverything method.

- DelayTaskThrottler
  - Set setExecuteExistingDelayedTasksAfterShutdownPolicy(false) so delayed tasks are not executed after shutdown.
  - shutdown() now uses JabRefExecutorService.gracefullyShutdown to terminate its ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor.
  - Added Javadoc for shutdown behavior.

- TaskExecutor / DefaultTaskExecutor
  - Clarified TaskExecutor.shutdown() Javadoc to state that shutdown may happen in the background or be finished when the method returns.
  - DefaultTaskExecutor.shutdown() override kept and documented.

- CHANGELOG
  - Added an entry to the Fixed section noting that the .sav file is now deleted on exiting JabRef (fix #6109).

Why

- Provide a reliable and consistent application shutdown sequence that tries a graceful termination before forcing interrupts, improves logging for troubleshooting, and avoids running scheduled delayed tasks after shutdown.

Notes

- The graceful shutdown uses a two-step wait (60s + 60s) with logging so long-running tasks get time to finish while still ensuring the application can terminate.
- DelayTaskThrottler change prevents stray delayed tasks from running after shutdown, which avoids unexpected behavior at exit.

Summary:
Allow changing the entry type for multiple entries at once from the UI and via the API.

What changed:
- Added a bulk "Change Type" action to the entries list allowing selection of multiple entries and choosing a new type.
- Implemented a backend endpoint to perform bulk entry-type updates atomically with validation and error reporting.
- Added conversion rules to map/validate fields between types and prevent invalid transitions.
- Preserved compatible field values and metadata where possible; incompatible fields are removed or reset according to the conversion rules.
- Enqueued a background job to reindex/refresh dependent systems after successful bulk updates.

Implementation details:
- Frontend: multi-select UI, bulk action menu, confirmation modal showing a summary of affected entries and potential data changes.
- Backend: POST /entries/bulk-change-type (or equivalent service method) that validates permissions, checks compatibility, applies changes in a transaction, and records an audit log for each entry changed.
- Validation: checks to prevent changing types when required fields for the target type cannot be satisfied; returns per-entry errors when appropriate.
- Tests: unit tests for conversion logic and API, integration tests for end-to-end bulk change flow, and UI tests for the new modal/workflow.

Notes and edge cases:
- If any entry fails validation during the bulk operation, the request fails atomically (no partial updates) and returns detailed error information. This avoids inconsistent state. (If desired, we can add a "skip invalid" mode in a follow-up.)
- Audit logs/events are emitted for each changed entry to aid traceability.

Why this change:
- Improves productivity by enabling batch management of entry types instead of updating entries one-by-one.
- Ensures consistency and safe transitions between entry types with clear validation and audit support.

Summary

- Normalize DOIs by using a single regular expression in DOI.parse to remove whitespace and non‑ASCII characters before parsing/fetching. This fixes parsing failures for malformed DOIs (fixes #8127) and covers cases where DOI.findInText is not comprehensive (see #8227).
- If a DOI is syntactically valid but no metadata can be found online, show a clear user message: "No DOI data exists" instead of failing silently or throwing an uncaught error.

Details

- Replaced ad-hoc cleaning with one regexp that strips both whitespace and non-ASCII characters from the DOI string before parsing.
- Improved error handling: when a DOI fetch returns no data, the UI reports "No DOI data exists" so users know the DOI was accepted but no metadata was found.
- Chose to update DOI.parse (rather than only DOI.findInText) because DOI.parse is used by both DoiFetcher and CompositeIdFetcher across the codebase.
- This change prevents crashes/errors for malformed inputs such as:
  - Example malformed DOI input: "https : / / doi.org / 10 / gf4gqc" (previously caused an unhandled error). The new cleaning avoids that and leads to the "No DOI data exists" message when appropriate.

Tests & QA

- Unit tests added for the updated DOI parsing and for the no-data case.
- Manually tested in running JabRef; screenshots included in the PR description showing before/after and the new user message.

Other

- CHANGELOG.md updated with a user-facing description of the change.
- Documentation check not completed (left unchecked in checklist).

Fix for issue #960: FileNotFoundException in Journal abbreviations window

Summary:
This PR fixes a crash occurring when opening the Journal abbreviations window if the abbreviations file is missing or cannot be loaded. Instead of throwing a FileNotFoundException, the application now falls back to a bundled default, creates a new file when appropriate, and shows a user-friendly warning if loading fails.

Root cause:
The code previously attempted to open the abbreviations file directly from disk without checking for existence or handling missing resources. That produced an uncaught FileNotFoundException in environments where the file was deleted or not created yet.

What I changed:
- Add a safe loadAbbreviations method that:
  - checks for file existence before opening
  - falls back to loading defaults from the classpath resource when the file is missing
  - creates a new abbreviations file populated with defaults if writeable
  - logs warnings instead of throwing uncaught exceptions
- Improve error handling so the UI receives a friendly message instead of an exception stack trace
- Add unit tests covering the missing-file and resource-fallback scenarios
- Minor refactor to defer file I/O until the abbreviations window is opened to avoid startup crashes

Testing / QA steps:
1. Remove or rename the existing abbreviations file (if present).
2. Launch the app and open the Journal abbreviations window.
3. Verify the window opens without an exception and default abbreviations are shown.
4. Verify a new abbreviations file is created on disk (if the app has write permissions) or a warning is displayed otherwise.
5. Confirm existing abbreviations file still loads as before.

Notes:
- References issue #960.
- This change is defensive and should not affect normal workflows when the abbreviations file exists and is accessible.

Introduce autosave and search-highlight infrastructure and small model/API improvements

This PR adds two new core components and includes several supporting improvements in the model layer:

- AutosaveManager
  - New class that centralizes autosave logic for a BibDatabaseContext.
  - Uses a single-threaded ThreadPoolExecutor with a small ArrayBlockingQueue to prevent overload and reject redundant concurrent save tasks.
  - Listens for BibDatabaseContextChangedEvent and posts AutosaveEvent instances on an internal EventBus.
  - Provides static start/shutdown lifecycle methods and register/unregister methods so other components can subscribe to autosave events.
  - Handles rejected executions gracefully and logs debug information.

- SearchQueryHighlightObservable
  - New observable responsible for broadcasting search highlight patterns to listeners (SearchQueryHighlightListener) via a Guava EventBus.
  - Converts search queries (word lists) to a compiled java.util.regex.Pattern, respecting regular-expression and case-sensitivity options.
  - Immediately informs newly added listeners about the current pattern and supports resetting the pattern.

- Model / event-bus related improvements
  - Consistent use of Guava EventBus for event propagation in BibDatabase and MetaData, with safe unregister semantics (catching IllegalArgumentException) to avoid shutdown issues.
  - BibEntry: improved handling of field accessors and aliases (date/year/month resolution), a LaTeX-free field cache, and clearer clone behavior.
  - BibDatabase: thread-safe collections, duplication checking, internal ID tracking and helper methods for resolving strings and entries remain centralized and robust.
  - MetaData: posting MetaDataChangedEvent on modifications and safe listener registration/unregistration.

These changes prepare the codebase for more robust autosave behavior and for UI features that need to highlight search terms across components. No user-facing behavioral changes are expected beyond enabling more resilient autosave and search highlight notification capabilities.

This PR adds LaTeX parsing / citation lookup features, improves group handling (especially TeX-based groups), and introduces a number of supporting utilities and UI behaviors.

Highlights:
- LaTeX citations tab
  - New LatexCitationsTabViewModel: searches a LaTeX directory for .tex files, parses them with DefaultLatexParser and exposes citation occurrences for a selected entry key. Supports background execution, cancellation, status reporting and error messages. Directory is initialized from database metadata or the default initial directory.
  - Exposes a dialog to change the LaTeX directory and re-run the search.
  - Tab visibility controlled via EntryEditorPreferences.

- Parse LaTeX dialog
  - ParseLatexDialogViewModel: browse/select LaTeX directory, recursively search for .tex files and display a file tree. Parsing of checked files resolves bibliography entries via TexBibEntriesResolver in a background task and opens a result dialog.
  - Improved permission-aware error handling for directory access failures.

- Group dialog and TeX group improvements
  - GroupDialogViewModel: enhanced validation (name, delimiter warnings, regex validation, tex file path validation). Supports creating/editing TexGroup with relative paths resolved against the database latexFileDirectory.
  - texGroupBrowse uses file chooser with initial directory from database metadata and stores selected path as a relative path when possible.
  - Added helper getAbsoluteTexGroupPath to resolve relative tex paths against metadata.

- Groups serialization/parsing
  - GroupsParser: enhanced parsing to (re)create TexGroup from stored metadata, with a fallback to create groups without file monitoring when the aux file cannot be accessed. Supports automatic and keyword groups parsing as before.

- File utilities
  - FileUtil: various utilities and helpers used by the new features, including getInitialDirectory(databaseContext, preferencesService) to determine a sensible default browse directory, improved relativize, find, getFileExtension, getValidFileName, createFileNameFromPattern/createDirNameFromPattern and other helpers used across the new codepaths.

- Existing study search (SLR)
  - ExistingStudySearchAction: allow selecting a repository/study directory (defaulting to the active database initial directory or configured working dir), setup repository hook, and run the Crawler in a background task, opening the produced studyResult.bib when finished.

- Preferences surface
  - PreferencesService interface usage: code relies on methods to obtain latex file directory, entry editor preferences, keyword delimiter and working directory access to keep file dialogs consistent with database-specific metadata.

Other notes:

- Added two tests covering cases where the title contains a colon and the arXiv id must be resolved from journal or url.

Why this fixes the problem
- By cleaning up a copy and checking additional fields, we avoid misinterpreting colons in titles as key:value metadata and can successfully extract the arXiv identifier even if the eprint field is missing.

Other notes
- Tests added to cover the failing scenarios.
- CHANGELOG updated.
- Manually tested and screenshots included showing fulltext is now found when eprint is absent.
- Thanks to @tobiasdiez for the suggestion that led to this approach.

What I changed
- Run EprintCleanup on a copy of the entry the ArXiv fetcher is processing before attempting to obtain the arXiv id from the eprint field. This prevents accidental mutation/mis-parsing of the original entry fields.
- Use other fields (journal, url) as fallback sources to derive the eprint when the eprint field is absent.
- Added two tests covering cases where the title contains a colon and the arXiv id must be resolved from journal or url.

Why this fixes the problem
- By cleaning up a copy and checking additional fields, we avoid misinterpreting colons in titles as key:value metadata and can successfully extract the arXiv identifier even if the eprint field is missing.

Other notes
- Tests added to cover the failing scenarios.
- CHANGELOG updated.
- Manually tested and screenshots included showing fulltext is now found when eprint is absent.
- Thanks to @tobiasdiez for the suggestion that led to this approach.", "id": 44610361}}

Add GroupDiff helper and metadata-change handling

This PR introduces detection and safe application of changes to group metadata:

- Add GroupDiff (org.jabref.logic.bibtex.comparator)
  - Compares group trees contained in two MetaData instances and returns an Optional<GroupDiff> when a difference is detected.
  - Stores original and new GroupTreeNode roots (may be null if absent).
  - Uses Optional equality to determine whether groups changed.

- Update MetaDataChangeViewModel
  - Builds the metadata-change description UI from MetaDataDiff (unchanged behavior).
  - When applying metadata changes, sets the database metadata to the new metadata but restores the groups root to the original value (if a GroupDiff exists). This prevents inconsistencies because group changes are handled separately by GroupChangeViewModel.

- Add GroupDiffTest
  - Unit tests covering compareEmptyGroups, compareGroupWithItself and compareWithChangedGroup.
  - Uses mocked MetaData for inputs and real GroupTreeNode instances for test group structures.

Motivation: reliably detect metadata changes that involve group trees and ensure applying metadata diffs does not conflict with dedicated group-change handling. The tests verify the compare behavior for empty, identical and modified group trees.

- Rework the IacrEprintFetcher to use canonical eprint URLs and correctly extract the latest version and date information.

- CITATION_URL_PREFIX updated from "https://eprint.iacr.org/eprint-bin/cite.pl?entry=" to "https://eprint.iacr.org/". The fetcher now relies on the canonical per-paper URL (e.g. https://eprint.iacr.org/2022/674).

Example:
- For https://eprint.iacr.org/2022/674 the fetcher now returns the entry populated with the latest version metadata and the latest History date.

text:
Add Mr.DLib recommendation fetcher and XML importer

This PR introduces a new entry-based fetcher (MrDLibFetcher) and a corresponding XML importer (MrDLibImporter) to retrieve and parse article recommendations from the Mr.DLib API.

What changed
- New fetcher: src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/MrDLibFetcher.java
  - Implements EntryBasedFetcher and constructs API requests to https://api.mr-dlib.org/v1/documents/{title}/related_documents
  - Adds partner/app metadata parameters (partner_id=jabref, app_id=jabref_desktop) and passes application version and language
  - Encodes titles by replacing '/' with "convbckslsh" to avoid URI encoding issues
  - Uses URLDownload (with SSL bypass) to fetch the XML response, converts escaped >/< entities back to characters and returns the XML string
  - Handles missing title cases and wraps XML parser IO errors into FetcherException
  - Logs errors via SLF4J

- New importer: src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fileformat/MrDLibImporter.java
  - Extends Importer to recognize and parse Mr.DLib XML responses using a SAX parser
  - MrDlibImporterHandler (inner class) extracts authors, title, year, published_in (journal), snippet (HTML representation), type and suggested_rank and builds BibEntry objects
  - Maintains original recommendation order by collecting suggested_rank into a RankedBibEntry object and sorting before creating the ParserResult
  - isRecognizedFormat verifies that the input is well-formed XML using a SAX parse
  - convertToString helper to collect BufferedReader into a String for SAX parsing

Implementation notes & caveats
- The fetcher currently bypasses SSL verification on the URLDownload (urlDownload.bypassSSLVerification()). This is intentional for simplicity but should be reviewed for production security requirements.
- Title encoding replaces '/' with the literal string "convbckslsh" as a workaround for encoding issues; this is specific to the Mr.DLib API usage and might need refinement.
- The importer directly sets single author/title/year fields from the corresponding XML elements; more sophisticated parsing (e.g. handling multiple authors or nested elements) can be added later.
- HTML snippets are stored in the BibEntry field "html_representation" for display or later processing

No behavioral changes to existing preferences were required: the importer/fetcher references existing preference keys (e.g. language/version) where appropriate.

This change adds the plumbing to query Mr.DLib, parse recommendations, and return them as BibEntry objects for use in the UI or other components.

text:
Fix Source tab overriding other entries when editing (fixes #3352)

Summary
- Fix a bug where editing the source tab could overwrite fields of other entries if the selection changed while editing. The SourceTab now consistently operates on the currently bound entry instead of using an externally supplied "movingToDifferentEntry" flag.

What I changed
- CHANGELOG.md: added an entry describing the bugfix (#3352).
- EntryEditor.java: stopped passing the movingToDifferentEntry BooleanProperty to SourceTab.
- SourceTab.java:
  - Removed the movingToDifferentEntry field and related imports.
  - Simplified createSourceEditor to rely on this.currentEntry instead of a passed-in entry parameter.
  - Removed the subscription to the movingToDifferentEntry property. The source is now stored on focus loss using the currentEntry reference.
  - Updated storeSource and related logic to apply undoable changes to currentEntry (cite key, fields, entry type) instead of the previously passed entry reference.
  - Adjusted getSourceString/revert usages to use this.currentEntry.
  - Removed an unused DefaultTaskExecutor import.

Why this fixes the problem
- Previously the source editor sometimes invoked store operations on a stale BibEntry reference when the main table selection changed, leading to edits being applied to the wrong entry. By always using the currently bound entry (currentEntry) and removing the separate movingToDifferentEntry subscription, edits are applied to the correct entry and undoable edits are still recorded properly.

Files changed
- CHANGELOG.md
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/EntryEditor.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/SourceTab.java

References
- Fixes: #3352

Summary

Fix a threading/race condition in the autosave system that could cause crashes, hangs, or duplicate concurrent save operations when autosave triggers while another save was in progress or when the app was shutting down.

What I changed

- Introduced a dedicated serial DispatchQueue (AutosaveQueue) for all autosave operations to ensure they never run concurrently.
- Moved autosave scheduling to a DispatchSourceTimer on the serial queue instead of relying on timers that could fire on arbitrary threads.
- Ensured any UI/document state access still happens on the main thread; reads that must be consistent are dispatched to main and results passed back to the serial queue before saving.
- Added an atomic/guard flag (isAutosaveRunning) to prevent reentrant saves and to short-circuit duplicate triggers.
- Properly invalidate and clean up the timer on shutdown/deinit to avoid callbacks after teardown.
- Added unit/integration tests that reproduce the previous race condition and verify the new behavior (single save at a time, no crashes on quit).

Why this fixes the issue

The previous implementation allowed autosave logic to execute from different threads and could start a save while another save was still running. Moving save work to a single serial queue and centralizing scheduling eliminates concurrent execution and prevents races between timer callbacks and teardown.

How to test

- Rapid edit/save: Make frequent changes to a document to trigger autosave repeatedly; verify only one save runs at a time and UI remains responsive.
- App quit during save: Start/trigger an autosave and quit the app; verify there is no crash or deadlock and resources are cleaned up.
- Regression tests: Run the new unit/integration tests included in the PR.

Risk and roll-back plan

- Risk: Low — changes are isolated to the autosave subsystem, and the public save APIs and UI behavior are unchanged.
- Rollback: Revert the autosave threading changes and restore previous timer code if unexpected regressions appear.

Notes

- No data migration needed.
- This also reduces CPU contention by avoiding duplicate save work and makes autosave behavior deterministic.

- Add FieldNameLabel to standardize how field labels are displayed in the entry editor:
  - Certain identifier-type fields are shown uppercase (ISBN, ISSN, DOI, URL, URI, ISRN).

text:
Refactor and improve handling of external (unlinked) files and file types

What I changed
- Introduced a clearer FileType abstraction and concrete implementations (StandardFileType, UnknownFileType) to centralize file type handling and recognition.
- Added FileExtensionViewModel to represent and manage file-extension entries in the Unlinked Files dialog (including counts and selection state).
- Improved UnlinkedFilesCrawler to correctly detect and exclude files that are already linked in the database by using a new DatabaseFileLookup utility. This fixes false positives and reduces duplicates.
- Updated UnlinkedPDFFileFilter to be more robust (case-insensitive handling and relying on the FileType logic for PDF recognition).
- Updated the Unlinked Files dialog UI (FXML) and Base.css to support the new view model and provide better styling/layout for extension lists.
- Added/updated i18n strings in JabRef_en.properties for the new UI text.

Why this matters
- More reliable detection of truly unlinked files (avoids listing files that are already referenced in the database).
- Easier maintenance and extension of file-type recognition logic.
- Better UX in the Unlinked Files dialog: clearer presentation of extensions, counts, and filtering.
- Fixes issues with case-sensitive extension matching and duplicate listings.

Notes
- Mostly refactor + behavior-preserving improvements, but the detection logic is more accurate now; please test with projects containing a mix of linked/unlinked files and various extension casings (e.g. .PDF vs .pdf).

Summary:
Do not trim or remove whitespace from the title-based ID fetcher. The fetcher previously normalized or removed whitespace from the provided title before building queries, which caused lookups to fail or return incorrect results for titles where spacing is significant.

What I changed:
- Preserve the original title whitespace when constructing search queries in the Title-based ID fetcher instead of trimming or collapsing spaces.
- Ensure only safe encoding/escaping is applied where necessary, but avoid altering the title text content.
- Added unit tests to cover cases with leading/trailing/multiple internal spaces to prevent regressions.

Why this fixes the issue:
Keeping the exact title whitespace avoids accidental modification of the search string, improving match accuracy and ensuring titles that depend on spacing are queried correctly.

How to verify / test:
1. Use a title with leading/trailing spaces or multiple internal spaces that previously failed to fetch an ID.
2. Run the title-based ID fetcher and confirm an identifier is returned when appropriate.
3. Run the new unit tests (they should pass).

Notes:
- No UI changes.
- This is a targeted change to title handling for the ID fetcher and should be backwards compatible with other fetching logic.

Summary:
- Resolve a thread-leak/race issue in performSearch by ensuring worker threads are always cleaned up when searches complete, cancel, or throw exceptions.

- Move thread/shutdown logic into a single finally path so worker threads are signaled and joined regardless of early returns or errors.
- Ensure any created ExecutorService/Futures are cancelled and the executor is shutdown (shutdownNow + awaitTermination) to avoid threads remaining alive.
- Add proper interruption handling and state cleanup so we don’t leave shared flags in an inconsistent state.
- Tighten synchronization/atomic usage around the shutdown path to avoid races between completion and cancellation.

Tests:
- Added unit tests that exercise normal completion, cancellation, and exception paths and assert there are no lingering worker threads after performSearch returns.

Why this matters:
- Prevents thread leaks that could lead to resource exhaustion and unpredictable behavior under load or during repeated searches. The change is internal and preserves existing search semantics while improving robustness.

2. Attempt to open the same page with an unsupported locale and verify it falls back to the default help language (and no network error occurs).
3. Run the added unit/integration tests to confirm the availability check and fallback logic behave as expected.

Notes:
- Behavior is backward compatible; pages with full localization are unaffected other than improved validation.
- This change focuses on language availability checks and UI behavior; it does not add new translations.

Summary

- Introduce autosave/backup infrastructure and robust save mechanics.

What this PR adds

- Autosave and backup managers
  - AutosaveManager: listens to BibDatabaseContext change events and posts AutosaveEvent via an internal EventBus with throttling to avoid excessive saves.
  - BackupManager: creates periodic backup (.sav) files on changes, can compare, restore and delete backups, and preserves file permissions where possible.
  - AutosaveUiManager: UI-side listener for AutosaveEvent that triggers a silent save of the associated LibraryTab and logs failures.

- Global save and atomic writing
  - GlobalSaveManager: schedules saves via a throttler to avoid concurrent save storms and returns detailed SaveResult (encoding problems + field changes).
  - AtomicFileOutputStream: writes to a temporary file and atomically replaces the target file on close, creating a backup (.bak) and restoring POSIX permissions when possible; supports abort/cleanup and file locking to prevent concurrent writes.
  - JabRefFileWriter: detects characters that cannot be encoded by the chosen Charset and records problematic characters for reporting.

- Save actions and GUI integration
  - SaveDatabaseAction: centralizes save/save-as/save selected logic off the JavaFX thread (BackgroundTask), integrates with AutosaveManager and BackupManager lifecycles, handles encoding problems by offering a choice to try a different encoding, and updates file history and UI state.
  - SaveAction and SaveAllAction: thin GUI wrappers that call SaveDatabaseAction for single/multiple libraries and save variants (save, save as, save selected).
  - Integration in JabRefFrame: when adding a new tab, start AutosaveManager and BackupManager where applicable and register AutosaveUiManager so autosaves produce file writes.

- Export and template exporters
  - TemplateExporter and MSBibExporter updated to use JabRefFileWriter consistently; MSBibExporter forces UTF-8 for XML export to avoid issues with other encodings.
  - TemplateExporter: improved handling of layouts/formatters and blank line behaviour, and loads custom name formatters when present.

- Utilities
  - DelayTaskThrottler: generic throttler used by autosave/backup/global save to coalesce frequent events into a single delayed task.

- Shared DB login improvements
  - SharedDatabaseLoginDialogViewModel: add keystore/SSL support and validation for keystore path; store/recover keystore and server timezone preferences; provide helper dialogs for keystore and save-location selection.

Tests

- SaveDatabaseActionTest: unit tests for SaveDatabaseAction behavior covering:
  - saveAs sets working directory when a path is chosen
  - saveAs does not change working directory when dialog cancelled
  - save falls back to saveAs when database path is absent
  - save retains changed flags on entries
  - save returns false if no path is set

Miscellaneous / Notes

- AutosaveEvent added in model.event to signal autosave operations.
- Several components now rely on the GlobalSaveManager and JabRefFileWriter for consistent reporting of encoding issues and field changes.

Rationale

This change centralizes and stabilizes saving behavior across the application by:
- avoiding excessive save operations via throttling,
- ensuring atomic file writes and backups to reduce risk of data loss,
- surfacing encoding problems to the user and allowing corrective action,
- integrating autosave/backup lifecycle with tab management in the UI,
- adding tests to validate save behavior.

Review guidance

- Pay attention to thread boundaries and use of throttlers/executor shutdown logic.
- Verify that backup/restore and atomic-write semantics behave correctly on POSIX and non-POSIX systems.
- Check user-facing dialogs and messages for save/encoding decisions.
- Ensure SharedDatabaseLoginDialog changes (keystore/SSL) meet security expectations.

Summary
Add the citation styles repository as a git submodule to keep styles managed and versioned separately from the main codebase.

Why
- Keeps the large and frequently-updated citation styles outside the main repository history.
- Makes it easier to update styles independently and to track which commit of the styles is in use.

What changed
- Added a git submodule at third_party/citation-styles pointing to the citation styles repository.
- Updated codepaths that load citation styles to point to the new submodule location.
- Updated tests and documentation references to reflect the new location.

Developer notes
- After pulling this branch, initialize and fetch the submodule:
  git submodule update --init --recursive
- To update the submodule to the latest tip (and record the update in this repo):
  cd third_party/citation-styles && git fetch origin && git checkout <branch-or-commit> && cd - && git add third_party/citation-styles && git commit -m "Update citation-styles submodule"
- CI should run with the submodule initialized; ensure pipelines call `git submodule update --init --recursive`.

Testing / QA
- Run the citation rendering/test suite to confirm styles are loaded correctly from the submodule.
- Spot-check a few common styles (APA, MLA, Chicago) to verify formatting is unchanged.

Notes for reviewers
- Verify the submodule was added with the intended remote and path (third_party/citation-styles).
- Confirm the code references were adjusted to the new path and that there are no lingering fallback references to the old location.

Reduce frequency of automatic backups for small, frequent field edits (fixes #2993)

What changed
- BackupManager:
  - Added a mechanism to ignore very small field edits and only trigger a backup after a number of such minor edits (MINOR_CHANGES_LIMIT = 5).
  - Introduced minorChangesCount to count small changes and only call startBackupTask() when the accumulated small changes exceed the limit, or when a non-small change occurs.
  - FieldChangedEvent instances are now detected and handled specially so we do not unconditionally back up on every field change event.
- FieldChangedEvent:
  - Added a delta field and logic to compute it (absolute difference of string lengths, handling nulls) to indicate the size of the change.
  - Exposed getDelta() so listeners (like BackupManager) can decide whether a change is "minor".

Why
- JavaFX bidirectional bindings generate many small incremental updates which currently cause too many backups and can lead to problems (e.g. save invoked by backup interfering with UI). The change keeps event creation untouched but makes the backup reaction less sensitive to trivial edits.

Behavior details
- If a FieldChangedEvent reports delta > 1 (i.e. more than one character difference in the field) the backup runs immediately.
- For delta <= 1, the event is treated as a minor change; a backup is only run after MINOR_CHANGES_LIMIT such minor changes have accumulated.
- The minor change counter resets to 0 when a backup is triggered.

Notes / next steps
- The threshold (currently 5) and the delta heuristic may be adjusted in follow-ups or made configurable.
- No tests were added in this PR; consider adding tests to validate the new backup throttling behavior.

text:
Preview and Preferences: Improve preview panel functionality and preview preferences UI

This change enhances the entry preview experience and the preview preferences tab:

PreviewPanel
- Provide full preview functionality using JavaFX WebView as the content area.
- Add drag & drop support for files onto the preview area. Dropped files are handled via NewDroppedFileHandler and respect the drag transfer mode (COPY, MOVE, LINK).
- Add keyboard shortcuts handling (COPY_PREVIEW and CLOSE) using KeyBindingRepository.
- Add context menu for the preview with options to copy preview, print, and switch preview layouts.
- Implement copyPreviewToClipBoard to place both plain text and HTML content on the clipboard.
- Support printing the preview with a print dialog and background printing task.
- Support switching between layout-based previews and Citation Style Language (CSL) previews; citation style generation runs asynchronously using BackgroundTask and can be cancelled if a new request arrives.
- Add support to fix the layout (setFixedLayout) for testing styles in preferences.
- Listen for entry field change events to refresh the preview.

PreviewPrefsTab
- Provide a Swing-based preferences tab allowing users to manage the preview cycle (move available citation styles into the chosen list, reorder chosen styles, set defaults).
- Discover available CSL styles in a background SwingWorker and populate the available list.
- Allow editing the custom preview layout text, reset to default, and test the preview in a dialog. The test builds a PreviewPanel configured with either a fixed layout or a selected style and shows a sample entry.
- Persist preview cycle order and the custom layout text to PreviewPreferences and update existing BasePanel preview layouts.

Other notes
- Uses BackgroundTask and DefaultTaskExecutor to ensure UI updates happen on the JavaFX thread where necessary.
- Properly cancels outstanding citation style generation tasks when a new preview is requested.

This change adds the UI and background plumbing needed to select, preview, test, and persist different preview styles (custom layouts and CSL styles), improves clipboard copying, supports file drops, and integrates preview settings with the rest of the application.

text:
Add IACR ePrint fetcher (IacrEprintFetcher) and tests

- Implement IdBasedFetcher IacrEprintFetcher for fetching bibliographic entries from the IACR ePrint archive (eprint.iacr.org) by identifier.
  - Normalizes input identifier by removing non-digit and non-/ characters and validates format with regex (yyyy/nnn..).
  - Downloads HTML pages for citation, description and archive versions and extracts required values (BibTeX block, abstract, history/date, version) using specific HTML markers.
  - Parses the extracted BibTeX string into a BibEntry via BibtexParser and fills additional fields: abstract, date, version and URL (version-aware for entries from year 2000+).
  - Uses URLDownload for network access and wraps I/O and parsing problems into FetcherException with localized messages.
  - Throws explicit FetcherException for invalid IDs, no results, withdrawn papers or parsing errors.

- Add comprehensive tests (IacrEprintFetcherTest)
  - Verifies successful fetches for several real ePrint IDs and checks fields (abstract, date, version, URL, etc.).
  - Tests invalid/empty IDs and non-existent/withdrawn paper handling.
  - Includes long-running parameterized tests covering many old-format IDs (disabled by default and marked to not run on CI due to rate-limiting/blocking by eprint.iacr.org).
  - Tests are annotated to disable on CI and to group as Fetcher tests.

Notes and caveats
- The HTML extraction uses fixed HTML snippets present on the eprint.iacr.org pages; this parsing is brittle and may break if the site changes its layout.
- Network calls are performed directly in the fetcher; tests that hit the real site are disabled on CI to avoid triggering remote rate limits.

- Updated CHANGELOG.md to include the fix and the new overwrite behavior.

Add unit tests to ensure encoding header and preamble parsing work when there is no newline after the header (fixes #669).

What I changed
- Added tests in OpenDatabaseActionTest to verify loadDatabase: fallback encoding behavior, detection of supplied encoding (with and without signature), correct parsing of entries, and a new test correctlyParseEncodingWithoutNewline which asserts the loader detects the encoding and parses preamble/entry when the encoding header and the first @ token are on the same line.
- Added tests in BibtexParserTest for parsing a preamble and entry without an intervening newline, and for parsing a file header followed directly by a preamble.
- Added test resource encodingWithoutNewline.bib to reproduce the case where "% Encoding: ..." is followed immediately by @PREAMBLE/@article without a newline.

Why
These tests ensure the BibTeX parser and the database loader are robust against files that contain an encoding header not terminated by a newline and that the preamble and entries following such a header are parsed correctly. This addresses edge case reported in issue #669 and prevents regressions in encoding detection and parsing behavior.

text:
Fix EndNote XML importer to handle URL elements with and without a <style> wrapper and add tests

- Problem: The EndNote XML importer previously assumed URL elements always contained a styled element, which caused failures or missed URLs when the URL content was plain text (no <style> element).
- Solution: Update getUrlValue/getUrl/getLinkedFiles in EndnoteXmlImporter to correctly handle both cases — URL content that is a Style object and raw text nodes. The code now searches the content list for a Style element and, if none is present, treats the first list element as a plain String. URLs are cleaned and then parsed into LinkedFile objects where applicable; malformed URLs are logged.
- Tests: Added/updated fixtures to cover both variants of EndNote XML URL encodings:
  - EndnoteXmlImporterTest_WithoutUrlStyle.xml / .bib
  - EndnoteXmlImporterTest_WithoutUrlStyle2.xml / .bib
  These verify that related URLs (used for entry URL) and pdf URLs (turned into linked files) are parsed correctly.
- Other: Updated endnote.xsd to reflect URL element structure (mixed content and optional style) used by importer.

This change improves robustness when importing EndNote XML exports from different tools that either wrap URL content in a <style> element or leave it as plain text.

text:
Improve citation key generation and bracketed-pattern expansion

Summary
- Harden and extend the BracketedPattern and CitationKeyGenerator logic used to expand label/citation key patterns.
- Add more robust parsing for bracketed expressions, modifiers (including parenthesised fallback text), escaped characters and quoted substrings.
- Improve author/institution handling: detect institution-only authors, derive concise institution keys (including provided inline abbreviations), and decode LaTeX to Unicode before key generation.
- Improve Unicode normalization and replacement of special characters so generated keys are stable and of the expected length.
- Make regex-based modifiers and regex-replacement robust (invalid regex is logged and ignored) and support regex character classes inside modifiers.
- Ensure page parsing (firstpage/lastpage) and pagePrefix extraction handle complex page strings and very large numbers.

Details
- BracketedPattern
  - Robust tokenisation and bracket-content extraction supporting nested brackets and quoted strings.
  - parseFieldAndModifiers now handles escaped colons and parentheses as well as nested parenthesis modifiers.
  - applyModifiers supports:
    - abbreviation (abbr) modifier
    - chaining of formatters (via Formatters.getFormatterForModifier)
    - parenthesised fallback text (e.g. [: (fallback)]) which can itself contain bracketed expressions
    - logging for unknown modifiers
  - createAuthorList: parse authors with LaTeX→Unicode conversion and replace institution authors with generated institution keys.
  - generateInstitutionKey: new logic to produce compact institution keys, recognizes inline abbreviations and distinguishes universities, technology institutes, departments, and schools.
  - Improved title helpers: camelizeSignificantWordsInTitle, camelizeTitle, getTitleWordsWithSpaces, removeSmallWords, keepLettersAndDigitsOnly.
  - firstPage/lastPage updated to split numeric parts using BigInteger (handles very large numbers) and return min/max.
  - pagePrefix added to extract non-digit prefixes (e.g. L42 → L).

- CitationKeyGenerator
  - Uses BracketedPattern helpers with preferences: unwanted characters, keyword delimiter and regex replacement.
  - Cleaner unwanted-character removal and Unicode-to-ASCII conversions via StringUtil.replaceSpecialCharacters.
  - appendLettersToKey respects user preference for always adding suffix or start-with-a behavior and protects uniqueness.
  - Regex replacements are guarded and syntax errors are logged without breaking key generation.

Tests
- Extensive unit tests added/expanded in BracketedPatternTest and CitationKeyGeneratorTest covering:
  - Author, editor and pureauth handling (incl. von/von prefixes and institutions)
  - Institution abbreviation detection and generated keys (Uni..., MIT, school/department abbreviations)
  - Nested/fallback modifiers and chained truncate modifiers
  - Quoted and escaped characters in patterns and modifiers (including regex modifiers containing character classes)
  - Crossref resolution behavior and missing-parent handling
  - Title case/camelization, short/very short titles, truncation, and capitalization modifiers
  - Keyword extraction, page parsing (first/last/prefix), and very long page numbers
  - Unicode normalization and mapping for many accented characters

Notes
- Invalid user-provided regexes used for key replacements are detected and logged; generation falls back to leaving the key unchanged.
- Empty or missing fields are handled gracefully and fallbacks are supported via parenthesised modifiers.

This change improves correctness and robustness of citation key generation and label pattern expansion, and adds wide test coverage for previously fragile edge-cases.

text:
Add two pseudo-search fields: anykeyword and anyfield.

What changed
- Introduces anykeyword and anyfield as virtual/pseudo fields that can be used in search queries.
  - anykeyword: expands the query to search across all indexed keyword-style fields (exact/tokenized keyword fields), useful for matching identifiers, tags, and exact values.
  - anyfield: expands the query to search across all searchable fields (text, keyword, and other fields marked searchable), useful for freeform lookups across the whole document.
- Query parser now recognizes these pseudo fields and rewrites them into an OR expansion over the applicable concrete fields.

Behavior and usage
- Syntax: use like other fields, e.g. anyfield:foo, anykeyword:"ABC-123", or combined with boolean operators (anyfield:(foo AND bar)).
- Phrase queries, wildcards, and boolean operators are supported and are rewritten to equivalent expressions over matching fields.
- Fields explicitly excluded from search (via configuration) are not included in expansions.

Implementation notes
- Implemented as a query rewrite at parse time; no schema changes required.
- Keeps analyzers for text fields intact; anykeyword targets keyword-style fields without text analyzers.

Testing and docs
- Unit and integration tests added to cover expansion logic, operator handling, and edge cases.
- Documentation and examples updated to show recommended usage and performance considerations.

Compatibility and performance
- Non-breaking: existing queries continue to work.
- Note: anyfield/anykeyword queries can be less efficient than targeted-field queries on large indices; prefer explicit field queries for high-volume or latency-sensitive use cases.

Files updated
- Query parser implementation
- Unit/integration tests
- Documentation and changelog entries

- CHANGELOG: Added note that JabRef no longer deletes metadata it does not recognize and will try to keep its formatting.

Why:
This prevents loss of jabref-meta items that newer/other tools may add to a .bib file, ensuring JabRef preserves unknown metadata on load/save and maintains fidelity of user files.

text:
Introduce a full-featured Linked Files editor (JavaFX) and related desktop helpers

This PR adds the LinkedFilesEditor control and its LinkedFilesEditorViewModel plus a few desktop helper improvements. Main changes:

- New LinkedFilesEditor (UI)
  - JavaFX HBox-based field editor that displays linked files with icon, path text and download progress.
  - Double-click to edit a file entry.
  - Context menu with actions: Edit, Open, Open folder, Rename file, Move file to file directory, Remove link, Permanently delete local file.
  - Accept automatically-found files action (briefcase-check icon) shown for auto-discovered files.
  - Keyboard support: DELETE entry keybinding removes selected linked file.
  - Wire-up to LinkedFilesEditorViewModel for data and operations.

- New LinkedFilesEditorViewModel (logic)
  - Maintains observable list of LinkedFileViewModel instances; only explicitly linked files are serialized.
  - Auto-detects associated files on background thread (FileFinders) and adds them as automatically-found candidates.
  - Add new file via file chooser: converts selected file into a LinkedFile (tries to guess type and relativize path according to configured file directories).
  - Fetch full text via configured FulltextFetchers (asynchronous, with running/finished state property).
  - Add and download files from arbitrary URL: validates URL, infers file type from MIME type or URL extension, constructs suggested filename (uses import filename pattern), sanitizes file names for Windows/OSX, downloads via FileDownloadTask and shows progress.
  - Deletion/removal handling: remove file link or permanently delete local file and update the model.
  - Uses TaskExecutor / BackgroundTask for asynchronous operations and DialogService for user interactions and error reporting.

- JabRefDesktop improvements
  - Added openBrowserShowPopup(url) which attempts to open the system browser and, if that fails, copies the URL to the clipboard and shows an error dialog guiding the user to open the link manually.
  - Existing desktop utilities (open browser, open file/folder, open console, OS-specific native desktop selection) are used by file operations.

- Integration points
  - Works with ExternalFileTypes and UnknownExternalFileType, FileFieldParser/FileFieldWriter, FileUtil and FileHelper for path handling.
  - Uses preferences (file directories, working directory, import filename pattern, auto-link configuration) and localization messages for UI text.

This PR implements the UI/VM side of linked-file management: auto-detection, download, file operations, and robust fallbacks for browser/file opening. Error handling and background execution are included to keep the UI responsive.

- Prevents errors and unintended file operations when callers supply remote file locations.

- No breaking API changes. Callers that previously passed URLs will now be correctly accepted. Callers expecting the system to download the remote file automatically should verify current behavior (this change only alters validation/handling, not automatic fetching).

Tests:
- New tests included to cover URL handling, validation, and serialization behavior.

text:
Add support for case-changing modifiers and improve key-pattern modifier parsing

This PR enhances BibTeX key generation by integrating the existing formatters and adding support for title/capitalize/sentence case modifiers in label patterns. Key changes:

- BibtexKeyPatternUtil
  - applyModifiers now uses Formatters.getFormatterForModifier(...) to resolve modifiers (falls back to explicit handling for known cases). This enables use of centralized formatters for modifiers like title_case, capitalize, sentence_case and others.
  - Improved handling of parenthesised alternate text modifiers (e.g. [author:(No Author)]) — these are now applied only if the field is empty.
  - Updated parseFieldMarker to correctly parse modifiers containing parenthesis and escaped characters (handles escaped colons and parentheses).
  - Minor behavior improvements around abbreviation generation, unknown modifier logging and empty-field handling.

- Formatters
  - Exposed lists of available formatters and composed ALL list. getFormatterForModifier(...) now looks up formatters by key and also handles the special string aliases "lower" and "upper".
  - CASE_CHANGERS includes TitleCase, Capitalize, SentenceCase, etc., so they are available for label modifiers.

- New Title model
  - Added Title class to represent parsed title words (used by title-case related formatters).

- Tests
  - MakeLabelWithDatabaseTest verifies generation of keys, duplicate handling, regex replacements and the new modifiers (lower/upper/title_case/capitalize/sentence_case, plus :abbr combinations).

Overall this change centralizes modifier handling, enables case-changing modifiers in bibtex key patterns, and hardens parsing of complex field markers. Files touched: BibtexKeyPatternUtil.java, Formatters.java, new Title.java and updated/added unit tests.

text:
Refactor and enhance main UI frame and background file-linking action

This PR introduces a number of user-interface improvements and background-task handling refinements:

JabRefFrame (main window)
- Reworked main frame to use JavaFX components (MenuBar, ToolBar, SplitPane, TabPane/DnD tab pane) and improved layout initialization.
- Add drag-and-drop support for opening .bib files via the tabbed pane.
- Integrate SidePaneManager and DndTabPaneFactory for draggable tabs and side components.
- Add GlobalSearchBar integration and keep search query in sync when switching tabs.
- Improved tab management: add/remove tabs, update tab titles with unique path parts, tooltips with absolute paths and track focused/active BasePanel in StateManager.
- Autosave/Backup integration: start/stop AutosaveManager and BackupManager for contexts as appropriate, register AutosaveUIManager for UI feedback.
- Undo/redo listener registration per BasePanel via an internal UndoRedoEventManager.
- Implement a telemetry opt-in dialog shown after startup if telemetry wasn't already asked, and persist the choice to preferences.
- Improve quit/close behavior: prompt to save modified local databases, properly convert/close shared databases, wait for save operations to finish before shutdown and tear down application resources.
- Provide key bindings (focus table, next/previous library, adjust table font sizes, global search focus) and toolbar/menu wiring for many actions.
- Add progress bar visibility control (placeholder for future reimplementation of indeterminate state).
- Misc: FileHistory handling, remembering last-focused tab, notifications via DialogService.

AutoLinkFilesAction
- Move file linking process to a background JavaFX Task and run it through a TaskExecutor to avoid blocking the UI thread.
- Show a progress dialog while searching for files using DialogService.showProgressDialogAndWait().
- Use AutoSetFileLinksUtil to perform file detection and link updates and capture edits in a NamedCompound undo entry, which is committed to the UndoManager on success.
- Improved executability binding: action is enabled only when a database is active and one or more entries are selected; status message updated accordingly.

Overall this change cleans up UI/UX, moves expensive operations off the UI thread, improves tab and state handling, and makes autosave/backup and telemetry behavior more robust.

Fix autosave implementation to avoid leaving temporary files and to reliably manage autosave state.

What changed
- Reworked AutoSaveManager to write autosave data to a dedicated autosave file (.$<originalName>$) via SaveSession.commit(backupFile).
- Disabled creation of extra backup files during autosave (withMakeBackup(false)) and preserve the database encoding when saving (withEncoding(panel.getEncoding())).
- Added and exposed helper methods to manage autosaves: getAutoSaveFile(File), deleteAutoSaveFile(BasePanel), clearAutoSaves(), and newerAutoSaveExists(File).
- Ensure previously running timers are cancelled before starting a new autosave timer to avoid leaking Timer objects; autosave uses the user-configured interval from preferences.
- Autosave only runs for modified BasePanels that have an associated database file.

Why
- Autosave previously left temporary/backup files behind and behaved inconsistently. The new implementation writes directly to a predictable autosave file name and prevents creation of intermediate backup files, resolving the issue reported in #1270.

Notes
- No public API breaking changes. The change improves reliability and cleanup of autosave files and adds convenient utilities for checking/deleting autosaves.

text:
Problem

Manual save and autosave could run at the same time and cause a race/exception when both tried to replace the same target file (moving the temporary file into place). This caused hard-to-reproduce errors when a manual save collided with an autosave.

What I changed

- Implemented a global save throttler: added GlobalSaveManager (singleton) which serializes save operations by scheduling them via a DelayTaskThrottler. Saves are queued/throttled and executed sequentially to avoid concurrent access to the same file.
- Introduced JabRefFileWriter to replace AtomicFileWriter in most places. JabRefFileWriter wraps an OutputStreamWriter and collects encoding-problem characters so callers can react to encoding issues after the write.
- Refactored SaveDatabaseAction to use GlobalSaveManager:
  - save(...) now schedules a save via GlobalSaveManager and waits on the Future result.
  - SaveResult returns encoding problems and field changes. SaveDatabaseAction registers undoable field changes from the result.
  - Saves are cancellable/handled if interrupted.
- Updated call sites to pass GlobalSaveManager.INSTANCE to SaveDatabaseAction (JabRefFrame, AutosaveUiManager, SaveAction, SaveAllAction, SharedDatabaseLoginDialogViewModel, tests).
- Moved file-writing logic into GlobalSaveManager.saveThrottled so autosave/manual saves share the same throttling/IO path.
- Replaced remaining usages of AtomicFileWriter with JabRefFileWriter (MSBibExporter, TemplateExporter, BackupManager, CLI argument save path).
- Made DelayTaskThrottler generic and adjusted its API (scheduleTask now accepts Callable<T> and returns ScheduledFuture<T>; schedule(Runnable) delegates to scheduleTask). Fixed some concurrency typing and logging around cancellation.
- Minor cleanups (removed stray newline in AtomicFileOutputStream, updated AutosaveEvent javadoc referencing GlobalSaveManager).
- Updated tests to use GlobalSaveManager.INSTANCE and adjusted mocks/fields.

Why

Serializing save operations avoids the race where two concurrent saves (manual + autosave) try to move temporary files over the same target file at the same time. The throttler acts as a simple queue/debouncer for save tasks.

Issues fixed

- Fixes #6684
- Fixes #6644
- Fixes #6102
- Fixes #6000

Notes / Backwards compatibility

- These are internal API changes; public UI/API is unaffected. SaveDatabaseAction now requires a GlobalSaveManager instance (changed call sites are updated in this PR).
- GlobalSaveManager provides a shutdown() method (used if needed during app shutdown).
- Save operations are now asynchronous internally but SaveDatabaseAction waits for completion and integrates results (encoding problems, field changes) as before.

Testing

- Manually tested saving and autosave behavior to ensure no exceptions occur when triggering manual save and autosave at the same time.
- Existing unit tests updated to construct SaveDatabaseAction with GlobalSaveManager.INSTANCE.

TODO

- Consider further cleanup of writer implementations or migrating to a centralized writer factory.
- Add unit tests that simulate concurrent save requests to stress the new throttler (not added in this PR).

Summary

Fixes the bug where the cleanup routine was executed on the wrong entry after fetching metadata from a DOI. This caused cleanup operations (e.g. field normalization, removal of junk fields) to be applied to a different entry than the one that received the fetched metadata.

What I changed

- Ensure the cleanup is applied to the entry that was updated by the DOI fetch operation, not to a previously selected or different entry. The code now passes and uses the correct entry reference when invoking cleanup.

Why

When fetching metadata by DOI, the fetch/update flow could lose the reference to the updated entry and mistakenly run cleanup on some other entry (for example the selection before the fetch). This produced inconsistent state and surprising results for users.

Testing

- CHANGELOG.md updated to mention this fix.
- Manually tested the DOI fetch + cleanup flow in a running JabRef instance to verify the cleanup is now applied to the correct entry.
- No automated tests were added in this PR.

How to verify

1. Take two entries in a library (A and B).
2. Select A, then trigger fetch metadata by DOI for B (or fetch DOI for an entry while selection changes). Previously cleanup might run on the wrong entry.
3. After this PR, the entry that received the fetched DOI metadata should be the one that gets cleanup applied (fields normalized/removed), and the other entry should remain unchanged.

Related

Fixes #6267

Summary
- Replace the internal LatexToUnicode implementation with the external latex2unicode library (via a small adapter).

What I changed
- Added dependency: com.github.tomtung:latex2unicode_2.12:0.2-SNAPSHOT (build.gradle).
- Added LatexToUnicodeAdapter which calls LaTeX2Unicode.convert(...) and normalizes the output (NFC).
- Removed the internal LatexToUnicode class implementation.
- Updated callers to use the new adapter (Layout formatter and BibEntry latex-free caching).
- Updated unit tests to reflect the new conversion behavior and one test marked as ignored.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md and external-libraries.txt to document the new dependency.

Behavioral differences / compatibility notes
- The new library produces precomposed Unicode characters and normalizes output; this fixes many prior conversion issues (see issues below).
- Some conversions now remove unknown commands instead of keeping them (tests adjusted accordingly).
- Combining-accent output changed to precomposed characters in several cases (tests updated).
- Non-breaking spaces produced previously for some constructions (e.g. 32~{mA}) are now regular spaces in the latex-free output.
- The special apostrophe-to-ŉ conversion is no longer performed; apostrophes remain as-is in those cases.

Tests
- Tests were updated to match the new conversion results; one test was annotated with @Ignore because the behavior is debatable and not a standard LaTeX command.

Motivation / Issues
- Motivation discussed in #2465. This change fixes many conversion problems previously reported, including the cases discussed in #2063 and #207.

Notes for reviewers
- Pay attention to the changed expectations in unit tests (they document the new behavior).
- The adapter keeps conversion logic outside JabRef, simplifying maintenance and taking advantage of the external library's updates and bug fixes.

- Backward-compatible: visible output is unchanged for documents without non-displayable fields.
- Fixes formatting issues where hidden/internal fields previously affected indentation.

Tests

- New tests verify that indentation is computed only from displayable fields and that output matches expected formatting for mixed-field inputs.

- Introduce VersionWorker: performs background check for the latest JabRef version, handles connection errors and presents results to the user (either via console output or dialogs) depending on whether the check was manual or automatic.

  - Add VersionPreferences class and supporting JabRefPreferences methods (storeVersionPreferences, getVersionPreferences) to persist the ignored update version.
  - Add storage/retrieval for preview preferences in JabRefPreferences (storePreviewPreferences, getPreviewPreferences).

Bugfixes and improvements

- Fix malformed changelog link HTML in NewVersionDialog so the changelog link is clickable and opens properly in the browser.
- Improve error reporting when the update server cannot be reached: log a warning, show a message to the user when the check was manually requested, and write a notice to the main frame output for automatic checks.

text:
Fix Unicode -> LaTeX conversion for characters outside the BMP (fixes #7387)

Summary
- Fixes a bug in UnicodeToLatexFormatter where characters with code points above Character.MAX_VALUE (i.e. represented as surrogate pairs) were handled incorrectly and could produce wrong output.
- Adds a mapping for the mathematical italic epsilon (U+1D716) to the HTMLUnicodeConversionMaps so it is converted to "$\\epsilon$".
- Adds a unit test that verifies conversion of a high-codepoint character and updates the changelog.

What I changed
- UnicodeToLatexFormatter.java
  - Properly handle supplementary code points by using code point-aware logic: appendCodePoint(...) for non-BMP characters and skip the extra index for the surrogate pair so it is not processed twice.
  - Keeps existing behavior for mapped characters while preventing surrogate halves from being treated as separate chars.

- HTMLUnicodeConversionMaps.java
  - Added an entry for U+1D716 (mathematical italic epsilon) mapped to "$\\epsilon$" and fixed a trailing-comma/formatting issue in the surrounding array.

- UnicodeToLatexFormatterTest.java
  - Added formatHighCodepointUnicodeCharacter() to assert correct conversion of a supplementary character ("\uD835\uDF16" -> "$\\epsilon$").

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Documented the bugfix.

Why this is needed
- Some Unicode characters are represented as surrogate pairs in Java. Previously the formatter could interpret the surrogate halves separately which resulted in incorrect conversions for characters with code points > Character.MAX_VALUE. This change ensures such characters are handled as single code points and converted correctly.

Tests & checklist
- Added unit test for the high-codepoint conversion.
- CHANGELOG updated.
- Manually tested in a running JabRef build.

Note
- The mapping of U+1D716 uses "$\\epsilon$" which may require amsmath in LaTeX documents.

text:
Fixes #5905

Summary:
Set BibEntry to 'changed' state before updating its entry type. Previously, the changed flag was updated after changing the entry type, so property listeners (for example, entry.typeProperty().addListener(...)->updateCodeArea()) observed the new type while changed == false. This caused SourceTab to generate incorrect BibTeX code.

What I changed:
- Ensure the BibEntry changed flag is set (setChanged(true)) before calling setType(...) so listeners see the entry as changed when the type is updated.

Why:
- Listeners that react to type changes rely on the changed state to decide how to update views/code. Setting the changed flag first prevents incorrect code generation and keeps the UI/state consistent.

Testing:
- Manually tested the changed behavior in a running JabRef instance. No automated tests or CHANGELOG updates were added.

- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance. No automated tests were added in this PR.

Allow users to add and delete multiple files at once from the General tab. This change updates the UI and backend to support multi-file uploads and bulk deletion operations, including selection controls, progress feedback, and validation.

  - Added client-side validation and user-friendly error messages (file size, type, and total file count limits).

- Backend/API
  - Endpoint(s) updated to accept an array of files for upload and to accept a list of file IDs for bulk deletion.
  - Bulk operations are handled atomically where possible; partial failures return per-file results so the UI can present detailed feedback.
  - Validation enforced server-side for file type, individual size, and overall limits.

- Tests and documentation
  - Unit and integration tests added/updated for multi-file upload and bulk delete flows.
  - Updated user-facing documentation and help text in the General tab describing multi-file behavior and limits.

Why:

Users requested the ability to manage multiple attachments at once to speed up workflows and reduce repetitive operations when uploading or cleaning up files in the General tab.

How to test:

1. Open the General tab.

Fix for issue #6966 — Open all linked files of multiple selected entries

Summary
- Extend the "Open file" action so it can open all linked files for multiple selected entries (previously required exactly one selected entry).
- Update actionable availability so the option is enabled when at least one selected entry has linked files.
