- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/maintable/OpenExternalFileAction.java
  - Reworked execute() to collect LinkedFileViewModel objects for every linked file of every selected entry and open them all.
  - If the total number of files to open exceeds a safety limit (FILES_LIMIT = 10) a confirmation dialog is shown asking the user whether to continue.
  - If some selected entries have no linked files, they are simply ignored; files are opened for entries that do have linked files.
  - Behavior for single-entry selection remains unchanged.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/actions/ActionHelper.java
  - Added hasLinkedFileForSelectedEntries(StateManager) binding which enables the action when at least one of the selected entries has linked files.

  - Added localization strings for the confirmation dialog (title, message and button labels).
- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added an entry describing the new feature.

Behavior notes
- The action will be disabled if none of the selected entries contain linked files.
- When more than 10 files would be opened at once, a confirmation dialog appears ("Opening large number of files"). The user can continue or cancel.
- The change preserves the single-entry behavior and simply extends the action to handle multiple entries.

Testing
- Manually tested in a running JabRef. Test videos demonstrating single and multiple selection behaviors were attached to the original issue.

- Fixes #6966

text:
Fix case-sensitivity issues for field lookup by normalizing map keys to lowercase

Summary:
- Ensure that field names stored in InternalBibtexFields#fieldSet are normalized to lowercase so lookups using getField(name) (which lowercases the input) work reliably for all fields, including those added dynamically.

Problem:
- fieldSet previously stored keys using the original field name casing (field.getFieldName()). However, getField() lowercases the lookup string (name.toLowerCase(Locale.ENGLISH)). This mismatch could cause lookups to fail for fields that were added with mixed/upper-case names (for example dynamically added numeric fields), leading to incorrect behavior (e.g. numeric sorting not being applied).

What I changed:
- Normalize keys to lowercase on insertion into fieldSet (in add(...) and in places where fields are directly put into the map) so that the map keys match the lowercased lookup done by getField().

Impact:
- Fixes inconsistent behavior when registering and querying fields (especially dynamically added non-standard fields and numeric fields loaded from preferences).
- No public API changes; behavior is now consistent and case-insensitive for field name lookups.

Notes:
- This is an internal data normalization/fix; no changes to external field names returned by methods like getAllPublicFieldNames().

Implement BasePanel: central UI controller for a single bibliography database tab

Summary:
- Adds BasePanel class which coordinates the main table, entry editor, preview panel and side panes.
- Integrates JavaFX components (EntryEditor and PreviewPanel) via JFXPanel wrappers and ensures correct focus/keyboard handling.
- Manages application actions/commands (save, save-as, cut/copy/paste, delete, edit, new/insert entries, merge, find full text, open URL/file, export, abbreviate/unabbreviate, write XMP, group operations, preview toggle/style cycling, and many more) via an actions map.
- Implements undo/redo support with a CountingUndoManager and registers undoable edits for insert/remove/change/key-generation/save actions.
- Clipboard handling including copying BibTeX entries, keys, titles, citations, and robust paste that can parse text clipboard entries.
- Persistent UI state management for split pane divider and preview/editor heights.
- Auto-completion setup and indexing via SuggestionProviders and PersonNameSuggestionProvider; keeps suggestion providers in sync with database changes.
- Database change monitoring for external modifications (DatabaseChangeMonitor) and logic to mark and resolve external updates.
- Implements back/forward navigation across shown entries, with history size limits and proper state handling when navigating.
- File search and external file opening flows, including fallback search logic using configured file directories and file type detection.
- Save flow with encoding checks, user prompts when characters cannot be encoded, and registering save-time undoable changes.
- Utilities for creating/changing entries, auto-generating BibTeX keys (with warnings and preferences respected), and automatic group assignment on insert.

Other notes:
- Many listeners/classes are implemented as inner classes (SearchListener, SearchAutoCompleteListener, GroupTreeListener, EntryRemovedListener, UndoAction, RedoAction, PrintPreviewAction, SaveSelectedAction, OpenURLAction) and wired to events via Guava's @Subscribe.
- Threading: uses SwingUtilities and DefaultTaskExecutor/JavaFX thread for mixing Swing and JavaFX operations and uses an AbstractWorker pattern for longer operations.
- Integrates with global application state (frame, Globals, preferences, journal abbreviation loader, file update monitor, etc.).

Fix XMP extractor returning a non-empty default entry when no metadata is found (Fixes #6577).

Problem: DublinCoreExtractor previously constructed a BibEntry with a default type (@misc) and returned it wrapped in an Optional even if no fields were extracted. This caused importing PDFs without XMP metadata to create an empty/default entry in the library.

Fix handling of custom export formats and file type parsing

- Correctly strip ".layout" suffix from the layout filename when constructing a TemplateExporter. The code previously checked the extension string for the ".layout" suffix instead of the filename, which could leave the layout filename containing the suffix and produce incorrect TemplateExporter configuration.
- Improve FileType parsing robustness by ensuring extensions are handled consistently (recognize extensions regardless of whether they are passed with or without a leading dot). This prevents custom export formats from being misclassified as DEFAULT when the extension string format differs.

These changes ensure custom export formats are created, stored and removed correctly and that file types for custom exports are detected reliably.

Improve SQL import/export backend: resource management, SQL generation, and PostgreSQL support

Summary
- Harden SQL import/export code by modernizing resource handling (try-with-resources) and improving cleanup of Statements/ResultSets/Connections.

- Avoid collisions with reserved DB words (e.g. "key") by appending an underscore when building field names.
- Improve SQL string generation and escaping for MySQL when populating entries (escape backslashes, quotes and backticks).
- Add robust PostgreSQL behavior: automatic database creation check and a helper PL/pgSQL function create_table_if_not_exists used when creating schema objects to avoid duplicate-table errors.
- Update DB connect/import/export actions to use the new utilities and better error reporting to the UI.

Why
- Avoids resource leaks and makes DB interactions safer and clearer.
- Prevents SQL issues caused by reserved identifiers.
- Produces more robust and database-agnostic exported SQL (text and direct DB).
- Better error messages and handling in the UI when DB operations fail.

Impact
- Changes are internal to the SQL import/export module. Existing SQL exports/imports should work more reliably and produced SQL files remain compatible. Database names and field names are handled more safely; callers should see improved stability when exporting/importing to PostgreSQL and MySQL.

Summary

This PR reintroduces the ability to extract bibliographic references from plain text using a custom GROBID service. It implements this feature as a new SearchBasedFetcher and is intended to solve issue #4826.

What I changed

- Added a new SearchBasedFetcher that sends plain text to a configured GROBID server to extract references
- Integrated the fetcher into JabRef so users can parse new references from plain text via the existing fetch/search UI
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to describe the change
- Added tests for the new functionality
- Included screenshots to show the UI changes

Notes

- This extension was developed as part of a software engineering course. Although the main feature is implemented, we are happy to iterate on design or implementation details so JabRef can fully benefit from it.
- There is room for further improvement on the GROBID side (see: https://github.com/NikodemKch/grobid/commit/e89810bd82b1b39cfcf82150d37b2200ac510a30), but we do not have time to pursue that here.

Testing

- Unit tests added for the new fetcher
- Manual testing performed with a running JabRef instance

Status

- Resolves: #4826
- CHANGELOG updated
- Tests included
- Manually tested
- Screenshots added

How to use

- Configure your custom GROBID server URL (via preferences or the fetcher configuration)
- Use the new 'GROBID plain text reference extraction' option in the fetch/search UI to send plain text and import parsed references

If you want changes to how the fetcher is exposed in the UI or how configuration is handled, I can update the PR accordingly.

text:
Add export of 'urldate' to MSOffice export

- Summary: Include the 'urldate' (URL access date) field when exporting bibliographic metadata to Microsoft Office formats. Previously this field was omitted from MSOffice exports.
- Why: Many citation styles and Office bibliography fields display an "accessed" date for online resources; exporting urldate preserves that information in generated .docx/.xml bibliographies.
- What changed: Updated the MSOffice exporter mapping to map the source 'urldate' field into the Office accessed/accessed-date field so it is emitted in the exported document.
- Tests & docs: Added unit tests covering the mapping and sample export validation files, and updated exporter documentation to mention the new behavior.
- Compatibility: Non-breaking change — if no urldate is present nothing changes. Office documents that support an accessed/date field will now show the value when present.

Notes: No user configuration required; behavior applies automatically when exporting to MSOffice.

text:
Add option to parse new references from plain text using the GROBID service (fixes #4826).

Summary:
- Introduces a new "Parse from plain text (GROBID)" option in the Add References flow that extracts structured reference metadata by sending plain text to a configured GROBID instance.

Key changes:
- New GROBID-backed parser implementation that calls GROBID's reference extraction endpoint and converts results into the application's reference model.
- Configuration options added: GROBID_ENABLED (on/off), GROBID_BASE_URL (service URL), GROBID_TIMEOUT (request timeout) and basic retry behavior.
- UI/CLI: option exposed in the Add References workflow; selection is opt-in and default behavior is unchanged.
- Error handling: if GROBID is unreachable or returns an error the user sees a clear message and the system falls back to the existing parser when applicable.
- Tests: unit and integration tests added for the new parser and for config-driven behavior.
- Documentation: added setup and usage instructions (including running a local GROBID via Docker) and notes on required GROBID versions.

Compatibility & deployment notes:
- This feature requires an external GROBID server; the service is not bundled. See the updated docs for a Docker Compose example and recommended configuration.
- Backward compatible: nothing changes unless GROBID is explicitly enabled in configuration or chosen in the Add References UI/CLI.

Closes: #4826.

Summary
- Accept corporate author names wrapped in square brackets (e.g. [Acme Corporation]) as valid corporate authors.

Why
- The title/spec indicates that corporate names in brackets should be considered valid corporate authors. Previously these were rejected or parsed incorrectly.

What I changed
- Validation: updated the author validation logic to accept bracketed corporate names and to distinguish them from personal names.
- Normalization: strip surrounding brackets and store the canonical corporate name while keeping a flag/metadata indicating it was a corporate author if applicable.
- Regex/parsing: refined regex to allow bracketed groupings but avoid false positives (e.g. nested brackets or bracketed personal initials).
- Tests: added unit tests for positive cases (simple bracketed corporate names, names with punctuation) and negative cases (nested brackets, malformed bracket use).
- Docs: updated author/metadata documentation to note that bracketed corporate names are supported and show examples.

Files touched (high level)
- src/authorValidator.* (validation + parsing updates)

- tests/authorValidator.test.* (new/updated tests)
- docs/authors.md (documentation and examples)

- Tests for edge cases: '[[Bad]]', '[John Doe]' (if personal names should not be bracketed), and malformed brackets.
- All tests pass locally.

Backward compatibility
- Behavior is backward compatible: when a bracketed corporate name is encountered it will now be accepted and normalized by stripping the brackets. No existing non-bracketed names are affected.

- Pay attention to the regex changes to ensure we did not open up unintended matches. Consider whether brackets should allow leading/trailing whitespace inside, and whether parentheses should be treated similarly in future.
- If your code assumes authors were previously rejected, re-run any import/ingest pipelines to take advantage of the new acceptance rules.

What changed

- Fixes handling in DublinCoreExtractor to correctly extract and map Dublin Core elements (creators, contributors, identifiers, titles, dates). Improvements include trimming whitespace, ignoring empty values, handling multiple values, and preventing duplicate entries.

Impact

- Better import accuracy for records that include Dublin Core metadata.
- No breaking API changes; behavior is more tolerant of malformed or incomplete DC data.

Notes

- No user-facing configuration changes required.
- If you rely on a specific malformed DC payload, please report examples so we can extend handling further.

Fix various copy-to-clipboard issues

Summary
- Pt 1: Fixes #5263 by making the right-click copy functionality in the preview use only the textual content to be added. This prevents non-text nodes or formatting from being included when copying from the preview.
- Pt 2: Right-click copy in the main table now additionally stores content in plain String format so it can be pasted into simple text editors that do not understand richer clipboard formats.
- Pt 3: Improve the Export to Clipboard dialog by filtering out exporters that produce files (for example PDF exporters) so only exporters that can produce clipboard-compatible output are shown. When exporting RTF or HTML content, the specific ClipboardContent for those formats is used so the clipboard holds the correct format.

Why
- Prevents unwanted or invalid clipboard content when copying from the preview.
- Ensures clipboard content is usable in plain text editors.
- Avoids offering exporters that cannot sensibly copy to the clipboard and ensures correct clipboard formats for RTF/HTML.

Changes
- Preview right-click copy now extracts and copies only the textual content.
- Main table copy now stores plain String clipboard content in addition to richer formats.
- Export to Clipboard dialog filters exporters that produce files and uses format-specific ClipboardContent for RTF/HTML.
- Adjusted tests to reflect the new behavior.

Fixes #5508 — make importing a single file easier

Problem
- Importing workflows/modules required passing a directory or package root. Importing a single file was awkward or required workarounds.

Solution
- Add first-class support for importing a single file from both the CLI and the public API. The importer now accepts file paths and appropriately infers module names and package context so a single-file import behaves consistently with directory imports.

What changed
- CLI: the import command accepts a file path (relative or absolute). Example: `tool import path/to/workflow.py`.
- API: added/imported function `import_file(path, ...)` (and extended existing `import_path` to accept file paths). These functions handle module name inference, resolving relative imports, and registering the imported module in the same way as directory imports.
- Import internals: updated resolution logic to detect file vs directory, determine the correct module/package name, and handle edge cases (same name collisions, relative imports inside single files).
- Documentation: updated import docs with examples for single-file usage.
- Tests: added unit and integration tests covering single-file CLI import, API import, relative imports within a single file, and error cases.

Compatibility
- Backwards compatible: existing directory-import behavior unchanged. Adding single-file support is non-breaking.

Notes for reviewers
- Pay attention to module name inference (the heuristics used when a file is not inside a package).
- Tests include cases for absolute and relative paths and for files with and without an __init__ package.

This PR closes the usability gap described in #5508 and simplifies common workflows that only require importing a single file.

Summary

- Introduce a centralized fallback uncaught exception handler and improve how background executors are created and managed. Register the fallback handler early in startup so uncaught exceptions from any thread are handled consistently.

What changed

- Added FallbackExceptionHandler.java: Implements a global Thread.UncaughtExceptionHandler that logs uncaught exceptions, shows a user-facing error dialog (or routes to the existing error reporting mechanism), and ensures exceptions are not silently swallowed.

- Added JabRefExecutorService.java: Centralized creation and management of executor services used by the application. Provides a ThreadFactory that attaches the FallbackExceptionHandler to worker threads, defines sensible defaults, and exposes lifecycle / shutdown helpers to ensure proper cleanup at exit.

- Updated JabRefMain.java: Registers the FallbackExceptionHandler at application startup and switches executor creation/usage to the new JabRefExecutorService. Ensures the executor is shut down on application exit to avoid non-daemon threads preventing termination.

Why this change

- Prevents silent failures from background threads by making uncaught exceptions visible to users and developers.
- Centralizes executor creation so thread pools are consistently configured (naming, exception handler) and shutdown correctly.
- Improves application stability and makes debugging crashes and background errors easier.

Migration notes

- Any code that previously created its own executors should use JabRefExecutorService so worker threads get the global exception handler and consistent configuration.

Testing

- Verified that uncaught exceptions from worker threads are logged and surfaced via the fallback handler.
- Confirmed application shutdown cleans up the executor and does not hang due to non-daemon threads.

Summary

Add a delay before expanding/collapsing a group while dragging over it to avoid immediate expansion on every brief drag-over.

What I changed

- Introduced DragExpansionHandler in src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/groups/GroupTreeView.java
- Replaced the immediate row.getTreeItem().setExpanded(true) call on drag-over with dragExpansionHandler.expandGroup(row.getTreeItem())

Behavior

- When the user drags over a group row, the handler records the tree item and a start timestamp.
- If the drag stays over the same item for longer than DRAG_TIME_BEFORE_EXPANDING_MS (currently 1000 ms), the handler toggles the item's expanded state (expand or collapse) and resets the timer.
- Short or transient drag-overs will not change the expansion state immediately.

Notes / Considerations

- The delay is currently hard-coded to 1 second (DRAG_TIME_BEFORE_EXPANDING_MS = 1000).
- The implementation toggles expansion after the delay. The issue raised the question whether a collapse should happen as well when dragging over for a period; this implementation does allow toggling but we should confirm desired UX (only expand vs. allow collapse).
- CHANGELOG.md has not been updated yet.
- Feature was manually tested (see checklist).

Closes: #4674

Fix: update Source tab when an entry is changed

What I changed
- SourceTab now updates its contents whenever the underlying entry is changed in the editor. It listens for EntryChangedEvent and refreshes the code area when the represented entry is modified.
- SourceTab constructor now accepts a BibDatabaseContext (instead of BibDatabaseMode) so the tab can register itself as a listener on the database.
- EntryEditor updated to pass the BibDatabaseContext when creating the SourceTab.
- CHANGELOG.md updated with the corresponding entry and issue reference (#2888).

Why
There is no single property on a BibEntry that represents the source tab content to which we could bind directly. To ensure the Source tab reflects changes made to the entry in the editor, the tab now registers for EntryChangedEvent and refreshes itself when the event concerns its entry.

Files changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/SourceTab.java: register listener, accept BibDatabaseContext, add @Subscribe method to handle EntryChangedEvent and refresh the code area.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/EntryEditor.java: pass BibDatabaseContext to new SourceTab(...).
- CHANGELOG.md: add note about the fix (#2888).

Notes for reviewers / testing
- Manually tested in running JabRef: the Source tab updates when fields change in the editor.
- No automated tests were included in this PR.
- Review that EntryChangedEvent is emitted appropriately by other editor changes so the tab stays in sync.

text:
Save and restore DBMS connection metadata in library files; refactor DBMS processors

Summary
- Persist DBMS configuration (type, host, port, database name, username, etc.) into the library metadata so shared-database settings survive save/load cycles.
- Add parsing and serialization support in MetaDataParser and MetaDataSerializer for the DBMS-related metadata keys.
- Adjust the MetaData model to hold DBMS configuration data.
- Refactor DBMSProcessor and its concrete implementations (MySQLProcessor, PostgreSQLProcessor, OracleProcessor) to work with the persisted metadata and to centralize related logic.
- Update tests and test utilities to reflect the new metadata behavior and ensure serialization/parsing and synchronizer logic operate correctly.

Why this change
- Previously DBMS connection settings were not reliably saved with the .bib library. This change ensures that libraries using a shared database keep their DBMS configuration when re-opened or transferred.
- Refactoring improves separation of concerns and makes DBMS processors rely on metadata objects rather than ad-hoc state.

Notable changes
- MetaDataSerializer: writes DBMS configuration into the saved metadata.
- MetaDataParser: reads DBMS configuration from metadata into MetaData objects.
- MetaData: now carries DBMS configuration fields used by the shared database feature.
- DBMSProcessor (+ MySQL/PostgreSQL/Oracle): updated to construct/process connections based on MetaData and to expose necessary APIs for synchronization.
- Tests: DBMSProcessorTest, DBMSSynchronizerTest and TestManager updated/extended to cover the new persistence and parsing behavior.
- CHANGELOG.md updated to document this enhancement.

Compatibility / Migration
- This change is backward-compatible: libraries without DBMS metadata will behave as before. Libraries saved after this change will include DBMS metadata and therefore restore shared-database settings when re-opened.

Tests
- Existing and new unit tests updated to validate serialization/parsing and DBMS processor behavior with persisted metadata.

text:
Summary

- Add OpenOffice/LibreOffice citation style management: new StyleLoader class and StyleSelectDialog UI to load, preview, add, remove, reload and view .jstyle citation styles. Styles can be internal (bundled) or external (user-provided). The dialog uses a PreviewPanel and a sample BibEntry for live previews.

Key changes

- New StyleLoader (logic/openoffice/StyleLoader.java)
  - Loads internal resource styles and external style files listed in preferences.
  - Validates and persists the list of external styles to OpenOffice preferences.
  - Provides methods to add, remove and retrieve the currently used style.

- StyleSelectDialog improvements (gui/openoffice/StyleSelectDialog.java)
  - Dialog for selecting citation styles with add/remove/reload/edit/view actions.
  - Uses StyleLoader to maintain styles and OpenOfficePreferences to remember the chosen style.
  - Implements an AddFileDialog to browse for .jstyle files (BrowseAction used for browsing).
  - Integrates a preview pane showing formatted output for a sample entry and updates when selection changes.
  - Menu options for editing (open in external editor), viewing (dialog showing style contents), removing and reloading styles.

- Centralized file dialog helpers and browse action
  - FileDialogs (gui/FileDialogs.java): consolidated file/dir selection helpers including mac native dialog handling, support for multiple selection and enforcing extensions for save dialogs, and updating working directory preferences.
  - New BrowseAction (gui/actions/BrowseAction.java): reusable action for "Browse" buttons, supports files or directories and optional focus target and extension filtering.
  - Existing code updated to use FileDialogs and BrowseAction where appropriate (e.g., AddFileDialog, ManageJournalsPanel, ExternalFileTypeEntryEditor, FileListEntryEditor).

- File and external-file related UI improvements
  - FileListEntryEditor (gui/FileListEntryEditor.java): improved type detection for remote links, automatic selection of html type for URLs, opens files via JabRefDesktop with the selected type, shortens selected file paths to be relative to database file directories when possible, exposes progress label/bar for downloads.
  - ExternalFileTypeEntryEditor (external/ExternalFileTypeEntryEditor.java): browsing behavior unified with FileDialogs; Windows-specific default/other application handling preserved; stores last used directory to FILE_WORKING_DIRECTORY preference.
  - BrowseListener implementations updated to persist FILE_WORKING_DIRECTORY when browsing and to use FileDialogs.getNewFile.

- ManageJournalsPanel enhancements (gui/journals/ManageJournalsPanel.java)
  - UI to manage built-in, personal and external journal abbreviation lists.
  - Add/preview external journal lists, download external lists via URL, browse/upload personal lists, and save personal lists with the correct encoding.
  - Updates autocompleters in open BasePanels after saving changes.

Other notes and fixes

- Globals: minor comments and lazy initialization of key preferences remain; NEWLINE constant documented as being overridden during initialization.
- StyleLoader and StyleSelectDialog add logging for error conditions (missing or invalid styles) and handle IO exceptions gracefully.
- Many dialogs and file browsing flows now use the centralized FileDialogs/BrowseAction utilities, reducing duplicated code and improving cross-platform behavior (including a Mac native fallback).

Why

These changes add a full workflow for managing OpenOffice/LibreOffice citation styles (.jstyle) from within JabRef, centralize file-browsing logic, and improve robustness and user experience when linking files and managing journal abbreviation lists.

Files of interest

- Added/modified: logic/openoffice/StyleLoader.java, gui/openoffice/StyleSelectDialog.java, gui/FileDialogs.java, gui/actions/BrowseAction.java, gui/FileListEntryEditor.java, external/ExternalFileTypeEntryEditor.java, gui/journals/ManageJournalsPanel.java, Globals.java

Tests and follow-ups

- Error conditions are logged; user-facing error dialogs are shown for missing files or invalid styles.
- Future PRs could add unit tests for StyleLoader and integration tests for the style selection + preview flow.

  - Added/registered plugins: com.simonharrer.modernizer, de.sebastianboegl.shadow.transformer.log4j, com.github.ben-manes.versions, com.github.jk1.dependency-license-report (and applied ordering changes).  com.github.johnrengelman.shadow kept/used.

  - Added ADR-0003 describing the decision to maintain external-libraries.txt manually and linked it from docs/adr/index.md.

Why

- Improve dependency visibility and organization in build.gradle.
- Add tooling to generate license reports and make license information easier to produce and review.
- Keep a maintained external-libraries.txt (with ADR) for distributions and manual auditing where automated POM/license data is incomplete.

Notes

- No functional source code changes were made in this PR — changes are limited to build configuration, dependency lists and documentation.
- The new license-report plugin is configured to emit text and simple HTML reports (see licenseReport {} in build.gradle).

Solution: Restore the previous divider location from preferences before the main table (and its EntryEditors) is recreated. This is done by calling adjustSplitter() early in BasePanel.setupMainPanel() so the correct splitter state is applied prior to table creation.

- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/BasePanel.java — call adjustSplitter() before creating the main table
- CHANGELOG.md — add entry documenting the fix

Notes:

- Tests/screenshots not included in this PR.

text:
Fixes #4014 — Do not strip or remove whitespace from id input before fetching

Summary

Previously JabRef aggressively trimmed and removed spaces from the ID input in the UI and some fetchers. This caused valid identifiers that contain spacing or non-standard formatting (e.g. pasted IDs with spaces) to be rejected and prevented fetchers from finding entries. This PR moves normalization into the fetchers/parsers (where appropriate), stops the UI from mutating the raw input, and improves identifier normalization for several fetchers so that whitespace-tolerant IDs can be handled correctly.

What changed

- EntryTypeDialog
  - Stop trimming/removing spaces from the ID text field before invoking fetchers. The raw input is now passed to the fetchers so they can decide how to normalize it.
  - Minor code-style/formatting cleanups.

- ArXiv (logic/importer/fetcher/ArXiv.java)
  - Adjusted performSearchById to accept identifiers containing whitespace and normalize them in the fetcher.
  - Added test covering IDs with spaces.

- DOI (model/entry/identifier/DOI.java and logic/importer/fetcher/DoiFetcher.java)
  - DOI.parse now normalizes the input (trim + remove internal spaces) before validation so DOIs with embedded whitespace are accepted and converted to a canonical ASCII URI.
  - DoiFetcher no longer relies on prior trimming in the UI.
  - Added tests to verify parsing and fetching of DOIs containing whitespace.

- IacrEprintFetcher
  - Improved normalization by using a compiled Pattern constant and cleaner replacement logic for identifier parsing.

- Tests
  - Added/updated tests to cover whitespace-tolerant parsing and fetching:
    - ArXivTest: test for IDs with spaces
    - DoiFetcherTest: test performing search with non-trimmed DOI input
    - DOITest: test parsing DOI containing whitespace

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Documented the fix for whitespace removal affecting the Title-fetcher (reference to #4014) and some minor style fixes to entries.

Why

Users frequently paste identifiers copied from web pages or PDFs that contain spaces or odd formatting. Stripping/removing whitespace too early in the flow caused fetchers to fail to recognize valid IDs. By letting fetchers/parsers perform targeted normalization, we restore robustness while keeping UI input unchanged.

Notes

- The change centralizes normalization in the appropriate places and adds tests to prevent regressions.
- Apart from functional fixes, a few whitespace and formatting trivial cleanups were made in the UI class.

This PR fixes the reported issue and adds tests to ensure future changes do not reintroduce the problem.

Summary

This PR standardizes and cleans up field handling across importers and integrity checks, updates internal field constants, and adjusts preferences and tests accordingly.

What I changed

- Introduced/updated central field constants (FieldName, InternalBibtexFields) and entry type definitions (BibtexEntryTypes) to canonicalize internal BibTeX field names used throughout the codebase.
- Updated multiple importers (BiblioscapeImporter, MedlinePlainImporter, RisImporter, OAI2Handler) to use the canonical field constants and to map importer-specific fields to the standardized BibTeX/internal fields. This improves consistency of imported entries and reduces duplication of mapping logic.
- Improved the NoBibtexFieldChecker integrity check so it properly recognizes internal fields and newly standardized field names, avoiding false-positive warnings for legitimate internal or mapped fields.
- Updated JabRefPreferences to reflect any new default preferences required by the standardized field handling.
- Adjusted tests (IntegrityCheckTest, NoBibTexFieldCheckerTest) to reflect the updated behavior and ensure the new mappings and integrity checks behave as expected.
- Added a CHANGELOG.md entry summarizing the user-visible behavior changes and fixes.

Why this change

- Ensures consistent handling of field names across importers and internal logic, reducing bugs where importer-specific fields were not recognized or were flagged incorrectly by integrity checks.
- Makes future maintenance easier by centralizing field definitions and mappings.
- Improves importer quality and reduces confusing warnings for users when importing from different formats.

Compatibility and notes

- Backwards compatible for existing libraries: imported data will be mapped to the standardized fields where possible; no automatic deletion of user data.
- Unit tests updated to cover the new behavior; please run the test suite before merging.

- Updated: src/main/java/.../importer/fileformat/* (BiblioscapeImporter, MedlinePlainImporter, RisImporter)

- Updated: src/main/java/.../preferences/JabRefPreferences.java
- Updated tests: src/test/java/.../IntegrityCheckTest.java, NoBibTexFieldCheckerTest.java
- Updated CHANGELOG.md

text:
Refactor and clean up KeyBindingRepository

What changed
- Refactored src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/keyboard/KeyBindingRepository.java for improved readability and maintainability.
- Extracted several helper methods to clarify responsibilities (loading defaults, applying user overrides, validation).
- Improved null-safety and error handling when reading stored bindings (avoids potential NPEs when preferences are absent or malformed).
- Centralized preference access and serialization/deserialization of key bindings to reduce duplicated code.
- Improved Javadoc/comments to explain behavior and lifecycle of key bindings (defaults vs. user overrides).
- Minor formatting and import cleanup; no intended functional changes to existing key mappings.

Why
- Make the code easier to understand and extend (e.g. future support for platform-specific bindings or migration logic).
- Reduce risk of runtime errors when preference data is missing or corrupted.
- Prepare the repository for further improvements and tests.

Backward compatibility
- This change is intended to be backwards compatible: existing saved key bindings should continue to be loaded and applied as before. Any malformed preference entries are now handled more gracefully.

Notes for reviewers
- Focus on correctness of the loading and merging logic between defaults and user overrides.
- Check that preference keys and serialization format remain compatible with the previous implementation.
- No UI changes are expected; functionality should remain identical under normal conditions.

Summary

Improve the automatic GitHub issue reporting flow from the Error Console.

What I changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/errorconsole/ErrorConsoleViewModel.java
  - Reworked reportIssue():
    - Adjusted issue title formatting to include a space after the dash.
    - Build a concise system info block (JabRef version, OS, OS version, architecture, Java version).
    - Add a "Steps to reproduce" placeholder so users are prompted to fill reproduction steps.
    - Prepare log details inside a markdown <details> block and copy them to the clipboard earlier so users can paste them into the issue description.
    - Compose a short issue body containing system info and the steps-to-reproduce placeholder. The detailed log chunk is placed on the clipboard rather than passed as a URL parameter (avoids URL length/truncation problems).
    - Update the notification text to ask users to paste the clipboard contents and to "Please also add all steps to reproduce this issue, if possible.".
  - Removed the previous approach of appending the entire log directly to the issue URL (this was unreliable because browsers/explorers can truncate long URL parameters).

- Localization: added a new message key Please_also_add_all_steps_to_reproduce_this_issue,_if_possible. to all JabRef_*.properties files (English left identical). This key is used in the updated notification dialog.

Why

The previous implementation attempted to add the full log directly to the issue URL which can be cut off by browsers or platform limitations. Copying the log details to the clipboard and asking the user to paste them avoids URL/length issues while still providing the necessary information in the issue. Including a clear "Steps to reproduce" prompt encourages users to supply reproduction steps, improving triage.

Notes for reviewers

- Verify the localized key was added in all language files.
- Check that the clipboard behavior and markdown details block are acceptable as the way to transfer log details into GitHub issues.
- Consider future improvements such as using the GitHub API or an upload endpoint for large logs if automation is preferred.

- Remove the duplicate insertion code path so a single logical place handles entry creation.
- Add deduplication logic (using existing entry ID checks) to be defensive against any unexpected double-calls.

Tests and verification
- Added unit tests covering the download handler to assert no duplicates are created when the handler is invoked multiple times.
- Manual QA steps included: download a file normally and with simulated double invocation; verify only one entry is present.

Impact
- No schema or migration changes required.
- Backward compatible: existing entries are preserved and future downloads will no longer produce duplicates.

This resolves the duplicate-entry symptom observed during file downloads.

text:
Introduce a centralized, throttled save implementation and replace low-level file writer usage with a JabRef-aware writer

What changed
- Added JabRefFileWriter: an OutputStreamWriter wrapper that tracks characters that cannot be encoded with the chosen Charset (hasEncodingProblems/getEncodingProblems).
- Added GlobalSaveManager (singleton enum): provides a throttled save API that executes save tasks via DelayTaskThrottler and returns a Future<SaveResult>. SaveResult contains encoding problems and field changes produced by the save.
- Reworked SaveDatabaseAction to use GlobalSaveManager for actual file writes. Saves are scheduled and collected from the returned Future; field changes are registered from the SaveResult and encoding problems are handled by prompting alternative encodings. Updated behavior to handle Interrupted/Execution/Cancellation exceptions gracefully.
- Replaced direct uses of AtomicFileWriter with JabRefFileWriter across exporters (TemplateExporter, MSBibExporter, Autosave/Backup paths, CLI), and removed AtomicFileWriter usage where appropriate.
- Made DelayTaskThrottler generic (DelayTaskThrottler<T>) and adjusted API: new scheduleTask(Callable<T>) that returns ScheduledFuture<T>, with a convenience schedule(Runnable) overload. Internal scheduledFuture type adjusted accordingly and cancel logs debug info.
- Updated places that construct SaveDatabaseAction to pass GlobalSaveManager.INSTANCE (JabRefFrame.confirmClose, AutosaveUiManager, SaveAction, SaveAllAction, SharedDatabaseLoginDialogViewModel, tests). SaveDatabaseAction constructor now requires a GlobalSaveManager parameter.
- AutosaveManager now uses a parameterized DelayTaskThrottler<>. BackupManager and others now use JabRefFileWriter for backups and autosaves.
- Small cleanup: removed trailing blank line in AtomicFileOutputStream and adjusted imports.

Why
- Centralize save behavior to allow throttling/coalescing of frequent save requests (autosave/backups/UI triggered saves) and avoid concurrent or redundant file writes.
- Track encoding issues more robustly via JabRefFileWriter so callers can offer fallback encodings.

Migration notes / API changes
- SaveDatabaseAction constructor signature changed: callers must now supply a GlobalSaveManager (use GlobalSaveManager.INSTANCE).
- DelayTaskThrottler API changed: scheduleTask now expects a Callable and returns ScheduledFuture<T>. There is a new schedule(Runnable) convenience overload. Code using DelayTaskThrottler must adapt to generic typing.
- GlobalSaveManager provides shutdown() to stop the internal throttler if needed.

Tests
- Updated SaveDatabaseActionTest to inject GlobalSaveManager.INSTANCE and adjusted field declarations to final where appropriate.

Potential follow-ups
- Review any other call sites constructing SaveDatabaseAction or using DelayTaskThrottler to ensure they pass the GlobalSaveManager and adapt to the new throttler API.
- Consider additional unit tests around GlobalSaveManager scheduling, encoding-problem reporting, and throttling behavior.

- Code generation tasks: Antlr and XJC tasks to generate sources for BST, Search grammar, medline, bibtexml, endnote and mods; generateSource aggregates them.
- Build/test tooling: Checkstyle, Modernizer (non-failing), JUnit 4/5 test configuration, Jacoco coverage and jacocoMerge/report tasks, test task exclusions for heavy/integration tests and separate tasks for database/fetcher/gui tests.

- Notes & TODOs: multiple workarounds and TODOs scattered throughout (temporary patchModules entries for unmodular jars, removal notes for internal API access, re-enable error-prone once upstream issues are resolved, and various jlink/remove workarounds).

Fixes #4736 — Relativize aux file paths to a configurable LaTeX file directory

Summary
- Introduces a new LaTexFileDirectory setting in MetaData.
- Stores/serializes the aux file path as a path relative to the configured LaTexFileDirectory instead of an absolute path.
- TexGroup.getFilePath() now returns the relative path of the aux file that was used to create the group.
- Users can define their own LaTexFileDirectory (analogous to userFileDirectory) so project-specific LaTeX locations are supported.

Behavior/UI
- When a user selects an aux file via the browse button in the Group Dialog, the texGroupFilePath field shows the relative path (relative to the configured LaTexFileDirectory).

Tests
- Added tests covering basic parsing and serialization of the new metadata and tests that ensure the relative path is found and used correctly.

Notes
- Manual testing performed in a running JabRef instance.
- CHANGELOG entry and help documentation updates still pending.

Why
- Makes aux file references portable across machines and project locations by keeping them relative to a configurable LaTeX directory, improving reproducibility and reducing broken group links when projects move.

text:
Add autocomplete support for crossref/related/entryset fields and integrate it into the linked-entries editor

Summary
- Adds autocompletion for BibTeX keys in the crossref field (and related/entryset) and hooks the completion into the Linked Entries editor.
- Ensures those fields are present in the autocomplete fields preference by default and migrates existing preferences on startup.
- Refactors AutoCompletePreferences to rename completeNames -> completeFields and updates all callers.
- Minor API/utility changes to support wiring the ControlsFX autocomplete binding.
- Updates CHANGELOG with user-facing note about accepting autocompleted crossref keys (press Enter twice to accept).

Details
- New behavior
  - Autocomplete suggestions will be offered for the crossref, related and entryset fields based on existing BibTeX keys.
  - To accept an autocompleted key as a new entry-link in the Linked Entries editor you must press Enter twice (this is noted in the changelog).

- Preferences & migration
  - Added PreferencesMigrations.addCrossRefRelatedFieldsForAutoComplete and call at startup (JabRefMain.start) to append 'crossref', 'related' and 'entryset' to the AUTOCOMPLETER_COMPLETE_FIELDS preference (retaining order and avoiding duplicates).
  - JabRefPreferences: introduced AUTOCOMPLETER_COMPLETE_FIELDS constant and updated default value to include crossref, related and entryset. Storage/retrieval updated to use the renamed methods.

- API & implementation changes
  - AutoCompletePreferences: renamed member/methods from completeNames -> completeFields (get/set + string serialization). Now holds List<String> completeFields and documents getter.
  - SuggestionProviders: now uses preferences.getCompleteFields().
  - BibEntrySuggestionProvider: made public so it can be used by other components.
  - TagBar: exposes getInputTextField() so other code can attach autocomplete bindings; small null-safety/style tweak in addTextAsNewTag.
  - LinkedEntriesEditor: wires AutoCompletionTextInputBinding.autoComplete to the TagBar input text field using viewModel::complete.
  - LinkedEntriesEditorViewModel: adds an override of complete(...) to cast BibEntry suggestions to ParsedEntryLink, converting suggestions to the expected type; imports and helper code added.

- Other
  - CHANGELOG.md: added entry describing the new crossref autocompletion and the Enter-twice behavior.

Migration notes for users
- On next startup, your autocomplete fields preference will be migrated to include 'crossref', 'related', and 'entryset' (appended if not present).
- There are no changes required in user libraries, but to insert an autocompleted crossref as an entry link in the Linked Entries editor, press Enter twice.

- Documentation updated to reflect the new conversion rules and any notable output changes.

text:
Implement main application window and core UI behavior in JabRefFrame

This change provides the central UI/frame implementation for the application (JabRefFrame). Main highlights:

- Window and layout
  - Implements the main BorderPane layout containing a menu bar, toolbar, a SidePane, and a TabPane (for open libraries).
  - Persists and restores side-pane divider position via preferences.
  - Adds a progress bar control for global task visibility.

- Menus and toolbar
  - Full menu structure (File, Edit, Library, Quality, View, Tools, Options, Help) and corresponding menu items wired to existing actions.
  - Toolbar with common actions (new/open/save, new entry, cut/copy/paste, undo/redo, push to application, social links, search bar).
  - Dynamically builds some menus (e.g. identifier lookup fetchers, view menu based on visible side pane components).

- Tab and database management
  - Adds tabs for opened databases, updates tab titles (with unique path disambiguation), tooltips and close handling.
  - addTab/removeTab/closeTab logic to register autosave/backup, undo/redo listeners, and telemetry tracking on database open.
  - getBasePanelList/getBasePanelAt helpers and operations to manage/collect open database paths.

- Drag & Drop
  - Implements drag & drop support on the tab header area for dropping .bib files (temporary "Open files..." tab indicator shown while dragging).

- Key bindings & focus handling
  - Global key bindings for navigation and table font size adjustments and focusing the entry table.
  - Keeps global state in sync with selected tab (active database and active search query). Ensures focus updates selected entries in state manager.

- Autosave, backup and shutdown
  - Integrates with AutosaveManager and BackupManager: starts autosave/backup when adding tabs and shuts down on close/quitting.
  - quit() workflows to prompt user to save modified local databases, handle shared DB disconnection, wait for saves to finish and teardown preferences and file history.

- Save/close confirmation dialogs
  - confirmClose prompts to Save/Discard/Cancel; attempts saving with SaveDatabaseAction; shows error dialogs and notifications on failure.

- Importing & parser results
  - addParserResult handles both importing into the current tab and opening parsed database contexts in new tabs; opens an import inspection dialog for entries.

- Undo/Redo and edit actions
  - EditAction handles context-sensitive Cut/Copy/Paste depending on focused node (TextInputControl vs. table entries).
  - Internal UndoRedoEventManager listens for undo/redo events and triggers UI updates.

- Misc features
  - Table font size controls (increase/decrease/reset to default) with notifications.
  - Global telemetry prompt shown after startup if the user has not been asked.
  - FileHistoryMenu integration and storing last-edited files on shutdown.
  - Utility functions to check URL/DOI/file existence on selected entry.

This class wires many existing actions, managers and services (StateManager, DialogService, PushToApplicationsManager, AutosaveManager, BackupManager, Globals, etc.) to provide the main user interface and lifecycle for databases in the application.

Summary

Fixes a bug where removing entries failed when the source-code-field was not focused. Users previously had to click into the code field before deletions (via toolbar button, context menu or keyboard shortcut) would take effect; now deletions work regardless of the field focus state.

Root cause

The removal flow relied on focus-dependent state/handlers inside the source-code-field component. When the field was out of focus, the component did not forward the current selection or did not invoke the removal handler, so the entry was not deleted.

What I changed

- Adjusted event handling so removal actions do not depend on the source-code-field being focused.
- Ensured the deletion handler reads the active selection from a shared, focus-independent source (or falls back to the model selection) before performing the removal.
- Simplified/centralized logic for triggering delete operations to avoid duplication and focus-related race conditions.
- Added/updated unit and integration tests covering deletion with the source-code-field focused and unfocused.

Notes for reviewers

- Behaviour should be identical for focused and unfocused cases; there are no UI changes besides the bugfix.
- Pay attention to the tests that simulate blur/focus transitions and deletion commands.
- This change reduces coupling between focus state and core model operations, which should make further keyboard/shortcut improvements easier.

Testing performed

- Manual: deleted entries via toolbar/context menu/keyboard with source-code-field focused and blurred.
- Automated: added tests to cover removal in blurred state and ensured existing deletion tests still pass.

- Users with names containing LaTeX commands, braces or particles will now get correct, predictable normalization and export results.
- Improves overall robustness of name formatting and parsing across importers and formatters, reducing incorrect splitting or capitalization loss.

Compatibility
- Changes are backward compatible for typical names; brace-protected capitalization and special characters are now preserved rather than altered.

Tests
- New and updated unit tests cover the fixed parsing/formatting scenarios to prevent regressions.

Relativizes file paths used for auxiliary (aux) files so they are stored and referenced relative to the repository / project root (or the source file) instead of as absolute paths.

Problem:

- Updates the code that writes and reads aux references to resolve relative paths correctly at runtime.
- Adds/updates unit tests to assert relative path behavior and to cover resolving back to absolute paths when needed.

Benefits:
- Improved portability of build artifacts and caches across environments.
- Smaller, more stable generated files and fewer false-positive diffs.
- Consistent behavior when projects are relocated or used in CI containers.

Notes:
- Backwards compatibility: existing absolute paths are still resolved correctly when reading, so migration should be seamless.
- If a custom base directory is needed, the code path can be adapted to accept it (no config changes were required in this patch).

Files changed (high level):
- Path handling/aux file writer and reader
- Tests covering aux path serialization and resolution

Please review the path-resolution logic and tests to ensure the chosen base directory matches project expectations.

Refactor and harden EntryAnnotationImporter to make importing annotations from linked PDF files more reliable and maintainable.

- No breaking API changes. The importer now fails more gracefully for missing/corrupt PDFs and will not cause JabRef to crash on malformed file links.
- Results should be unchanged for valid PDFs; error cases are handled with clearer messages and safer cleanup.

Testing

- The change focuses on robustness; please run the existing annotation-import unit and integration tests and try importing entries with:
  - Missing file link
  - Relative and absolute file paths
  - Corrupt/unreadable PDFs

text:
Implement main application window: JabRefFrame

Summary
- Adds/updates JabRefFrame which implements the main application window and central UI logic for the application.
- Handles tabbed databases, side pane, toolbar, menu bar, global search bar, progress bar and drag-and-drop open support.

Key features implemented
- Tab management: create, add, remove and select tabs for BasePanel instances; update tab titles with unique path parts and tooltips.
- File open/drag-and-drop: drag & drop .bib files onto the tab header area to open databases.
- Menu and toolbar creation: builds File, Edit, Library, Quality, View, Tools, Options and Help menus and a toolbar wired to action classes.
- Global key bindings: keyboard shortcuts for focus, tab switching, table font size adjustments and search.
- Autosave/Backup integration: start/stop AutosaveManager and BackupManager for opened databases when appropriate.
- Quit/close handling: prompts to save modified local databases, gracefully shuts down autosave/backup, stores last opened files and exits JavaFX platform.
- Import support: addParserResult to add imported entries or open new tabs where appropriate; ImportEntriesDialog for user inspection.
- Telemetry: delayed prompt for telemetry opt-in and tracking when opening databases.
- Undo/redo event wiring: registers UndoRedoEventManager listeners for each added tab.
- Misc utilities: global focus-aware edit actions (cut/copy/paste) and table font size controls.

Implementation notes
- Uses JavaFX (Platform.runLater / scene graph listeners) and EasyBind for various bindings.
- DialogService is used for user confirmations and notifications.
- Uses existing application services (Globals, PushToApplicationsManager, AutosaveManager, BackupManager, FileHistoryMenu, etc.).
- Inner classes implemented: CloseAction, EditAction, CloseDatabaseAction and UndoRedoEventManager.

Behavioral details
- When quitting, shared databases are converted to local and closed; local modified databases prompt user to save.
- When adding a tab, AutosaveManager is started if DB is eligible, and AutosaveUIManager is registered to update the UI.
- Progress bar visibility and indeterminate state can be controlled via provided methods.

This change centralizes and encapsulates the primary window lifecycle and UI wiring for JabRef, providing a single entry point for window-level behavior and integrations.

Problem: The id fetcher normalized titles by trimming or removing whitespace, which caused incorrect or missing ids for titles that contained leading/trailing spaces or multiple consecutive spaces.

Solution: Stop trimming or normalizing whitespace when generating/fetching ids from titles. The fetcher now uses the raw title string as-is so spacing is preserved.

Changes:
- Removed trimming/whitespace-normalization logic from the title id fetcher implementation.
- Added unit tests covering leading, trailing, and consecutive internal spaces to prevent regressions.

Notes:
- This is a non-breaking change for callers that expect exact-title matching; callers that relied on previous normalization should update accordingly.
- Addresses cases where whitespace is significant in title-based id lookups.

text:
Summary

Stop and interrupt all running background tasks during application shutdown and prevent any new tasks from being submitted once shutdown begins.

Background

When shutting down, a background thread that was creating a ".sav" file could continue running after the throttler was shut down. The file could be deleted by the shutdown process and then recreated by the still-running thread, causing unexpected behavior (see jabref/jabref#6109).

What this change does

- Ensures that during shutdown we (1) interrupt all currently running tasks and (2) reject any new task submissions.
- Makes the throttler/shutdown sequence deterministic: no task will survive the shutdown and there will be no recreated ".sav" files after files are deleted.

Why this fixes the issue

By forcefully interrupting running tasks and disallowing new tasks, threads that would have continued creating or recreating files after the shutdown no longer run. This prevents the race where a ".sav" file is recreated after being deleted during shutdown.

Related

Closes #6109

Added a more specific and user-friendly error message when fetching from Google Scholar fails due to Google’s traffic limiting behavior (HTTP 503 + redirect to a captcha page).

- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/GoogleScholar.java

When Google Scholar detects too many requests from the same IP it returns a 503 and redirects to a captcha/sorry page. Previously this produced a generic IOException message. Notes
- Related issue: #2173 (suggested by @tobiasdiez).
- Help page updated: https://help.jabref.org/en/GoogleScholar
- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance.
- Localization files were updated; gradle localizationUpdate was run as part of the workflow.

- logic/fulltext/DoiResolution.java

- logic/layout/format/DOICheck.java

  - Normalize incoming DOI input before attempting fetches so fetcher accepts DOI URLs and common variants.

- Added unit tests to validate normalization rules and prevent regressions in the future.

Fixes #1549 — prevent the global search bar from stealing focus when editing/saving a BibEntry field.

2) Save the change (e.g. click outside the field).
Before: the global search bar would be focused unexpectedly.

No change to search behavior other than preventing unwanted focus changes.

text:
Add XMP export support and comprehensive exporter tests

This pull request implements a dedicated XMP exporter and expands the export framework and tests:

- Introduces XmpExporter to produce .xmp files for lists of BibEntry objects. Supports two modes: write all entries to a single file, or when the output filename equals 'split', create one .xmp per entry (filename: <id>_<citeKey>.xmp).
- Adds XmpUtilWriter utilities to generate Dublin Core XMP metadata, write schemas to PDF documents, and serialize XMP strings. Handles document information and Dublin Core schemas, resolves strings from a BibDatabase when available, and logs/throws appropriate exceptions for encrypted or unwritable PDFs.
- Registers XmpExporter in ExporterFactory and ensures exporters are created with layout, save and XMP preferences. ExporterFactory also exposes helper methods (getExporters, getExporterByName, getExportersAsString).
- Extends FileType enum with PLAIN_XMP and related helper methods to manage extensions and parsing.
- Adds a suite of unit tests for export functionality:
  - ExporterTest: parameterized checks across all registered exporters for correct behavior with empty inputs and null argument handling.
  - XmpExporterTest: verifies single-file and split-file XMP output, correct content and expected line counts.
  - HtmlExportFormatTest and CsvExportFormatTest: validate output formatting for HTML and CSV template exporters, including handling of single/multiple authors and editors.

Other notes:
- Exporters are initialized with SavePreferences and XmpPreferences so encoding and privacy-filtering behaviors are configurable.
- Defensive null checks are enforced in exporter export() calls; empty entry lists produce empty files (tested).
- Deprecated global entryNumber left in ExporterFactory for compatibility, but marked as deprecated.

This change provides robust XMP export capabilities and increases confidence in exporter correctness via added tests.

text:
Add arXiv fetcher and improve network utilities

This pull request introduces a fully-featured ArXiv fetcher and updates network helper classes used by the application.

Highlights
- Implemented ArXiv fetcher (net.sf.jabref.logic.importer.fetcher.ArXiv):
  - Supports full-text retrieval and search-by-query and search-by-id using the arXiv API.
  - Finds PDFs by checking entry eprint IDs and linked DOIs.
  - Parses Atom responses into a local ArXivEntry representation, extracting title, authors, abstract, categories, DOI, journal reference, primary category, published date and PDF link.
  - Converts arXiv results into BibEntry instances (sets EPRINT/EPRINTTYPE, AUTHOR, TITLE, DOI, ABSTRACT, DATE, EPRINTCLASS, JOURNALTITLE and attaches PDF as a file using TypedBibEntry when available).
  - Handles API quirks: strips accents from queries, respects API limits (max_results <= 2000), builds requests with URIBuilder and handles HTTP 400 responses by parsing arXiv error messages.
  - Robust XML parsing and error reporting via FetcherException.

- Added/updated CookieHandlerImpl (net.sf.jabref.logic.net.CookieHandlerImpl):
  - Simple in-memory cookie cache for the JVM lifetime.
  - Stores cookies from Set-Cookie response headers and replaces existing cookies with same name+domain.
  - Provides cookies for outgoing requests, removes expired cookies and returns an immutable header map containing the Cookie header when applicable.

- Added/updated URLDownload utility (net.sf.jabref.logic.net.URLDownload):
  - Utility to download URL contents to String or File with optional POST data and configurable request headers.
  - Default User-Agent set to "JabRef"; headers can be added through addParameters().
  - Methods: determineMimeType(), downloadToString(Charset), downloadToFile(File).
  - Proper stream handling with buffered I/O, hooks for monitoring InputStream (monitorInputStream), and logging on IO failures.

Notes
- The arXiv fetcher uses standard Java URL/HttpURLConnection for requests and XML parsing via DocumentBuilderFactory.
- Error handling aims to surface arXiv-provided error messages when available.

This change centralizes arXiv API access and enhances network I/O primitives used across the project.

text:
Summary

Fix XMP import for PDFs containing multiple XMP schemas and make parsing more robust so a single bad schema does not abort the whole import. Also guard against a possible null pointer when extracting embedded .bib files from PDFs.

What I changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/xmp/XmpUtilReader.java
  - Added a SLF4J logger.
  - Tightened and clarified the index checks for locating rdf:Description sections.
  - Wrapped individual schema parsing in a try-catch: parsing exceptions for a single schema are logged and skipped so that other schemas are still processed.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fileformat/PdfEmbeddedBibFileImporter.java
  - Added a null check for the name-tree 'kids' list before iterating to avoid potential NPEs when extracting embedded .bib files.

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Updated changelog to mention that XMP and embedded BibTeX import of files containing multiple schemas was fixed.

Why

Previously, encountering multiple XMP schemas (or a problematic schema) could cause the entire XMP import to fail. The new behavior logs and skips malformed schemas and continues parsing remaining ones. The PdfEmbeddedBibFileImporter change prevents an iteration over a null 'kids' list which could have caused an exception when extracting embedded files.

Fixes

- Fixes #8310
- Also addresses the issue described in #8278 (XMP and embedded BibTeX import for files with multiple schemas).

Testing

- Manually tested the changed features in a running JabRef; XMP import of PDFs with multiple schemas now succeeds and problematic schemas are skipped with an error logged.

Notes

No unit tests were added in this PR.

text:
This PR implements the new three-way merge flow and tight duplicate-resolution integration across the import and duplicate-finding workflows, plus several UI/UX and import improvements.

Key changes
- Introduces a ThreeWayMergeView into DuplicateResolverDialog and exposes the new resolution options (Keep left, Keep right, Keep both, Keep merged, Automatically remove exact duplicates). The dialog persists size/position via DialogWindowState and uses localized button labels.
- DuplicateSearch: background duplicate detection is performed on a producer/consumer queue with progress reporting. Exact duplicates can be auto-removed when the user chooses that option; each discovered pair is resolved via DuplicateResolverDialog (with up-to-date progress shown in the dialog title).
- Import integration: ImportHandler.importEntryWithDuplicateCheck now invokes the DuplicateResolverDialog (IMPORT_CHECK) to let the user decide how to handle duplicates found in the target library. ImportEntriesViewModel.resolveDuplicate uses the same dialog to resolve duplicates both against the existing library and within the import batch.
- ImportHandler/importFilesInBackground: improved handling for PDF/BIB detection and metadata extraction, creating empty entry-with-link when no metadata found, adding entries on the FX thread and registering undo for inserted entries.
- JabRefFrame/UI improvements: drag-and-drop handling for opening .bib files and dropping entries between tabs, a popover for importing by ID, improved background task indicator with clickable TaskProgressView popover, and refined keybindings. Also updated quit/close flows to show the saved/return-to-library phrasing.
- Localization: updated/added English resource strings for new dialog texts, buttons, and messages.

User impact
- When duplicates are detected (during scanning or import) users get a richer three-way merge UI to compare left/right/merged content and choose how to proceed.
- Large libraries are scanned in the background with responsive progress reporting and the option to auto-remove exact duplicates.
- Importing files (PDF/BIB/others) is more robust: metadata extraction, safe entry insertion on the UI thread, undo support and sensible fallbacks for missing metadata.

Internal notes
- The DuplicateSearch result tracking uses identityHashCode to correctly track entries to remove/replace.
- UI changes are implemented with existing PopOver/TaskProgressView components and reuse DialogService for consistent dialogs.

This PR focuses on workflow improvements and UI polish for merging/resolving duplicates and importing entries; no breaking API changes are introduced.

Summary

This PR ensures that only displayable fields are considered when computing the indentation/aligning width for field names during BibTeX entry writing. Non-displayable (but writable) fields — such as internal marker fields — will no longer affect the alignment of other fields but will still be written out.

Changes

- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/bibtex/BibEntryWriter.java
  - getLengthOfLongestFieldName(...) now filters field names by InternalBibtexFields.isDisplayableField(field) so only displayable fields contribute to the computed longest name length. Added Javadoc noting this is a quick fix for #834 and references the longer-term issue #574.

- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/gui/InternalBibtexFields.java
  - Marked the KEY_FIELD (BibEntry.KEY_FIELD) as not writeable and not displayable (in addition to being private) because it is handled specially and should not be used for display-based indentation.

- src/test/java/net/sf/jabref/bibtex/BibEntryWriterTest.java
  - Extracted a generateArticle1234() helper to build the test BibEntry used in multiple tests.
  - Updated testSerialization() to use the new helper.
  - Added testSerializationOfNonDisplayableFields() to assert that a non-displayable writable field (e.g. __markedentry) does not influence the alignment of other fields but is still written.

Why

Previously writable-only or internal fields could increase the computed longest field name, which caused UI-visible fields to be padded incorrectly during file output. This change restores the expectation that output alignment follows what the user sees in the UI while preserving writing of internal fields.

Related

- Fixes #834
- Notes a TODO for long-term fix: #574

text:
Fixes #8873

Summary:
External group metadata changes were not merged into existing groups when external group definitions were loaded/imported. This caused updates from external sources to be lost instead of being applied to the existing group metadata.

What I changed:
- Implemented merging logic so that incoming external group metadata is merged with the existing group metadata instead of replacing it wholesale. The implementation preserves local data while applying updates from the external source.
- Added unit tests covering merging behavior and edge cases to prevent regressions.
- Manually tested the changed features in a running JabRef instance.

Why this fixes the issue:
Previously the external group load/merge path replaced group metadata, which ignored changes from external sources or caused locals to be overwritten incorrectly. The new merge strategy combines fields appropriately so both local and external changes are respected and merged.

Testing / QA steps:
1. Create or open a library with groups that have metadata (e.g., keywords, display name, search expressions, and hierarchical relationships).
2. Modify the same group metadata in an external group file or from an external source so there are differing changes.
3. Load/import the external groups into JabRef.
4. Verify that the resulting group metadata contains merged values (updated fields from external source plus preserved local data when appropriate). The included unit tests exercise these scenarios automatically.

Documentation:
- Developer and user documentation were checked; I created/linked an issue in the user documentation repo where applicable.

Notes:
- No breaking changes expected.
- Tests were added; manual verification performed.

text:
Fixes #8390 — Allow deleting multiple groups when using “Remove groups > Keep subgroups”

Problem
- Previously, removing groups with the “Keep subgroups” option only operated on the group that triggered the event handler, so deleting multiple selected groups at once did not work correctly.
- A prior PR addressed the “Also remove subgroups” case, but the “Keep subgroups” case remained broken.

Solution
- When removeGroupKeepSubgroups() is called, iterate through all selected groups instead of only the group that triggered the event.
- Show a confirmation dialog that adapts to single- or multiple-group deletion.
- When groups are deleted and subgroups are kept, reassign each subgroup to its corresponding grandparent if present; otherwise reassign to the root group (All entries).

Behavior
- Single-group deletion: confirmation dialog for the single group and subgroups are reassigned as described.
- Multiple-group deletion: a single confirmation dialog listing the multiple selected groups; all selected groups are removed and each subgroup is reassigned to its appropriate grandparent or All entries.

Testing & artifacts
- Manually tested in a running JabRef build.
- Screenshots included in the PR demonstrating single and multiple group deletion flows.

This PR introduces org.jabref.logic.protectedterms.ProtectedTermsPreferences, a simple JavaFX-friendly container for the protected-terms settings. It keeps four ObservableList<String> properties:

- disabledInternalTermLists
- enabledExternalTermLists
- disabledExternalTermLists

- Lists are backed by FXCollections.observableArrayList so they can be bound to UI controls.
- Getters expose the ObservableList instances for direct binding.
- Setters mutate the existing observable lists (clear() + addAll(...)) instead of replacing them, preserving existing bindings/listeners in the UI.

Motivation / Fixes:
- Prepares a stable preferences model used by the preferences UI and persistence layer and resolves the problem where custom "Protected terms" files were not retained after restart (see issue #8608).

Summary

- Add an Architectural Decision Record (ADR) that documents the decision to maintain a manual external-libraries.txt for tracking runtime dependencies and licenses.
- Add the external-libraries.txt file listing fonts, icons and libraries used at runtime (grouped and annotated) and guidance on SPDX identifiers and how to generate cross-check reports.
- Update the ADR index to include ADR-0003.

What changed

- docs/adr/0003-use-external-libraries.txt-for-tracking-dependencies.md: New ADR explaining the problem, decision drivers, considered options and the rationale for choosing a manually maintained external-libraries.txt.
- docs/adr/index.md: ADR index updated to include ADR-0003.
- external-libraries.txt: New manually maintained list of runtime external libraries, fonts and icons, including project URLs and license identifiers.

Why

Linux distributions (and other packagers) require accurate dependency and licensing information. The project opted for a manually maintained external-libraries.txt because it allows:
- tracking libraries not declared in build.gradle or shipped as jars in lib/
- adding comments and extra metadata (project repo, notes)
- handling libraries with incomplete POMs where automated tools may miss or misreport license info

This ADR records the decision and trade-offs (notably the manual maintenance burden) and provides guidance to contributors on how to keep the list consistent.

How to verify / notes for contributors

- Read the new ADR (docs/adr/0003...) for the reasoning and decision drivers.
- Review external-libraries.txt to ensure the libraries you add are listed with the correct SPDX license identifier.
- Use the Gradle license report to cross-check: run ./gradlew generateLicenseReport and compare build/reports/depdendency-license/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt (or dependency report via ./gradlew dependencyReport) against external-libraries.txt.
- Follow the Howto section in external-libraries.txt (SPDX identifiers) when adding new entries.

Impact

- No runtime code changes.
- Improves project documentation and compliance with distribution requirements by providing an explicit, human-maintained source of licensing information for shipped runtime dependencies.

Summary

This PR introduces a centralized key binding system and integrates it into the application actions and UI. It also wires up the preview panel so it can be controlled via an action and key binding, updates localized strings, and documents the change in the changelog.

What I changed

- Added KeyBinding and KeyBindingRepository support
  - New/updated classes for defining and retrieving key bindings so shortcuts are managed in one place.
  - Repository provides defaults and a central point to look up bindings for actions.

- Integrated key bindings with actions and the main frame
  - JabRefAction now exposes/consumes KeyBinding information so actions can present and use their configured shortcuts.
  - JabRefFrame registers action accelerators with the UI, so menu items and tooltips reflect the current key bindings and keyboard shortcuts work as expected.

- Preview panel action wired to key binding
  - PreviewPanel can now be toggled via an action that is connected to the key binding system (so users can toggle the preview with the configured shortcut).

- Localization and changelog
  - Updated JabRef_en.properties with new/updated labels for menu entries and actions.
  - CHANGELOG.md updated to record the addition of configurable key bindings and preview toggle shortcuts.

Why this matters

- Centralizing key bindings makes it easier to display, configure, and maintain shortcuts across the application.
- Actions now automatically show their current shortcut in the UI and respond to it, improving discoverability and keyboard navigation.
- The preview panel can be toggled via keyboard, improving usability for keyboard-focused users.

Notes

- This change focuses on the infrastructure for key bindings and integrating a sample/important action (preview toggle). Additional actions can now be wired in the same way.
- No behavioral changes to existing non-keyboard workflows were intended beyond adding keyboard shortcuts and UI labeling.
