text:
Implement GroupTreeView UI for the Groups panel

This PR adds/updates the GroupTreeView Java implementation used for the groups side panel. The component is implemented in plain Java (to avoid FXML parsing overhead) and provides a full-featured, performant groups UI with the following highlights:

- TreeTableView based groups tree with three columns: main (icon + name), number of hits, and custom expansion node.
- Debounced search field (400 ms) for filtering groups, with clear button support (ControlsFX workaround via reflection).
- Selection binding between the TreeTableView and GroupTreeViewModel, including support for multiple selection and prevention of selecting via right-click.
- Custom row factory that:
  - Applies pseudo-classes for root / sub-element styling
  - Removes the default disclosure node and provides a custom expansion column
  - Adds a context menu for group operations (edit, remove, add subgroup, sort, add/remove selected entries)
  - Supports drag-and-drop for moving groups and dropping BibEntry objects into groups, with visual dropping pseudo-classes
  - Supports double-click to open the edit group dialog
- Drag expansion handler that toggles expansion after a sustained hover during drag (1 second delay) to allow expanding a node while dragging.
- Respect for the user preference to show group counts; number column binds to the ViewModel when enabled.
- New group button at the bottom with dynamic styling depending on the tree state.

Notes and TODOs:
- The clear button for the search field uses reflection to call ControlsFX TextFields.setupClearButtonField as a workaround. A TODO is left to remove this reflective access when possible.

How to test:
1. Open the Groups panel and verify groups are rendered with icon, name and hit count (if enabled in preferences).
2. Type in the filter field and confirm filtering occurs after a short debounce.
3. Use the context menu on a group to edit, add subgroups, remove, sort, and add/remove selected entries.
4. Drag a group to another position and verify re-parenting behavior; drag a BibEntry from elsewhere onto a group to add it.
5. Hover over a (collapsed) node while dragging for ~1s and confirm it expands.
6. Double-click a group row to open the edit dialog.

This change improves startup performance by avoiding heavy FXML parsing and consolidates group UI behavior in a single Java class.

text:
Summary:
Add DOAB (Directory of Open Access Books) as a new web search source so the app can return open-access book metadata alongside existing search results.

What this PR does:
- Implements a DOAB provider that queries the DOAB API and normalizes responses to our search result schema.
- Integrates the DOAB provider into the search aggregator so results from DOAB are included in combined results.
- Maps DOAB fields (title, authors, publisher, year, ISBN, URL) into the UI-friendly result format.
- Adds provider-level error handling, caching, and simple rate-limiting to avoid API overuse.
- Adds configuration entries (DOAB_ENABLED, DOAB_BASE_URL, optional DOAB_API_KEY) and documents them.
- Updates search UI to display source label "DOAB" and book-specific metadata where available.
- Adds unit tests for the DOAB client and integration tests that use mocked API responses.

Notes on configuration and rollout:
- The feature is behind a config flag (DOAB_ENABLED=false by default). No DB migrations required.
- Provide DOAB_BASE_URL in environment/config; API key is optional (support for key is included if needed).

Testing and verification:
- Unit and integration tests included in this PR. CI should pass.
- Manual test: enable DOAB in config, perform a search (e.g. "open access") and confirm DOAB results appear with correct metadata and source label.

Impact and considerations:
- Small additional latency for searches that include DOAB; results are merged and shown alongside other sources.
- Provider will degrade gracefully on API failures (errors are logged and skipped).
- Rate limiting and caching are in place to reduce API load.

Docs:
- Added brief documentation on how to enable and configure DOAB in the project README/config docs.

This PR contains a set of cleanup, bugfix and robustness improvements across import/parsing logic, UI/CLI open/import handling, and group parsing tests.

Highlights
- Importers and parsers
  - Stabilized BibTeX and XML-related importers by tightening parsing logic in BibtexParser and BibTeXMLImporter to avoid incorrect field handling and null-pointer situations.
  - Improved Medline and MODS importers (MedlineImporter, ModsImporter) for more robust tag/field extraction and better handling of missing or unexpected elements.
  - Improved PDF metadata importers (PdfContentImporter, PdfXmpImporter) to better detect and import metadata from PDF content and XMP streams.
  - General improvements to ParserResult to better carry parsing warnings and errors back to callers.

- Opening/importing flow and UI/CLI
  - OpenDatabase and OpenDatabaseAction now better handle ParserResult objects and edge-cases when opening files, reducing crashes and showing clearer feedback when import problems occur.
  - JabRefGUI and ArgumentProcessor updated to coordinate command-line file arguments and GUI open/import behavior more reliably (improved handling for CLI-driven open/import scenarios).

- Groups parsing and tests
  - Fixed GroupsParser to correctly parse complex/edge-case group definitions. Updated GroupsParserTest accordingly.
  - Test utilities adjusted (BibEntryAssert) to match parser fixes and to provide clearer assertions for imported entries.

- Misc
  - Updated CHANGELOG.md to document notable fixes and improvements contained in this change.

Why this matters
- Users will see fewer crashes and better feedback when importing bibliographic data from a variety of formats and when opening files from the CLI or GUI.
- Group definitions are parsed correctly, and tests have been updated to lock in expected behavior.

Notes
- No user-facing API changes were made beyond improved behavior for opening/importing and better error reporting. Unit tests updated to reflect corrected parsing behavior.

Improve autosave and backup feature to reduce risk of data loss and make behavior more predictable and configurable.

What this PR does:
- Introduces a debounced autosave mechanism to avoid excessive disk writes during rapid edits.
- Implements atomic save: write to a temporary file and rename into place to prevent partial/corrupt files.
- Adds configurable autosave interval and behavior (interval, on-focus-change, on-exit).
- Adds rotating backups: keep a configurable number of timestamped backups and remove oldest backups beyond retention limit.
- Improves error handling and logging for save/backup failures; adds retry logic for transient IO errors.
- Shows a UI indicator for autosave/backup status and displays non-blocking notifications on failure or success.
- Ensures existing backups remain compatible; new backups use a predictable timestamped naming scheme.

Files/areas changed:
- Core save logic (debounce, atomic write, retry)
- Backup manager (rotation, naming, retention)
- Settings/configuration UI (expose autosave interval, enable/disable, retention count)
- Logging and notification components
- Unit and integration tests for autosave and backup behavior
- Documentation: user guide and settings reference updated

Migration/Compatibility notes:
- Existing backups are preserved; new backup files follow the updated naming scheme.
- Default autosave settings are conservative; users may opt-in to more aggressive intervals via settings.

Testing performed:
- Unit tests covering debounce, atomic write, and backup rotation added/updated.
- Manual QA: verify autosave on edit, focus change, and application exit; verify backup creation, retention, and recovery from simulated crashes; confirm UI indicator behavior.

Notes / Risks:
- Atomic writes and backup rotation add minimal overhead; retention count should be tuned for disk-constrained environments.
- If IO errors persist, user notifications will surface the problem; operators should monitor logs for repeated failures.

This PR closes: improve autosave/backup reliability and user control.

What I changed
- Removed import and field for PreferencesService from ClipBoardManager.
- Changed ClipBoardManager constructors:
  - Added a no-arg constructor that delegates to the existing three-argument constructor (Clipboard, primary selection, ImportFormatReader).
  - Removed the constructor overload that required a PreferencesService parameter.
- Replaced usages of the injected preferencesService inside ClipBoardManager with Globals.prefs (FieldWriterPreferences, ImportFormatPreferences) and kept other behavior the same (e.g. FileUpdateMonitor usage).
- Updated Globals to instantiate ClipBoardManager via the new no-arg constructor and added a brief comment indicating that ClipBoardManager can be injected.

Files modified
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/ClipBoardManager.java
  - Removed PreferencesService field and ctor param
  - Use Globals.prefs for preferences access in BibEntryWriter, BibtexParser, and DoiFetcher
  - Removed unused import
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/Globals.java
  - Instantiate ClipBoardManager without passing prefs and add comment about DI

Why
- Decouple ClipBoardManager from direct injection of PreferencesService and rely on the centralized Globals.prefs instance. This simplifies construction where the PreferencesService was not readily available and moves toward easier injection of ClipBoardManager itself.

Notes / Migration
- This is a breaking change for any code that constructed ClipBoardManager with a PreferencesService parameter; callers must be updated to use the new constructors (no-arg or the three-argument ctor without preferences).
- The code now reads preferences via Globals.prefs; ensure Globals.prefs is initialized before using ClipBoardManager.

Summary:
This PR implements "Extended Hints" as an alternative approach to the previously proposed #4971. It adds a flexible hints mechanism that attaches richer metadata to items (hints can include types, priorities, and scopes) while preserving existing behavior for callers that don’t opt-in.

Motivation:
- #4971 introduced a hints API, but the approach had trade-offs around API surface and backward compatibility.
- This PR provides an alternative design that aims for: clearer semantics, easier extension, and minimal breaking changes.

What changed:
- Introduced a new ExtendedHint type that supports: id, type, priority, scope, and optional metadata payload.
- Replaced the old single-string hint usage in internal pipelines with ExtendedHint where applicable, while keeping adapter layers for existing string hints.
- Added conversion helpers to coerce legacy hints to the new format automatically.
- Updated consumer APIs to accept either a string hint or an ExtendedHint object (overloaded signatures where applicable).
- Implemented serialization/deserialization logic for ExtendedHint so hints are preserved across persistence/IPC boundaries.
- Updated validation and schema checks to include ExtendedHint properties.

How this differs from #4971:
- ExtendedHint is structured (typed) rather than a loose string format.
- Focus on a minimal compatibility layer so legacy code continues to function without immediate refactor.
- Provides explicit priority and scope fields to help downstream systems make deterministic decisions.

Backward compatibility:
- Legacy string hints are supported through conversion helpers. No breaking changes expected for code using the previous API.
- Consumers can migrate incrementally to typed ExtendedHint objects.

Tests:
- Added unit tests covering creation, validation, and conversion of ExtendedHint.
- Added integration tests verifying that legacy string hints are accepted and preserved through pipelines.

Docs:
- Documentation updated to describe the ExtendedHint format, migration path from string hints, and use cases for priority/scope.

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus review on the conversion helpers and serialization codepaths to make sure there are no edge cases where legacy hints could be lost.
- I kept the public APIs backwards-compatible but recommend we deprecate plain string hints in a follow-up once consumers have migrated.

If anything is unclear or you'd like the implementation shaped differently from #4971, I can adjust this approach.

Summary:
- Add SearchBasedParserFetcher helper interface to simplify implementation of search-based, non-BibTeX web fetchers that accept Lucene QueryNode queries.
- Improve LinkedFile modeling: more robust online-link detection, path normalization and safe serialization, plus utility methods for emptiness and locating files in library directories.
- Add extensive unit tests for FileFieldParser covering URLs, malformed inputs, escaped characters, Windows paths and various field subsets.

Details:
- SearchBasedParserFetcher
  - New interface that extends SearchBasedFetcher and provides a default implementation of performSearch(QueryNode).
  - performSearch builds a URL from the provided QueryNode via getURLForQuery(...), downloads the content, parses it using getParser().parseEntries(...), and runs doPostCleanup(...) on each entry.
  - Declares helper abstract methods getParser(), getURLForQuery(QueryNode), and a default doPostCleanup(BibEntry) (no-op by default).
  - Proper error translation for URISyntaxException, MalformedURLException, ParseException and IO errors into FetcherException.

- LinkedFile
  - Introduces a stricter URL regex and centralized URL_PATTERN for online-link detection; isOnlineLink normalizes input (trim + lowercase) prior to matching.
  - Path normalization: when setting a link that is not an online link, backslashes are normalized to forward slashes.
  - Adds NULL_OBJECT sentinel and convenience methods isEmpty() and instance method isOnlineLink().
  - Implements custom serialization (writeObject/readObject) to safely serialize transient JavaFX properties used for GUI drag & drop.
  - findIn(...) now uses Path.of and properly handles absolute paths, checks existence, and delegates to FileHelper.find for relative lookup; catches InvalidPathException and returns Optional.empty() on invalid inputs.

- Tests
  - FileFieldParserTest: parameterized tests added to validate parsing and conversion of file-field strings into LinkedFile objects. Cases include:
    - valid and malformed URLs (with and without escaped colons), arXiv links, and ftp-like strings
    - Windows paths with escaped backslashes
    - escaped separators and XML-encoded characters
    - missing description/type fields and multiple semicolon-separated files
    - behavior for strings interpreted as URLs vs file paths

Why this change:
- Reduce boilerplate in fetchers that must accept advanced (fielded) searches by providing a common implementation path from QueryNode -> URL -> parsed BibEntry list.
- Make LinkedFile behavior more robust when dealing with online links vs local file paths, ensure correct serialization for GUI use, and improve reliability of file discovery in libraries.
- Increase test coverage for file-field parsing to prevent regressions and handle many real-world input variants.

Files changed/added:
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/SearchBasedParserFetcher.java (new helper interface)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/LinkedFile.java (URL detection, normalization, serialization, findIn improvements)
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/util/FileFieldParserTest.java (new/expanded tests)

Changelog:
- The Unreleased section documents added functionality (e.g. extra "Copy DOI" option) — this PR adds implementation and tests related to file/URL handling and the new fetcher helper.

Summary: Change path validation so invalid paths are treated as validation failures instead of throwing exceptions.

What I changed:
- The path validation routine now catches internal parsing/IO errors and returns a failed validation result (or false) for invalid inputs.
- Added explicit handling for null, empty, and malformed paths so they are reported as invalid without throwing.
- Updated and added unit tests to assert no exceptions are thrown for invalid paths and that valid paths still pass validation.

Backward compatibility: Intended to be compatible for typical use, but callers that relied on exceptions for control flow should be updated to check the validation result instead.

Tests: New tests cover null/empty inputs, illegal-character paths, and normal valid paths to ensure expected behavior.

- Documentation updated to mention the new setting.

text:
Add JabRefCLI: a command-line argument parser and help/usage support

This PR introduces JabRefCLI, a dedicated class to parse and handle command-line options for JabRef. It centralizes CLI behavior, provides consistent parsing and usage output, and exposes convenience methods for common flags and option values.

Key changes
- Add src/main/java/org/jabref/cli/JabRefCLI.java
  - Parses options using Apache Commons CLI (DefaultParser / HelpFormatter).
  - Supports a comprehensive set of options: --help/-h, --nogui/-n, --automaticallySetFileLinks, --generateBibtexKeys/-g, --blank/-b, --version/-v, --debug, --console and the following long options with arguments: --import/-i, --importToOpen, --importBibtex/-ib, --output/-o, --exportMatches/-m, --fetch/-f, --aux/-a, --prexp/-x, --primp/-p, --prdef/-d.
  - Provides convenience getters for checking options and retrieving option values (e.g. getFileExport(), getBibtexImport(), getFetcherEngine(), getExportMatches()) and access to leftover positional arguments.
  - Usage/help printing integrates dynamic lists from Globals to show available import and export formats and includes a nicely formatted footer with issue report information.
  - Graceful parse error handling: logs a warning, prints usage and throws a runtime exception.
  - getVersionInfo() / displayVersion() helper for printing build/version info.

- Add CLI localization strings
  - Localization entries (resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties) include messages and usage text needed by the CLI (e.g. option descriptions and the fetcher syntax message).

- Small formatting/behavior details
  - Help output width set to 100 characters.
  - Export/matcher/fetcher option syntax helper: getExportMatchesSyntax().

Why
- Provide a single place to handle all command-line operations and keep parsing logic separate from application startup code.
- Produce clearer, localized help output that includes dynamic information (available import/export formats) drawn from existing Globals.

Notes
- The changelog (CHANGELOG.md) already contains an Unreleased section documenting many recent changes; this PR adds the CLI functionality referenced by new localization strings and CLI behavior.
- Follow-up: wire JabRefCLI into the application entry point to actually act upon the parsed options (opening in nogui mode, importing/exporting, running fetchers, etc.).

Summary
- Trim whitespace and remove non-ASCII characters when parsing DOIs to make DOI parsing more robust against malformed input (fixes #8127).

- Model: DOI.parse now strips all whitespace and non-ASCII characters before constructing the DOI object (DOI.java).

- i18n: Added localization key for the new error message (JabRef_en.properties).
- Tests: Extended DOITest to cover parsing DOIs containing whitespace and non-ASCII characters and added cases for already-cleaned DOIs (DOITest.java).
- Changelog: Documented the change in CHANGELOG.md.

Why
- Users may paste DOIs that include stray whitespace or non-ASCII characters (e.g. copied from PDFs or other sources). Normalizing input improves reliability of DOI lookup and import.
- Explicitly handling IOExceptions from the DOI download provides a clearer, localized error when no DOI data can be fetched.

Testing
- Unit tests updated/added for various DOI input formats (whitespace, non-ASCII, already-cleaned) to verify correct normalization and parsing.

Compatibility
- This is a backwards-compatible improvement to DOI parsing. Existing, valid DOIs continue to work. The change may allow previously failing DOI strings to be parsed successfully.

text:
This PR contains multiple UI and behavior improvements across the main application frame, linked-file handling and the global search bar, plus localization and changelog updates. Key changes include:

- JabRefFrame (UI / main window)
  - Improved drag-and-drop handling for opening .bib files and accepting entries dragged between tabs, including a visual "Open files..." drop tab indicator.
  - Centralized initialization of key bindings and improved handling of global shortcuts (focus entry table, library navigation, new-entry shortcuts, paste handling on macOS).
  - Background-task UX enhancements: progress indicator in the toolbar now shows a TaskProgressView popover listing running tasks; waiting-for-background-tasks prompt before quitting.
  - Telemetry opt-in prompt: Ask user to share anonymous telemetry data (scheduled to show after startup delay) and persist the user choice.
  - Tab management improvements: better tab context menu, tab close flow, and consistent library open/close/save/backup/autosave teardown handling.

- LinkedFileViewModel (linked files & downloads)
  - Download flow improvements: file type inference from MIME / URL, preparation of a BackgroundTask for downloading to the configured file directory, and duplicate name handling.
  - Robust SSL handling with explicit handshake check and user confirmation when certificate chain cannot be validated.
  - Utilities for renaming/moving files, conflict detection and user confirmation when overwriting files; improved error reporting for file operations.
  - New helpers to parse PDF metadata and present merge dialog sources (embedded, XMP, Grobid, verbatim, content).

- GlobalSearchBar (search UX)
  - Validation for regular-expression searches (invalid regex feedback) and an icon-based visual validator.
  - Improved search modifier controls (regex, case-sensitivity, fulltext, keep-search-string) with contextual visibility and behavior.
  - Autocompletion integration with a customized popup skin to provide name-suggestion selection handling.
  - Debounced search execution to avoid excessive search runs while typing and updating results info in the UI.

- Localization and Changelog
  - Updated English resource bundle with strings for empty-entry confirmation, telemetry prompts, download messages and many other UI texts.
  - CHANGELOG.md updated with Unreleased notes enumerating added, changed and fixed features.

Other notes:
- Various bug fixes and small refactors across these classes to improve robustness (e.g. validation, safe path handling, background task binding, undo/redo event handling).

Files changed (high level):
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/JabRefFrame.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/LinkedFileViewModel.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/search/GlobalSearchBar.java
- src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties
- CHANGELOG.md

This PR focuses on improving user experience for core workflows: opening/importing libraries, searching, background tasks monitoring, and working with linked files.

text:
Summary

This PR improves the custom export filter management in the preferences and the export customization dialog. It includes updates to CustomExportList, FileType, and ExportCustomizationDialog to provide better validation, handling of file types/extensions, and a more robust UI for adding, editing and removing custom export templates.

Key changes

- CustomExportList
  - Improved loading and saving of custom export entries.
  - Added validation to prevent duplicate or invalid entries and better handling of missing/obsolete entries when upgrading from older configurations.
  - Ensured consistent ordering and persistence format for custom export templates.

- FileType
  - Extended/updated file type handling related to export formats (extensions and detection). This ensures custom export templates map to correct file extensions and that export file type checks are more reliable.
  - Small refactor to centralize file type logic used by the export dialog and preference storage.

- ExportCustomizationDialog
  - Improved UI flow for creating and editing custom export templates: clearer validation messages, prevention of invalid names or extensions, and safer overwrite behavior.
  - Added enable/disable and remove actions with confirmation where appropriate.
  - Provided better feedback to users when templates are invalid or conflict with existing templates.

Why

These changes make it easier and safer for users to create and manage custom export filters. Validation reduces configuration errors, and improved file type handling avoids mismatches between template names and actual exported file extensions.

Testing notes

- Open Preferences -> Export -> Customize export filters (ExportCustomizationDialog).
- Add a new custom export template: try valid and invalid names/extensions to verify validation prevents bad inputs.
- Try adding a template that duplicates an existing name/extension to confirm duplication is prevented or prompts correctly.
- Edit an existing template and ensure changes persist after closing Preferences and restarting the app.
- Remove a template and confirm it is removed from the persisted configuration.
- Export an entry using a custom template and verify the output file has the expected extension and content.

Backward compatibility

- Existing custom export configurations should be migrated/validated on load. Invalid or duplicate entries will be handled gracefully (validated or discarded) to avoid runtime errors.

Notes

This PR focuses on the preferences and dialog UX/validation and does not change the export engine implementation itself. Further improvements could include import/export of custom template sets and previewing template output within the dialog.

What this change does
- Adds a new xjc configuration and repositories for JAXB/XJC artifacts.
- Adds JAXB/XJC dependencies (javax.xml.bind:jaxb-api and org.glassfish.jaxb:jaxb-runtime/xjc, version 2.4.0-...).
- Introduces a Gradle task named xjc that runs Ant's XJC to generate JAXB classes into src/main/gen for the following importers:
  - medline  -> package org.jabref.logic.importer.fileformat.medline (medline.xsd)
  - bibtexml -> package org.jabref.logic.importer.fileformat.bibtexml (bibtexml.xsd)
  - endnote  -> package org.jabref.logic.importer.fileformat.endnote (RSXML.dtd; passes -dtd and -disableXmlSecurity)
  - mods     -> package org.jabref.logic.importer.fileformat.mods (mods-3-7.xsd + mods-binding.xjb; uses -npa since package-info.java is added manually)
- Declares inputs and outputs for the task (resource XSD/DTD dirs and generated source dirs).
- Ensures code generation runs before compilation by making tasks.compileJava depend on xjc.
- Attempts to set the system property javax.xml.accessExternalSchema = all (note in-file comment says this does not yet work).

Notes / Potential issue
- There is a suspicious line property('env.) inside the endnote xjc block that appears incomplete and may cause a build error; it should be reviewed/removed or corrected.
- The mods generation uses -npa because package-info.java is provided manually to control namespace prefix mapping.

Why
- Centralizes XJC-based JAXB code generation into the Gradle build so generated sources are created automatically before compilation, keeping the generated sources in src/main/gen and avoiding manual regeneration steps.

text:
This PR contains a set of refactorings and enhancements across Globals, GUIGlobals and LayoutEntry to improve initialization, background task management, GUI setup and layout-format processing.

Key changes
- Globals
  - Centralizes a number of global constants and singletons (BUILD_INFO, SIGNATURE, REMOTE_LISTENER, IMPORT_FORMAT_READER, etc.).
  - Adds lazy initialization for KeyBindingPreferences via getKeyPrefs() (using the global prefs).
  - Adds methods to start background tasks (focus listener, stream eavesdropper, file update monitor) and to start/stop the AutoSaveManager cleanly.

- GUIGlobals
  - GUI-only initialization moved to init() to avoid X server issues in non-GUI environments (prevents Xlib connection errors).
  - Sets up table icons and tooltips for different file types, special fields and custom external file types.
  - Loads Emacs keybindings when enabled in preferences.
  - Centralizes colors and editor-related constants and updates entry editor colors from preferences.

- LayoutEntry
  - Refactored to accept a JournalAbbreviationRepository dependency (removes hidden dependency on global state for journal abbreviation operations).
  - Robust mapping of formatter names to LayoutFormatter implementations, with backward-compatible aliases (e.g. HtmlToLatex/HTMLToLatex, UnicodeToLatex/UnicodeToLatex) and a NotFoundFormatter fallback.
  - Improved option parsing: parseMethodsCalls supports quoted parameters (including escaped quotes) and generic method parameter parsing.
  - Adds support for additional layout types in non-entry layouts (encoding name, filename, filepath) and throws clear UnsupportedOperationException where entry-specific constructs are used in begin/end layouts.
  - Improves handling of field/group blocks, nested entries warnings, and highlighting of search hits.

Other notes
- Logging and warnings have been added/improved for missing icons, nested field entries, and formatter lookup problems.
- Several small API/behavior compatibilities are preserved (e.g. handling legacy formatter names).

These changes improve modularity (injecting repositories), robustness of formatter parsing, and safer GUI initialization and lifecycle management for background tasks and autosave.

text:
Fix search highlighting in HTML preview and support JavaScript-safe regexes

What changed
- Add an EscapeMode to SearchQuery to support two escaping strategies: JAVA (Pattern.quote) and JAVASCRIPT (escape JS regex special chars).
- Add SearchQuery.getJavaScriptPatternForWords() to return a Pattern with JavaScript-escaped words when needed.
- Implement PreviewViewer.createJavaScriptRegex(Pattern) to convert a Java Pattern into a JavaScript regular expression literal and escape unescaped forward slashes so the regex can be safely used in the preview's mark.js highlighting.
- Use the new JS-escaped pattern in PreviewViewer.highlightSearchPattern() when calling mark.js/unmark to avoid JavaScript syntax errors for patterns containing "/" and other special characters.
- Ensure GrammarBasedSearchRule is constructed with both caseSensitive and regex flags where appropriate in SearchRules.

Why
- Previously, search patterns coming from the application were not escaped properly for use as JavaScript regex literals used by the preview highlighter (mark.js). Patterns containing forward slashes or JS-special characters could break the script and prevent highlighting.

Effects
- Search highlighting in the preview is now robust for both plain text and regex-based queries.
- The application keeps consistent behavior between Java-side search and the JavaScript-based preview highlighting.

Notes
- No behavioral changes to the search matching logic; this is an interoperability/escaping fix between Java regexes and the preview's JavaScript regex usage.

Fixes #8513 — Support two-argument form of \abx@aux@cite macro in DefaultAuxParser

What I changed
- Updated the citation-matching regex in DefaultAuxParser to accept the two-argument form of the abx aux cite macro (e.g. \abx@aux@cite{0}{Key}). The new pattern uses a named group (?<citationkey>) to extract the citation key and accepts an optional numeric first argument.
- Switched the parsing code to read the citation key from the named group.
- Added a unit test (testTwoArgMacro) and an aux test resource (papertwoargmacro.aux) that exercises the two-argument macro and verifies the parser behavior is identical to the normal single-argument case (entries found, zero unresolved keys, expected counts).
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to note the fix.

Why
Some biblatex versions write \abx@aux@cite in a two-argument form. The previous regex only recognized the single-argument form, causing subsidiary-file generation from such .aux files to produce incorrect results. The change makes the DefaultAuxParser handle both forms reliably.

- src/test/resources/.../papertwoargmacro.aux — test resource with two-arg macros
- CHANGELOG.md — note about the fix

- Manually tested. The implementation uses a named regex group for clarity instead of relying on numeric group indices.

text:
Add zbMATH fetcher and integrate it into the web fetchers

What
- Implement a new ZbMATH fetcher (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ZbMATH.java) that supports search-based, id-based and entry-based fetching of bibliographic data from Zentralblatt Math (zbmath.org).
- Register ZbMATH in WebFetchers so it is available in the search-based, id-based and entry-based fetcher collections.
- Add a standard field for zbMATH identifiers (ZBL_NUMBER) to StandardField.
- Provide post-processing/cleanup for fetched entries (move msc2010 -> keywords, move fjournal -> journal, remove braces from journal/title).
- Update CHANGELOG (Unreleased) to document the addition of zbmath and the ability to add entries via zbMATH ID.

Why
- Let users update entries from zbMATH and add new entries by providing a zbMATH identifier, expanding the set of supported public bibliographic databases.

How
- ZbMATH uses the zbMATH citation-matching API to resolve entries and the bibtexoutput endpoint to retrieve BibTeX data.
- Uses Unirest for the citation-matching JSON request and URLDownload.bypassSSLVerification() before building bibtexoutput URLs.
- Implements Parser via BibtexParser and applies targeted cleanup using existing cleanup utilities.

Tests
- Add ZbMATHTest with unit tests for searching by query, by id, by entry, and cases where no match is found (src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ZbMATHTest.java).

Notes
- The fetcher integrates with existing import/identifier infrastructure and follows the existing fetcher interfaces. Error handling delegates network and parsing errors to FetcherException.
- Post-cleanup intentionally fixes systematic mapping issues reported by the fetcher (e.g. special zbMATH fields).

text:
Summary

Fixes an issue where multiple background task popups could stack on top of each other when opening the Background Tasks popover repeatedly. This prevents duplicate PopOver windows and toggles visibility correctly.

What I changed

- Added a field progressViewPopOver to JabRefFrame so a single PopOver instance is reused.
- When opening the Background Tasks view: if no popover exists, create and show it; if it exists and is showing, hide it; otherwise update its content and show it. The PopOver title, arrow location and content node are set accordingly.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to mention the fix.

Files changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/JabRefFrame.java: introduce progressViewPopOver and implement show/hide/toggle logic for the background task PopOver.
- CHANGELOG.md: add note about the fix.

Why

Previously each click created a new PopOver, which allowed multiple instances to stack visually. Reusing a single PopOver and toggling its visibility ensures only one popup is shown at a time and fixes the UI clutter.

Testing

- Manually tested in the running application to confirm that clicking the Background Tasks indicator toggles the popover and prevents stacking. Screenshot included in the original issue/PR description.

Fixes

Closes #6472 (https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/6472)

text:
Add synchronization logic and tests for special fields and keywords

This change implements utilities to synchronize special fields with the keywords field and back, and adds comprehensive tests for keyword and field behavior:

- Introduces SpecialFieldsUtils (deprecated helper) to:
  - Update a special field and optionally sync it to the keywords field (updateField).
  - Export a special field value into keywords (exportFieldToKeywords).
  - Import matching keywords into special fields (importKeywordsForField).
  - Sync all special fields to keywords and vice versa (syncKeywordsFromSpecialFields, syncSpecialFieldsFromKeywords).
  - Helper to adjust keyword lists when special fields are changed (synchronizeSpecialFields).

- Adds unit tests in SpecialFieldsUtilsTest to verify:
  - Special fields are exported to keywords and cause FieldChange events.
  - Export overwrites existing keywords as expected.
  - No changes are produced when fields/keywords are empty.
  - updateField removes special-field keywords when keyword-sync is enabled and returns the expected FieldChange objects.

- Adds/extends tests in BibEntryTests covering:
  - Keyword parsing, adding, removing, and related change notifications.
  - Date field alias handling (date/year/month conversions).
  - Latex-free field retrieval and alias resolution.
  - General field/set/clear behavior and protection of reserved fields.

These changes improve correctness and test coverage around special-field/keyword synchronization and many aspects of BibEntry field handling.

- Introduces SuggestionProviders, a small factory that encapsulates creation of SuggestionProvider instances for a given field. Update build.gradle to fully configure the project build, dependencies, tests, code quality and release pipeline.

- Repositories: mavenLocal, jcenter and Sonatype OSS.
- Dependencies: pin a comprehensive set of libraries (notable versions: pdfbox 2.0.11, bcprov 1.60, guava 26.0-jre, log4j 2.11.1, slf4j 1.8.0-beta2, controlsfx 8.40.15-SNAPSHOT, junit-jupiter RCs for tests, error_prone for static analysis, etc.).

- Coverage: jacoco tool version set and a jacocoMerge task plus xml/html reporting for CI/coveralls.

- Versioning: when built with the 'dev' property, append a snapshot marker including date, branch and commit hash to project.version (safe filename characters enforced).
- Other utilities: jmh benchmark settings (warmup/iterations/fork), a downloadDependencies helper task to pre-download most dependencies.

This commit centralizes the Gradle configuration and documents important pins and build/release tasks used by the project.

Introduce explicit SpecialField model and migration to separate previously encoded special fields into dedicated fields

Summary
- Add SpecialField and SpecialFieldValue model types to represent application-defined special fields (e.g., read status, priority) and their allowed values.
- Implement a migration (SpecialFieldsToSeparateFields) that converts old encodings of special fields into separate fields when opening/upgrading a library.

  - src/main/java/org/jabref/migrations/SpecialFieldsToSeparateFields.java: migration logic to convert old special-field encodings to separate fields.

  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/specialfields/SpecialFieldValueViewModel.java: view model to display and manipulate special field values.

  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/FieldNameLabel.java: updated to show special-field icons/tooltips when appropriate.

- New model classes (SpecialField, SpecialFieldValue) should be used for future work involving special/semantic fields.
- When adding new special fields or values, update IconTheme and localization strings accordingly.

text:
Implement opening all linked files for multiple selected entries

Summary
- Add an action to open all linked files from multiple selected entries in the main table.
- If the total number of files to be opened exceeds a safety limit (FILES_LIMIT = 10), a confirmation dialog is shown to avoid accidental mass-opening.

What changed
- Added OpenExternalFileAction (src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/maintable/OpenExternalFileAction.java):
  - Collects LinkedFileViewModel instances for every linked file of every selected entry and calls open() on each.
  - Prompts the user with a confirmation dialog when more than 10 files would be opened.
  - Ignores entries without linked files (only processes entries that have files).
  - Treats online links as present and opens them accordingly.
- Extended ActionHelper (src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/actions/ActionHelper.java):
  - Added hasLinkedFileForSelectedEntries(StateManager) boolean binding used to enable/disable the Open file action when at least one selected entry has linked files.
  - Kept/used other helper bindings for file presence checks and multi-database detection.
- Localization: existing strings for the large-file warning/dialog are used (Opening large number of files / confirmation text).
- CHANGELOG.md updated (Unreleased -> Added): documents the new feature and references issue #6966.

Behavior & rationale
- The action allows users to open all linked files of multiple selected entries at once (useful for batch inspection).
- To prevent overwhelming the system / user, the action asks for confirmation when opening a large number of files (default threshold = 10). This is configurable in code as a constant for easy adjustment.
- Only entries with linked files are considered; missing/online files are handled as before by the existing LinkedFileViewModel logic.

Files touched
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/maintable/OpenExternalFileAction.java (new/modified behavior)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/actions/ActionHelper.java (new binding: hasLinkedFileForSelectedEntries)
- CHANGELOG.md (documented under Unreleased -> Added)

Issue
- Fixes / implements feature request: #6966

Summary

- Improve handling of journal abbreviation files and make the repository react reliably to external changes. Fixes parsing corner cases and strengthens file-watching behavior.

What changed

- AbbreviationParser
  - Made parsing more robust: ignores blank lines and comment lines, trims fields, and handles quoted values and different separators more reliably.
  - Better validation of parsed entries to avoid malformed abbreviations being loaded.

- JournalAbbreviationRepository
  - Improved loading and caching behavior: repository now handles lazy loading and explicit reloads more predictably.
  - Added thread-safety and cache invalidation when underlying files change.
  - Ensures lookups remain case-insensitive and that local/user files override defaults as expected.

- FileUpdateMonitor
  - Fixed issues in the monitor implementation so listeners are consistently notified when watched files are modified.
  - Improved resource handling to avoid leaks and race conditions when starting/stopping monitoring.

- Tests
  - Updated ManageJournalAbbreviationsViewModelTest to reflect repository behavior changes.
  - Added/updated JournalAbbreviationRepositoryTest to cover parsing edge cases, loading precedence, and reload-on-change behavior.

Why this matters

These changes fix several edge cases that previously caused invalid journal abbreviation entries to be loaded or prevented the UI from updating when abbreviation files were changed externally. The result is a more reliable user experience when managing and using journal abbreviations.

Notes

- Behavior preserved: user/local abbreviation files still take precedence over the bundled defaults.
- The parser changes are conservative: they aim to accept valid abbreviation definitions while rejecting malformed lines.
- Tests were extended to cover the new behaviors and to prevent regressions.

text:
Add FileUpdateMonitor to watch files for external modifications and notify registered listeners.

- Introduces org.jabref.gui.util.FileUpdateMonitor which implements Runnable and uses java.nio.file.WatchService to monitor parent directories of specific files for ENTRY_MODIFY events.
- Maintains a Multimap<Path, FileUpdateListener> (Guava ArrayListMultimap) mapping exact file paths to their listeners. When a modify event is detected, the monitor resolves the event path against the watched directory and invokes fileUpdated() on all listeners registered for that file.
- Public API:
  - addListenerForFile(Path file, FileUpdateListener listener) — registers the file (by watching its parent directory) and adds the listener. May throw IOException when registering the directory.
  - removeListener(Path path, FileUpdateListener listener) — removes a previously registered listener for a file.
- Threading/behavior: run() opens and uses a WatchService in a try-with-resources block, loops taking WatchKeys, handles OVERFLOW and ENTRY_MODIFY events, resets keys, and exits cleanly on interruption. On unexpected termination, a debug log is written.

Notes / possible follow-ups:
- Currently addListenerForFile registers the parent directory on each call without tracking duplicate registrations; consider deduplicating registrations and unregistering directories when no listeners remain.
- The implementation assumes the WatchService is created in run(), so addListenerForFile must be called after the monitor thread has started (otherwise watcher will be null) — consider moving WatchService creation or adding synchronization/guarding to avoid NPEs if needed.

Refactor and clean up MainTable implementation to improve readability, robustness and selection behavior.

What I changed

- Restructured code in src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/maintable/MainTable.java by extracting several helper methods to reduce method size and improve clarity.

- Simplified and centralised listener registration and removal to prevent potential memory leaks and duplicate handlers.
- Improved keyboard/navigation handling so scrolling and page navigation behave more consistently after model changes.
- Small performance optimizations in painting/refresh logic to reduce stalls for large databases.
- Added and updated inline comments and JavaDoc to clarify intent of key blocks.

MainTable is a central UI component. Over time some logic became hard to follow and brittle during rapid model changes (filtering, sorting, or external updates). The refactor improves maintainability and fixes observable issues with selection and navigation, especially for larger libraries.

Testing

- Manually verified selection persistence when applying/removing filters and sorting.
- Tested keyboard navigation, scrolling, and row selection across a large sample library.
- Verified no regressions in basic table interactions (click/select/copy/drag).

Notes / Follow-up

- The refactor is intentionally conservative: external behaviour stays the same where possible, but internal structure is clearer for future improvements.
- Consider adding focused unit/UI tests for selection and model-update scenarios in a follow-up PR.

- No automated tests were added in this PR.

text:
Fix crossref resolution to comply with biblatex specification (#5045)

What I changed
- Updated BibEntry.getResolvedFieldOrAlias to correctly resolve certain biblatex crossref fields from the referred entry.
- Instead of using a simple flatMap fallback, the code now explicitly resolves these mappings when the referring entry is of type InProceedings:
  - booktitle -> title
  - booksubtitle -> subtitle
  - bookauthor -> author
- Existing behavior for other fields and when a direct field is present is unchanged. The resolved value is still passed through BibDatabase.getText as before.

Why
- BibLaTeX specifies that some fields of an inproceedings entry should inherit corresponding fields (title, subtitle, author) from the cross-referenced book entry. The previous logic did not perform these mappings, causing incorrect/missing values when relying on crossref inheritance.

Notes
- Fixes #5045.
- Manually tested in a running JabRef. Unit tests and CHANGELOG entry are still TODO and should be added in a follow-up.

- This package targets the dev channel only and is not meant for publishing to the Chocolatey community feed without approval.

- If package id, versioning scheme, or publishing destination need to change, update the nuspec and CI workflow accordingly.

text:
Improve main application frame and update changelog

This PR makes multiple enhancements to the main application window (JabRefFrame) and updates the Unreleased changelog entries. Key changes include:

- Drag & Drop: Add support for dragging .bib files onto the tab header area. A temporary "Open files..." tab is shown during the drag-over and dropped databases are opened or imported into the current panel.
- Telemetry prompt: Schedule a telemetry opt-in prompt to be shown once (after ~1 minute) when the user has not yet been asked. The user's choice is stored in preferences.
- Key bindings: Centralize initialization of global key bindings (focus table, next/previous library, font size adjustments, search) and consume handled events appropriately.
- Toolbar & menu wiring: Build the main toolbar and menu bar with wired actions (new/open/save, entry actions, push-to-application integration, global search bar placement, grouped toolbar sections, and many menu items wired to existing actions).
- Tab management & titles: Improve tab creation, selection and close handling (addTab, addParserResult), update tab titles using unique path parts, set tooltips to absolute file paths, and handle tab reordering/closing. Use FileUtil.uniquePathSubstrings to keep tab titles meaningful when multiple DBs are open.
- Autosave & Backup lifecycle: Start autosave and backup where applicable when opening a database and ensure AutosaveManager/BackupManager are shut down when closing tabs or quitting. Ready-for-autosave logic honors shared vs local DB and LOCAL_AUTO_SAVE preference.
- Quit/close flows: Implement confirmClose with Save/Discard/Return options and integrate SaveDatabaseAction for saving; Gather opened filenames for preferences when quitting; wait for saves to finish before teardown; perform Platform.exit() during quit.
- Progress bar: Expose setters to toggle visibility and indeterminate state for the status progress bar.
- Utilities & robustness: Collect canonical paths for open DBs and log IOException when path resolution fails; other small robustness and UI updates (e.g. focus handling, undo/redo event wiring, importing entries via ImportEntriesDialog).
- CHANGELOG.md: Update Unreleased section (short DOI field formatter added and a number of fixes listed).

These changes improve usability (drag & drop, clearer tab titles), reliability (autosave/backup management, save-on-close), and privacy transparency (telemetry prompt).

Refactor MainTableColumnFactory and add support for special columns and tooltips

This PR improves and extends the main table column factory used to build the entry table UI. Key changes:

- Centralized column creation in MainTableColumnFactory#createColumns(): builds group, file, DOI/URL, eprint, extra file type and normal BibTeX field columns as configured in preferences.
- File column improvements:
  - Adds a linked-files column with an icon, tooltip and context menu when more than one file is present.
  - Single-file entries are opened directly on primary click.
  - Extra file-type specific columns are generated for configured external file types.
- DOI / URL and eprint columns:
  - Create a combined DOI/URL column (icon in header) that prefers one field over the other depending on preferences.
  - Cell click opens the identifier in the external viewer (JabRefDesktop) with error handling.
  - Tooltips are shown with the identifier value and human readable text.
- Special fields support:
  - Adds rendering for special fields (icons, tooltips and menus). Ranking field displays an interactive Rating control.
  - Adds a comparator for SpecialField.RANKING and (new) ReadStatusFieldComparator for SpecialField.READ_STATUS so these columns sort meaningfully.
  - Single-value special fields toggle on primary click; multi-value fields present a context menu to select a value.
- Group column displays group color strip and installs a tooltip listing matched groups.
- Several small helpers: setExactWidth, createFileIcon, createSpecialFieldIcon, createSpecialFieldMenu and createGroupColorRegion to keep cell factories concise.

No behavior changes to user preferences; this reorganizes and implements UI behaviors to match configured column settings and improves interactivity and sorting for special columns.

Summary

Add a proper "save changes and exit" flow so the application no longer loses user work when closed.

What this PR does

- Adds a Save & Exit action that is triggered from the application menu, the window close button, and the global/OS exit shortcut.
- Shows a confirmation dialog when there are unsaved changes with three choices: Save and exit, Discard and exit, Cancel.
- Persists application state to disk when the user chooses Save and exit (or when autosave-on-exit is enabled).
- Handles OS signals/window manager close events to run the same save/confirm logic so shutdowns are graceful.
- Adds an optional autosave-on-exit setting so users can skip the confirmation dialog if they prefer.
- Updates UI (menu/toolbar) and keyboard shortcuts to expose the exit action.
- Adds unit/integration tests covering: unsaved-change prompt, saving on exit, discarding changes, cancelling exit, and autosave behavior.
- Updates user documentation to describe the new behavior and configuration option.

Why

Prevent accidental data loss and provide a predictable, consistent exit flow across platforms. This makes closing the app safer and improves the user experience.

How to test

1. Make a change in the application that marks the document/state as modified.
2. Close the window (click close or use the exit shortcut).
   - Expect a confirmation dialog.
   - Choose "Save and exit": verify changes are persisted to disk and the app exits.
   - Repeat and choose "Discard and exit": verify the app exits without saving.
   - Repeat and choose "Cancel": verify the app remains open and changes are still present.
3. Enable autosave-on-exit in settings, make changes, then exit: verify changes are saved automatically without the dialog and the app exits.
4. Send a SIGTERM/SIGINT (or use the OS window close) and verify the same save/confirm behavior occurs.
5. Run the new tests and confirm they pass.

Notes

- This PR focuses on the exit/save flow and does not change normal file-save semantics outside of exit handling.
- Backwards compatibility: default behavior preserves the previous experience (confirmation shown unless autosave is enabled).

Pin Error Prone to a specific version to avoid automatic updates

What I changed
- In build.gradle I added an explicit configuration named "errorprone" and added the dependency com.google.errorprone:error_prone_core:2.3.1 to that configuration.

Why
- The net.ltgt.errorprone Gradle plugin creates an "errorprone" configuration that will otherwise resolve to the latest available Error Prone release. That makes builds non-deterministic and can cause unexpected breakage when a new Error Prone version is released.
- By explicitly creating the configuration and adding the dependency after plugins are applied, we pin Error Prone to 2.3.1 (latest as of 2018-08-17) and ensure reproducible builds.

Impact
- Builds and CI will now use Error Prone 2.3.1 instead of automatically jumping to newer versions. This stabilizes the build and prevents surprises from upstream changes.

Notes
- This change addresses issue #4176. We should update the pinned version intentionally when we want to adopt a newer Error Prone release and verify compatibility.

text:
Add zbMATH entry-based fetching and citation-matching support

What this PR does
- Adds zbMATH as an entry-based fetcher and makes it available in the list of entry-based web fetchers.
- Implements EntryBasedParserFetcher for the ZbMATH fetcher. When searching by entry, the fetcher now uses zbMATH's citation matching API to find a zbl_id and then retrieves the BibTeX for that identifier. If a ZBL identifier is already present in the entry, it is used directly.
- Improves the default EntryBasedParserFetcher.performSearch handling: it now treats a null URL as "no result" (returns an empty list) and surfaces malformed URI exceptions correctly.
- Adds the standard ZBL_NUMBER field to StandardField (StandardField.ZBL_NUMBER).
- Updates unit tests for ZbMATH to use the new standard field and adds tests for searching by entry, searching with no match, and searching when the ID is present in the entry.
- Updates CHANGELOG to mention that zbMATH was added to public databases used for updating bibliographic information.

Implementation details
- ZbMATH.getURLForEntry builds a citation-matching request using available entry fields (title, journal, year, pagination, volume, issue, authors) and calls https://zbmath.org/citationmatching/match. The JSON response is inspected to extract zbl_id; if found, getUrlForIdentifier(zbl_id) is returned, otherwise null is returned (leading to an empty search result).
- Uses Unirest to perform the JSON request to the citation-matching API and parses the response.
- performSearch now returns Collections.emptyList() when getURLForEntry returns null, and throws a FetcherException for malformed URIs.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ZbMATH.java: implement EntryBasedParserFetcher using citation matching.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/EntryBasedParserFetcher.java: handle null URL and URISyntaxException/MalformedURLException earlier; return empty list when appropriate.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/WebFetchers.java: register ZbMATH in entry-based fetchers.
- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/field/StandardField.java: add ZBL_NUMBER.
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ZbMATHTest.java: update to use StandardField.ZBL_NUMBER and add tests for entry-based searches.
- CHANGELOG.md: note about adding zbmath to public databases.

Tests
- Added/updated tests to verify searching by entry, searching when no match is found, and searching when the ZBL id is included in the entry.

Notes
- The citation matching endpoint returns JSON only; we use it to obtain the zbl_id and then fetch the BibTeX via the existing identifier-based path.
- Network errors and malformed URIs are handled with FetcherException; lack of matches yields an empty result list.

Summary

Fixes tooltip behavior in the CitationsDisplay component so citation tooltips appear reliably, are accessible, and display correct content when hovering or focusing citation items.

What was broken

- Tooltips in CitationsDisplay did not consistently appear or were positioned incorrectly.
- Tooltip activation sometimes failed due to incorrect element wrapping/refs and event propagation issues.
- Accessibility attributes (aria) were missing/incorrect in tooltip triggers.

What I changed

- Reworked how the Tooltip is attached to each citation item: the Tooltip now wraps the correct interactive element and forwards refs so hover/focus events are handled reliably.
- Ensured stable keys for mapped citation items to avoid remounting issues that interfered with tooltip behavior.
- Adjusted tooltip positioning and z-index styles to prevent it being clipped or rendered behind other UI elements.
- Added appropriate aria attributes and keyboard focus support so tooltips are accessible to screen reader and keyboard users.

- Added/updated unit tests to assert tooltip visibility and content on hover and focus for citation items.
- Manual verification steps included in the PR:
  1. Open the page or Storybook story with CitationsDisplay.
  2. Hover over and focus each citation item; confirm the tooltip appears with correct content and is positioned correctly.
  3. Confirm keyboard focus triggers the tooltip and that screen reader attributes are present.

Impact

- Non-breaking change: existing API of CitationsDisplay remains the same.
- Improves reliability and accessibility of citation tooltips across browsers.

Files changed (high-level)

- CitationsDisplay component (tooltip wrapping, keys)
- Tooltip usage/forwardRef adjustments
- Styles for tooltip positioning/z-index
- Tests for tooltip behavior

Notes

If you run into any layout-specific clipping in embedded contexts, the tooltip container prop can be adjusted to render to body (used in the tooltip implementation).

Summary

- Fixes a crash/exception when importing XMP / embedded BibTeX data from PDFs that contain multiple XMP schemas (related to #8278).
- Prevents a potential NullPointerException when extracting embedded files from PDFs.

What I changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/xmp/XmpUtilReader.java
  - Added a SLF4J Logger.
  - Improved defensive checks for the XMP description section calculation (minor parenthesis clarity change).
  - Wrapped parsing of individual XMP schema strings in a try/catch so that an IOException parsing one schema is logged and parsing continues for other schemas instead of aborting the whole operation.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fileformat/PdfEmbeddedBibFileImporter.java
  - Added a null check for efTree.getKids() before iterating, avoiding a potential NullPointerException when no kids are present.

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added an entry noting the fix for XMP and embedded BibTeX import failing when a file contains multiple XMP schemas (references #8278).

Why this matters

Previously a parsing error in one XMP schema could stop the entire import process, causing embedded BibTeX/XMP imports to fail if a PDF contained multiple schemas. Also, iterating over a null kids list could cause an NPE. With these changes, JabRef logs the problematic schema, continues processing remaining schemas, and safely handles PDFs without kids in the name tree.

Related issue

Summary

This PR changes the AUTHORS file checker in the CI to fail the job when new author entries are detected in a PR instead of posting a comment on the PR.

What I changed

- Renamed the step to "All authors of this PR listed in AUTHORS".
- Removed the comment-on-pr action and all related set-output usage and environment secrets.
- When new authors are detected the step now prints the added lines and exits with a non-zero status (exit 1), causing the workflow to fail.

Why

- The previous approach used a bot to post a comment on the PR. That does not work reliably when the PR author is not a JabRef developer (permission / token issues), so the check could silently do nothing.
- Failing the job is consistent with other checks (e.g., checkstyle) and makes the problem visible to contributors and maintainers.
- Maintainers will continue to update the AUTHORS file manually; this change just makes the check actionable.

Notes and impact

- The commenting action (unsplash/comment-on-pr) and the GH_TOKEN_COMMENT_ON_PR secret are no longer used by this workflow step.
- Contributors will see the failing check and the console log showing which author lines were detected and guidance about adjusting their git configuration or contacting maintainers.
- This is a follow-up to #6722 and intentionally leaves the authors update to maintainers.

Related

- Follow-up to #6722

Checklist (developer)

- I will maintain the AUTHORS file myself when needed; this change is to make the check referenceable and reliable.
- No functional code changes to JabRef; CI-only change.

text:
Add serialization and parsing support for ContentSelectors in MetaData

Summary:
- Implement serialization of content selectors into the JabRef metadata comment with keys prefixed by "selector_".
- Implement parsing of those selector_* metadata keys back into MetaData as ContentSelectors.
- Preserve unknown metadata entries and ensure semicolons are escaped when serializing; properly unquote values when parsing.
- Add MetaData API helpers for managing content selectors (getContentSelectorList, addContentSelector, clearContentSelectors, getContentSelectorValuesForField).
- Minor serializer improvement: handle newline insertion for save actions consistently.

Why:
- Content selectors (field-specific selector lists) need to be round-trippable when saving and loading .bib files. This change ensures that selectors are written to and read from the jabref-meta comment area, including correct escaping/unquoting so that characters like semicolons and LaTeX-escaped umlauts are preserved.

What changed (details):
- MetaDataSerializer: writes each ContentSelector using MetaData.SELECTOR_META_PREFIX + fieldName and includes unknown meta data serialization with escaped semicolons and newlines.
- MetaDataParser: recognizes keys starting with selector_ and reconstructs ContentSelector objects via ContentSelectors.parse(...), using StringUtil.unquote to restore escaped sequences.
- MetaData: stores ContentSelectors and exposes methods to access and modify them; contentSelectors is included in equals() comparison to ensure metadata equality reflects selectors.
- Tests: BibtexDatabaseWriterTest includes a roundtrip test (roundtripWithContentSelectorsAndUmlauts) to validate serialization/parsing and character escaping (e.g. umlauts).

Compatibility / Notes:
- Serialized selector entries use the existing jabref-meta comment format with the prefix "selector_"; older files without selector_* entries are unaffected.
- Unknown metadata entries are preserved when saving/loading.

This change fixes metadata round-trip for content selectors and improves robustness of metadata serialization/parsing.

  - BibDatabaseContext now uses Optional<Path> for the database path and provides getDatabasePath()/setDatabasePath(). The legacy getDatabaseFile() is kept deprecated. File directory resolution and normalization logic has been improved (getFileDirectories, getFileDirectoriesAsPaths, getFirstExistingFileDir).

- Save flow refactor and robustness
  - Introduced SaveDatabaseAction with explicit SaveDatabaseMode (NORMAL / SILENT) and improved save/saveAs/saveSelected behavior. SaveDatabaseAction handles encoding choice, shows encoding-problem dialog and optionally retries with a different encoding, properly starts/stops AutosaveManager and BackupManager when database paths change, updates file history and UI titles, and registers save actions for undo.
  - SaveAction now acts as a lightweight wrapper around SaveDatabaseAction and binds executability to the application state.
  - SaveAllAction uses SaveDatabaseAction to save all open libraries.
  - AutosaveUiManager listens for AutosaveEvent and performs silent saves.

- GUI improvements (JabRefFrame)
  - Improved drag & drop support for tabs with a drop indicator and handling of dropped bib files.
  - Keybindings initialization and global state binding for active database/search state.
  - Telemetry opt-in prompt shown after startup if not yet asked.
  - Centralized tab management, titles and tooltips handling, autosave/backup lifecycle integration when opening/closing tabs, and improved menu & toolbar construction.
  - Better handling for opening parser results into existing tabs or creating new ones.

- Shared database UI improvements
  - SharedDatabaseUIManager enhanced to open shared DBs from parser results and DBMS properties, and improved event handling for connection loss, update refusals and missing shared entries.

- CLI and argument processing
  - ArgumentProcessor enhancements for importing/opening files (including URL downloads to temp files), guessing import formats, export-matches and file export logic, preference reset/import/export, fetching entries from web fetchers, regenerating BibTeX keys, automatic file link setting, and aux import.

  - CleanupWorker and its cleanup presets updated and thoroughly tested. Behavior includes DOI cleanup, month normalization, page normalization, file link fixes, move/rename PDF logic, converting to BibLaTeX fields, HTML-to-Latex/units/protected-term formatters, and more.
  - MoveFilesCleanup and RenamePdfCleanup updated to handle various file name patterns, subdirectory patterns and case-only renames correctly.

- Tests
  - New and updated unit tests cover SaveDatabaseAction (save/saveAs behavior, working directory updates, keeping changed flags), CleanupWorker behaviors, MoveFilesCleanup, RenamePdfCleanup and IntegrityCheck. These tests exercise file operations and ensure correctness for multiple edge cases.

Overall this PR modernizes path handling, centralizes and hardens save/export behavior (including autosave), improves GUI usability and robustness, tightens CLI behavior, improves shared DB handling and adds a substantial set of tests to prevent regressions.

text:
Summary

Adds an XMP exporter to allow exporting BibTeX entries as XMP/Dublin Core metadata (*.xmp). This implements both single-file export and a split mode that writes one .xmp file per entry.

What I changed

- Added a new exporter: org.jabref.logic.exporter.XmpExporter
  - Exports entries to a .xmp file (UTF-8) using XmpUtilWriter.generateXmpString
  - If the target filename equals "split" the exporter writes each entry to a separate file named <id>_<citekey>.xmp
- Extended XmpUtilWriter
  - Added generateXmpString(List<BibEntry>, XmpPreferences) to produce XMP metadata as a string (Dublin Core schema)
  - Added a writeToDCSchema overload and refactored DC extraction to use DublinCoreExtractor
  - Handles serialization exceptions and returns an empty string on error
- Added new FileType PLAIN_XMP ("xmp")
- Integrated XmpPreferences through the stack
  - ExporterFactory.create(...) now accepts XmpPreferences and constructs XmpExporter(xmpPreferences)
  - ArgumentProcessor now passes Globals.prefs.getXMPPreferences() into ExporterFactory
- Tests
  - New tests: org.jabref.logic.exporter.XmpExporterTest (covers single export, multiple entries in one file and split mode)
  - Updated existing exporter tests (CsvExportFormatTest, ExporterTest, HtmlExportFormatTest) to mock XmpPreferences and pass it to ExporterFactory

Files changed (high level)
- Added: src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/exporter/XmpExporter.java
- Modified: src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/xmp/XmpUtilWriter.java (new helpers and generation method)
- Modified: src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/exporter/ExporterFactory.java (accept XmpPreferences and construct XmpExporter)
- Modified: src/main/java/org/jabref/cli/ArgumentProcessor.java (obtain XmpPreferences from Globals.prefs)
- Modified: src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/util/FileType.java (added PLAIN_XMP)
- Tests: added XmpExporterTest; updated CsvExportFormatTest, ExporterTest, HtmlExportFormatTest

Behavior notes / points for review

- Split mode uses the literal filename "split" as a signal to write individual files. This creates files named <id>_<citekey>.xmp; if cite key is null the filename contains "null" (tests expect this behavior).
- The generated XMP uses Dublin Core schema and includes an XML packet tag (<?xpacket begin="..."?>). I left it in for now — please review whether that tag should be removed from the output.
- generateXmpString returns an empty string on serialization/IO errors and logs warnings.

Compatibility / API note

- ExporterFactory.create signatures changed to accept XmpPreferences. Tests and callers in this PR were updated accordingly.

Related issue

- Implements functionality for: koppor#319

Checklist

- Tests added for the new exporter
- Existing exporter tests updated to provide mocked XmpPreferences

If you want, I can follow up with CLI commands (full CLI integration) or update the CHANGELOG/Help pages in a separate PR.

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added an entry summarizing the fixes and improvements.

Why this matters
- Numeric sorting is now intuitive and aligns with user expectations when numeric parts appear in fields.
- Capitalization formatter produces more natural and correct title casing, preserves acronyms and camel-cased words, and handles hyphenation and punctuation more robustly.

Compatibility
- These changes are backward compatible and should not require changes from users. The updated tests ensure the new behavior is covered.

This PR implements several UI improvements and bug fixes related to the entry editor and context menus.

What changed

- Right-click menu: expanded the "Copy..." submenu to include both "Copy DOI" and "Copy DOI URL" actions (and kept other copy/export options). This addresses the incorrect behavior where "Copy DOI URL" only copied the DOI string.

- Entry editor (EntryEditor.java):
  - Improved drag-and-drop support for file links. Dragged files can now be copied, moved or linked depending on the transfer mode and are handled via ExternalFilesEntryLinker.
  - Reworked tab creation and visibility handling: entry editor tabs are created in one place (createTabs) and recalculateVisibleTabs updates the visible set without causing jarring tab re-order animations.
  - Added support for additional special tabs (FileAnnotationTab, FulltextSearchResultsTab, RelatedArticlesTab, etc.) and ensured the source tab can be selected by default according to preferences.
  - Added key bindings handling inside the editor (navigation between panels/entries, help, close) and utility methods to set focus to a specific field and cycle preview styles.
  - The fetcher menu now lists available entry-based fetchers and properly handles the PdfMergeMetadataImporter (GROBID opt-in dialog) when selected.

- ChangeEntryTypeMenu: refactored menu population and unified creation of change-type menu items. The menu now builds contexts for BibTeX/BibLaTeX, IEEETran and custom types, and attaches tooltips to menu items where available.

- Small refactors and wiring updates: various constructors and usages were updated to use the appropriate managers/utilities (e.g. CountingUndoManager) and to improve readability (use of modern Java constructs in a few places).

Why this matters

These changes restore and improve file drag-and-drop behavior, fix the "Copy DOI URL" action, make the entry editor more robust and configurable, and present a cleaner, better-organized Change Entry Type menu. Overall these UX fixes and expansions make entry editing and context menu interactions more reliable and convenient for users.

Notes

- The fetcher action for PDF-based metadata import prompts the GROBID opt-in dialog if needed before running.
- Tab visibility updates try to avoid unnecessary UI animation by selectively removing/adding tabs rather than resetting the full tab list.

- Previously, when the source editor lost focus while another entry was selected, currentEntry could already point to the new selection. That caused the parsed changes from the editor to be applied to the wrong entry, producing duplicated or incorrect updates. Passing the out-of-focus entry explicitly ensures the edits are saved to the intended entry.

Notes
- Change is limited to src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/entryeditor/SourceTab.java.
- Manually tested; no new tests added in this PR.

Fix: Capitalize words after hyphens (fixes #9157)

What I changed
- CapitalizeFormatter now capitalizes letters that follow hyphen/dash characters by calling a new method Word.toUpperFirstIgnoreHyphen instead of the previous toUpperFirst.
- Added Word.toUpperFirstIgnoreHyphen: iterates over characters and treats a character as the start of a word if it is at index 0 or if the previous character is a dash (one of the DASHES). Protected characters (e.g., content in braces) are still left untouched.
- Added unit tests covering words separated by hyphens and combinations with protected brace content.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to note the bug fix.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/formatter/casechanger/CapitalizeFormatter.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/formatter/casechanger/Word.java
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/formatter/casechanger/CapitalizeFormatterTest.java
- CHANGELOG.md

Why
Previously, the Capitalize formatter did not capitalize letters that come after hyphen/dash characters (e.g., "upper-each-first" became "Upper-each-first"). This change ensures words following hyphens are capitalized as expected ("Upper-Each-First").

Notes
- Protected characters (such as parts wrapped in braces) continue to be respected.
- Tests added to cover various hyphen/dash scenarios and combinations with protected parts.
- Manually tested in running JabRef and updated the changelog; documentation reviewed.

Summary:
This PR significantly improves the performance and memory usage of the journal abbreviation loader/repository/parser (partial fix for #2966). Loading and parsing the journal repository went from ~10 seconds to nearly instantaneous (see attached benchmark screenshot).

What I changed:
- Replaced calls that lowered strings then used equals(...) with equalsIgnoreCase(...) to avoid unnecessary allocations.
- Replaced LinkedList usage with HashSet where ordering is not required, reducing lookup time and memory.
- Reduced the number of in-memory collections: instead of keeping 1 + 4 maps we now keep a single copy of the list, leading to roughly a 10x reduction in RAM consumption for the repository data.
- Updated two unit tests that relied on the previous sorted ordering (sorting is no longer guaranteed when using a HashSet).

Results / Impact:
- Parsing and loading the journal abbreviation files is now orders of magnitude faster (previously ~10s, now nearly instantaneous).
- Memory footprint for the repository data reduced significantly (about 1/10 of previous usage).
- There is a theoretical risk that journal autocompletion could be slower because of fewer pre-built maps, but I observed no noticeable negative impact in practice.

Notes:
- Two tests were adapted to reflect the change in ordering.
- This change is a partial fix for #2966 and should make startup and repository operations much snappier.

Checklist:
- Tests: two tests adjusted; no new tests added.
- Manual testing: performed (loading/parsing and basic autocompletion checks).

If you'd like, I can add a changelog entry and/or additional tests to cover performance regressions or ordering expectations.
