text:
Add MSBib (Microsoft Office 2007 bibliography) import/export support

This PR introduces conversion utilities and mappings between JabRef BibTeX/BibLaTeX entries and the MSBib XML format used by MS Office/Word. Main changes:

- New MSBibMapping: a bidirectional mapping between BibTeX/BibLaTeX field names and MSBib field names, plus entry-type mapping helpers (getMSBibEntryType, getBibLaTeXEntryType) and LCID helper (currently returns English / 0).
- New MSBibEntry: an in-memory representation of an MSBib source with XML (de)serialization helpers (populateFromXml and getEntryDom). Handles authors/editors lists, pages, standard numbers (ISBN/ISSN/LCCN/MRN), address splitting into city/state/country, thesis-type handling, patent number, journal name, date accessed parsing/output, and stripping non-XML characters when exporting.
- New MSBibConverter: converts JabRef BibEntry -> MSBibEntry, including LaTeX -> Unicode conversion for field values, mapping of fields via MSBibMapping, special handling for pages, booktitle->conferenceName, month/year fallbacks, number vs patentNumber logic, and populating authors/editors.
- Tests / fixtures: added multiple MSBib XML fixtures and a .bib/.xml pair (MsBibExportFormatTest2/3/6.xml, MsBibKeyTest.bib / MsBibKeyTest.xml) to cover export cases: keywords export, thesis types, standardNumber formatting, author serialization and empty author handling.

Notes for reviewers / TODOs:
- Language/LCID mapping currently only supports English (getLCID/getLanguage are stubs returning English/0).
- MSBibMapping stores some BibTeX-only fields with a BIBTEX_ prefix so unsupported fields are preserved.
- DateAccessed parsing assumes common numeric formats and exports MonthAccessed/DayAccessed/YearAccessed when possible.
- Address parsing uses a simplified regex (city, state, country) which may not cover all international formats.

This adds foundational MSBib support allowing reliable export/import of common fields and preserves BibTeX-specific data in BIBTEX_* fields.

Summary

Fix a bug where editing the BibTeX source in the Entry editor could cause incorrect parsing (e.g. when a field contains braces {}) because parsing was triggered on every text change. Also improve detection of leftover/unparsed BibTeX fragments and surface parsing problems to the user.

Problem

- The Source tab parsed the source on every change which prevented the user from temporarily leaving unbalanced braces (e.g. removing opening and closing '{' sequentially) while editing. This caused spurious parser errors.
- The BibtexParser could leave an unparsed epilog fragment without issuing any warning. Such silent failures made it hard to know when part of the input was ignored.
- The existing NotificationPane did not reliably show the parsing warnings/errors to the user.

What I changed

1) SourceTab
- Delay parsing/store of the source until the source text area loses focus (on focus-out) instead of on every text change. This lets the user edit temporary unbalanced braces without triggering the parser prematurely.
- Added a DialogService dependency and show an error dialog when validation messages (parser warnings/errors) are present. The NotificationPane code is left in place but the DialogService is used because the NotificationPane appeared not to work in the observed scenario.
- When the parser result contains warnings, an IllegalStateException is thrown so the UI path can show the error to the user.

2) EntryEditor
- Pass DialogService into the SourceTab constructor.

3) BibtexParser
- Make MetaDataParser final (small cleanup).
- After parsing, check the database epilog with a regex to find leftover fragments that look like a field assignment (pattern like "identifier = ...,"). If such a fragment exists and there were no warnings, add a warning to parserResult to indicate that part of the input was not parsed.

4) Tests
- Update SourceTabTest to construct SourceTab with an FXDialogService (to satisfy the new constructor parameter).

Why

- Triggering parsing only on focus out avoids false-positive parser errors while the user is in the middle of an edit (for example when removing braces). This improves user experience while editing raw BibTeX.
- The epilog check helps detect cases where the parser silently skipped a trailing BibTeX fragment and ensures the user is notified.
- Showing a dialog ensures the user gets immediate feedback about parsing/validation issues.

Notes and follow-ups

- I left the NotificationPane code in place; if desired we can replace/remove it after a review and choose one consistent UI channel for reporting parser errors.
- The epilog detection uses a simple regex heuristic; it is not a complete parser-level validation but is intended to catch common cases of leftover field assignments. If necessary this check can be refined.
- Manual tests were performed. Additional unit tests could be added to cover the epilog-detection behavior and the focus-out storing logic.

Related issue

- Fix for #4256 (parsing issue when field contains {})

Summary

This PR updates the preview preferences and the preview rendering pipeline so that preview-related settings can be configured through the preferences UI and are respected by the preview layout at runtime.

What I changed

- Preferences UI
  - Updated PreviewTab.fxml and PreviewTab.java to add/adjust controls that expose preview settings to the user and wire them to the view model.
  - Improved bindings and lifecycle handling between the preview tab view and PreviewTabViewModel.

- Preferences model
  - Extended PreviewPreferences to store the newly exposed preview settings and to provide defaults and accessors used by the UI and preview renderer.

- Preview rendering
  - Modified PreviewLayout to read and apply the preview preferences so that rendering behavior reflects user configuration.

- Documentation
  - Added an entry to CHANGELOG.md describing the new preview preference capabilities and behavior changes.

Why this change

Users need control over preview behavior and appearance. Centralizing these options in preferences and ensuring the preview renderer respects them improves configurability and provides a consistent user experience.

Notes

- The ViewModel ties the UI controls to the persisted PreviewPreferences, so changes made in the preferences tab are saved and applied immediately.
- The changelog entry summarizes the user-visible changes.

text:
Fix NullPointerException when a referenced entry in an Open/LibreOffice document is removed (fixes #4932).

What I changed
- OOBibBase: instead of creating an UndefinedBibtexEntry when a key cannot be found, the code now throws a BibEntryNotFoundException with the citation marker and a localized message. This prevents the subsequent NPE caused by handling an undefined/empty entry.
- OOBibStyle: added Objects.requireNonNull checks in getCitationMarkerField to fail fast when entry or database is null and avoid hidden NPEs later.
- CHANGELOG.md: added an entry describing the fix.

Why
When an entry referenced from an Open/LibreOffice document was removed from the library, code paths previously produced an NPE because an undefined placeholder got handled incorrectly. Throwing BibEntryNotFoundException surfaces the problem immediately and shows the offending reference marker to the user.

Notes
- This closes/fixes #4932.
- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance. No unit tests were added in this change.

text: This pull request addresses the issue where the `changed` property in `BibEntry` is set after updating the entry type, leading to incorrect behavior in property listeners. text:
This PR adds/updates the project build and third-party library documentation.

Key changes
- Comprehensive Gradle build configuration (build.gradle) including:
  - Plugins: application, shadow, install4j, ANTLR support, jmh, modernizer, checkstyle, jacoco, errorprone, java flavours, etc.
  - Platform flavours for native J2V8 libraries (linux_x86_64, macosx_x86_64, windows_x86_32, windows_x86_64) and appropriate dependencies.
  - Dependency declarations for all runtime and test libraries used by the project.
  - Source sets and generated sources handling (src/main/gen) and UTF-8 processing for resources.
  - ANTLR tasks to generate Java sources for BST (ANTLR3) and search grammar (ANTLR4).
  - Shadow JAR setup and per-flavour fat-jar tasks, plus release packaging tasks (releaseJar, media) using install4j.
  - Version snapshoting when building with the dev property (appends date, branch and commit info).
  - Test task configuration with categorized tests (database, fetcher, GUI), Jacoco merge/reporting and test reporting.
  - jmh benchmarking configuration and modernizer configuration (failOnViolations=false).
  - Checkstyle configuration and build tasks ordering.

- Added/updated external-libraries.txt documenting fonts, icons and all third-party libraries and their licenses. This file is maintained manually in sync with build.gradle and lib/ jars and includes guidance on SPDX license identifiers and how to produce a dependency report using Gradle.

Notes for developers
- To generate sources: ./gradlew generateSource
- To build a fat jar: ./gradlew releaseJar (produces JabRef-<version>.jar in build/releases)
- To create installers/releases: ./gradlew release (install4j required; set install4jDir if necessary)
- Environment variables used: AzureInstrumentationKey (for resources), CERTIFICATE_PW (for signing installer/jar in media task)
- The external-libraries.txt must end with an empty line for the final entry to appear in About.html; update this file whenever adding/removing dependencies or libraries.

This PR centralizes build logic and documents third-party components and licenses, improving reproducibility and clarity of release packaging.

text:
Keep unknown meta data instead of discarding it (#2704)

Summary
- Previously JabRef discarded metadata items it did not recognize. This change preserves unknown metadata during parsing and serialization so those items are not lost on save.

What changed
- MetaData: added storage for unknown metadata (Map<String, List<String>>) and accessor/mutator (getUnknownMetaData, putUnkownMetaDataItem).
- MetaDataParser: unknown metadata keys are no longer ignored; they are stored in the MetaData object by default.
- MetaDataSerializer: unknown metadata items are written back into the serialized metadata map. When serializing we try to preserve formatting where possible (escape ";" and add newlines as needed).
- Tests & resources: added a test resource (unknownMetaData.bib) and a round-trip test (roundtripWithUnknownMetaData) to ensure unknown metadata survives read+write.
- CHANGELOG.md: document the behavior change.

Notes / limitations
- The parser does not fully parse the internal formatting of unknown metadata items (we assumed full control of metadata format before). This implementation attempts to keep formatting as much as possible, with small adjustments (escaping semicolons and inserting newlines). If special formatting is required for a specific unknown metadata type we can adapt later.

Why
- Preserving unknown metadata avoids data loss when users or external tools add custom metadata entries, and it allows users to rename or move metadata keys (e.g. a renamed groupstree) without losing their content.

Related
- Issue: #2704

Checklist
- CHANGELOG update included
- Tests added
- Manual testing performed

text:
Summary

This PR reintroduces the ability to parse plain-text reference strings and import resulting entries into the current JabRef library by using a GROBID backend. It implements a new SearchBasedFetcher backed by a GrobidService and integrates a small UI for pasting plain references.

What I changed

- UI
  - Added a toolbar/menu item and icon for "New entry from plain text" and bound it to a keybinding (Ctrl+Shift+N).
  - Added a dialog (Plain References Parser) where users paste plain references (separated by double empty lines) and press "Add to current library" to parse and import.
  - Localization strings for the dialog and notifications.

- Core functionality
  - Added GrobidService: a small HTTP client wrapper to call a GROBID server's processCitation API.
  - Added GrobidCitationFetcher: a SearchBasedFetcher that splits the input into individual citations, calls the GrobidService for each, parses the returned BibTeX and returns BibEntry objects.
  - Integrated the new fetcher into WebFetchers.
  - The parsing runs in the background and on success entries are imported into the active database using ImportHandler.
  - Telemetry: events are tracked when parsing occurs.

- Tests
  - Added unit tests for GrobidCitationFetcher and GrobidService (integration-style tests that call the configured GROBID server URL used in this PR).

Files touched (high level)
- GUI: JabRefFrame, ExtractBibtexDialog.fxml/java, BibtexExtractorViewModel, IconTheme, StandardActions, KeyBinding, JabRef_en.properties
- Logic: GrobidService, GrobidCitationFetcher, WebFetchers
- Tests: GrobidCitationFetcherTest, GrobidServiceTest
- CHANGELOG.md updated

Behavior / Usage

- Open the new action (toolbar/menu or Ctrl+Shift+N), paste plain references (separate multiple references by double empty lines) and press "Add to current library".
- The text is sent to a GROBID server; returned BibTeX entries are parsed and imported into the currently open database. The parsing runs in the background and shows simple notifications about progress and the number of parsed entries.

Notes / Limitations

- A custom GROBID server URL is currently hard-coded (http://grobid.cm.in.tum.de:8070). This was done for the feature implementation; the server and its configuration can be adapted later. See the PR description/issue for details.
- Tests assume the availability/behavior of the external GROBID endpoint used here; they can fail if the server is not reachable.
- The feature was implemented to solve issue #4826 and was developed as part of a software engineering course; the authors are open to adjustments to match project standards or to make the server configurable.

Changelog

- Added entry to CHANGELOG.md noting reintroduction of extracting references from plain text using GROBID (#5614).

If you want, I can follow up with making the GROBID URL configurable in preferences and adding more robust error handling for server/network failures.

Summary

Fix a crash where JabRef would die silently on Linux systems that ran out of inotify instances (fs.inotify.max_user_watches). The application previously attempted to create file-system watchers and crashed without warning when the kernel limit was exceeded.

What I changed

- Add defensive checks and exception handling around creation of inotify/WatchService watchers.
- Detect inotify resource exhaustion and handle it gracefully: log the error, show a user-facing error dialog with guidance, and continue running instead of exiting silently.
- Provide a fallback behavior (disable automatic watching for the affected paths and fall back to a polling watcher where appropriate) so core functionality remains available.
- Add automated tests that simulate watcher creation failure to ensure the app does not exit and the error is properly reported.
- Add a short changelog entry/documentation note explaining how to reproduce the problem and recommended system tweak (increasing fs.inotify.max_user_watches) for power users.

Behavior before vs after

- Before: JabRef would fail to start or would terminate silently when the OS-level inotify watch limit was reached, providing no helpful feedback to the user.
- After: JabRef catches the failure, logs diagnostic information, shows a clear error dialog explaining the problem and possible remedies, continues running, and reduces watcher usage for affected paths.

How to reproduce (manual)

1. On Linux, reduce the inotify limit: sudo sysctl -w fs.inotify.max_user_watches=128
2. Start JabRef and open a library with many files or enable file watching for many directories.
3. Previously the app would die; with this change you should see an error dialog and the app remains responsive.

Notes for reviewers

- Review focused on file-watcher initialization and platform-specific code paths (Linux/inotify).
- Check the user-visible error message text and logging details for localization and privacy-sensitive content.
- Tests mock the watcher factory to force a failure scenario; no changes to production file I/O behavior outside of watcher initialization.

Risk

Low — this adds defensive handling around an existing failure mode and provides a safe fallback. Reviewers should confirm the fallback behavior is acceptable for users who rely on live file-watching.

text:
Summary
Fixes a bug where custom Protected Terms lists were not persisted across restarts (Fixes #8608). The problem was caused by returning unmodifiable ObservableList wrappers from ProtectedTermsPreferences: listeners attached to those wrappers are weak and could be garbage-collected, preventing changes from being observed and saved.

What I changed
- Return the original ObservableList instances from the getters in ProtectedTermsPreferences instead of wrapping them with FXCollections.unmodifiableObservableList. This ensures strong references for listeners so changes are reliably observed and stored.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to note the fix.

Why
Using unmodifiable observable wrappers caused the listeners to be weakly referenced and collected, so modifications to protected terms were not detected and therefore not saved. Returning the underlying ObservableList keeps listeners alive and fixes the issue (see https://stackoverflow.com/a/44343014 for background).

Files changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/protectedterms/ProtectedTermsPreferences.java: return underlying ObservableLists from getters
- CHANGELOG.md: add entry about the fix

- Fixes: #8608
- Manually tested the change in a running JabRef instance to verify that custom protected terms are persisted across restarts.

text:
Add JabRefPreferences implementation (PreferencesService)

Summary
- Introduces JabRefPreferences, a singleton implementation of PreferencesService that centralizes application preference management.
- Provides a comprehensive defaults map for application-wide settings and methods to read, write, import/export and reset preferences.

Key features
- Defaults and initialization: populates a large set of default preference values (UI, export/import, preview, OpenOffice, proxy, editor, cleanup, telemetry, etc.) and applies language-dependent defaults.
- Storage backend: wraps java.util.prefs.Preferences with convenience getters/setters for String, boolean, int, double and lists; supports putStringList/getStringList with escaping for semicolons.
- Type helpers: color parsing (RGB <-> Color), reading/writing Charset, FilePreferences, TimestampPreferences, ProxyPreferences, RemotePreferences, CleanupPreset, PreviewPreferences, KeyBindingRepository and many other preferences objects used across the app.
- Customization support: store/load/purge custom entry types, custom export formats, custom importers and bibtex key patterns, entry editor tab lists and custom tabs.
- Export/Import: exportPreferences/importPreferences to XML files and memory-stick-mode export on flush.
- Persistence utility APIs: clear, flush, purgeSeries, overwritePreferences (testing only), hasKey, getAsOptional and getObject for introspection.
- Telemetry and user id management: generates/stores user id, handles telemetry preference flags and asked-to-collect state.
- UI-related preferences: column widths/names, special field columns, preview cycle/style, main table sort types, side pane positions, font handling and more.

Notes and considerations
- Singleton semantics: class enforces a singleton (getInstance) and provides overwritePreferences for tests only (documented).
- Backing store exceptions are logged; export/import throw JabRefException with localized messages for callers to surface.
- Many settings are persisted as strings and deserialized later; code handles parsing and sensible defaults where necessary.

This change centralizes preference logic used across the application and provides typed accessors to avoid scattering Preference API usage throughout the codebase.

Remove SSL/TLS configuration from the application code and configuration files. SSL termination is intended to be handled by the load balancer/reverse proxy (or platform) so the app no longer manages certificates or TLS settings itself.

What changed
- Removed SSL-related configuration entries and initialization code.
- Deleted/updated environment variables and config keys used for certificate paths, keys, and TLS options.
- Removed certificate files, self-signed cert generation, and related scripts.
- Updated deployment manifests and docs to reflect that TLS termination is external.
- Adjusted tests and CI config that referenced in-app SSL behavior.

Why
- Centralize TLS termination at the platform/load balancer level for simpler management and better security.
- Reduce complexity in the application and eliminate certificate handling responsibilities from app deployments.

Impact & Migration
- Deployments must be fronted by a TLS-terminating proxy (ingress controller, load balancer, API gateway, etc.).
- Remove any now-unused environment variables or secrets from deployment configs and secret stores.
- Ensure health checks and internal communication use HTTP (or mutual TLS between services if required by infra) as appropriate.

Testing
- CI and unit/integration tests updated and passing.
- Verified in staging behind the platform TLS terminator; app operates correctly with external TLS termination.

Rollback
- The previous SSL configuration can be restored from the prior commit/branch if in-app TLS needs to be re-enabled.

Notes
- Update operational runbooks and onboarding docs to show where TLS is configured and how certificates are managed outside the app.

text:
Add DOAB (Directory of Open Access Books) fetcher and JSON array support

This PR introduces a new DOABFetcher to retrieve book metadata from https://directory.doabooks.org via their REST API and map the results to BibEntry objects. The fetcher handles authors vs. editors, keywords, DOI/URL/URI, publisher, language, subtitle, pages and year (with integer/string fallback), and merges metadata arrays into proper BibTeX fields.

To support DOAB's array-based JSON responses, JsonReader.toJsonArray(InputStream) was added alongside the existing toJsonObject method. The DOAB fetcher is registered in WebFetchers (search-based fetchers) so it is discoverable by the application.

A DOABFetcherTest unit test was added to validate parsing and mapping for several example queries. Error handling and parsing fallbacks (e.g. pages/year parsing and editor name preprocessing) are included to make the importer robust against variations in DOAB responses.

Summary

This PR finalizes the removal of the JGoodies library from JabRef. It follows up on @Siedlerchr's work in PR #4891 and removes the remaining JGoodies dependency and all related usages from the codebase.

What I changed

- Removed JGoodies from build configuration (dependency entries cleaned up)
- Deleted or replaced code that depended on JGoodies utilities/components
- Updated imports and refactored affected classes to use standard Java/Swing or internal helper code
- Cleaned up tests and resources referencing JGoodies

Why

Removing JGoodies reduces our external dependency surface, simplifies maintenance, and centralizes UI/layout/validation logic in-project (or delegates to standard platform APIs). This completes the work started in #4891.

Testing

- Project builds successfully after changes
- Unit tests updated where necessary and all relevant tests pass
- Basic manual UI checks performed on screens affected by refactors — please review UI layouts for regressions

Notes for reviewers

- Pay attention to UI/layout/validation behavior in the areas where JGoodies utilities were used; look for subtle spacing/alignment differences
- If you rely on JGoodies in any third-party integrations, update those integrations accordingly (no public API in JabRef should intentionally expose JGoodies types)

Acknowledgements

Thanks to @Siedlerchr for the initial work in #4891 that made this complete removal possible.

First attempt at autocompletion for crossref (Fixes koppor#257)

  - CHANGELOG updated with a note about the new autocompletion feature.

- This is an initial implementation; no tests were added in this PR.
- Manually tested in a running JabRef instance (as noted in the original issue checklist).

This pull request adds user-configurable XMP privacy filter support and associated tests, plus small UI/util updates and localization.

Summary of changes:
- Add XmpPrefsTab: a new preferences tab that allows users to enable an XMP privacy filter and manage a list of fields that should not be written to XMP metadata. The tab includes a table with add/delete controls and persists settings to JabRefPreferences.
- Add/modify localization: new/updated English strings for the XMP privacy settings (JabRef_en.properties), including the label "Do not write the following fields to XMP Metadata:" and section header for XMP export privacy settings.
- Improve cell factory (ValueTableCellFactory): enhanced generic table cell factory (supports graphics, tooltips, context menu creation and primary-click menu handling) used to render the delete icon and handle clicks in the preferences table.
- Add XmpExporterTest: unit tests for XMP export behaviour covering single-entry export, multiple entries in a single file, splitting exports into separate files, and the effect of the privacy filter (mocking XmpPreferences to ensure excluded fields are omitted).
- Changelog note: documents the fix where the list of XMP exclusion fields in preferences is now saved. (See CHANGELOG entry referencing issue #4072.)

Why this change:
- Users need a convenient way to prevent sensitive or unwanted fields from being written into PDF XMP metadata. The new prefs tab plus saved preferences enable this workflow.
- Tests ensure the XMP exporter produces the expected RDF blocks and respects the privacy filter, preventing regressions.

Notes for reviewers:
- The XMP prefs UI binds the table to a ListProperty of XMPPrivacyFilter objects and persists the list via JabRefPreferences.XMP_PRIVACY_FILTERS and the enable flag via USE_XMP_PRIVACY_FILTER.
- ValueTableCellFactory enhancements are used to render the delete icon column and handle mouse events/menu behavior consistently.
- The unit tests create temporary files and assert exact RDF snippets (joined by '\n') — be mindful of platform line endings when running locally.

Summary

This PR significantly improves the performance and memory usage of the journal abbreviation loader and repository (partial fix for #2966). Loading/parsing the built-in journal abbreviation lists used to take on the order of ~10 seconds; with these changes startup/loader time is reduced to almost nothing.

What changed

- AbbreviationParser
  - Replaced LinkedList with a HashSet for storing Abbreviation objects (initialized with a large capacity). Duplicates are naturally deduplicated by the set, avoiding an explicit contains() check.
  - Imports adjusted accordingly.

- JournalAbbreviationRepository
  - Replaced the previous approach of keeping multiple maps and a SortedSet with a single HashSet of Abbreviation objects (pre-sized for expected data size). This reduces memory consumption dramatically (one copy instead of four maps + set).
  - Lookups now use stream-based checks with equalsIgnoreCase comparisons (helper methods isMatched / isMatchedAbbreviated) instead of constructing lowercased keys. This avoids expensive String allocations and toLowerCase calls.
  - API/behavior changes: getAbbreviations() now returns an unmodifiable Set (order is no longer guaranteed), addEntries() accepts a Collection, and addEntry handles duplicates by checking the set and logging/removing the previous entry.
  - Convenience methods (getNextAbbreviation, getMedlineAbbreviation, getIsoAbbreviation) delegate via map-style Optional operations.

- FileUpdateMonitor
  - Consolidated duplicated getTempFile implementation into a single static synchronized helper that returns a Path and documents that it may return null if creation fails.
  - Minor ordering/formatting changes and cleaned up code duplication.

Tests

- Adjusted tests that relied on sorted ordering of abbreviations:
  - ManageJournalAbbreviationsViewModelTest expected file content updated to match the set-based ordering changes.
  - JournalAbbreviationRepositoryTest removed/updated assertions that depended on sorted order and behaviors that no longer apply.

Rationale and trade-offs

- Main performance wins come from avoiding repeated toLowerCase allocations and from using HashSet to avoid O(n) contains checks on a linked list.
- Memory usage is reduced by storing a single collection of Abbreviation objects rather than multiple maps keyed by lowercased strings.
- Lookup behavior is now a linear search over the HashSet using case-insensitive equality checks — in practice this has not shown any noticeable negative impact, while providing major improvements in load time and RAM usage.

Notes

- The change removes any deterministic ordering of the abbreviations collection. Any code/tests that depended on sorted order need to be adapted.
- getTempFile in FileUpdateMonitor now returns a java.nio.file.Path (and the Javadoc updated accordingly).

Performance

- Loading/parsing time reduced from ~10s to near-zero in local measurements.

Checklist

- No CHANGELOG change in this PR.
- Tests were adapted where they depended on previous ordering behavior.

Summary

This PR fixes an issue where the "Make paths of linked files relative (if possible)" cleanup action incorrectly modified web URLs, which caused broken links and other follow-up problems. Web/online links are now detected and left untouched during the relative-path cleanup.

What changed

- RelativePathsCleanup: skip converting links that are detected as online links; only attempt to relativize local file paths.
- LinkedFile: improved isOnlineLink check by trimming and lowercasing the input before checking for "http://", "https://" or "www." to make detection more robust.
- CHANGELOG.md: added an entry describing the fix and referencing the issue.

Files modified

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/cleanup/RelativePathsCleanup.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/LinkedFile.java
- CHANGELOG.md

Notes

- Fixes #5861
- Manually tested with both local file links and web URLs to ensure local paths are still relativized while web URLs remain unchanged.
- No changes to user-visible settings or UI behavior; only alters the cleanup logic to avoid touching online links.

Summary:
Fixes an issue where importing metadata from certain PDFs could fail due to exceptions thrown by the XMP parser. This change prevents a single problematic XMP schema from aborting the entire import.

What I changed:
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/xmp/XmpUtilShared.java
  - Broadened the catch from XmpParsingException to Exception to ensure any unexpected exception (e.g. IllegalArgumentException from a schema) is caught and rethrown as IOException instead of breaking the loop that processes XMP data. Added a comment acknowledging the pragmatic nature of the change.
  - Removed the now-unused import for XmpParsingException.
- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added an entry under "Fixed" noting that importing from XMP would fail for certain PDFs. (Fixes #9383)
- .github/workflows/check-links.yaml
  - Updated the workflow to ignore CHANGELOG.md on push events so that the link check workflow isn't triggered for changelog-only updates.

Why:
Some PDFs contain malformed or unexpected XMP schema data that caused the XMP parser to throw exceptions (including IllegalArgumentException). Because XMP parsing is performed repeatedly, allowing a single schema error to stop processing resulted in failed imports for otherwise valid files. Catching Exception here is a defensive, pragmatic workaround to ensure the import process continues; the exception is still propagated as an IOException so callers remain aware of parse failures for the failing stream.

Testing / verification:
- Manually tested importing PDFs that previously triggered the issue; import no longer fails due to parser exceptions.
- CHANGELOG entry added and workflow adjusted as a small CI convenience.

Notes:
- The catch of Exception is acknowledged in a code comment as not ideal stylistically but chosen to avoid breaking the entire import loop. If desired, this could be refined later to catch specific additional exception types once the root causes are better understood.

Fixes: #9383

text:
Add predatory journal detection to the Integrity Checker

Summary
- Integrates predatory-journal checking into JabRef's integrity checks so entries that match known predatory journal names are flagged.

What I changed
- New loader: PredatoryJournalLoader
  - Downloads/reads predatory journal data from multiple external sources (CSV and HTML sources such as stop-predatory-journals GitHub and BeallsList) and extracts entries.
  - Provides an option to update the built-in list at startup or on-demand.
- New repository: PredatoryJournalRepository
  - Stores predatory journal data in an H2 MVStore-backed map and exposes methods to add and search names.
  - Implements fuzzy matching (cosine similarity on character bigrams) to detect near-matches.
- New checker: PredatoryJournalChecker
  - Implements EntryChecker and inspects configured fields on an entry (journal/journaltitle, publisher, booktitle) and produces IntegrityMessage when a match is found.
- Integration points
  - Launcher.applyPreferences now loads the predatory journal repository (PredatoryJournalLoader.loadRepository(true)) and assigns it to Globals.predatoryJournalRepository.
  - IntegrityCheck now includes PredatoryJournalChecker in the list of entry checkers (for both BibTeX and biblatex modes using the appropriate fields).
  - IntegrityCheckAction uses Globals.predatoryJournalRepository through existing flows.
- Localization
  - Added a new message key: "match found in predatory journal list" to the English resource bundle.
- Built-in data
  - Added a resource file journals/predatoryJournalList.mv (initial store data) included in resources.
- Tests
  - Added PredatoryJournalCheckerTest with various positive/negative/case/format tests.
  - Updated/used IntegrityCheckTest to ensure behavior and to use PredatoryJournalLoader (loadRepository(false)) for tests.

Why
- To help users detect potentially predatory journals/publishers automatically as part of the Integrity Check workflow, improving data quality and raising awareness of suspicious publication venues.

Notes / Implementation details
- Matching is fuzzy: PredatoryJournalRepository uses cosine similarity over character bigrams with a default similarity threshold passed by the checker.
- PredatoryJournalLoader supports CSV and HTML scraping patterns and gracefully logs problems reaching sources.
- The repository is initialized from a built-in MVStore file (predatoryJournalList.mv) and optionally updated from remote sources on startup.

Testing
- Unit tests cover checker behavior for matching and non-matching names and ensure case-insensitive and slightly-differing-format matches are detected.
- Manual and logging paths added to safely handle unreachable external sources.

If you want to review
- Main new files: PredatoryJournalLoader, PredatoryJournalRepository, PredatoryJournalChecker
- Integration: Launcher.applyPreferences, IntegrityCheck constructor
- Tests: PredatoryJournalCheckerTest, IntegrityCheckTest updates

Summary

Fixes an issue where certain keybindings in the entry editor were not recognized when the application was installed in a non-English (localized) environment. Users saw that shortcuts either did nothing or were bound to the wrong actions after switching locale or on localized installations.

Root cause

Keybindings were being looked up using localized action/display names (strings from resource bundles). Because those strings change with locale, the lookup failed or returned incorrect matches outside the default language.

What I changed

- Reworked keybinding lookup to use stable, locale-independent action IDs/command identifiers instead of localized labels.
- Added a fallback that safely handles missing bindings to avoid losing shortcuts if a resource bundle entry is missing or renamed.
- Updated the entry editor keybinding registration so it registers and resolves bindings by ID at startup.
- Added unit/integration tests covering multiple locales to prevent regressions.

Files changed (high level)

- Keybinding registration/resolution in the entry editor module
- Tests for keybinding resolution across locales
- Small localized resource handling update to support the fallback behavior

Testing

- Verified that shortcuts work in English and multiple localized installations (example locales: de, fr, ja).
- Confirmed previously broken shortcuts now trigger the correct actions.
- Ran unit tests and integration tests; updated/added tests to cover the fix.

Backward compatibility and impact

- Existing user-configured keybindings are preserved; the change only affects how bindings are resolved internally.
- No user action required; the fix is transparent and safe to deploy.

This resolves the reported issue where entry editor shortcuts did not function correctly on localized installations.

Summary

This PR updates how file fields and linked files are handled and fixes related parsing in the search-based fetcher. It also adjusts tests and updates the CHANGELOG accordingly.

What I changed

- Modified LinkedFile model to improve parsing/serialization of file-field entries and to better represent stored file metadata.
- Updated SearchBasedParserFetcher to use the revised LinkedFile handling when constructing entries returned from remote search-based importers. This ensures file fields extracted from fetched results are parsed consistently and attached to entries correctly.
- Adjusted FileFieldParserTest to match the new parsing behavior and to cover edge cases that were previously incorrect or missing.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to document the change.

Why

The previous handling of file fields could produce inconsistent LinkedFile objects and caused incorrect behavior when entries were created from search-based fetchers. By centralizing and improving parsing/serialization logic in LinkedFile and updating the fetcher to use it, file attachments from imported entries are now reliable and follow a single representation.

Tests

- Updated and extended unit tests (FileFieldParserTest) to validate the new parsing behavior and to prevent regressions.

Notes

- No public API breaking changes are intended for callers that use high-level entry/linked-file APIs, but internal representations were improved; please review any custom code that manually parses file-field strings.
- See CHANGELOG.md for user-facing notes about the fix.

- What: Ensure that all renaming operations performed as part of file-entry cleanup are executed on the JavaFX Application Thread (using Platform.runLater or equivalent), instead of running on background threads.

- How: Wrap the renaming logic in a Platform.runLater (or an existing FX scheduling utility) so the actual file-entry rename runs on the JavaFX thread. Refactor helper methods so callers no longer need to manage thread switching themselves.
- Tests: Updated/added tests to verify cleanup behavior and to ensure no threading violations occur. Manual verification performed for typical cleanup scenarios.
- Backwards compatibility: No public API changes. Behavior changes only in that renames are now guaranteed to execute on the FX thread.

This change improves stability of cleanup and prevents subtle threading bugs when file-entry renames interact with JavaFX-bound state.

text:
Fix menu/button graphics and improve EntryEditor UI and behavior

This PR contains several related fixes and enhancements:

- ActionFactory
  - Workaround for ActionUtils not setting graphics correctly: unbind graphic properties and explicitly set graphics from Action.getIcon() for MenuItem, Menu and Button controls.
  - Added getAssociatedNode(MenuItem) which uses reflection to access the internal ContextMenuContent.MenuItemContainer#getLabel() to find the label node associated with a MenuItem. This is used to show tooltips on menu items.
  - configureMenuItem now subscribes to SimpleCommand.statusMessageProperty() and shows/hides a Tooltip on the menu item label accordingly.
  - Provides helper factory methods to create menu items, check menu items, menus, submenus and icon buttons while ensuring "icon-button" styling and correct graphics.
  - Note: getAssociatedNode relies on private JavaFX internals via reflection (impl_styleableGetNode and MenuItemContainer#getLabel) and is therefore somewhat fragile across JavaFX versions.

- EntryEditor (FXML + Java)
  - Added a vertical toolbar to the entry editor (EntryEditor.fxml) with icon buttons (close, change type, generate BibTeX key, update from web, delete entry, previous/next entry). Each button uses JabRefIconView and has a tooltip.
  - Wired toolbar controls in EntryEditor.java (typeChangeButton, fetcherButton, typeLabel) and implemented setupToolBar() to:
    - Update the type label and show a ChangeEntryType context menu when clicking the label or the type-change button.
    - Populate a fetcher menu from WebFetchers and show it when clicking the fetcher button.
  - Implemented drag-and-drop behavior that respects the user's FileDragDropPreferenceType and the TransferMode (COPY, MOVE, LINK) to copy/add/move files to the entry using ExternalFilesEntryLinker.
  - Added key bindings specific to the entry editor (panel/tab navigation, entry navigation, help and close actions) using preferences-provided key bindings.
  - Tab handling: created list of EntryEditorTab instances, a recalculateVisibleTabs() method to efficiently update visible tabs without causing ugly animations, and a subscription to entry.typeProperty() to update the displayed type and visible tabs.
  - Implemented generateCiteKeyButton(), fetchAndMerge(), close(), deleteEntry(), and navigation actions wired to the UI.

Other notes:
- The reflection-based approach to access menu label nodes is a pragmatic solution to attach tooltips to menu items but may break on future JavaFX updates. A TODO to find a more robust solution (or reuse JabRefIconView) is present in the code.

text:
Add Snap packaging for JabRef

This PR introduces snap/snapcraft.yaml to package JabRef as a strict-confinement snap (base: core18). Key points:

- Defines snap metadata (name, icon, license, summary, description, adopt-info).
- Confinement: strict, grade: stable, architecture: build-on: amd64.
- Exposes common plugs: home, unity7, opengl, network-bind, removable-media (note: users must connect removable-media to access external drives).
- Adds system-files plugs to write native messaging host files for Firefox/Chrome/Edge/Chromium so the bundled native messaging manifests are placed on the host.
- Apps:
  - jabref: main app, runs bin/JabRef, uses gnome-3-34 extension.
  - browser-proxy: helper that runs lib/jabrefHost.py and is used as the native messaging host.
- Environment variables set:
  - _JAVA_OPTIONS to use $SNAP_USER_DATA for user.home
  - GTK_USE_PORTAL=1 to prefer portal dialogs
- Parts:
  - jabref: fetches the portable Linux archive from builds.jabref.org, stages x11-utils, and runs override-build steps to:
    - set the snap version from lib/app/.jpackage.xml
    - rewrite bundled native messaging JSON manifests to point to /snap/bin/jabref.browser-proxy
    - fix python shebang in lib/jabrefHost.py to /usr/bin/python3
    - remove the original bin/JabRef (replaced by a local launcher)
  - jabref-launcher: a local part that provides the JabRef-launcher at bin/JabRef (organize: JabRef-launcher -> bin/JabRef)

This configuration prepares the snap for building JabRef with a proper launcher and native messaging integration for browsers, fixes the python shebang, and derives the snap version from the upstream packaging metadata.

Summary

This PR fixes several PostgreSQL import/export issues (see #473) by reverting or correcting over-eager try-with-resources usage and other small bugs that caused connections/statements/resultsets to be closed prematurely or SQL queries to be malformed. The changes should restore the ability to import/export to an external SQL database.

Key changes

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added entry: "Fixed #473: Import/export to external database works again".

- DbConnectAction.java
  - Fixed a typo in a comment and use a try-with-resources around a test Connection so it closes immediately after verification.

- SQLUtil.java
  - queryAllFromTable now returns a ResultSet without closing the Statement (removed try-with-resources). This avoids closing the underlying Statement before the caller has used the ResultSet.
  - Removed a redundant stmnt.close() in executeQuery (clean up; the code path already handles closing).

- PostgreSQLExporter.java
  - Do not create the test Connection in a try-with-resources block (it must remain open for use after createPLPGSQLFunction). Return an open Connection instead of closing it immediately.

- PostgreSQLImporter.java
  - readColumnNames now returns a ResultSet without closing the Statement so callers can iterate safely.

- DbImportAction.java
  - Reworked try-with-resources to open Connection and obtain ResultSet in the same try(...) header so the ResultSet can be consumed safely while the Statement/Connection are still open.
  - Reorganized dialog-handling logic (minor refactor and formatting). Fixed building of the error message shown to the user.

- DBExporter.java
  - Fixed SQL-building issues in populateEntryTypesTable: moved StringBuilder into the loop to avoid reusing it incorrectly and ensured the UPDATE query ends with a semicolon.

Why these changes

Recent attempts to "fix" resource leaks with try-with-resources inadvertently closed Statements/Connections while callers still needed their ResultSets, primarily affecting PostgreSQL import/export flows. This PR restores the needed lifetime for Connections/Statements/ResultSets and fixes related SQL string issues so imports/exports should work again.

Notes

- The author noted this "may" solve issue #473 — please review and test against your PostgreSQL setups.
- Callers that receive ResultSet now have to ensure proper closing of the enclosing Statement/Connection (as done in updated callers here). Review other usages if necessary.

text:
Implement biblatex-style inheritance of fields from cross-referenced entries and add comprehensive tests

Summary
- Implement logic to resolve fields from a cross-referenced entry according to the biblatex inheritance rules.
- Add a large suite of unit tests (CrossrefTest) to cover forbidden fields, special mappings (author/bookauthor, maintitle/booktitle/journaltitle mappings), cases where title-like fields must not be inherited, and general same-name inheritance fallback.
- Update CHANGELOG to list this fix under Unreleased.

Details
- Added getSourceField(...) in BibEntry to encapsulate the inheritance mapping logic and forbid inheritance of specific internal fields (IDS, XREF, ENTRYSET, RELATED, SORTKEY).
- Implement special-case mappings for combinations of parent/child entry types (e.g. MvBook -> InBook/BookInBook/SuppBook, Book/Collection/Proceedings/Reference variations, and IEEETran Periodical -> Article/SuppPeriodical) so that fields like MAINTITLE/BOOKTITLE/JOURNALTITLE map to TITLE/SUBTITLE/TITLEADDON appropriately.
- Fall back to same-name inheritance for the remaining fields when allowed.
- getResolvedFieldOrAlias(...) follows crossref links (via BibDatabase.getReferencedEntry) and uses getSourceField(...) to decide which source field to read from the referred entry.

Tests
- CrossrefTest covers:
  - forbiddenFields: ensure internal/forbidden fields are not inherited
  - authorInheritance: author and bookauthor inheritance for book/mvbook scenarios
  - mainTitleInheritance / bookTitleInheritance / journalTitleInheritance: verify mapped title fields are inherited as specified
  - noTitleInheritance: verify title/subtitle/titleaddon/shorttitle are not inherited where disallowed
  - sameNameInheritance: verify same-name inheritance for many fields for proceedings -> inproceedings scenario

Why
This change fixes issue #5045 by making field resolution for cross-referenced entries conform to the biblatex specification. The added tests ensure behavior is well-specified and prevent regressions.

Files changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/BibEntry.java: add/getSourceField and update getResolvedFieldOrAlias behavior
- src/test/java/org/jabref/model/entry/CrossrefTest.java: new comprehensive test coverage
- CHANGELOG.md: document the fix under Unreleased

Backwards compatibility
Behavior only affects resolution of fields via crossref; existing stored fields are unchanged. The change tightens which fields are inherited and adds special mappings to match biblatex rules.

WIP: DB sync performance improvements and FX-thread test helpers

Summary
- Introduces several performance and thread-safety improvements in DB synchronization (DBMSSynchronizer/DBMSProcessor) by offloading expensive operations to background tasks and synchronizing critical sections.
- Adds a testing-friendly FX-thread helper to TaskExecutor and implements it in CurrentThreadTaskExecutor and DefaultTaskExecutor so tests can simulate JavaFX behavior.
- Makes targeted UI changes to ensure listeners and dialog calls run on the JavaFX thread (Platform.runLater / TaskExecutor.runInFXThread) to avoid blocking and race conditions.
- Small cleanup/fixes (equals formatting in StudyDatabaseItem, UiThreadList latch handling, export of modifiable entries list in BibDatabase).

What changed (high level)
- DBMSSynchronizer
  - Added TaskExecutor field and constructor param, use BackgroundTask + TaskExecutor for heavy operations (metadata sync, partitioned fetching of shared entries).
  - Made synchronizeLocalDatabase and checkCurrentConnection synchronized to avoid concurrent transaction/state issues.
  - lastEntryChanged marked volatile.
  - Changed logic to perform expensive DB fetches on background threads and then insert into local DB on success.

- DBMSProcessor
  - updateEntry() is now synchronized to prevent transaction errors from concurrent access.

- TaskExecutor / DefaultTaskExecutor / CurrentThreadTaskExecutor
  - TaskExecutor interface gained runInFXThread(Runnable) to abstract executing code on the FX thread (or the current thread for tests).
  - DefaultTaskExecutor delegates runInFXThread to existing runInJavaFXThread helper.
  - CurrentThreadTaskExecutor implements runInFXThread by running the runnable on the current thread (useful for unit tests that do not run a JavaFX runtime).

- UI classes
  - GroupNodeViewModel: defer registering the entries list listener to Platform.runLater to ensure correct lifecycle and prevent weak listener GC issues.
  - MainTableDataModel: avoid wrapping the database entries list with additional UI wrappers in the hot path; only wrap the SortedList where needed.
  - SharedDatabaseUIManager: use TaskExecutor.runInFXThread (via DefaultTaskExecutor) for dialog interactions so callers remain safe and tests can control FX behavior; also pass Globals.TASK_EXECUTOR into DBMSSynchronizer.
  - UiThreadList: improved latch handling and exception safety in the Platform.runLater callback.

- BibDatabase
  - Added getEntriesModifieable() to expose the modifiable observable list where necessary (used internally by sync code/tests).

- Tests
  - Updated DBMSSynchronizerTest and SynchronizationTestSimulator to use CurrentThreadTaskExecutor so tests can run without JavaFX thread.

Motivation
- Reduce blocking of JavaFX thread and avoid long-running DB or network operations being executed directly on the FX thread.
- Improve stability and correctness by preventing concurrent transactions/connection checks from interfering with each other.
- Make unit tests deterministic by allowing FX-thread bound code to be run synchronously in tests via CurrentThreadTaskExecutor.

Notes / TODOs
- This is a WIP / follow up to #8494. More synchronization or restructuring might be required for other update paths; some TODOs are left in code (e.g. consider batching updates / further backgrounding).
- The change to expose a modifiable entries list is internal and should be reviewed for API safety.
- I was not able to push to the original branch, so this PR follows up the previous work.

Tests
- Existing synchronization tests updated to use CurrentThreadTaskExecutor and continue to pass (intended to ensure behavior without a JavaFX thread).

text:
Refactor FieldFactory for safer initialization and cleaner API

Summary
- Clean up and simplify the FieldFactory implementation. The change centralizes field registration and initialization, removes mutable public state, and adds defensive checks to avoid NPEs and duplicate registrations.

What changed
- Consolidated field creation logic into a single, well-documented initialization path.
- Replaced exposure of mutable collections with unmodifiable views to prevent accidental external modification of the registered fields.
- Added defensive null/duplicate checks when registering fields to ensure consistent state.
- Made initialization thread-safe and idempotent so repeated calls are safe.
- Removed redundant code paths and clarified intent with inline comments.

Why this change
- The previous implementation allowed mutation of field registry from outside and had fragile initialization semantics. This refactor reduces the risk of incorrect runtime state, makes the class easier to reason about, and prevents subtle bugs caused by duplicate or null registrations.

Backward compatibility and risk
- No behavioral changes to existing field definitions are intended. The change should be low risk, limited to internal factory wiring.

Testing
- Existing unit/integration tests were run to ensure no regressions in behavior. Manual verification of common code paths that obtain Field objects was done.

Notes
- This is an internal refactor of FieldFactory; callers should not be affected. If any code relied on modifying the field registry externally (which was unsafe), that code will need to be updated to use a supported extension mechanism.

Merged the two separate "New library" commands (BibTeX and BibLaTeX) into a single "New library" command that creates a new library using the default library mode from preferences.

  - Renamed the label and localization key from "Default bibliography mode" to "Default library mode" (GeneralTab.fxml and JabRef_en.properties).

Fix TagBar#setTags bug — ensure programmatic updates are applied

Summary
- Fixes a bug in TagBar.setTags where the method ignored the supplied collection and instead tried to re-set the existing tags, preventing the UI from updating when tags were set programmatically.

Problem
- TagBar.setTags(Collection<T> newTags) previously called this.tags.setAll(tags) (the internal field) instead of using the provided newTags parameter. As a result, calling setTags(...) had no effect or behaved unexpectedly.

Changes
- Update TagBar.setTags to use the provided newTags collection (this.tags.setAll(newTags)).

Impact
- Programmatic updates to TagBar (used across various field editors, e.g. linked entries, tag editors) now correctly update the underlying list and the UI.

Testing
- Manually call setTags(...) on a TagBar instance with a collection of values and verify the tag list and displayed tags update accordingly.
- Verify that adding/removing tags via the UI still works as before.

Files changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/util/component/TagBar.java (fix setTags implementation)

Notes
- No API changes. This is a behavioral bugfix affecting UI state synchronization.

Summary

Fixes an issue where changes to the Custom preview layout in Preferences were not saved (Fixes #6447). The root cause was that the code used localized names (l10n) as identifiers for preview layouts. The custom/text-based preview returned a localized name which caused lookups and persistence to fail across different locales.

What I changed

- Introduced a stable internal identifier for the text-based preview layout: TextBasedPreviewLayout.NAME = "PREVIEW". The getName() method now returns this internal name and getDisplayName() returns the localized label shown in the UI.
- Added getDisplayName() to the PreviewLayout interface and implemented it for the relevant layout classes (TextBasedPreviewLayout, BstPreviewLayout, CitationStylePreviewLayout). For citation styles, getDisplayName() returns the style title while getName() still returns an appropriate identifier.
- Updated the logic that finds and persists preview layouts to rely on the internal name for identification but to use display names for UI presentation and sorting. This prevents localization from breaking lookups used when storing/restoring preferences.
- Updated UI code (preferences preview tab, preview notifications, preview viewer) to display the localized display name instead of the internal name.
- Small refactors and fixes in PreviewTabViewModel (use of current layout variable, sorting by display name, selection lookup using TextBasedPreviewLayout.NAME) and PreviewTabView (search and list cell display).
- Updated the changelog entry to mention this fix.

Files touched (high level)

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/layout/TextBasedPreviewLayout.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/preview/PreviewLayout.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/PreviewTabView.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preferences/PreviewTabViewModel.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preview/PreviewPanel.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/preview/PreviewViewer.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/bst/BstPreviewLayout.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/citationstyle/CitationStylePreviewLayout.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/preferences/JabRefPreferences.java
- CHANGELOG.md

Why this fixes the bug

Previously the custom preview layout used a localized name as its identifier. When saving and restoring preferences the code attempted to match layouts by name; because the name varied by locale the lookup failed and changes appeared not to be saved. By separating a stable internal name (used for identification/storage) from a localized display name (used in the UI) the lookup/persistence is robust to localization while still showing translated labels to users.

Fix handling of unknown LaTeX commands and empty arguments in HTML and Unicode formatters (fixes #1321)

Summary
- Make the LaTeX→Unicode and LaTeX→HTML layout formatters behave more sensibly for unknown commands and commands with empty/braced arguments.
- Add unit tests to lock the new behaviour and update the CHANGELOG.

What changed
- Behaviour
  - Unknown commands now keep their argument when present: "\\aaaa{bbbb}" → "bbbb".
  - Unknown commands without arguments keep the command text: "\\aaaa" → "aaaa".

  - Combining-accent handling remains supported for single-character arguments.

- Code
  - src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/logic/layout/format/HTMLChars.java: improved handling of command bodies and empty arguments; clearer variable names; use String instead of Object for map lookups and remove unnecessary casts.
  - src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/logic/layout/format/LatexToUnicodeFormatter.java: analogous fixes for Unicode formatter, including better handling when no accent mapping exists and small refactors (String types instead of Object).

- Tests
  - src/test/java/net/sf/jabref/logic/layout/format/HTMLCharsTest.java: new tests for unknown commands, unknown commands with arguments, and unknown commands with empty arguments; common setup extracted.
  - src/test/java/net/sf/jabref/logic/layout/format/LatexToUnicodeFormatterTest.java: same new tests added for the Unicode formatter.

- Documentation
  - CHANGELOG.md: add entry referencing #1321.

Why this matters
- Fixes display problems where LaTeX commands disappeared from the preview/list view for unknown commands or when commands were used with empty braces (common pattern like "\\LaTeX{}").
- Adds tests to prevent regressions and improves code clarity in the formatting classes.

text:
Fix various copy-to-clipboard issues

Summary
- Fixes several clipboard-related bugs (including #5263). The changes ensure the correct data formats (plain text, HTML, RTF, XML) are placed on the system clipboard and avoid using non-text exporters for clipboard export.

What I changed
1) Preview copy (right-click copy in preview)
- Use only the textual content of the preview when copying, instead of taking the whole HTML node content. This prevents HTML markup from being included in plain-text copies and resolves #5263.
- PreviewViewer now reads the preview text via document.getElementById("content").getTextContent() and puts HTML separately into ClipboardContent.

2) Citation style preview clipboard handling
- CitationStyleToClipboardWorker.processPreview now returns a ClipboardContent containing both HTML and plain text (so WYSIWYG and plain-text editors receive appropriate representations).
- Other preview formats (RTF, XSL-FO, HTML) now also populate the plain-text entry in ClipboardContent, improving interoperability with simple text editors.
- Tests updated to read the string from the returned ClipboardContent.

3) Export to clipboard dialog
- Filter exporters to only include text-based exporters (txt, rtf, rdf, xml, html, htm, csv, ris) so binary formats (e.g. PDF) are not offered for clipboard export.
- ExportToClipboardAction now returns an ExportResult carrying both exported content and the exporter FileType. The clipboard population chooses the best ClipboardContent field (HTML, RTF, XML) based on extension and always stores a plain-string fallback.
- Background task failure is handled so exceptions are logged but do not crash the UI. Temporary export files are still cleaned up.

Other
- CHANGELOG.md updated to mention these fixes.
- Adjusted unit tests for CitationStyleToClipboardWorker to work with the new ClipboardContent return type.

Why
- Previously, copying from the preview could include unwanted HTML or miss plain-text representations; some exporters that produce non-text output were incorrectly available for clipboard export; and clipboard content sometimes lacked plain-string fallback for simple editors. These changes make clipboard copy behaviour predictable and compatible across editors.

Notes
- Tests were adjusted to reflect the API changes. The changes were manually tested.

Problem
During application shutdown, attempts to stop or unregister event sources that were never registered could throw exceptions or prevent JabRef from completing shutdown cleanly.

What this PR does
- Adds defensive checks to ensure unregistered or null event sources are ignored during shutdown.
- Catches and logs exceptions raised while stopping event sources so one bad source cannot block the whole shutdown process.
- Ensures executor services and related shutdown steps always run even if some event sources are missing or fail to stop.
- Adds tests covering shutdown with unregistered event sources to prevent regressions.

Why this matters
This makes application shutdown more robust: JabRef will no longer be stopped or hung by missing or faulty event sources. Behavior for properly registered sources is unchanged; failures are logged for diagnosis.

text:
Add OS X integration helpers and toolbar compatibility

This PR introduces platform-specific support for macOS and a small UI compatibility helper:

- Add osx/macadapter/MacAdapter.java
  - Registers macOS application event handlers (using com.apple.eawt): OpenFilesHandler, AboutHandler, PreferencesHandler, QuitHandler and AppReOpenedListener.
  - Forwards events to the JabRefFrame: open files, about, preferences (placeholder), quit (delegates to JabRefFrame.quit() and respects the user response), and re-open app window.
  - Designed to be registered with the running JabRefFrame via registerMacEvents(JabRefFrame).

- Add src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/OSXCompatibleToolbar.java
  - Subclass of JToolBar that sets the client property JButton.buttonType to "toolbar" for JButtons on OS X to get the native (toolbar-style) appearance.

- Bundle lib/AppleJavaExtensions.jar
  - Contains Apple EAWT classes required on macOS (com.apple.eawt) so the MacAdapter can compile/run where needed.

- JabRefFrame.java
  - Contains existing callbacks (openAction, about, quit) referenced by the MacAdapter. No functional changes to logic in this PR, but these methods provide the integration points used by the MacAdapter.

Notes
- The MacAdapter is macOS-specific; it checks that the JabRefFrame is non-null before acting. Non-macOS platforms are unaffected.
- To enable handlers at runtime on macOS, call new MacAdapter().registerMacEvents(frame) during application startup when running on OS X.
- Preferences handling is left as a placeholder for future wiring.

This change improves the native macOS experience by handling Finder file-open events, About/Preferences/Quit, and provides toolbar styling consistent with macOS conventions.

text:
Fix and harden AutoSave behavior

Summary
- Improve AutoSaveManager to make autosave scheduling and shutdown more robust.
- Update CHANGELOG.md to document the fix and behaviour improvements.

What changed
- Refactor scheduling logic in AutoSaveManager to ensure the autosave task is properly managed and cancelled on shutdown/close.
- Use a dedicated scheduled executor (single thread) with a daemon thread factory so autosave threads do not prevent JVM exit.
- Add guards and exception handling around save operations to avoid uncaught exceptions and NPEs during autosave.
- Ensure scheduled tasks are cancelled and the executor is shut down when autosave is disabled or the manager is disposed.
- Improve logging around autosave start/stop and error situations.

Why
- Prevents autosave tasks from leaking threads and blocking application shutdown.
- Makes autosave more resilient to runtime errors and configuration changes.
- Documents the change in the changelog for users.

Testing
- Manually verified that autosave starts/stops correctly, exceptions are logged but do not crash the app, and the application can exit cleanly with autosave enabled.

Notes
- No behavioral change to user-facing autosave intervals; this is an internal hardening and reliability improvement.

Add CI integration and packaging updates to build and publish JabRef as a Snap package.

What changed

- .github/workflows/snap.yml
  - New/updated GitHub Actions workflow to build and publish the Snap. The workflow builds the project, creates the snap artifact, and publishes it to the Snap Store (or a channel) using repository secrets. It supports manual dispatch and tag-based triggers for releases.

- build.gradle
  - Adjusted the Gradle build configuration to produce the artifacts required by snapcraft (snap-build tasks / packaging hooks). This includes configuring the Java runtime and any necessary packaging steps/dependencies so the Snap build works in CI and locally.

- snap/snapcraft.yaml
  - Updated Snapcraft manifest to reflect current runtime and packaging needs: application entry points, required plugs/slots, confinement, stage-packages, desktop integration (desktop file, icons), environment variables, and any specific Java runtime integration.

Why

- Provide an automated, reproducible way to build and publish JabRef as a Snap, making installation and updates easier for users on Ubuntu and other snap-enabled Linux distributions.
- Keep the packaging manifest and CI in sync with the Gradle build to avoid breakage between local builds and CI publish.

Notes for reviewers / maintainers

- CI credentials: The workflow expects secure repository secrets (e.g. SNAPCRAFT_TOKEN or SNAP_STORE_CREDENTIALS) to authenticate with the Snap Store. Ensure those secrets are added before enabling automated publish.
- Triggers: The workflow can be triggered manually and is wired to run on tag pushes (for releases). Review the trigger configuration if you want different behavior (e.g. push to main or scheduled builds).
- Local testing: To build and test locally:
  1) Ensure snapcraft is installed on your machine.
  2) Run the Gradle tasks as configured (e.g. ./gradlew assemble or the snap build task).
  3) From the snap directory run snapcraft to create the .snap file.
  4) Install locally with sudo snap install --dangerous <path-to-snap> and verify the application starts.

Potential follow-ups

- Add automated tests for the Snap on supported channels or using a dedicated test matrix.
- Add documentation to CONTRIBUTING.md or release notes describing how to add Snap credentials and how the publish flow works.

Compatibility

- These changes are additive and focus on packaging and CI. They do not alter runtime code paths beyond what is necessary to enable packaging and to declare runtime dependencies in the snap manifest.

Fix EndNote XML importer to accept URLs that are not wrapped in a <style> tag (fixes #6199)

What I changed
- Endnote XML schema: marked <url> as mixed="true" so text nodes inside <url> are preserved by JAXB (src/main/resources/xjc/endnote/endnote.xsd).
- Importer logic: updated EndnoteXmlImporter.getUrlValue(...) to inspect Url.getContent() and handle both cases:
  - when the content contains a Style element, use Style.getContent() (previous behavior),
  - when the content contains raw text (String), use that as the URL value.
  The value is still cleaned as before.
- Tests: added fixtures covering url elements without a style wrapper:
  - EndnoteXmlImporterTest_WithoutUrlStyle.xml / .bib
  - EndnoteXmlImporterTest_WithoutUrlStyle2.xml / .bib

Motivation
- Some EndNote/Bookends exports put the URL directly as text inside <url> rather than inside a <style> element. The importer previously assumed a <style> child always existed and therefore missed those URLs. This change makes the importer robust to both patterns.

Compatibility
- Backwards compatible: behavior for style-wrapped URLs remains unchanged. This only broadens supported input formats.

Summary

Make the BibTeX parser tolerant of input where entries are not separated by a newline. Previously the parser could fail or merge entries when a closing brace (}) for one entry was immediately followed by the @ of the next entry on the same line.

Problem

- Some BibTeX files have entries concatenated without a trailing newline between them (e.g. "...}
@article{...}" vs "...}@article{...}").
- The parser assumed a newline boundary between entries and could mis-parse or error on such inputs.

Changes

- Update the BibTeX parsing logic to accept an entry boundary when a closing brace is followed immediately by the start of the next entry (an '@') or by EOF, not just when a newline is present.
- Improve tokenization/state transitions so that entries are recognized correctly even when there is no separating newline or when only whitespace is present.
- Add unit tests covering:
  - Two entries concatenated on the same line (no newline between them).
  - Entries separated by spaces/tabs but no newline.
  - Mixed correct and malformed spacing to ensure robustness.

Testing

- New unit tests added to validate parsing of adjacent entries without newlines.
- Existing tests run to ensure no regressions in normal parsing behavior.

Notes

- This change is backwards compatible and only relaxes the boundary conditions; it should not affect properly formatted BibTeX files.

Problem
- The Source tab did not react to changes made to an entry (edits, renames, moves, deletes), forcing users to manually refresh the view to see updates.

3. Rename or move the entry -> verify the Source tab reflects the new name/path.
4. Delete the entry -> verify the Source tab clears or shows the empty/placeholder state.

Notes
- No DB migrations required.
- Debounce keeps performance impact minimal while ensuring UX consistency.

- The UI toggle was not writing the updated value into the preferences store (missing/mismatched preference key and save call). The in-memory state updated, but the change was never committed to persistent storage.

- Ensure the backup option is saved to the correct preference key when the user applies or confirms preference changes.
- Fix bindings between the UI control and the preferences model so toggles update the model reliably.

3. Re-open Preferences: the toggle should reflect the saved state.
4. Restart the application and verify the backup option persists.

Notes

- No migration steps required; the change is backward compatible. If the preference was previously unset, the app will continue to use the existing default until the user sets the option.
- Tests added to prevent regression.

Additionally, unit tests have been added to `BibDatabaseContextTest.java` to cover various scenarios, including cases where the database file path is empty, relative, or absolute. These tests help verify that the changes work as expected and prevent future regressions.

This PR is a follow-up to #2744 and fixes #2739.

Summary
Remove the GitHub Actions workflow "Check outdated depencencies" that automatically created issues for outdated dependencies.

Motivation
We already use Dependabot to detect and open PRs for outdated dependencies. The workflow duplicates that functionality and creates noisy issues (see example: https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/5856). We prefer Dependabot PRs over separate issues.

What this PR does
- Deletes the repository workflow that checked for outdated dependencies and created issues (the "Check outdated depencencies" workflow).

How to verify
- After merging, the workflow should no longer appear in the Actions tab.
- No new "dependencies" issues should be created by the removed workflow.
- Dependabot should continue to open PRs for dependency updates.

Relevant links
- Example noisy issue: https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/5856
- Query of open dependency issues: https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3Adependencies

Notes
This change removes duplicated automation; dependency updates will continue to be handled by Dependabot PRs. If needed in the future, we can reintroduce a workflow with different behavior (e.g., opening PRs instead of issues).

text:
Summary

This PR adds the infrastructure to publish a JabRef development/nightly Chocolatey package (jabref-nightly) and the corresponding GitHub Actions workflow to create it.

What changed

- Added a new GitHub Actions workflow: .github/workflows/update-chocolatey-jabref-nightly.yml
  - Triggers: pushes to branch chocoDev and a daily schedule (cron)
  - Job createnightly: checks for SSH secret and copies current master builds to the nightly folder on the build server
  - Job createchoco: runs on windows-latest, computes SHA256 for the MSI, runs GitVersion and injects version/checksum into the chocolatey install script
- Added Chocolatey package files for the dev/nightly package under buildres/chocolatey/jabref-dev:
  - jabref-dev.nuspec (package metadata template; version placeholder = AssemblySemFileVer)
  - tools/chocolateyinstall.ps1 (installer script; URL points to nightly builds and contains CHECKSUM placeholder)
- Added ADR documenting the decision to offer jabref-nightly as a Chocolatey package: docs/adr/0009-offer-jabref-nightly-as-chocolatey-package.md
- Updated GitVersion.yml to provide defaults for WeightedPreReleaseNumber and to set assembly file version format
- Small workflow/name change for Snap -> Snap Nightly (.github/workflows/snap.yml)
- .gitignore updated to ignore *.nupkg files

Notes and remaining tasks (from issue #5031)

- Verify uninstallation behavior when both stable and dev packages are present — ensure the Chocolatey package specifies a unique softwareName / matching uninstall pattern
- Wire the nuspec version: the nuspec currently contains a placeholder (AssemblySemFileVer). The workflow must replace or generate the final package version at packaging time
- Add the correct packageSourceUrl to the nuspec
- Confirm the checksum output wiring in the workflow: the checksum step currently prints a set-output with name secretspresent, but the later sed expects steps.checksum.outputs.checksum (variable name mismatch)
- Ensure secrets are configured (buildJabRefPrivateKey) for SSH access and that the workflow has permission to copy artifacts from the builds server
- Finalize and test the package creation, upload and Chocolatey publishing process

Fixes

- Fixes #5031

Testing / verification

- Run the workflow on the chocoDev branch (or manually) with secrets configured and verify that the generated installer script contains the correct checksum and version
- Build a .nupkg locally from the buildres/chocolatey/jabref-dev directory to validate metadata, installer behavior and that the package installs/uninstalls as expected

If you want, I can follow up with a small patch to fix the checksum output variable name and to replace the nuspec version automatically in the workflow.

Fix NPE when launching JabRef with a .bib file passed as a command-line argument

- This is a follow-up to #3325. Passing a .bib file as a command-line argument could cause a NullPointerException because getParent() was called on a path that could be relative or otherwise yield no parent. Converting to an absolute path ensures getParent() behaves as expected.

Notes
- Fixes #3342
- Manually tested the scenario in a running JabRef
- No changelog or automated tests were added in this change; adding a unit test to cover this case would be a recommended follow-up.
