Summary:
Enable Lucene query parsing as an optional/feature-flagged query parser for the search subsystem.

What this change does:
- Adds a new Lucene query parser module and integrates it into the search API.
- Introduces feature flag/config option (enable_lucene_parser) to toggle Lucene parsing on/off at runtime.
- Implements query string parsing that supports Lucene syntax (fielded queries, boolean operators, grouping, ranges, wildcards, phrase search, proximity, fuzzy).
- Adds validation and safe-fallback: invalid or unsupported Lucene queries fall back to the existing simple parser to preserve backward compatibility.
- Extends API to accept a parser_type parameter ("simple" | "lucene") and honors the feature flag.
- Adds unit and integration tests covering parsing, edge cases, and fallback behavior.
- Updates docs with usage examples, configuration option, and notes about differences from the simple parser.

Why:
- Lucene syntax gives power users a richer, more expressive query language for complex searches.
- Keeping it feature-flagged ensures gradual rollout and safe opt-in while preserving current behavior for existing users.

Migration / Configuration:
- Default behavior remains unchanged unless enable_lucene_parser is set to true or parser_type is specified as "lucene".
- To enable: set enable_lucene_parser=true in the search configuration or call the API with parser_type=lucene.

Examples:
- Simple fielded query: title:apollo AND author:smith
- Phrase search: "quick brown fox"
- Range query: date:[2020-01-01 TO 2020-12-31]

Testing & QA notes:
- Verify normal searches remain unchanged when the feature flag is off.
- Test representative Lucene queries for correctness and expected results when enabled.
- Confirm that malformed Lucene queries are handled gracefully and that the fallback parser returns sensible results.

Notes / Known limitations:
- Not all Lucene analyzers/tokenizers are reproduced; this implements the parsing layer only. Analyzer behavior may differ from a full Lucene engine in edge cases.
- Performance tested on typical workloads; complex queries may be more expensive — monitor query latency after enabling.

Files changed (high level):
- search/parser/lucene_parser.* (new)
- search/parser/index.* (integration points)
- config/search.yml (new flag)
- api/search_controller.* (parser_type support)
- tests/parser/* (new tests)
- docs/search_queries.md (updated)

Summary of changes

- Prevent spurious field updates from editor bindings (src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/AbstractEditorViewModel.java):
  - When binding the editor text to the entry field, normalize the stored entry value's newlines to ControlsFX format (replace OS.NEWLINE with "\n") before comparing with the new value.
  - Compare trimmed values to avoid registering changes triggered by autosave/save reloads; this prevents frequent cursor jumps and unnecessary undo edits.
  - Keep a reference to the field binding so it is not discarded (already present in code).
  - When a real change is detected, set the field on the entry and add an UndoableFieldChange to the application UndoManager.

- Avoid applying NormalizeNewlinesFormatter during cleanup (src/main/java/org/jabref/model/cleanup/FieldFormatterCleanup.java):
  - If the configured formatter is an instance of NormalizeNewlinesFormatter, skip running it and keep the original value (newValue = oldValue) so the cleanup does not introduce newline-only changes.
  - Preserve existing behavior for other formatters, including removal of fields when the formatter returns an empty string and generating FieldChange objects for modifications.

Rationale

These changes reduce noise from newline normalization and autosave-induced reloads by preventing unnecessary field writes and undo events. They also avoid the cleanup job from performing redundant newline normalization, which could otherwise produce needless changes.

Introduce DragExpansionHandler to control tree-item expansion during drag-and-drop in GroupTreeView

What changed
- Added a new inner class DragExpansionHandler in GroupTreeView.java to manage timed expansion/collapse of TreeItem nodes when hovered during a drag operation.
- Replaced the direct immediate expansion call (row.getTreeItem().setExpanded(true)) with dragExpansionHandler.expandGroup(row.getTreeItem()).
- Added a dragExpansionHandler field and initialized it in initialize().
- The handler uses a 1000 ms threshold (DRAG_TIME_BEFORE_EXPANDING_MS) to avoid immediate node expansion and to toggle expansion state only after sustained hover.

Why
- Previously, nodes expanded immediately when dragging over them which led to a noisy and unintuitive UX. The new handler delays expansion to prevent accidental expansions and provides a more controlled toggle behavior after a brief hover.

Behavior details
- On first hover of a tree item during a drag, the handler records the hovered item and timestamp but leaves its expansion state unchanged.
- If the hover persists beyond 1 second, the item’s expansion state is toggled and the timer is reset, preventing rapid repeated toggles.

Notes
- Change is localized to GroupTreeView and does not affect other components.
- No API changes; behavior is purely UX-focused.

Fixes #4736 — Relativize .aux file paths with respect to a per-user LaTeX file directory

Summary
- Add support for a per-user LaTeX file directory in MetaData so aux file paths can be stored and resolved relative to that directory.
- When a TexGroup is created or shown, the aux file path is relativized (or expanded) using the LaTeX file directory. The stored/serialized path is now relative when possible.
- Add UI to set the LaTeX file directory in the Library Properties dialog. When browsing for an aux file in Group Dialog the selected path is shown as a relative path if applicable.
- Update metadata parsing/serialization so the LaTeX directories are read/written using the new key (fileDirectoryLatex-<user>). Existing group import/export is adjusted accordingly.
- Add/adjust tests to cover parsing, serialization and relative path behavior for TexGroup.

What changed (high level)
- Model
  - MetaData: store per-user LaTeX file directories (get/set/clear methods + equality/serialization support).
  - TexGroup: now holds MetaData and user, expands absolute/relative paths using file directories on construction, and returns relativized path via getFilePath().
- Logic
  - FileHelper: added relativize helper to turn absolute paths into paths relative to a matching file directory.
  - MetaDataParser/MetaDataSerializer: parse and write the new LaTeX file directory metadata (key: fileDirectoryLatex-<user>).
  - GroupsParser: pass MetaData through when parsing TexGroup so groups can be constructed with the LaTeX directory context.
- UI
  - LibraryPropertiesDialog: added a field and browse button to configure the LaTeX file directory and persist it to metadata.
  - LibraryPropertiesDialogViewModel: added properties and change detection for the LaTeX file directory.
  - GroupDialog: browse button now stores the selected aux file path as a relative path when possible.
- Tests
  - Updated/added tests for metadata serialization (fileDirectoryLatex), groups parsing and TexGroup behavior (including a test ensuring getFilePath() returns a relative path).

Notes
- The new metadata key used for serialization/parsing is fileDirectoryLatex-<user>. Parsing is implemented so existing metadata without that key remains unaffected.
- Default user value for TexGroup when not supplied uses a combination of system user name and host name (to maintain uniqueness across users/machines where needed).

Files touched (non-exhaustive): MetaData, TexGroup, FileHelper, MetaDataParser, MetaDataSerializer, GroupsParser, GroupDialog, LibraryPropertiesDialog(.fxml/.View/.ViewModel), and related tests.

  - When no group is selected in the side pane, show all entries by using the AllEntriesGroup (via DefaultGroupsFactory.getAllEntriesGroup()). This replaces the previous behavior of doing nothing when selection was empty.

  - Add a 400 ms debounce for the group search field in GroupTreeController using reactfx FxTimer to avoid publishing every keystroke to the (potentially expensive) search/filter task. This reduces work for large group structures and improves responsiveness.

  - BindingsHelper.mapBacked now returns MappedList<B, A> (type parameters updated) to reflect the mapped list element order.

  - Removed some unused imports and applied minor formatting cleanups.

- Fix correctness when no groups are selected (show all entries).
- Avoid selecting the special AllEntriesGroup as a user-chosen group.
- Improve performance and UX for searching/filtering groups in large group trees.
- Fix bugs in recursive tree creation and filtering logic that caused incorrect show/hide and update behavior.

text:
Remove FXDialogService default constructor and stop creating standalone instances

Summary
- Remove the no-argument (deprecated) and single-argument constructors from FXDialogService. Keep the constructor that requires both a Window and a Pane.
- Ensure the application reuses the FXDialogService instance created by JabRefFrame instead of creating new instances with potentially null state (which caused NPEs, see #4840).

What changed
- JabRefGUI: create a single JabRefFrame early, call init() on it and use mainFrame.getDialogService() everywhere instead of constructing new FXDialogService() or holding a separate DialogService field. Also pass the frame's dialog service into VersionWorker and other callers.
- JabRefFrame: construct its FXDialogService(mainStage, this) in the constructor and expose init() (made public) so JabRefGUI can initialize the frame explicitly.
- FXDialogService: removed the default and single-arg constructors and the @Deprecated constructor javadoc; retained the (Window, Pane) constructor.
- DefaultInjector: no longer creates a new FXDialogService(); it returns JabRefGUI.getMainFrame().getDialogService().
- EntryAddChangeViewModel / EntryDeleteChangeViewModel / ExternalFileTypeEntryEditor: replaced new FXDialogService() usages with JabRefGUI.getMainFrame().getDialogService().
- SourceTabTest: adjusted to use a mocked DialogService (mock(DialogService.class)) instead of instantiating FXDialogService directly.

Why
- Creating FXDialogService via a default constructor produced instances with null mainWindow or improper state and resulted in NullPointerExceptions. The app already creates a single, fully-initialized FXDialogService in JabRefFrame; this change ensures that instance is reused across the application.

Notes
- This addresses issue #4840.
- Some changes affect dependency provisioning (DefaultInjector relies on JabRefGUI.getMainFrame()). JabRefGUI must be initialized before those dependencies are requested.
- Adjusted tests to mock DialogService where appropriate.

Manual testing
- Manually tested the changed features in a running JabRef instance.

Follow-ups
- Consider adding more unit tests to cover dialog-service-dependent behavior and update the CHANGELOG entry.

These changes improve user feedback for source-editing: validation errors are shown more prominently via a dialog, and source edits are persisted on focus loss rather than on every keystroke to reduce unnecessary updates. text:
Add support for a custom DOI base URI via a new "Customization" preferences tab and ensure DOI links opened from the identifier editor respect that setting.

What this PR does
- Adds a new Preferences tab (Customization) with a checkbox and text field to enable/enter a custom DOI base URI.
- Persists the setting using the existing PreferencesService API (DOIPreferences) and new preference keys (USE_CUSTOM_DOI_URI, BASE_DOI_URI) with sensible defaults in JabRefPreferences.
- Makes the identifier editor use the custom DOI base when opening DOI links: IdentifierEditorViewModel.openExternalLink now checks DOIPreferences and calls getExternalURIWithCustomBase(...) on DOIs.
- UI wiring: CustomizationTab.fxml + CustomizationTab and CustomizationTabViewModel implement the UI and view-model bindings. The tab is registered in PreferencesDialogViewModel so it appears in Preferences.
- Minor editor improvements: the custom DOI text field is disabled when the checkbox is not selected; tooltips added to identifier buttons.

Files changed (high-level)
- GUI: CustomizationTab.fxml, CustomizationTab.java, CustomizationTabViewModel.java, PreferencesDialogViewModel.java, GeneralTab.java (binding additions), IdentifierEditor.java, IdentifierEditorViewModel.java
- Model/Preferences: DOIPreferences.java, JabRefPreferences.java, PreferencesService.java
- Identifier handling: DOI.java (provides getExternalURIWithCustomBase used by view model)
- Tests: IdentifierEditorViewModelTest.java (sanity test for identifier validation on empty text)
- Changelog: CHANGELOG.md entry under Unreleased describing the addition.

Why
- Some institutions or users prefer resolving DOIs via an alternative/custom resolver (for example, to route through an institutional proxy). This change makes it possible to configure a custom DOI base URI globally and uses it when opening DOI links from the UI.

How to test
1. Open Preferences → Customization and enable "Use custom DOI base URI for article access"; enter a custom base (e.g. https://my-resolver.example/doi).
2. In an entry DOI field, click the link/open action in the identifier editor. The browser should be opened with the DOI URL constructed from the configured base (e.g. https://my-resolver.example/doi/10.xxxx/yyy).
3. Toggle the preference off and verify the default resolver (https://doi.org/) is used instead.
4. Run unit tests (IdentifierEditorViewModelTest included) to ensure basic view-model behavior remains correct.

Notes
- Defaults remain backward compatible: custom DOI usage is disabled by default and base defaults to https://doi.org.
- Preference changes are applied via the normal preferences save flow; a restart warning is shown if needed by other preference tabs (no restart required for this setting to take effect).

text:
Use JavaFX Application as main entry point and centralize startup initialization

This change refactors the application entry point to extend javafx.application.Application and consolidates the startup logic into a single initialization routine. Key behaviors implemented/ensured by this update:

- Main entry now launches JavaFX Application (JabRefMain extends Application) and calls the existing Swing-based GUI initialization on the Swing EDT.
- Prevent JavaFX from implicitly exiting on platform threads via Platform.setImplicitExit(false) to allow mixed JavaFX/Swing lifecycle handling.
- Register and configure proxy settings early (including setting a ProxyAuthenticator when proxy authentication is enabled).
- Initialize global components and preferences: Globals.prefs, background tasks, language settings, journal abbreviation loader, import/export formats, custom entry types, layout/save preferences, and protected terms loader. ProtectTermsFormatter is wired to the protected terms loader.
- Run preference migrations to upgrade older preference formats to current expectations.
- Update InternalBibtexFields (special fields, timestamp field and numeric fields) from preferences.
- Single-instance / remote-server behavior: start a remote listener when configured; if another JabRef instance is already running, forward the command-line arguments to that instance and exit cleanly (shutdown thread pools and call Platform.exit()).
- Override OS newline sequence from stored preferences.
- Use ArgumentProcessor to parse command-line arguments and shut down early when requested.
- Ensure the main Swing GUI (JabRefGUI) is created on the Swing event dispatch thread.

Overall, this PR modernizes the launch mechanism by using JavaFX Application lifecycle while preserving the Swing GUI initialization and improving startup sequencing (proxy, migrations, globals, single-instance handling and clean shutdown when delegating commands to an already running instance).

Add ExportToClipboard support for LibraryTab and unit tests; wire up context menu

This PR implements the following changes and improvements:

- ExportToClipboardAction
  - Added an overloaded constructor that accepts a LibraryTab so the action can be created in contexts where no JabRefFrame is available (e.g. right-click context menus on the main table).
  - Preserves existing behavior when instantiated with a JabRefFrame by falling back to the current library tab when needed.
  - Uses PreferencesService, ClipBoardManager and TaskExecutor injected in the constructor to make the action testable and decoupled from global singletons.
  - Exports selected entries using a chosen Exporter to a temporary file, reads its contents, and places the result on the clipboard (with appropriate HTML/RTF/plain text clipboard types).

- RightClickMenu
  - Updated the copy submenu to create ExportToClipboardAction using the new LibraryTab-aware constructor so the menu action works from the table context.

- Tests
  - Added/updated unit tests for ExportToClipboardAction (ExportToClipboardActionTest), CopyMoreAction (CopyMoreActionTest) and NewEntryAction (NewEntryActionTest).
  - Tests cover cases such as: no selection, partial/complete success for copy operations, exporter selection dialog, and the expected notifications and clipboard writes.
  - Tests use mocks/spies and a CurrentThreadTaskExecutor to run background tasks synchronously for deterministic assertions.

Other notes
- Temporary files created during export are cleaned up in a finally block.
- PreferencesService is used to read/write import/export preferences (including last used export format and file-directory context) to make exports resolve file links correctly.

This change improves modularity and testability of clipboard export functionality and plugs the feature into the right-click menu for table entries.

text:
Fix handling of URLs in file fields (fixes #7359)

Problem
- URLs stored in the BibTeX `file` field could not be handled reliably on Windows. Colons and certain path formats caused Path API failures (InvalidPathException) or misinterpretation of URLs as local paths, producing exceptions or incorrect LinkedFile objects.

Solution
- Revamped FileFieldParser parsing and conversion logic so file entries are first collected as strings and then converted in a safer way:
  - convert(...) is now package-private and documented; it normalizes the entry to at least 3 fields and then decides how to create a LinkedFile.
  - If the link looks like an online link (LinkedFile.isOnlineLink), we try to construct a URL and fall back to storing the raw string if URL construction fails.
  - For non-online links, if the path string contains "//" we assume it is meant to be kept as a string (avoids Linux/Windows ambiguity). Otherwise we try Path.of(...) and fall back to storing the raw string on InvalidPathException.
- LinkedFile gained an additional constructor taking (String description, String link, String fileType) to represent non-valid paths/links as text (used by the parser when Path/URL conversion is not possible). Existing constructors delegate accordingly.
- Parsing code has been improved to avoid erroneously adding intermediate state and to better handle escaped characters and separators.

Tests and cleanup
- Added comprehensive parameterized tests in FileFieldParserTest to cover online and file link parsing, malformed URLs, escaped characters, and other edge cases.
- Adjusted FileFieldWriterTest formatting (minor cleanup) and removed duplicated/irrelevant deprecated tests.

Changelog
- CHANGELOG.md updated to note the fix: "We fixed an issue where URLs in `file` fields could not be handled on Windows. [#7359]"

Notes
- The convert(List<String>) method has a side effect of clearing/modifying the provided list during conversion; tests wrap inputs with a mutable list when calling it directly.
- Behavior is backward compatible: valid Paths are still created as Path-backed LinkedFile objects; invalid paths or malformed URLs are preserved as string-backed LinkedFile entries so the GUI can still render them without throwing exceptions.

Fixes #3505 — prevent NPE in search bar when stylesheet resource is not found

What I changed
- Root cause: using "../" in resource paths to reach parent packages can fail for resources, causing the CSS file for the search bar not to be found and triggering a NullPointerException.
- Fix: load the stylesheet using a reliable resource lookup (avoid relying on "../" path traversal) and add a defensive null-check so missing resources no longer cause an NPE. The search bar will fall back gracefully if the CSS is unavailable.

Why
- In some runtime/package configurations the relative "../" resource path does not resolve. This change ensures the CSS is located correctly (or missing is handled) and prevents the app from crashing or the search UI from disappearing.

Testing / manual verification
- Start the app (IDE and packaged JAR) and confirm the search bar appears.
- Verify there is no NPE in the logs on startup or when opening the search bar.
- Confirm UI looks acceptable even if stylesheet is unavailable.

Notes / TODO
- CHANGELOG and tests have not been updated in this PR.
- If desired, we can add unit/integration tests to assert resource loading behavior across classloader contexts.

WIP: Fix LatexFieldFormatter line-wrapping

Summary
- Adjusts the LatexFieldFormatter to explicitly exclude the "review" and "abstract" fields from automatic line wrapping.
- Aims to prevent unwanted wrapping/formatting for fields that often contain multi-line LaTeX content or free-form paragraphs.

What changed
- LatexFieldFormatter now checks field names and skips wrapping for "review" and "abstract".
- This is intended to preserve original line breaks and LaTeX constructs that were being broken by the formatter.

Why
- Current behavior produced incorrect line breaks in certain fields, causing formatting regressions reported in related issues.
- Excluding these fields addresses a common source of those regressions without broadly disabling wrapping.

Related issues
- Fixes/addresses: #114, #186, #185

Notes / Next steps
- This is a WIP; more fields or edge cases may need to be excluded or handled differently depending on further reports.
- Please run the test suite and check LaTeX-heavy entries (abstracts, reviews) to confirm this resolves the reported problems. Feedback welcome before finalizing.

text:
Add zbMATH fetcher and entry-based search support

Summary
- Integrates a new zbMATH fetcher into the list of public web databases (so it can be used when updating an entry from the web). Fixes #7437.
- Implements entry-based searching for zbMATH by using the zbMATH Citation Matching API to find a zbl_id and then fetching the bibtex record for that identifier.

What changed
- Added ZbMATH fetcher (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ZbMATH.java):
  - Implements SearchBasedParserFetcher, IdBasedParserFetcher and EntryBasedParserFetcher.
  - Entry-based search: builds a citation-matching request from available entry fields (title, journal, year, pagination, volume, issue, authors) and queries the citation matching JSON API. If a zbl_id is returned, the fetcher resolves it to a bibtex URL and parses the entry.
  - Preserves existing id-based / query-based functionality.
- Registered ZbMATH in the available entry-based fetchers (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/WebFetchers.java).
- Added a new standard field ZBL_NUMBER to StandardField (src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/field/StandardField.java) to hold zbMATH identifiers.
- Improved EntryBasedParserFetcher.performSearch default handling (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/EntryBasedParserFetcher.java):

Add small utility that generates a LaTeX table of all characters known to the converter and fix several incorrect character mappings.

What this PR does:
- Adds a program that prints a LaTeX table with: the character number, the character as Unicode (\symbol{nnn}), the resulting LaTeX symbol as it appears, and the LaTeX code used.

- Fixes a number of incorrect symbol mappings in the converter so the generated LaTeX entries make sense.

- Using \usepackage[utf8]{inputenc} only helped with accented characters; printing raw Unicode in the .tex file was inconsistent across environments.
- The set of packages and fonts used for rendering affects which symbols appear correctly; a better font and additional packages may improve coverage.
- This work is related to issue #1761 but does not include that change.

Testing and documentation:
- Manually tested changed features in a running JabRef.
- Created an issue to update the help page at help.jabref.org for any outdated documentation references.

- Introduced AbbreviationChecker to detect abbreviated journal/book names using JournalAbbreviationRepository.

Notes

- The changes centralize usage of the journal abbreviation data for validation and make auto-completion more powerful by incorporating content selector values from metadata.
- Error handling and logging were added where content selector wrapping could fail due to incompatible suggestion provider types.

Add PreferencesDialog UI and behaviors

This change introduces the PreferencesDialog class which implements the main application preferences dialog. Main features and responsibilities:

- Builds a side-menu driven preferences dialog with a ListView of PrefsTab instances and a details pane for each tab.
- Adds a search box to filter preference tabs via PreferencesSearchHandler and selects the first match.
- Provides Import/Export/Show/Reset preferences controls with file dialogs and confirmation dialogs handled by DialogService.
- Implements import/export/reset flows: importing and exporting use JabRefPreferences APIs and show appropriate warnings; resetting clears preferences and prompts for a restart.
- Implements storing and applying preference changes: validates all tabs, stores tab settings, flushes preferences, updates GUI globals (entry editor colors), and refreshes tables.
- Adds updateAfterPreferenceChanges() to rebuild the ExporterFactory (using custom exporters, layout formatter prefs, save prefs, and XMP prefs) and refresh entry editor tabs.
- Uses ViewLoader to load the FXML dialog pane and applies a custom stylesheet.
- Integrates with existing application services/objects: Globals.prefs, JabRefFrame, DialogService, TaskExecutor, and ExternalFileTypes.

Other notes:
- Preference tabs are created and registered here (GeneralTab, FileTab, TablePrefsTab, TableColumnsTab, PreviewPrefsTab, ExternalTab, GroupsPrefsTab, EntryEditorPrefsTab, BibtexKeyPatternPrefTab, ImportSettingsTab, ExportSortingPrefsTab, NameFormatterTab, XmpPrefsTab, NetworkTab, AdvancedTab, AppearancePrefsTab).
- The dialog exposes a Save button which validates and persists all tab settings before closing.

This change centralizes preferences UI wiring and the interaction with persistent preferences and application-level updates.

Fixes a bug where linked file paths were being converted to relative paths even when the link was a web URL. Web URLs (http:// and https://) will no longer be modified; only local file paths are made relative.

Notes

- No changes to external API expected. This is a bugfix-only change.
- Tests added to prevent regressions.

Fix threading cleanup in performSearch to prevent thread/resource leaks and race conditions when searches are cancelled or when multiple searches run in succession. This change ensures search-related threads are properly shut down and that ongoing searches are cancelled cleanly.

Summary
- When a DOI resolves to a URL whose host has a tailored fetcher implemented, the DOI Resolution Fetcher will now return nothing so the tailored fetcher can handle the resource.

Why
- Previously the DOI Resolution Fetcher would follow the DOI and attempt to fetch content even for hosts that have dedicated fetchers. This caused duplicated work and occasionally incorrect extraction because the generic fetcher would run before the specialized handler.

What changed
- DOIResolutionFetcher: after resolving the DOI to a URL, check the host against the fetcher registry. If a tailored fetcher exists for that host, return nothing/empty instead of returning a fetch result.
- Fetcher selection flow: this change ensures tailored fetchers are preferred for their target hosts.
- Tests: added unit tests covering cases where the DOI resolves to
  - a host with a tailored fetcher (expect no result from the DOI resolver),
  - a host without a tailored fetcher (expect normal DOI resolution result),
  - non-resolving DOI (unchanged behavior).

Compatibility notes
- Behavior only changes when a tailored fetcher is registered for the resolved host. No other flows are impacted.

Other
- No database migrations or configuration changes required.
- This clarifies responsibility: DOI resolution will only supply a fallback when no specialized handler exists.

Summary

Remove the custom SSL certificate configuration that was added to JabRef. This change temporarily eliminates the user-configurable SSL certificate setting to help identify the root cause of https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/9171.

What I changed

- Removed the custom SSL certificate setting and any UI/preferences wiring for it.
- Reverted behavior to use the JVM/default truststore for HTTPS connections.

Why

The custom SSL configuration appears to be related to failures reported in issue #9171. Removing it isolates whether the custom handling is the source of the problem. This is intended as a diagnostic / short-term change; if the setting is not the cause we will restore or redesign it with a safer implementation.

Behavioral impact

- JabRef will now rely on the JVM's default truststore for HTTPS connections instead of an application-provided/custom certificate store.
- Users who relied on the prior custom SSL setting to trust self-signed or internal certificates will need to add those certificates to their JVM/system truststore until a new solution is provided.

How to test / manually verify

1. Start JabRef and verify the SSL-related preference is no longer present in Preferences.
2. Attempt to perform the network operations that previously used the custom certificate (e.g. connecting to internal servers or services). Confirm behavior matches using the JVM truststore.
3. Reproduce the failure reported in issue #9171 to see whether it still occurs with the custom configuration removed.

Notes for reviewers

- This is intentionally a narrow change to help debug a regression. If this change is accepted, consider adding a clear note to the user-facing documentation/CHANGELOG that custom SSL configuration was removed and provide guidance to users needing custom certificates.
- If we determine the custom configuration is not the cause, we should plan a safer re-introduction (for example, clearer UI, better validation, or documented fallback behavior).

Checklist

- CHANGELOG update: not yet added — should be included if this change ships to users.
- Tests: none added (behavioral / diagnostic change); consider adding tests if a new implementation is produced.
- Manual testing: performed as described above (please re-run on multiple platforms if possible).

- Added unit tests that cover single-level and multi-level inheritance, field overriding, and edge cases (no fields on intermediate classes).
- Minor documentation update describing inheritance behavior and examples.

Why this matters:
Previously, models/components that relied on inheritance could miss fields inherited from parent classes, causing incorrect schemas, missing serialized properties, and unexpected runtime behavior. This fix makes inheritance predictable and consistent.

- New/updated unit tests added and all tests pass locally.
- Manual verification of serialization/deserialization for inherited fields.

Compatibility/Migration:
- Backwards compatible: behavior aligns with intuitive class inheritance. No migration steps required.

Files touched (high-level):
- field collector / schema builder implementation (inheritance merging logic)
- unit tests
- documentation on field inheritance

Summary:
Fixes an issue where closing the library did not properly shut down the backup and autosave manager, which could leave background tasks running, leak resources, or cause exceptions during application shutdown.

Root cause:
The library shutdown sequence skipped coordinated teardown of the backup/autosave subsystem and did not unregister or stop scheduled tasks/listeners. As a result, autosave/backup timers could continue to run after the library was closed and reference disposed resources.

What I changed:
- Ensure the library close/Dispose path explicitly stops and disposes the BackupManager and AutosaveManager.
- Add proper ordering so autosave and backup are shut down before other components they depend on.
- Unregister listeners and cancel pending backup/autosave tasks on shutdown.
- Hardened shutdown with null checks and synchronization to avoid races when close is invoked concurrently.
- Added unit/integration tests that simulate closing while autosave/backup are active to verify no tasks remain and no exceptions are thrown.
- Added informative log messages during shutdown to aid debugging.

Testing and verification:
- New tests cover shutdown while autosave/backup are scheduled and ensure no active timers remain after close.
- Manual test steps for QA:
  1. Start the app and enable autosave/backups with a short interval.
  2. Open library and trigger some autosaves/backups.
  3. Close the library and observe that no autosave/backup tasks run afterwards and no exceptions appear in logs.

Impact and compatibility:
- Backwards-compatible behavior change limited to a safer shutdown sequence; low risk.
- Prevents resource leaks and intermittent exceptions during application termination.

Notes for reviewers:
- Review the shutdown ordering and synchronization in the library close path.

Introduce abstract query syntax and unified query conversion

What
- Add support for an abstract query syntax and centralize conversion logic to site-specific search queries.
- Implement QueryParser and ComplexSearchQuery to parse and represent fielded/boolean queries (AND / OR / NOT, field:value pairs, phrase and term handling).
- Update SearchBasedFetcher and SearchBasedParserFetcher to use the new parsing/conversion infrastructure.
- Adapt existing fetchers (ArXiv, GoogleScholar, IEEE, SpringerFetcher) to produce provider-specific query strings from the abstract representation.
- Add ADR documenting the design decision (docs/adr/0015-support-an-abstract-query-syntax-for-query-conversion.md).
- Update tests (QueryParserTest, ArXivTest) and CHANGELOG, and adjust module and build descriptors.

Why
- Provide a single, extensible way to express complex queries across multiple search providers.
- Make it easier to add new fetchers and normalize query behavior across providers.

Breaking changes / migration notes
- Fetcher implementations now rely on the abstract query representation; implementors of custom fetchers should adapt to the new API (see SearchBasedFetcher/SearchBasedParserFetcher changes).
- Query parsing behavior is now standardized; some edge-case query strings may be interpreted differently. Existing callers that build provider-specific queries manually should migrate to building abstract queries or use the parser.

- Core: src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/QueryParser.java, src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ComplexSearchQuery.java

- Integration: src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/{SearchBasedFetcher,SearchBasedParserFetcher}.java
- Tests: src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/QueryParserTest.java, src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ArXivTest.java
- Docs: docs/adr/0015-support-an-abstract-query-syntax-for-query-conversion.md

Notes for reviewers
- Focus on QueryParser and ComplexSearchQuery for correctness of parsing and escaping semantics.
- Verify provider-specific conversions in each fetcher to ensure generated query strings match provider expectations.
- Check the updated tests for examples of supported syntax and intended behavior.

text:
Introduce a complete JavaFX-based Groups side pane and tree implementation

What this PR adds

- GroupSidePane: A Swing wrapper that embeds the JavaFX GroupTreeView via JFXPanel (uses CustomJFXPanel on Linux). It registers/unregisters database listeners, listens to FieldChangedEvent for group field changes, and updates the main table according to the selected groups. The pane also exposes a ToggleAction and persists visibility in preferences.

- GroupTreeController: Full-featured controller for the groups tree UI.
  - Configures the TreeTableView with multiple columns (icon/name, hits, custom disclosure arrow).
  - Selection binding between the TreeTableView and the view model (multi-selection supported).
  - Debounced search input (reactfx timer) to avoid running the filter task on every keystroke.
  - Context menu for group operations (add/edit/remove subgroups, add/remove selected entries, sort recursively).
  - Drag & drop support: move/insert groups, drop entries onto groups to add them; visual feedback via pseudo-classes for drop position.
  - Reflection-based workaround to attach a clear button to the search field (with safe error logging if it fails).

- GroupTreeViewModel: ViewModel managing the group tree content and interactions with StateManager and MetaData.
  - Observes active database changes and updates the root group and selected groups accordingly.
  - Propagates selection changes to StateManager so the main table is filtered by selected groups.
  - Implements group operations (add subgroup, edit group, remove group or subgroups, remove/ add selected entries, recursive sort) and writes group changes back to MetaData.
  - Uses SwingUtilities/Platform.runLater where UI thread transitions are required and contains TODO notes for undo support and assignment side effects.

- BindingsHelper: Utility helpers for JavaFX bindings used across the new UI code.
  - any/all boolean bindings for ObservableList predicates.
  - includePseudoClassWhen helper to bind pseudo-class states to observable booleans.
  - mapBacked: a mapped list implementation that eagerly maps elements for faster access.
  - A set of robust bidirectional content bindings for properties, lists and maps with internal locking to avoid feedback loops.

- RecursiveTreeItem: A recursive TreeItem implementation that supports
  - child factory and expanded property binding,
  - filtering via an ObservableValue<Predicate<T>>; nodes are shown if they match the filter or if any descendant matches,
  - uses BindingsHelper.mapBacked to eagerly create child nodes.

Notable implementation details and caveats

- Group edits/creation/removal update MetaData immediately, but undo actions are currently not implemented (TODOs remain).
- Some operations (e.g., changing grouping method) ask for user confirmation; certain warnings about side effects are noted as TODOs.
- The search clear-button uses reflection to call ControlsFX helper. Failure to access that method is logged but does not break functionality.
- Styling relies on custom pseudo-classes (root/sub, dragOver-top/center/bottom, any-selected/all-selected) to provide visual cues.

Why this change

This PR modernizes the Groups UI by moving the group tree to a JavaFX-based view-model driven implementation with better interactivity (search, drag & drop, contextual actions) and tighter integration with the application's StateManager and metadata handling.

Testing notes

- Manual testing recommended for:
  - selection synchronization across databases,
  - drag & drop (group reordering and dropping entries),
  - add/edit/remove group flows,
  - search/filter behavior (debounced input),
  - behavior on Linux (CustomJFXPanel path).

Future work

- Implement undo support for group modifications and assignment changes.
- Add additional validation / disabling of context menu items depending on group state.
- Consider unit tests for BindingsHelper and RecursiveTreeItem filtering behavior.

Add serialization support and tests for save-action formatter cleanups in metadata

Summary
- Implement serialization of FieldFormatterCleanups (save actions) into MetaData so that configured field-formatting cleanups are written to and read from .bib metadata.
- Add unit test to verify the exact string representation produced by MetaData.getAsStringMap() for saveActions.

Details
- FieldFormatterCleanups: provides methods to convert configured cleanups to/from a metadata representation (getAsStringList(), parse()). Default and available formatters are defined and used when parsing or serializing.
- MetaData: when serializing metadata (getAsStringMap()), saveActions entries are serialized with proper quoting and newlines so that the resulting metadata string matches the expected format consumed by FieldFormatterCleanups.parse().
- Added MetaDataTest with two tests:
  - serializeNewMetadataReturnsEmptyMap: verifies an empty MetaData serializes to an empty map.
  - serializeSingleSaveAction: constructs a FieldFormatterCleanups with a single enabled LowerCaseFormatter for the title field, stores it, and asserts that the serialized metadata matches the expected format (including newlines and separators).

Files changed/added
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/exporter/FieldFormatterCleanups.java: serialization/parsing and helper methods for formatter cleanups.
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/MetaData.java: metadata serialization logic (getAsStringMap) updated to correctly emit saveActions lines.
- src/test/java/net/sf/jabref/MetaDataTest.java: new unit tests validating metadata serialization for save actions.

Why
- Ensures that user-configured save-time field formatters are persisted in the .bib file metadata and can be reliably read back by JabRef.
- Adds tests to guard the exact serialization format and prevent regressions in metadata handling.

Notes
- The serialization format includes an enablement line ("enabled"/"disabled"), followed by the formatter descriptions and appropriate newline separators. This format is compatible with the FieldFormatterCleanups.parse(...) implementation.

text:
Fix cleanup run on wrong entry when fetching from DOI

Summary:
When fetching bibliographic data by DOI or other identifiers the import cleanup was mistakenly run on the wrong entry (the entry into which the user wanted to merge), which could modify the local entry instead of the fetched one. This PR ensures the post-import cleanup is applied to the fetched entry before showing the merge dialog.

What I changed:
- In FetchAndMergeEntry, call ImportCleanup.doPostCleanup on the fetched entry (fetchedEntry.get()) instead of the local entry.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md to document the fix.

Why:
Applying cleanup to the wrong entry could lead to unintended modifications of the user’s database entry. Running cleanup on the fetched entry makes the merge dialog operate on a cleaned, consistent record.

Notes:
- Manually tested in a running JabRef.
- Fixes #6267.

Fix parsing of StandardNumber fields when converting MSBib entries to BibTeX

What I changed
- Corrected the regex and matching logic in BibTeXConverter.parseSingleStandardNumber to properly extract identifiers like ISBN, ISSN, LCCN, MRN and DOI from the MSBib "StandardNumber" string.
- Switched from matcher.matches() (which required the whole string to match) to matcher.find() so individual identifier patterns can be found inside a concatenated string (e.g. " ISBN: 123 ISSN: 456").
- Trim the captured value before inserting into the field map.

Why
- The previous pattern expected an extra leading colon and used matches(), so it failed to detect identifiers in the common formats produced by MSBibConverter (which produces strings like " ISBN:  ..." or "LCCN: ..."). As a result, standard numbers were not extracted and mapped to the correct BibTeX fields.

Impact
- ISBN/ISSN/LCCN/MRN/DOI values in the MSBib StandardNumber will now be correctly parsed and set on the resulting BibEntry (improves import/export fidelity for MS Word bibliography data).

Select the first matching tab in the Preferences window when the user types a search query so the most relevant settings panel is brought into view automatically.

What changed
- When a search is performed in the Preferences window, the code now scans tabs and selects the first tab that matches the query (by tab title or by content match depending on existing search logic).

Why
Previously users could search for a setting but still have to manually open the tab that contains the matching setting. Automatically selecting the first matching tab improves discoverability and reduces extra clicks.

- Added logic to iterate tabs in their visual order and select the first tab whose title or contents match the search query.
- Respects existing matching rules and only changes which tab is selected, not the search result highlighting.
- Does not change tab order or search scoring; ties are resolved by tab order.

Tests & QA
- Unit/integration tests added for: query that matches the first tab, query that matches a later tab, query that matches multiple tabs (first match wins), and query with no matching tabs.
- Manual verification steps:
  1. Open Preferences.
  2. Enter a search term that matches a setting located in a non-active tab.
  3. Confirm the Preferences window switches to the first tab containing a match and highlights the matched setting.

Compatibility
- Backwards compatible: only the visible selected tab changes in response to searches. No breaking API changes.

text:
Add Snap packaging and CI for JabRef

This PR introduces Snap packaging and a GitHub Actions workflow to build (and optionally publish) a snap of JabRef.

What changed
- Add .github/workflows/snap.yml: a workflow that runs on pushes to the snapcraft branch and on a daily schedule. It:
  - checks for the SNAPCRAFT_LOGIN_FILE secret
  - checks out the repository
  - runs snapcore/action-build to build the snap (with --debug)
  - if the secret is present, publishes the built snap to the Snap Store using snapcore/action-publish and releases it to the edge channel

- Add snap/snapcraft.yaml: Snapcraft metadata for the jabref snap. Key points:
  - name: jabref, strict confinement, base: core18
  - plugs: desktop, desktop-legacy, wayland, unity7, home, opengl, network-bind, removable-media, plus system-files entries for native messaging host files
  - apps: jabref (command: bin/JabRef) and browser-proxy (lib/jabrefHost.py)
  - environment: sets _JAVA_OPTIONS to use the snap user data directory
  - parts:
    - jabref: uses plugin: dump and downloads the portable Linux distribution from builds.jabref.org (JabRef-5.2-portable_linux.tar.gz). The override-build sets the snap version from the packaged .jpackage.xml, rewrites native messaging host paths to the snap browser-proxy, and removes the shipped JabRef launcher to be replaced by the launcher part.
    - jabref-launcher: local part (snap/local) that provides the actual JabRef launcher binary (organized as JabRef-launcher -> bin/JabRef).

Notes
- The CI workflow will only publish if the SNAPCRAFT_LOGIN_FILE secret is provided in the repository secrets.
- The snap uses the prebuilt portable Linux archive built by the project CI (https://builds.jabref.org/master/JabRef-5.2-portable_linux.tar.gz) as its source.

This change enables automated Snap builds and (when credentials are available) automated publishing to the Snap Store, making it easier to distribute JabRef to users on Snap-enabled Linux distributions.

Introduce a TaskExecutor abstraction and refactor threading-related code to make UI and background task execution explicit and testable

What changed
- Add TaskExecutor interface with two implementations:
  - DefaultTaskExecutor: production executor for background and JavaFX UI tasks
  - CurrentThreadTaskExecutor: synchronous executor used for deterministic testing
- Update UiThreadList to use TaskExecutor for scheduling list updates on the UI thread
- Refactor UI components to accept/use TaskExecutor:
  - SharedDatabaseUIManager
  - MainTableDataModel
  - GroupNodeViewModel
  - StudyDatabaseItem
- Refactor DBMS synchronization components:
  - DBMSProcessor and DBMSSynchronizer now schedule work through TaskExecutor
  - Improved synchronization lifecycle and error handling
- Small related model change in BibDatabase to cooperate with the new threading flow
- Update tests to use CurrentThreadTaskExecutor for deterministic behavior:
  - DBMSSynchronizerTest
  - SynchronizationTestSimulator

Why this was done
- Decouple threading concerns from business logic to make execution explicit and easier to reason about
- Make synchronization and UI updates deterministic in tests by allowing synchronous execution
- Reduce concurrency-related flakiness in tests and improve maintainability by centralizing task scheduling

Notes for reviewers
- Focus on usages of TaskExecutor in updated classes to ensure tasks are scheduled on the intended thread
- Tests were updated to use the synchronous executor; verify no behavioral changes in production execution paths
- This is primarily a refactor to improve testability and threading separation; functionality should remain unchanged

Why:
- To fix long-standing issues in name normalization (see related tests for cases such as "Smith SH", hyphenated initials, LaTeX-encoded names) and to make string utilities safer and consistent across various input forms used in importers and formatters.

Notes:
- This is primarily a logic/refactor change with extensive unit-test coverage to catch regressions and ensure correct behavior for many edge cases in author name handling and string utilities.

Add LinkedFile model, editor, view-model and file field (de)serialization with tests

This PR implements UI and model support for linked external files (e.g. PDFs) and adds comprehensive parsing/serialization tests for the file field.

Key changes:
- Model: Added/updated org.jabref.model.entry.LinkedFile
  - Implements Serializable with custom writeObject/readObject to support drag-and-drop and transfer of linked files.
  - Provides helpers: isOnlineLink(), findIn(...) to locate files in configured file directories, observables for UI bindings, equals/hashCode/toString.

- View model / UI:
  - org.jabref.gui.fieldeditors.LinkedFileViewModel: view-model for a single linked file with properties for download progress, automatic-find flag and operations: open, openFolder, rename, moveToDefaultDirectory, delete, edit. Uses RenamePdfCleanup and MoveFilesCleanup for rename/move actions and FXDialogService for user interactions.
  - org.jabref.gui.fieldeditors.LinkedFilesEditor: JavaFX control that displays a list of linked files, supports drag & drop (both internal reordering and adding files from the filesystem), double-click editing, keyboard delete action, context menu (Edit, Open, Open folder, Rename, Move, Remove link, Permanently delete) and a small progress indicator / accept button for automatically found files. Uses a ViewModelListCellFactory to build item nodes with icon, description, link, progress bar and accept button.

- Tests:
  - org.jabref.model.entry.FileFieldWriterTest: unit tests for FileFieldWriter quoting/encoding and FileFieldParser.parse behavior (empty input, parsing descriptions, escaped characters, Windows path escaping, handling of separators and missing fields).
  - org.jabref.model.entry.FileFieldBibEntryTest: verifies that a LinkedFile added to a BibEntry is serialized correctly both for a single entry's toString() and when saving a database via BibtexDatabaseWriter.

Notes / behavior details:
- LinkedFile.isOnlineLink() currently checks for http(s) prefixes or presence of "www." to treat links as online resources.
- Rename and move operations prompt the user before performing file system actions and handle conflicts via confirmation dialogs.
- Drag & drop supports adding files (copy/link) and reordering items via a serializable LinkedFile payload placed on the dragboard.

This change adds file-links editing functionality and improves the reliability of file field parsing/serialization with unit coverage.

Summary of changes

- Centralized background task management: Added background task tracking to StateManager (backgroundTasks list) with derived bindings anyTaskRunning, anyTasksThatWillNotBeRecoveredRunning and tasksProgress. New helper methods allow adding and observing background tasks.

- Improved drag-and-drop UX: Enhanced JabRefFrame drag-and-drop handling to show a temporary "Open files..." tab indicator when dragging .bib files, accept entry drag from the main table, and open dropped bib files or drop entries into the correct tab.

- LibraryTab lifecycle and loading improvements:
  - Better handling of asynchronous database loading: loading animation, feedData to set up the tab when the ParserResult arrives, and dataLoadingTask lifecycle management.
  - Autosave/backup management: installAutosaveManagerAndBackupManager() checks database readiness before starting AutosaveManager and BackupManager. cleanUp() ensures managers are shut down when closing tabs.
  - Indexing integration: updateIndex calls on load and incremental indexing on entry add/remove/field change (IndexingTaskManager and PdfIndexer usage).

- NewEntryAction enhancements: NewEntryAction now supports explicit entry type creation or interactive type selection and tracks new-entry telemetry (NewEntry event with EntryType property). It also guards against being invoked with no open database.

- Miscellaneous
  - Focus owner is bound to the scene focus owner (JabRefFrame). StateManager exposes focusOwner property.
  - Several internal wiring/refactor changes to better connect JabRefFrame, LibraryTab and StateManager (e.g., easier binding of open databases, active search propagation, and undo/redo event handling).

Why this change

These changes centralize background-task state, surface background activity in the UI, improve drag-and-drop behavior, harden library tab lifecycle and autosave/backup handling, and add telemetry for new entries. Overall the PR improves responsiveness, observability and user experience around long-running tasks and database operations.

- Add a short delay before running the global search to improve responsiveness when typing, especially on large libraries.

What changed
- Introduced a SEARCH_DELAY (400 ms) and use reactfx FxTimer to debounce text input before invoking performSearch(). This replaces the previous immediate subscription (EasyBind.subscribe).

- Minor API updates: replaced uses of java.io.File with java.nio.file.Path when resolving the database filename for the search results dialog (use getDatabasePath().map(Path::getFileName).map(Path::toString)).

- CHANGELOG updated to mention improved search performance and link to forum bug report.

Why
- Running the search immediately on every keystroke caused poor UI performance with very large bibliographies. Debouncing input by a short delay avoids excessive repeated search invocations and greatly improves typing responsiveness.

Testing
- Manually tested with a very large .bib ("Huge" file). Search responsiveness is much improved.
- Entry editor still causes noticeable load; this is out of scope for this change.

Notes
- No functional behavior changes to search results; only the timing of when searches are executed was changed.
- Tests were not added for this UI change.

- Thanks to @halirutan for pointing to the relevant code and inspiration for this approach (see #3553).

Add APS fulltext fetcher (ApsFetcher) and register it

- Introduces ApsFetcher, an implementation of FulltextFetcher that attempts to locate APS (American Physical Society) PDF URLs for entries with a DOI. The fetcher:
  - Resolves the DOI via doi.org redirects to obtain the APS-specific casing/ID.
  - Constructs the PDF URL using the pattern https://journals.aps.org/prl/pdf/{id}.
  - Sends a HEAD request (Unirest) to verify the PDF is available and returns the URL if the response status is 200.
  - Logs warnings on connection errors and handles malformed URLs.
  - Declares TrustLevel.PUBLISHER.

- Registers ApsFetcher in WebFetchers.getFullTextFetchers so it is used as part of the fulltext fetcher set (alongside other publisher and meta-search fetchers).

- Adds unit tests (ApsFetcherTest) covering:
  - Successful PDF discovery for a DOI with original casing.
  - Successful discovery when DOI is supplied in lowercase (ensures resolution and correct casing are used).
  - Behavior when access is unauthorized (returns empty).
  - Behavior for unknown/non-APS DOIs (returns empty).

Notes:
- This approach avoids using the APS Harvest API and instead relies on doi.org redirects as a workaround to obtain the APS-specific identifier required for the PDF URL.

text:
Improve progress reporting for fulltext-index operations

Summary
- Make indexing progress fine-grained by enqueuing operations per-file instead of per-database. This allows a sensible "x of y linked files added to the index" message and progress bar.
- Ensure the indexing task contributes to the global background-task average progress (so the top-right progress indicator reflects indexing progress).

What changed
- IndexingTaskManager: rewritten to use a ConcurrentLinkedQueue<Runnable> and an internal counter (numOfIndexedFiles). Tasks for creating/removing/adding index entries are enqueued per file and executed sequentially. Progress and messages are updated on the JavaFX thread via DefaultTaskExecutor.
- PdfIndexer.createIndex: signature simplified — it no longer requires a BibDatabase parameter and now only creates a fresh index. Writing entries is done via addToIndex calls (used by IndexingTaskManager).
- RebuildFulltextSearchIndexAction: updated to call createIndex() and then addToIndex(...) so the per-file task queue is populated.
- i18n: added message strings for "Indexing for %0" and "%0 of %1 linked files added to the index".
- Tests: PdfIndexerTest and PdfSearcherTest updated to reflect the new createIndex() / addToIndex(...) flow and to stub context.getEntries() where needed.

Notes
- The implementation uses synchronized sections to guard run state and a concurrent queue for thread-safety.
- Functionality of the index (what is indexed) is unchanged; this is a behavioral change for progress reporting and task scheduling.

Fixes: #7961

- UI options panel to choose between 'The ACM Digital Library' and 'The Guide to Computing Literature' and to include abstracts in downloads.

- Implements getWarningLimit(), getPreferredPreviewHeight(), getTitle(), getHelpPage(), and stopFetching() so it integrates with existing importer UI.

Notes:
- Uses URLDownload (with proper User-Agent) and respects application encoding/preferences.
- Returns Optional<BibEntry> and handles malformed responses safely.

Why:
- Ensure reproducible builds and avoid unexpected behavior from automatic Error Prone upgrades.

Summary:
Fix cross-reference resolution to follow the biblatex specification. This PR updates the existing crossref inheritance and merging logic so entries resolved via crossref behave according to biblatex rules, avoiding incorrect value propagation and ensuring explicit fields are preserved.

What I changed:
- Reworked the crossref resolution algorithm to follow biblatex semantics for field inheritance and merging.
- Ensure explicitly provided fields on the child entry are not overwritten by values from the parent entry.
- Correct handling for multi-level/chain crossrefs (resolve ancestors in the correct order and merge only allowed fields).
- Respect biblatex rules for which fields should be inherited vs. copied vs. ignored (e.g., title, author, editor, year behavior aligned with spec).
- Added/updated unit tests covering direct and chained crossrefs, missing parents, and conflicting fields to prevent regressions.

Why this fixes the bug:
Previously the resolver could overwrite child entry data or incorrectly merge fields, producing output that did not conform to the biblatex specification. The new logic enforces the proper inheritance semantics so bibliographies generated from crossref-linked entries match expected biblatex behavior.

Compatibility and notes:
- Existing databases should keep their entries; behavior for some crossref cases may change to be spec-compliant (this is intentional).
- No breaking API changes; internal resolver behavior updated.

Testing:
- Unit tests added/updated to cover the corrected behaviors.
- Manual spot-checks performed with representative bib files demonstrating direct and chained crossrefs.

Fixes: Bugfix/5045 (crossref resolution compliance with biblatex specification).

Summary
Replaces the old NormalizeNamesFormatter with the new AuthorList (AuthorListParser) implementation and fixes #318 (also references #950).

What changed
- Removed comma as a delimiter for author names in the name normalizer. Commas are ambiguous in BibTeX-style names (e.g. "Last, Jr, First") and can incorrectly split a single author into multiple entries.
- Introduced colon (:) as an explicit delimiter for separating multiple authors in the AuthorListParser.
- Replaced NormalizeNamesFormatter usage with the new AuthorList parsing/formatting logic.

Why
Using commas as delimiters caused incorrect author parsing for valid BibTeX name strings where commas denote "last, jr, first" parts. Switching to an explicit delimiter (colon) and using a dedicated AuthorList parser avoids ambiguity and preserves correct name parsing.

Compatibility / Migration notes
- If code or user input relied on comma-separated author lists, those should be updated to use colon-separated lists instead (or use BibTeX-style name fields which the parser now respects).

- Updated CHANGELOG to document the fix.

- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/sql/DBStrings.java (add dbParameters)
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/sql/SQLUtil.java (append dbParameters to JDBC URL)
- src/main/java/net/sf/jabref/sql/exporter/MySQLExporter.java (enable allowMultiQueries, use setCatalog)
- CHANGELOG.md

Notes:
- dbParameters defaults to an empty string, so other database servers are unaffected unless parameters are explicitly set.

What

- Implements feature request #1294: the OpenOffice/LibreOffice style selection dialog now filters for "*.jstyle" files and opens in the directory of the last selected style file.
- Fixes a NullPointerException when selecting an invalid jstyle file which previously prevented opening the style selection dialog.

Summary of changes

- CHANGELOG.md: Added entry for feature request #1294 and noted the NPE fix.
- FileDialogs: Replaced usage of the special Globals.NONE sentinel with an explicit extension parameter and check for empty extension; the file chooser now supports passing file extension filters.
- BrowseAction: Added an extension parameter and updated builder methods to pass file-extension filters through to FileDialogs.
- ExternalFileTypeEntryEditor / FileListEntryEditor / ManageJournalsPanel: Updated calls to file chooser to use the new extension parameter (defaulting to "" when not needed).

  - Improved layout/formatting and popup handling; added setDirectoryPath helper.
  - Selecting an invalid style no longer causes the dialog to break.
- StyleLoader: Validate styles with isValid() before adding them (both when adding new styles and when loading persisted styles). Invalid styles are ignored and an error is logged.
- Globals: removed the previous Globals.NONE usage in favor of explicit empty extension handling.

Why

- Improves usability when adding or selecting OOo/LibreOffice citation styles by focusing the file chooser on ".jstyle" and remembering the last used directory.
- Prevents crashes/blocked dialogs caused by invalid style files and avoids silently loading invalid styles.
- Cleans up the API for file dialogs by making extension filtering explicit.

- src/main/java/...: FileDialogs, BrowseAction, StyleSelectDialog, StyleLoader, ExternalFileTypeEntryEditor, FileListEntryEditor, ManageJournalsPanel, Globals
- CHANGELOG.md

Notes

- The new behavior logs invalid style files instead of throwing an exception; users will not be able to add invalid styles.
- Backwards compatibility: callers that previously relied on Globals.NONE should now pass an empty string for no filtering.

Refactor PDF rename cleanup and improve linked-file handling

What changed
- RenamePdfCleanup: Reworked the cleanup action that renames PDF files. The implementation now delegates linked-file updates to LinkedFileViewModel rather than manipulating paths directly. This improves correctness when updating BibEntry file links and when moving/renaming files on disk.

- No UI-facing changes expected beyond the improved correctness of rename operations.
- If you rely on custom workflows that expect the old (now-buggy) behavior, please review linked-file paths after upgrading.

text:
Introduce Localization utility for application internationalization

Summary:
- Add Localization class to manage loading and caching of translated messages and menu titles.

What changed:
- Load resource bundles from l10n/JabRef and l10n/Menu using UTF-8 via EncodingControl to support non-ASCII translations.
- Cache unescaped translations in an internal LocalizationBundle for fast lookups and JavaFX binding support.
- Provide public accessors lang(key, params...) and menuTitle(key, params...) to retrieve translated strings with placeholder replacement (%0..%9).
- Add special handling for menu translations: when a menu translation contains an ampersand (&) and is identical to the plain translation, strip the & for usages outside menus to avoid issues.
- Implement setLanguage(language) to switch locales, set defaults for Java and Swing, avoid unnecessary reinitialization, and fall back to English on errors.
- Implement lookup that logs a warning when a translation is missing and falls back to the key itself.
- LocalizationBundle (inner class) overrides ResourceBundle methods and intentionally returns containsKey=true to pretend all keys exist (needed for JavaFX inline binding).

Why:
- Improve i18n support by ensuring proper charset handling (UTF-8), caching for performance, consistent placeholder replacement, and correct handling of menu mnemonics (&) in non-menu contexts. Logging and fallbacks make behavior more robust when resources are missing or initialization order is incorrect.

Notes:
- Developers should use Localization.lang(...) and Localization.menuTitle(...) for all translatable UI strings.
- getMessages() exposes the cached messages bundle for components that need direct access.

Summary:
Add a new XMP Exporter that enables exporting image metadata in XMP format. The exporter supports both embedded XMP (for JPEG/TIFF) and sidecar .xmp files, and maps existing EXIF/IPTC fields into the XMP schema.

What I changed:
- Implemented an XMP exporter module (core/export/xmp_exporter.*).
- Added CLI flag and UI integration to trigger XMP export (CLI: --export-xmp, UI: Export > XMP...).
- Implemented field mapping from EXIF/IPTC to XMP and schema generation.
- Added support for writing embedded XMP into JPEG/TIFF and creating .xmp sidecar files.
- Added unit and integration tests for exporter logic and file output.
- Updated docs with usage examples and supported fields list.

Why:
Provide a standardized, extensible metadata export option for workflows requiring XMP (interoperability with Adobe products, DAM systems, and archival workflows). This preserves existing metadata and provides a portable XMP representation.

How to test:
1. Run unit tests: make test or pytest tests/test_xmp_exporter.py
2. From CLI: ./app --export-xmp path/to/image.jpg
   - Verify sidecar .xmp is created when configured for sidecar, or XMP is embedded into JPEG/TIFF when configured.
3. From UI: open an image and use Export > XMP... verify options and resulting file(s).
4. Inspect output XMP with exiftool -xmp:all image.jpg (or exiftool image.xmp) to confirm mapped fields are present and values match original EXIF/IPTC.

Backward compatibility:
- This change is additive and non-breaking. Existing export flows remain unchanged unless the new CLI flag or UI option is used.

Notes / Next steps:
- Extend mapping to cover additional custom tags as needed.
- Add an option to control namespace prefixes and custom namespaces.
- Optimize large-batch export performance in a follow-up.

Files of interest:
- core/export/xmp_exporter.*
- cli/commands/export.py (CLI flag)
- ui/components/export_dialog.*
- tests/test_xmp_exporter.*
- docs/exporters.md (XMP section)

Why

- Prevents accidental text entry in the Name field when users intend to confirm the dialog via keyboard.

How to manually verify
1. Open the group menu and click "Add subgroup".
2. Confirm that the OK button is focused (visible focus ring) when the dialog appears.
3. Press Enter and verify the dialog's OK action is triggered.
4. Confirm you can still focus the Name field manually (Tab -> Name) and type as usual.

Notes
- No visual changes to the dialog layout.
- Behavior remains the same when focusing the Name field manually; only the initial focus target changed.
- If you have automated UI tests relying on the Name field autofocus, update them to reflect this new behavior.

Summary
- Ensure downloaded files always get a file type assigned. If inference from MIME type and URL extension fails, fall back to PDF as default. This prevents downloads without an extension and ensures consistent handling of downloaded files.

- Added the StandardExternalFileType import and minor whitespace cleanup.
- CHANGELOG.md: added an entry describing the fix and adjusted a small formatting issue.

Why
- Previously, when JabRef could not infer the file type, downloaded files could end up without a file extension. Falling back to PDF avoids missing extensions and matches common expectations for downloaded attachments.

Issue
- Fixes #5816

- Add a new JSTOR fetcher that can retrieve bibliographic metadata from JSTOR pages/URLs and parse it into BibEntry objects.
- Register the new fetcher in the central WebFetchers registry so it becomes available in the UI and importer infrastructure.
- Include unit tests for the JSTOR fetcher to verify parsing behavior and edge cases.

Files changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/WebFetchers.java
  - Register the new JstorFetcher so it is discovered/available like other web fetchers.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/JstorFetcher.java
  - New fetcher implementation for JSTOR:
    - Detects JSTOR article URLs or identifiers.
    - Performs HTTP requests to fetch article pages / metadata.
    - Parses title, authors, year, journal, DOI, and other common fields into a BibEntry.
    - Handles common failure modes and returns appropriate ImporterResult/Optional types.

- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/JstorFetcherTest.java
  - Unit tests exercising the fetcher:
    - Successful parsing of a representative JSTOR page.
    - Tests for missing fields or malformed pages.
    - Verifies correct mapping to BibEntry fields.

Why this change

- JSTOR is a common academic resource; adding a dedicated fetcher improves users' ability to import references directly from JSTOR pages.
- Central registration ensures the fetcher integrates with the existing web-import UI and automated import pipelines.

Notes for reviewers

- Focus review on correctness of the HTML parsing logic and resilience against minor changes in JSTOR page structure.
- Ensure the fetcher complies with existing network/timeout and user-agent conventions used by other fetchers.
- Tests use sample HTML fixtures / mocked HTTP responses (see test file). If additional fixtures are required, they can be added in a follow-up.

Follow-ups / TODO

- Add more tests covering additional JSTOR page layouts and edge cases.
- Consider adding rate-limiting or caching if needed when used at scale.
- If JSTOR provides an API or machine-readable metadata endpoint, consider switching to that for more robust parsing.

text:
Summary

This PR implements multiple new features, UI improvements and bug fixes described in the Unreleased section of the CHANGELOG. The changes touch importing, file handling, fetchers, network preferences, and numerous small UX fixes and localization updates.

Main changes

- New user-facing features
  - Added context-menu options to copy DOI and copy DOI URL for entries (fixes previous behavior where "Copy DOI url" only copied the DOI). (#8389)
  - Added an option to open/reveal the folder holding a saved file and select the file. (#8195)
  - Added a new network preferences section to allow managing custom SSL certificates. (#8126)
  - Added two new ID/web fetchers: SemanticScholar and ResearchGate.

- Import & file handling
  - Centralized import logic via ImportHandler: supports importing files in background, creates empty entries with links when metadata is missing, imports BibTeX files, handles PDF metadata extraction and warnings, sets automatic fields and citation keys, and assigns imported entries to groups.
  - Improved drag & drop behavior in the main table: dropping files on a row will either import entries (top/bottom) or link/copy/move files to the target entry depending on drop location and transfer mode. MainTable now delegates to ImportHandler and ExternalFilesEntryLinker appropriately.
  - Unlinked files dialog can export a list of selected file paths to a text file.
  - Paste/copy/cut integrate with import logic and duplicate checking.

- Fetching / parsing
  - Entry-from-ID and generate-by-ID flows run in background tasks and prompt user to add entries manually when fetchers fail.
  - Plain-text BibTeX extraction: supports both local BibTeX extractor and optional GROBID remote parsing. Errors from GROBID are handled and user is notified; parsed entries are imported and telemetry events are tracked.

- Indexing / fulltext
  - LibraryTab integrates with IndexingTaskManager and PdfIndexer to (optionally) index linked PDFs for fulltext search. A preference controls whether fulltext indexing is enabled; the indexer is updated with the library's tab title.

- Localization & strings
  - Many new/updated strings were added to JabRef_en.properties (DOI-related texts, import/export messages, SSL/Certificate texts, progress messages, etc.).

- Misc / Fixes
  - Exports now use UTF-8 encoding consistently (including when embedding BibTeX/XMP into PDFs).
  - Various improvements and defensive checks across UI and background tasks (task cancellation, progress reporting, validation of selected directories, etc.).
  - Changelog updated (Unreleased) summarizing added / changed / fixed items.

Notes for reviewers

- Pay extra attention to long-running/background flows (GenerateEntryFromIdAction, EntryTypeViewModel fetching behavior, BibtexExtractorViewModel GROBID flow and error handling) to ensure exceptions and user notifications are correct.
- ImportHandler.importFilesInBackground and the undo handling were extended — please review undo compound edits and thread interactions carefully.
- Drag & drop behavior in MainTable now relies on drop-location semantics (top/center/bottom) — verify platform drag behavior and modifier key mapping.

Tests & QA

- New behaviors were tested manually: importing PDFs/BIBs, searching for unlinked files and exporting list, drag & drop import/link/copy/move, entry-by-ID flows, and GROBID parsing path.
- Localization strings were added; translators should be notified to update other locales.

References

- See CHANGELOG.md (Unreleased) for a high-level summary and issue references.
