Summary

This PR adds an abstract query parsing and mapping layer to convert user-provided queries in a simplified Lucene-like syntax into a structured ComplexSearchQuery that can be forwarded to fetcher APIs. The goal is to let users formulate advanced (fielded) searches in a uniform syntax and allow fetchers to consume structured queries (authors, title phrases, journal, year/year-range, and default terms).

What was added

- QueryParser: Parses a simplified Lucene query string into a ComplexSearchQuery using Lucene's StandardQueryParser. (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/QueryParser.java)
- ComplexSearchQuery: New model + builder representing structured fielded queries (default field phrases, authors, title phrases, journal, single year, year range) with parsing helpers and validation. (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ComplexSearchQuery.java)
- SearchBasedFetcher / SearchBasedParserFetcher: Added/updated default performComplexSearch/getComplexQueryURL behavior and helper to route complex queries to existing performSearch/getURLForQuery when the backend does not support advanced parameters. (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/SearchBasedFetcher.java, SearchBasedParserFetcher.java)
- Fetcher updates: Several fetchers were extended to accept ComplexSearchQuery and to construct API-specific query strings/URLs from it:
  - ArXiv: supports performComplexSearch using field prefixes and ignores unsupported year-range where appropriate. (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ArXiv.java)
  - GoogleScholar: implements performComplexSearch and maps ComplexSearchQuery fields into a Google Scholar query. (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/GoogleScholar.java)
  - IEEE: implements SearchBasedParserFetcher and provides getComplexQueryURL mapping ComplexSearchQuery -> IEEE API parameters. (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/IEEE.java)
  - SpringerFetcher: constructs complex query strings from ComplexSearchQuery for the Springer API. (src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/SpringerFetcher.java)
- Tests: Unit tests for query parsing and related behavior were added/updated.
  - QueryParserTest: verifies parsing of default and fielded terms, year and year-range, multiple same-field values. (src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/QueryParserTest.java)
  - ArXivTest: adapted/extended to exercise SearchBasedFetcher capabilities. (src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ArXivTest.java)
- ADR: documentation describing the chosen query syntax and rationale. (docs/adr/0015-support-an-abstract-query-syntax-for-query-conversion.md)
- Module / build updates: project module-info and build.gradle updated to include required Lucene modules/dependencies used by the new parser.

Behavior / Notes

- Supported field names (case-insensitive): author, title, journal, year, year-range, plus unfielded (default) terms.
- Multiple values for the same non-unique fields (e.g. multiple authors/title phrases/default terms) are supported and collected.
- Unique fields (journal, year/single-year/year-range): only a single value is stored; the builder enforces constraints (single year OR year-range). The QueryParser sorts and inserts terms; for unique fields the alphabetically first instance in the query string is used (see QueryParser javadoc).
- Default implementations ensure backward compatibility: if a fetcher does not override performComplexSearch/getComplexQueryURL, the complex query will be converted to default field phrases and routed to performSearch/getURLForQuery.
- Quoting: ComplexSearchQuery builder strips/normalizes quotes and wraps values in quotes where appropriate so fetchers receive consistent phrases.

Why

This change standardizes how advanced, fielded searches are expressed by users and enables fetchers to use more precise API parameters where available. Using a Lucene-derived syntax reduces learning curve and enables reuse of tested parsing code.

For reviewers / testing

- Run unit tests (especially QueryParserTest and fetcher tests).
- Spot-check fetcher behavior for complex queries (author:, ti:, journal:, year:, year-range:) and verify results are consistent with previous behavior when only simple queries are used.
- Review the ADR for the intended syntax and limitations.

Files of interest

- Added/changed: src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/QueryParser.java
- Added/changed: src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ComplexSearchQuery.java
- Updated interfaces: src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/SearchBasedFetcher.java, SearchBasedParserFetcher.java
- Fetchers updated: ArXiv.java, GoogleScholar.java, IEEE.java, SpringerFetcher.java
- Tests: src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/QueryParserTest.java, src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/importer/fetcher/ArXivTest.java
- ADR: docs/adr/0015-support-an-abstract-query-syntax-for-query-conversion.md

Preview & search: fix JS regex generation, centralize escaping, and add tests

What I changed

- PreviewViewer
  - Centralized JavaScript marking snippets and introduced createJavaScriptRegex(Pattern) to produce a JS regex literal (now escapes unescaped forward slashes). This avoids producing invalid JavaScript when the search pattern contains '/'.
  - Reworked highlightSearchPattern() to always call unmark and optionally pass a callback which invokes markRegExp with the generated JS regex literal.
  - Added constants for JS snippets and a Pattern to detect unescaped forward slashes.
  - Removed an unused StringBuilder in copyPreviewToClipBoard().

- SearchQuery
  - Reworked escaping logic into an EscapeMode enum with two implementations (JAVA and JAVASCRIPT) that know how to format/escape words.
  - Moved the JAVASCRIPT escaping pattern inside the enum and implemented format(...) methods to centralize escaping behavior.
  - Simplified pattern assembly using Streams/Collectors instead of manual StringJoiner/branching.
  - Kept behavior: when regex search is disabled, words are escaped according to the chosen escape mode.

- Grammar-based search rules / SearchRules
  - GrammarBasedSearchRule now uses SearchRules.getSearchRule(caseSensitive, regex) for choosing the concrete search rule implementation.
  - SearchRules.getSearchRule has package visibility so it can be reused from the grammar rule implementation.

- Tests
  - Updated ContainBasedSearchRuleTest to use assertTrue/assertFalse and refactored makeBibtexEntry() to use the fluent builder pattern.
  - Added GrammarBasedSearchRuleTest covering regex matching and non-matching cases for grammar-based rules.

Why

- Previously, Java regex patterns containing unescaped forward slashes could produce invalid JavaScript regex literals inside the preview's mark.js calls. createJavaScriptRegex now escapes forward slashes and returns a literal like /.../gmi to be used in markRegExp. Centralizing escaping also makes the code clearer and easier to maintain.
- Consolidating search escaping strategies in an enum simplifies the logic and makes it extensible.
- Making SearchRules.getSearchRule accessible enables the grammar-based rule to pick correct search rules (regex vs. contains).
- Added/updated tests to cover regex behavior and clean up assertions.

Notes

- createJavaScriptRegex attempts to convert a Java Pattern into a JS regex literal, but it does not reconcile differences between Java and JavaScript regex engines beyond escaping forward slashes and applying gmi flags.
- No behavioral change expected for normal searches; this mainly fixes edge cases with patterns containing '/'.

Summary

- Introduces a new database structure supporting: 1) schema names for PostgreSQL, and 2) table name prefixes for MySQL/MariaDB.

What changed

- Database layer: queries and table resolution now honor a configured Postgres schema or a MySQL/MariaDB table prefix.
- Configuration: added new settings (environment/config keys) to control the naming:
  - POSTGRES_SCHEMA (or db.schema) — optional schema to use in PostgreSQL.
  - TABLE_PREFIX (or db.tablePrefix) — optional prefix for MySQL/MariaDB table names.
- Migrations & SQL templates: all migration scripts and SQL templates have been updated to create/operate on schema-qualified tables (Postgres) or prefixed table names (MySQL/MariaDB).
- Docs & tests: documentation updated with configuration and upgrade steps; DB integration tests updated to cover schema and prefix behavior.

Why

- Support multi-tenant or namespaced deployments with Postgres schemas.
- Allow co-locating multiple installations in the same MySQL/MariaDB database using table prefixes.

Upgrade / Deployment notes

1. Backup your database before applying changes.
2. Set the new configuration keys in production:
   - For PostgreSQL: set POSTGRES_SCHEMA to the desired schema name (leave empty for current behavior).
   - For MySQL/MariaDB: set TABLE_PREFIX to the desired prefix (leave empty for current behavior).
3. Create the schema and grant privileges (Postgres):

Improve Group dialog validation and UX

This PR enhances the GroupDialogViewModel by adding comprehensive validation and better handling for all group types. Key changes:

- Added validators for group name (presence), duplicate names (warning), and name containing the keyword delimiter (warning).
- Added validators for keyword groups: non-empty search field, non-empty search term, and regex validity when regex mode is enabled.
- Added validators for free search groups: non-empty search term and regex validity when case-sensitive regex search is selected.
- Added validation for TeX groups: checks that a provided path points to an existing .aux file in the working directory.
- Validators are dynamically bound/unbound to the composite validator when the selected group type changes, so only relevant validations are active.
- validationHandler shows the highest validation message in a dialog and prevents the dialog from closing when validation fails.

Group creation and UI improvements:

- resultConverter now constructs the correct group implementations for Explicit, WordKeyword, RegexKeyword, Search, Automatic (keyword/persons) and Tex groups; resulting groups get color, description and icon set.
- texGroupBrowse opens a file dialog filtered to .aux files and stores a relativized path (relative to configured file directories / working directory).
- Exposed validation status getters and JavaFX property accessors for use by the view.

Error handling:

- resultConverter catches IllegalArgumentException and IOException and displays an error dialog with details.

This change improves robustness of group creation/editing by preventing invalid input (bad regexes, missing fields, invalid .aux paths) and giving users clear feedback.

# Changed database structure: table names are very generic [#9312](https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/9312)

Fixes #9312


- **PGSQL**: `jabref` schema added (table names unchanged).
- **MySQL**/**MariaDB**: prefix `JABREF_` added to table names.
- **ORACLE**: code unchanged as much as possible.

In any case, fields of the tables unchanged.

## checkBaseIntegrity (VersionDBStructure)

To check the integrity of the DB and to implement the automatic migration, variable `VersionDBStructure` was added in the table` METADATA`  to indicate the version of structure.

> Thank you LIM0000 for your PR.
Indeed, this solves the issue for `Remove groups > Also remove subgroups`.
However, a similar issue remains for `Remove groups > Keep subgroups`.
Please, could you look at this closely-related issue?

## Proposed solution:
Fixes https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/8390

- When removeGroupKeepSubgroups() is called, iterate through all selected groups instead of the group that triggers the event handler.
- Popup a confirmation dialog and confirm if user decides to delete:
  - single group
  - multiple groups (if multiple groups selection)
- All subgroups are assigned to their corresponding grandparents if there are any. Otherwise, they are assigned to `All entries`.

Fixes #7660
## Brief summary
1. Run EprintCleanup on a copy of the entry the ArXiv fetcher is fetching before getting arXiv id from the eprint field;
2. Add two test method. One finds full text with title containing colon and journal, while another finds full text with title containing colon and url.

## Problem
When finding full text, this BibTeX reference works:
```
@Article{booth_bayes-trex_2020,
  author        = {Serena Booth and Yilun Zhou and Ankit Shah and Julie Shah},
  journal       = {arXiv:2002.10248v4 [cs]},
  title         = {Bayes-TrEx: a Bayesian Sampling Approach to Model Transparency by Example},
  year          = {2020},
  month         = dec,
  archiveprefix = {arXiv},
  eprint        = {2002.10248},
  url           = {http://arxiv.org/abs/2002.10248v4},
}
```
![#7660-0](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/48386227/115873907-13c97c80-a476-11eb-821f-24598bd1a8a9.png)

But when `eprint` field is missing, no full text will be found:
```
@Article{booth_bayes-trex_2020,
  author        = {Serena Booth and Yilun Zhou and Ankit Shah and Julie Shah},
  journal       = {arXiv:2002.10248v4 [cs]},
  title         = {Bayes-TrEx: a Bayesian Sampling Approach to Model Transparency by Example},
  year          = {2020},
  month         = dec,
  archiveprefix = {arXiv},
  url           = {http://arxiv.org/abs/2002.10248v4},
}
```
![#7660-1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/48386227/115873922-188e3080-a476-11eb-80e7-222c58ee4e09.png)

## Solution
Since the title contains colon and arXiv uses colon to represent key and value, the title may be recognized mistakenly. So use other fields to get the eprint field to avoid this problem. Thanks to the advice from @tobiasdiez .

After fix:

A similar bug as #420 happened when the encoding was changed in the database properties dialog. This is now fixed in this PR. 

Sorry for introducing these bugs in the first place.

This fixes #2390. The last implementation used `EntryConverter.FIELD_ALIASES_LTX_TO_TEX`. This implementation is based on `BibtexEntryTypes` and `BiblatexEntryTypes`. 

## Issue
`JabRefPreferences.CUSTOM_TAB_NAME_num_` should be used to really determine the fields to check. This, however, is really a **huge** architectural rework.

It has to be checked, in following (seldom) situation:

- Field X is defined in JabRef's BiblatexEntryTypes
- Field X is added by the user to a general tab

JabRef now complains that X is Biblatex only.

## Further changes
 * ISBN and ISBN are now BibTeX fields, too.
   - Reason: Even though, both are not listed in [WikiPedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BibTeX) and the [lncs style](ftp://ftp.springer.de/pub/tex/latex/llncs/latex2e/splncs03.bst), I see them so hard tied to a book and article, that I would add it. In the case of a DOI, JabRef (more or less) enforces it by offering that field in the "General" tab. Moreover, [it is part of plainnat.bst](http://tex.stackexchange.com/a/52046/9075) and [natbib](https://www.ctan.org/pkg/natbib) is a popular package.
 * `FieldName.COMMENT` instead of `FieldName.COMMENTS` (affects OaiImporter only)
 * Preferences: Use FieldName constants at `setLanguageDependentDefaultValues()`

## Previous discussion about reworking IACR fetcher #8876
> We need to rewrite the IacrEprintFetcher to rely on https://eprint.iacr.org/ID (example: https://eprint.iacr.org/2022/674) only.

## Proposed solution
Fixes #8876 
1. `CITATION_URL_PREFIX` changes from `https://eprint.iacr.org/eprint-bin/cite.pl?entry=` to `https://eprint.iacr.org/`
2. new variable `VERSION_URL_PREFIX = https://eprint.iacr.org/archive/versions/` to retrieve latest version
![333](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/49628911/174420015-1a3f66a4-b4e1-42ad-8aa7-7b6ce015eef5.png)

In some instances, connecting to an existing JabRef instance may take longer
than the original 200ms timeout. Here we increase that timeout to a full
second. If it takes longer than that to connect to an existing instance,
chances are something else bad is going on.

Additionally, in a case where we attempt a ping but it fails for some reason,
but we're also unable to bind the port to listen ourselves, we give the
user a more informative error message about the potential cause of that
problem, and offer two possible solutions: figure out what other process
is already binding the port, or file a bug if that process happens to be
JabRef (since that would indicate that a 1s timeout isn't sufficient).

Fixes #8653.

This PR improves the performance of the journal abbreviation loader/repository/parser and thus is a partial fix for https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/2966.
Previously, loading and parsing the journal repository files took nearly 10 seconds and now almost nothing:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5037600/28175332-3b59e1da-67f4-11e7-9560-f2a504205c0a.png)
Main boost came from using `equalsIgnoreCase` instead of using `equals(text.toLowerCase())` and changing `LinkedList` to `HashSet` as we don't care about the ordering.
I had to adopt two tests which relied on the sorting.

Moreover, only one copy of the list is now stored in memory opposed to the 1 + 4 maps previously (equates to 1/10 RAM consummation). In principle, this makes the journal auto completion slower but I couldn't notice any negative impact.

text:
Addresses #2993

The frequent events are due to the bidirectional binding which transfers every change directly into the BibEntry. If we want fewer events, the only solution will probably be to break the binding, which would be very disappointing for the JavaFX implementation. In my point of view the problem is not on the side of event creation. After all, every change should trigger an event and JavaFX triggers many changes. Imho, this should be fixed in how we react to events.

I also noticed the exception, but do not get a dialog. This seems to happen because of the save operation invoked by the backup.

A solution might be to do less backups, by:
 1. Doing backups only every X events and not for every event
 2. Ignoring FieldChangeEvents in the Backup
 3. Adding the size of the field change in the FieldChangeEvent class, so that you can ignore it if only 1 character changed.

This PR combines options 1. and 3., i.e.: The backup manager ignores events that are very minor and only does a backup if enough of them have happened (currently set to five).

As discussed in #244, especially at https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/224#issuecomment-147650492, it would be good to show the currently active developers.

JabRef offers the team "developers", which are the currently developers of JabRef. There is also the organization, but these guys are more involved in the overall steering of JabRef and related projects (homepage, journal lists, ...) and not the concrete development and reviews of PRs in the JabRef code.

Similar to the AUTHORs list, I keep the alphabetical order. This is untypical, but more easy to create.

Side note: You have to have `GRADLE_OPTS` to be set to `-Dfile.encoding=UTF-8` on Windows to have the gradle build working correctly. See [README.md](https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/blob/master/README.md#building-jabref-from-source).

This fixes #1450 

After changing the preferences the mainTable is using a new `SplitPane` object to divide table and `EntryEditor` - in the course of creating the actual table existing entryEditors are closed which causes a saving of the current `EntryEditor` height in the prefs. To prevent this the previous state of the divider for the SplitPane is restored based on the prefs before the mainTable is recreated.
